CHAPTER 2 - RACES & BACKGROUNDS

The sun dipped low on the horizon, casting long shadows over the jagged peaks of the Cragspire Mountains. At the foot of these ancient stones, two figures trudged onward: Skrag, the half-ogre warrior with the strength of a giant, and Lustag, his steadfast Dwarven priest companion. The duo had faced many perils together, but today, their path led them into the depths of a long-abandoned temple, said to hold a relic of great power—a crystal heart that pulsed with the raw energy of Essence, the very life force of the world.

As they approached the crumbling entrance, Lustag tightened his grip on his holy symbol, whispering a quiet prayer to his god. "We tread upon sacred ground, Skrag," he said, his voice a gruff murmur that echoed off the stone walls. "This place has been untouched for centuries. The spirits here may not welcome intruders."

Skrag nodded, his enormous frame almost blocking the fading light as he peered into the darkened interior. "Then we ask permission, Lustag," he rumbled, his voice low but respectful. "If the spirits wish us harm, we will not stay long."

Together, they stepped inside. The air was thick with the scent of dust and old stone, and the silence was broken only by the drip of water from the cracked ceiling. They walked cautiously, the echo of their footsteps swallowed by the vastness of the temple's main hall. At its centre stood an ancient altar, covered in moss and entwined with roots that seemed to pulse with the rhythm of a heartbeat.

Skrag approached the altar, his eyes narrowing as he spotted the crystal heart resting atop it. It was a strange object—translucent, but with a swirling core that seemed to glow faintly in the dim light. He hesitated, sensing an unseen force at work. "This must be the heart of the temple," Skrag said, his hand outstretched but not yet touching the relic. "I can feel its Essence."

Lustag stepped forward, his keen eyes studying the crystal. "Aye, but something is amiss," he muttered. He closed his eyes, calling upon his divine connection. The air around him shimmered, and a soft glow enveloped his hands. "There’s a disturbance here, Skrag. The Essence is... tainted. It’s been corrupted."

Before Skrag could respond, the ground beneath them trembled. From the shadows emerged twisted figures, their bodies little more than bone and sinew, animated by dark Essence. They were the temple’s ancient guardians, twisted into undead abominations by the very life force that once gave them peace.

“We are not alone," Skrag growled, drawing his massive war club. The undead charged, their skeletal hands reaching for the intruders. "By the grace of my god, begone!" Lustag shouted, raising his holy symbol high. A pulse of pure Essence burst forth, scattering the nearest abominations. But more kept coming, their eyes glowing with the same corrupted light as the heart on the altar.

Skrag roared, swinging his club in a wide arc, shattering bone and splintering ribs. He fought with a controlled fury, each strike precise and calculated—a testament to the discipline he had learned under Lustag’s guidance. Yet, for every guardian he felled, two more seemed to rise from the cracks in the stone.

"Lustag, the heart! It’s feeding them!" Skrag bellowed, backing toward the altar as the undead pressed closer.

Lustag’s eyes widened with realization. "The crystal has become a conduit for corrupted Essence," he said, his voice grim. "We must sever its connection to the temple, or these creatures will overwhelm us."

Without hesitation, Skrag turned, raising his club high above the crystal heart. "May this bring peace to your temple," he said, then brought the club down with all his might.

The impact shattered the crystal, sending shards flying in every direction. A blinding light erupted from the heart, bathing the temple in a brilliant flash of pure Essence. The undead guardians let out a final, echoing wail before crumbling to dust, their corrupted souls released from their twisted bodies.

For a moment, there was silence. Skrag and Lustag stood panting, their chests heaving as they surveyed the now-empty hall. The tainted energy was gone, replaced by a gentle hum of natural Essence that pulsed through the air like the beating of a great heart.

"You did it, Skrag," Lustag said quietly, placing a hand on his companion’s arm. "You brought peace to this place."

Skrag shook his head, lowering his weapon. "No, Lustag. We did it together, as we always have."

The two turned and made their way back toward the temple entrance. As they stepped into the fading light of dusk, Lustag paused, looking up at Skrag with a rare smile. "You know, for a brute, you’ve got a surprising amount of grace," he teased.

Skrag laughed, a deep, rumbling sound that echoed across the mountains. "And for a grumpy old dwarf, you’ve got a soft heart," he retorted.

Together, they descended the steps of the forgotten temple, leaving behind a place that was no longer haunted by corruption. The story of Skrag and Lustag, the half-ogre warrior and the Dwarven priest, would spread once again—another chapter in the legend of two unlikely heroes whose bond transcended race, defied expectation, and proved that friendship is the greatest source of power the world has ever known.

Their tale, like the Essence itself, was a reminder that life’s true strength lies in unity, and that together, even the most improbable allies can bring light into the darkest of places.

RACES

From the ancient and noble elves to the stout and resilient dwarves, the races within these pages are designed to inspire your imagination and provide a wide array of options for character creation and role-playing. Each race offers a unique blend of rich history, distinctive abilities, cultural traditions, and physical traits. Whether you’re captivated by the elegance and grace of elvenkind, the clever adaptability of halflings, or the fierce strength of the orcish clans, you’re sure to find a race that aligns with your preferences and playstyle.

During character creation, you’ll choose one race, one heritage, and a background for your character. Each choice defines part of your character’s story, strengths, and role within the world. You’ll also select a number of languages based on your choices. Once your race, heritage, and background are decided, they cannot be changed later. After choosing your race and heritage, you’ll proceed to select a background, which will be detailed further in the next section of this chapter.

RACIAL ENTRIES

Each entry includes details about the race and presents the rules elements described below.

DESCRIPTION

This entry gives a physical description of the race, weight and height, starting age and lifespan, usual ethics and any relevant cultural details.

ABILITY MODIFIERS

These modifiers are applied directly to your corresponding ability score.

SIZE

This entry lets you know the size of your race. PC races will usually be small, medium or large. Size has a certain impact on the game and potentially limits your use of equipment.

SPEED

This entry lists how far a member of the race can move each time they use an action (such as Stride) to do so.

POWER POINTS

Power points are determined by your character class and a few other factors. These Power Points are what the caster would use to cast any spells that they know. Any modifier is granted as a bonus per level.

LANGUAGES

This tells you the languages that members of the race speak at 1st level. If your Intelligence ability modifier is 5 or higher, you can select more languages from a list given here. More about languages can be found at the end of this chapter.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

Your race may grant you one or more specialist skills. A specialist skill is always considered to be trained and gains an additional +1 bonus.

OTHER ABILITIES

Any other entries in the sidebar represent abilities, senses, and other qualities all members of the race manifest.

HERITAGES

Each race has a number of heritages which reflect its cultural differences and where it grew up. You must select a heritage from those available as part of your race selection.

FEATS

Each race has a selection of feats available to them. As long as you meet the prerequisites, you may select a racial feat at 1st level. At 5th level and then every 5 levels thereafter, you may select an additional racial feat. Feats are explored in more detail in Chapter 5.

ASCENDAN

Among the ancient races of the world, none are as enigmatic as this elusive and secretive lineage of humanoids. Often called the "First Race" or known by the name "Alphar," the Ascendan are widely believed to be the oldest of all humanoid peoples.

The Ascendan are an ancient and mysterious race, believed to have existed since the very dawn of magic in the world. According to legend, they were created by the dragons, who sought to imbue a humanoid race with the raw power to control and shape the arcane forces. The Ascendan were thus born with an innate mastery of magic, able to manipulate the elements and alter reality with ease.

Over the ages, the Ascendan became renowned as the most powerful and revered wielders of magic. They established secluded, hidden cities, choosing to live apart from the other races. Their immortality and unparalleled arcane abilities fostered a sense of superiority, leading them to believe they were distinct from the mortal realm. They built grand libraries and towering spires, dedicating their existence to the study and mastery of the arcane arts.

As centuries passed, the Ascendan became increasingly insular, retreating further into isolation while subtly shaping the world from the shadows. They developed a complex society rich in tradition and ritual, believing that their longevity bestowed upon them a solemn duty to preserve the world’s knowledge and history. In time, they became the guardians of ancient tomes, powerful artifacts, and the lost secrets of ages past.

Despite their immense power, the Ascendan were not invulnerable. They faced countless challenges throughout the centuries—from rogue sorcerers hungry for their power, to fearsome creatures and magical beasts that viewed them as a threat. Yet, the Ascendan always managed to prevail, drawing upon their vast magical knowledge and the wisdom of the ancients to protect themselves and their secrets.

Today, the Ascendan are a dwindling race, with only a few remaining in the world. Many of their once-glorious cities lie in ruins, and their magnificent temples and towers have crumbled with the passing of time. Yet, those who endure still wield formidable power, their mastery of magic unmatched. Their wisdom and knowledge remain highly coveted by those who are aware of their existence. The Ascendan continue to watch over the world from the shadows, using their ancient insights to guide and protect the other races from the hidden dangers that threaten the balance of the realm.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Ascendan males stand around 5' 5" tall, females are slightly shorter. Ascendan are very slim and have a perfect physical build. They usually weigh about 140 lbs.

Ascendan have a slightly golden complexion with large, slightly snake-like eyes.

The Ascendan have no bodily hair, which is believed to be a result of their magical abilities. They were said to have once had hair, but as their magical power grew stronger, it burned away their hair and left them with smooth, hairless skin. They also began to cover themselves in intricate tattoos, which they believed would enhance their magical abilities and provide them with protection against dark magic.

Ascendan typically reach physical adulthood around the age of 70 and will never be seen outside of their cities until they reach this age. Ascendan are immortal.

A starting Ascendan character has an initial age of 80+5d6 years.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Modifiers Str -1, Con -1, Int +2, Cha +2

Size: Medium; Speed: 25 feet Power Points: +1

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: High Tongue, Low Tongue, Wyrmish

Additional Languages: Choose from any other language that is not rare.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain the Ascendan Lore and Dragon Lore specialist skills.

OTHER ABILITIES

Darkvision: You can see in darkness without the need of a light source, though your vision in darkness is in black and white.

Ley Blood: Magic is in your blood, and you have a powerful affinity with it. You gain a +1 racial bonus to all attempts to sense magic. You also gain a +1 racial bonus to Arcana, Occultism and Spellcraft checks.

Arcane Knowledge: You may select any one arcane or ethereal cantrip (PP 0) and add it as an innate spell with the focus trait.

Forbidden Magic: You have absolutely no connection with either divine or verdant magic and cannot cast spells from these traditions. You have a -2 penalty to all saving throws against these traditions of magic and must also make a Will saving throw against beneficial spells of these traditions when cast upon you with a success allowing the spell to affect you normally.

ASCENDAN HERITAGES

Once you have selected the Ascendan race for your character, you must select one of the below Ascendan heritages. This heritage grants you some unique abilities.

AFELE

Often known as the Archaic, you are a guardian of knowledge and a keeper of the greatest secrets of your race. The tattoos on your body emanate a cool blue colour when you are spell casting.

You have lived amongst tomes and knowledge for your entire life and gain a +1 racial modifier to all Research skill checks. Furthermore, you also gain the Detect Signature specialist spell which you cast using your spellcraft bonus.

Loyalties You are sworn to protect knowledge in all its guises.

CHRONARA

The guardians of the Sky Doors are the highest cast in Ascendan society. When an Ascendan baby is allocated to their caste, they are bathed in the energy of a sky door to determine if this caste is their path in life. Only 2% of Ascendan will be chosen for this path, so you are naturally promoted to the position of leaders of your society. The tattoos on your body emanate a faint green colour when you are spell casting.

You gain the Shifting Step specialist spell which you cast using your spellcraft bonus. You also gain a +2 racial bonus to all Recall Knowledge checks concerning anything with the teleportation trait.

Loyalties The Sky Doors must be protected at all costs.

MENORA

Called Medicai by outsiders, menorah are the masters of the mind and body. You have been trained from a young age in the study of anatomy and how to both manipulate and repair the body. The tattoos on your body emanate a warm red colour when you are spell casting.

You gain a +2 racial bonus to all Treat Wounds (Medicine) checks and may select any one spell with the healing trait which costs one less PP to Warp.

Loyalties All life is sacred, and you will always do your best to avoid bloodshed.

PELORA

The Pelora are often called dragons, due to their close bond with such creatures. You are the warriors and military minds of your people. It is a great honour to be allocated to this caste as you will spend more time away from your people than other members of your race. The tattoos on your body emanate a dim yellow colour when you are spell casting.

You gain a +2 racial bonus to all Power Recovery (Meditation) checks. Furthermore, you also gain the Battle’s Call specialist spell which you cast using your spellcraft bonus.

Loyalties Honour and your word are the most important things to you.

URLOCH

You have lost the golden hue to your skin which has been replaced with a silvery blue tone. You have no tattoos on your body as your connection to the Ascendan source has been lost. You are an outsider, a renegade, or an outcast from Ascendan society, you are Urloch. Not all your kind are evil, but you certainly carry an amount of resentment from your people and feel abandoned or betrayed by them.

When you were a child, no caste called to your being during the testing of the sky door and you were sent away to live as an outcast, forever removed from your society and culture.

You lose the Ley Blood, Arcane Knowledge and Forbidden Magic Ascendan abilities. You gain an additional PP per level and may select any one spell with a maximum PP cost of 2 to add to your repertoire. This spell may be selected from any tradition. Furthermore, when you fumble a spell check, you add a +10 modifier to all fumble rolls.

Loyalties Undermine the efforts of the Ascendan people at all costs.

DWARF

Dwarves are masterful artisans renowned for creating works of incredible beauty. Their deep appreciation for precious stones and metals fuels their craftsmanship. They often choose to reside near rich veins of these resources, building vast mountain complexes and sprawling underground cities that form massive subterranean settlements.

Living beneath the earth, often in isolation from surface dwellers can sometimes make dwarves seem greedy and secretive and it does take them a long time to trust members of other races. Once you have the trust of a dwarf however, it will take a lot to break this trust. Their language is rarely taught to those of other races and they can go to great lengths to prevent a non-dwarf from teaching it.

Dwarves can come across as grumpy and bad tempered, fond of spouting profanities and complaining about everything.

DESCRIPTION

Dwarf males stand around 4' 5" tall, females are slightly shorter. Dwarves are a very stocky race and once dressed in armour often look wider than they are tall. The sheer denseness of their bodies gives them increase body weight, generally averaging 200 pounds.

Male Dwarves are passionate about their beards and grow them too great lengths. Only male Dwarves have beards. Female Dwarves grow their hair to great lengths and have the same respect for it as a male does his beard.

Dwarves typically reach physical adulthood around the age of 40, though their traditionalist culture places more value on completing coming of age ceremonies unique to each clan than reaching a certain age. A typical dwarf can live to around 350 years old.

A starting dwarf character has an initial age of 38+3d6 years.

Dwarves respect craftmanship, order and stability and any loyalties will be based around such things.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Modifiers Str +1, Con +2, Dex -1, Wis +1, Cha -1 Size: Medium; Speed: 20 feet Power Points: 0

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Dengaris, Low Tongue Additional Languages: Choose from any common language and Gaian.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Dwarven Lore and Stone Lore specialist skills.

OTHER ABILITIES

Darkvision: You can see in darkness without the need of a light source, though your vision in darkness is in black and white.

Hardy: Due to their natural resistances, dwarves receive +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison and magic.

Lead Boots: Dwarves make terrible swimmers and as a result of this suffer a -4 racial penalty to all swim checks.

DWARVEN HERITAGES

Once you have selected the dwarf race for your character, you must select one of the below dwarven heritages.

AZGAR

Known to surface dwellers as Fire Dwarves, the Azgar inhabit blazing deserts or volcanic chambers beneath the earth. Azgar have a remarkable adaptation to hot environments from ancestors who once dwelled in the elemental plane of fire. This grants you Fire Resistance and you treat environmental heat effects as if they were one step less extreme (incredible heat becomes extreme, extreme heat becomes severe, and so on).

DENGAR

Often referred to as Hill Dwarves, the Dengar are the most widespread members of the dwarven race. Although they live under the earth in great mountain complexes, all of their settlements have surface entrances and waypoints. The hardy Dengar are famed crafters and are sought after for their construction skills.

You also gain an additional crafting specialty. You gain advantage on all checks made with this speciality.

MORGAR

The noble Morgar live in high mountainous cities and are said to have the blood of giants coursing through their veins. Taller than most Dwarves the Morgar cannot grow hair from the heads but have very elaborate beards. The Morgar are often referred to as Mountain Dwarves.

Due to your honourable nature, you gain advantage on all Detect Deception (Sense Motive) checks. Furthermore, you are always considered to be trained when using the noblest of dwarven weapons those of the axe and hammer weapon groups.

STORGAR

It is strongly believed that the Storgar have the blood of earth elementals coursing through their veins. Storgar, generally live amongst other dwarven heritages but have distinctive brown skin and jet-black hair.

Your DR is increased by 1 due to your tough skin. Furthermore, you gain a +2 racial bonus to all checks to resist being shoved or moved involuntarily. Unfortunately, your attachment to the earth also forces you to make a DC 5 flat check when any friendly spell with the movement trait is cast upon you. If you fail this check, the spell does not work.

THENGAR

Your skin is ashen and your hair darker than other dwarves. The Thengar have long since inhabited the darker depths of the earth, acting as protectors of ancient tombs and burial sites. Thengar live in small family settlements, each dedicated to the defence of such a location.

You have Essence Resistance and gain a +1 racial bonus to your DB and Saving Throws against the attacks of creatures of the Undead Type.

ELF

Elves share a deep bond with the natural world, always seeking to live in harmony with their surroundings. To them, magic is simply another facet of nature, and they possess an innate talent for wielding it. Due to their immortal lifespan, elves often set aside projects for decades or even centuries, returning to them when inspiration strikes once more. This tendency to drift away is often misinterpreted by other races as a lack of focus or discipline.

As a result of their close bonds and keen sensitivity to nature, elves are often reserved and retain their secrets within their kinship groups and groves. This closeness to nature often makes forming lasting relationships with outsiders all the more difficult. They are blessed with immortal life and yet often see this as a curse, especially in their interactions and friendships with non-elves.

DESCRIPTION

Elves average 6' 2" tall, with females of the race ranging only a few inches shorter (racial variants also dictate this). All have very lithe forms with Elven males weighing around 120 pounds. Elves have swept back ears which top off in delicate points. Other than the hair which grows from their heads, Elves have no body hair. All Elves have chiselled features, and this combined with the thinness of their bodies often makes them seem delicate. Their eyes are wide and almond-shaped, featuring large and vibrant-coloured pupils that make up the entire visible portion of the eye. These pupils give them an alien look and allow them to see sharply even in very little light.

Elves reach physical adulthood around the age of 20, though they aren’t considered to be fully emotionally mature by other elves until closer to the passing of their first century. They are the longest lived of all the races, Elves are immortal and it is difficult for a member of another race to determine their age. It is said that Elves eventually tire of life and drift away from the mortal realms.

A starting elf character has an initial age of 108+4d6 years.

Elven loyalties are often directed towards nature and chaotic ideals.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Modifiers Dex +1, Con -1, Int +1 Size: Medium; Speed: 30 feet Power Points: +1

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Aelvish, Low Tongue

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language, Faechant and Gaelic.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Elven Lore as a specialist skill.

OTHER ABILITIES

Fey Blood: Your powerful link to the fey grants you advantage to all saving throws made against sleep magic.

Immortal: You do not age and gain advantage on all saving throws made against disease. You don’t need to sleep and will gain the benefits of a night’s rest simply by entering a trance state for 4 hours.

Keen Senses: You have superior senses that grant you a special +1 racial bonus to your Perception Skill.

Nightvision: You can see in dark areas and with a small amount of light can see well.

ELVEN HERITAGES

Once you have selected the elf race for your character, you must select one of the below elven heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

DRELVARNI

Not all elves believe in the protection of nature and the purity of their souls. The Drelvarni believe in advancement of the elven race and can only be described as supremacists. Few exist, but those that do are a constant thorn in the side to the other Elven people. Drelvarni tend to have jet black hair and very pale skin.

Known as a Shadow Elf, you are not necessarily evil, just more selfish than others of your kind. You gain a +1 racial bonus to Constitution.

Loyalties Unlike other elves, your loyalties are more likely to concern subjects other than nature.

ELARNI

Known as Sun Elves to other races, your people hail from the humid parts of the world such as deserts and jungles. Living under the intense heat and humidity grants the Elarni a single-minded purpose not often seen by other elves, as this environment can be quite harsh. Elarni wear their thick black hair in tight braids and dreadlocks, have dark brown skin tones and green or blue eyes.

This grants you incredible resilience to warm environments. You gain Fire Resistance and gain advantage to all Subsist (Survival) checks.

NOLDORNI

When humans and other races think of elves, the Noldorni or Star Elves are usually what they imagine. Slightly taller than others of your race and always having blonde hair and striking blue eyes, they are a perfect elven specimen, although some might say slightly alien.

You are closer to the source than other elves and may select any one arcane or verdant cantrip at 1st level which you may cast as an innate spell with the focus trait. You also gain a +1 racial bonus to Make an Impression (Diplomacy) checks.

SILVARNI

Known as Wood Elves for their love and defence of the forest and all things natural, these elves prefer to remain deep in the forests, away from humans and other races. Silvarni can be identified by their dark hair, usually black or brown and often have a coppery or green hue to their skin.

You have a love for the forest and ignore all-natural difficult terrain. Furthermore, natural formidable terrain is classed as difficult terrain for you. You also gain advantage to all Stealth checks made whilst in forested terrain (GM discretion).

SINDARNI

To other humanoid races, Sindarni are known as Moon Elves. Unlike other elves, Sindarni have a strong compulsion not only to interact with but reside amongst other humanoid races to fully understand them. Sindarni are slender and graceful with pale, often with an icy blue hue skin colour. They have blue or silvery white hair which is always worn long.

You have an inborn ability to detect and understand magical phenomena. You gain a +1 racial bonus to Cast a Spell (Spellcraft) checks made to cast spells of the Insight school. In addition, you gain a +1 racial bonus to Identify Power and to Decipher Writing of a magical nature.

TOLDERNI

Known as Snow Elves, Tolderni dwell deep in the frozen north and have gained incredible resilience against cold environments. Tolderni prefer to avoid contact with other humanoid races and can be quite aggressive to outsiders. They have pale skin and a mixture of hair and eye colours.

As a Tolderni, your exposure to the frozen terrain grants you Cold Resistance. Furthermore, you gain advantage on all Subsist (Survival) checks.

GNOME

Gnomes spend their days solving puzzles and mysteries. Knowledge is sought above all else and many members of the race have simply packed up and left their homeland in the pursuit of knowledge. Magic is considered to be the pinnacle of all knowledge, so it is not uncommon to find Gnomish spell casters of all sorts. Gnomes can also be quite secretive and generally hide their settlements away from the prying eyes of other races.

Constantly searching for the next thrill, gnomes constantly wander in search of magical knowledge and other experiences. They have an outlook on life that is sometimes considered random and even dangerous to other races as they will take many risks in pursuit of their goals. Gnomes trace their blood back to their fey roots, but it is clear to see that they also have a link to dwarves, for whom they have a strange affiliation with, often residing in dwarven settlements.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Gnomes are small in stature, standing just over 3 feet in height with a slight build. They are often mistaken for small children.

Gnomes usually have quite pale skin tones, but in reflection have wildly vibrant hair and eye colours. Gnome hair colour ranges from black to vibrant blues and greens. Likewise, their eyes can be a varied display of colours, often with each eye being a different colour.

Gnomes typically reach physical maturity at the age of 40, although their chaotic and wild nature often makes it hard for members of other races to understand this. They are long lived, with a lifespan of between 500 to 600 years.

A starting gnome character has an initial age of 38+4d6 years.

Gnome loyalties can vary greatly from companionship with a small animal, to adopting an entire city.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Modifiers Str -1, Dex +1, Con +1, Cha +1 Size: Small; Speed: 20 feet Power Points: +1

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Glimbol, Low Tongue, Faechant

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language and Gaelic.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Fey Lore & Gnome Lore as specialist skills.

OTHER ABILITIES

Detect Magic: You have the innate ability to detect the presence of active magic and gain a +2 racial bonus to all Sense Magic (Power Manipulation) checks. Additionally, you may develop the Power Manipulation skill without meeting its normal requirements and may make Sense Power checks untrained.

Gnome Resistance: Your connection to the fey grants you the ability to shrug off magic better than others. You may use a reaction when targeted by a spell to gain advantage to the saving throw.

Be aware that this ability does not apply to area effect spells.

Nightvision: You can see in dark areas and with a small amount of light can see well.

GNOME HERITAGES

Once you have selected the gnome race for your character, you must select one of the below heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

FURINI

The Furini live deep within forests amongst the mysterious fey. They are rarely seen in the realms of other races and prefer to live in quiet isolation practicing their magic and studies with an almost fevered dedication.

Due to the strength of your fey blood, you gain the fey trait, in addition to the gnome and humanoid traits. You may choose one spell school. You gain a +1 racial bonus to Cast a Spell (Spellcraft) checks made from this school and reduce all its warping PP costs by 1 (min 1).

NERINI

The appearance of a Nerini is vastly different to other gnomes. Their hair is always black; they have very pale skin and sport braided beards. They live in small settlements, often integrated with other gnomes or halflings. The Nerini have long since separated from their fey origins and seek to find inspiration to the questions through more divine means.

You gain Essence Resistance. Furthermore, your Cha & Wis racial modifiers are swapped around (Wis +2 & Ch 0) and you gain a +2 racial bonus to the Religion skill. Unfortunately, your links to the realm of fey are severed and this means that you can never be an ethereal or verdant spell caster and your Death State is reduced by 1.

SORINI

The Sorini have long since integrated with other races there small communities thriving within them.

The influx of greater input and knowledge from these different races and cultures has finely attuned your senses.

You gain a scent as a secondary sense. This means you can use your sense of smell to determine the exact location of a creature. The GM will usually double the range if you're downwind from the creature or halve the range if you're upwind. In addition, you gain a +1 racial bonus to Perception checks.

SVIRNI

The Svirni have live underground close to the borders of the fade. They are devoid of body hair and very suspicious of surface dwellers. Svirni can often be found living in dwarven settlements.

Due to your many years underground, your vision has adapted and you gain Darkvision. Additionally, you gain advantage on all Create (Varies) checks.

TIRVNI

The Tirvni are the most common species of gnome in the world. They live in small settlements on the fringes of human society, often close to woodland areas. Tirvni are friendly and welcoming to strangers, always curious and keen to make new friends.

The fey blood still runs within you, and you may select a spell of up to 2 PP (ethereal or verdant) and cast it as an innate spell with the focus trait.

HALFLING

Halflings are incurable opportunists. They rarely think ahead for more than a few minutes, and their plans more often than not go wrong. They are not the strongest of individuals and have long discovered methods to get around situations without resorting to the use of brute force.

Halflings are joyful and happy by nature, always seeing the good in every situation. They enjoy savouring the simple things in life such as a fine ale or a sweet pipe weed. They often avoid notice in the worlds of larger folk which suits them just fine. While many halflings do not have the ambition to leave their hearths and join a crusade or adventure, some prefer trouble to the mundane day to day of normal life.

Halflings like to eat and drink and will always be looking for the next meal or refreshment break. Add to this a lust for sharing and hearing tales of great adventure, means that it is unsurprising to find so many halflings in and around inns and taverns.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Halflings are small humanoids who look vaguely like small human children, but their larger hands and feet usually make this confusion rare. They rarely grow to be more than 3 feet in height. Halfling proportions vary but they rarely weigh more than about 70 lbs.

Most halflings have a ruddy complexion and dark or red hair. They cannot grow true beards but excel at long sideburns. Halflings shun the wearing of shoes and prefer to walk barefoot; this leads to rough calloused soles on their feet over time.

Halflings reach physical adulthood around the age of 20. A typical halfling can live to be around 150 years old.

A starting halfling character has an initial age of 18+2d4 years.

Halflings value friendship and family above all other things (well perhaps accept food, ale and pipe weed), thus their loyalties will usually reflect such things.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Modifiers Str -1, Dex +2, Con +1, Cha +1

Size: Small; Speed: 20 feet

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Munblish, Low Tongue

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Halfling Lore as a specialist skill.

OTHER ABILITIES

Extremely Nimble: Being nimble and light on your feet, you gain a +2 racial bonus to all Balance (Acrobatics) and Sneak (Stealth) checks.

Foolhardy: Your natural curiosity often lands you in trouble but also grants you an uncanny resistance against fear. You gain advantage to all fear-based saving throws.

Sure Shot: You have a keen eye when attacking with all types of ranged weapons. You gain a +1 racial bonus to all bow and sling attack checks.

HALFLING HERITAGES

Once you have selected the halfling race for your character, you must select one of the below heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

DUR-FOD

Often referred to as dark foot or dark feet halflings, Dur-fod live away from other halflings and make their homes in tunnels and caves, rarely venturing out in the day. Dur-fod are far more suspicious of other races than usual for halflings and try to avoid them as much as possible. There are even rumours of savage cannibalistic Dur-fod living in the dark places of the world.

You gain Nightvision and a +1 racial bonus to Perception skill checks.

GUL-FYR

Although rare, upon occasion a halfling will be born to one of the other heritages bearing the touch of sorcery. It is unknown how such halflings come into being, but their presence cannot be dismissed. These halflings, sometimes called magic fellows, possess some innate skill with magic which is unknown to others of their kind.

You may select any one arcane cantrip and cast it as an innate spell with the focus trait. You also gain an additional PP each level. Furthermore, you reduce your Con racial modifier by 1 to 0 but gain a +1 racial modifier to your Int.

LYS-FOD

Often referred to as light foot or light feet halflings, Lys-fod are the most common halflings in the world. Lys-fod can be found living in human communities as well in small villages of their own. Lys-fod possess a true sense of wanderlust and love to become involved in the dealings of others.

You gain two additional languages of your choice, chosen from among the common and uncommon languages available to you, and if you take the Linguist feat, you gain another new language. Furthermore, you receive a +1 racial bonus to the Culture skill.

STOUT-FYR

Often referred to as stout fellow halflings, Stout-fyr love nothing more than to tend to their crops and animals. It is rare that a Stout-fyr will leave their village for any reason, but when they do, they are solid dependable folk.

You gain advantage on all saving throws against effects with the mental trait. Additionally, you gain a +1 per level bonus to HP.

TALL-FYR

Out of all of the halflings, Tall fyr, sometimes called tall fellows are the closest to resemble humans. Tall-fyr resemble human children and are often mistaken as such. Unfortunately, being able to pass off as human children so easily has opened doors of opportunity for these halflings that are often closed to others, and they often find themselves running street gangs and such.

You gain advantage to all Bluff (Deception) and Make an Impression (Diplomacy) checks.

HUMAN

The most widespread of all civilized races are humans, Humans strive to expand, constantly pushing the limits of what they are capable of. Unfortunately, this drive to succeed throws them into sometime hostile situations with other races and other humans.

Humans are widely regarded as the most versatile and yet volatile of races. They form great communities of learning and knowledge as well as those capable of great destruction and bloodshed. Whereas other races have a clear definition or purpose, humans seem to have none.

Humans can be found in all environments from arctic to desert, mountains to shadowlands, you will discover their presence everywhere. Some form mighty empires and kingdoms, driven to explore and conquer, whereas others are simply satisfied to raise crops and families in a simple life.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Humans' physical characteristics are as varied as the world's climes. Humans have a wide variety of skin and hair colours, body types, and facial features. Generally speaking, their skin has a darker hue the closer to the equator they or their ancestors lived.

Humans reach physical adulthood around the age of 15, though mental maturity occurs a few years later. A typical human can live to be around 90 years old. Humans often intermarry with people of other ancestries, giving rise to children who bear the traits of both parents.

A starting human character has an initial age of 14+1d6 years.

Humans are so varied and different to each other that their loyalties can cover just about anything.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Size: Medium; Speed: 25 feet Power Points: +0

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Low Tongue, One Regional Language

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain lore based upon your ethnicity. This is either a lore based upon people (Hill Man Lore) or one based upon your heritage (Urban Lore).

OTHER ABILITIES

Skilled: Humans have far more varied cultures and upbringings than the members of other races. Your ingenuity grants you an additional skill point each level.

Versatile: Your natural versatility allows you to select two ability scores at 1st level, granting each a +1 racial modifier.

Bonus Feat: Humans may select an additional racial feat and an additional general feat at 1st level.

HUMAN HERITAGES

Once you have selected the human race for your character, you must select one of the below heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

ARCTIC

You have grown up amongst the people of the frozen north. Scraping out an existence in such a harsh environment is all that you have ever known. Your people may have been herders, hunters or fisherman, living in small communities amongst the tundra or icy coasts. It was often a nomadic life as you followed the migrations of animals. Living in such a harsh environment has taught you how to survive.

You gain advantage on all Subsist (Survival) checks and increase your Death State by 1. Furthermore, you gain +1 racial bonus to your Constitution ability score.

CITY

You are from a city or large town. You like to think that you’re more civilized and refined than those living outside of it. You tend to be friendly and relatively open-minded, as you’re accustomed to dealing with strangers and more exposed to different worldviews and ideas. However, ancient grudges and old enmities are hard to forget, so you might hold some prejudice against the dwellers of a neighbouring town, or foreigners from a certain land.

You gain the Skill Focus general feat and may add a +1 racial bonus to your Charisma ability score.

DARK

You have grown up in the deep dark places of the world. You may have lived in a small mining community; or in an extensive, intricate warren, sprawling beneath the earth’s surface; or maybe in great halls and fortresses, carved into the side of hills or mountains. In any case, you had little contact with people outside of your community, having spent much of your life without ever seeing the light of the Sun.

You gain Nightvision and may add a +1 racial bonus to your Wisdom ability score.

DESERT

To you, the most inhospitable of places was home, the desert. You have had a mostly nomadic upbringing, traveling from one oasis to another to replenish water supplies and trade goods. You were taught how to defend yourself and survive in the outdoors from a very young age. Desert folks are known for their fiery and passionate temperament, as well as for the great importance they give to oaths and promises, be it for good or ill. As the old saying goes “the Desert never forgets, and never forgives”

You gain a +1 racial bonus to Constitution ability score. Furthermore, you gain advantage on all Subsist (Survival) checks.

FEY

Members of the Fey Culture are the descendants of those who used their magical arts to shield their communities from the perils of the mortal world. You lived deep in the forest, in a strange village, hidden on the top of an ancient tree; or in the weird, moonlit halls of an enchanted castle, on islands that seems to appear only when certain conditions are met. They live peaceful, dream-like lives, in what seems an unending succession of feasts, parties, and celebrations. They tend to be unconcerned by the problems of the outside world, unless they menace to threaten the well-being of their idyllic communities.

You gain a +1 racial bonus to your Charisma ability score. Furthermore, you gain +1 Power Point per level.

HILL

You claim the highlands and rugged hilly areas as home. Most of your people were herders or farmers, living in large homesteads, villages, or small fortified clan houses. They tended to be rough, unsophisticated people. You’re wary of strangers, but love to sing and dance, and have a penance for theatrical gestures. In fact, skalds and minstrels are sacred amongst your people, who regard them as keepers of their traditions and messenger from the Spirits.

You gain a +1 racial bonus to Constitution. Additionally, you gain advantage on all Climb (Climbing) checks. 

NOBLE

You were born to privilege and education, hailing from a family of lesser or greater noble bloodline. Your family are landed gentry and have some influence in the area that you were raised. To the common folk, the life of a noble seems one of idyllic luxury but growing up as a noble or member of the aspiring gentry, you know the reality: a noble’s lot is obligation and intrigue. Whether you seek to escape your duties by adventuring or to better your station, you have traded silks and pageantry for an adventurer’s life.

You gain a +1 racial bonus to Charisma. Additionally, you gain advantage on all Recall Knowledge (Culture) checks based upon your local area. 

NORTHMAN

You are not sure where your family come from and probably have little interest. Going back several generations, your people broke away from civilised lands away from the political backstabbing of society. They formed small villages and learnt to earn their living from the land, hunting, warring with other clans and some trading. You value self-independence and survivalism but also honesty, traditions and freedom.

You gain advantage on all Demoralise (Intimidate) checks. Furthermore, you gain +1 racial bonuses to your Strength ability score. 

PASTORAL

You originate from a small rural community such as a farmstead or village. Your people are peaceful simple folk who enjoy nothing more than a tale and a pint at the end of a long day toiling in the fields. With a strong back and an understanding of seasonal cycles, you tilled the land and tended crops. For whatever reason you have left your peaceful life. Your farm could have been razed by invaders, you could have lost the family tying you to the land, or you might have simply tired of the quiet life, but at some point, you became an adventurer.

You advantage on all checks that involve, crops, raising animals and weather cycles. Furthermore, you gain +1 racial bonus to your Constitution ability score. 

PLAINS

You have always been accustomed to wide open spaces and vast steppe lands. Your people may have gathered in small, fortified towns atop low hills, or simply have wandered the plains in search of food and glory. You were born to the saddle and know your way around a horse or potentially other steed.

You gain advantage on all checks that involve a mount. Furthermore, you gain +1 racial bonuses to your Dexterity ability score.

TRIBAL

Your people are viewed as primitive by others. They reside deep in the wilderness as a small band of semi-nomadic tribes. The shamans guided you from an early age and spoke of great things that you were destined to achieve. You may have elaborate tattoos upon your body and ritual scarring. These tattoos carry great significance to you as they represent your rite of passage.

You gain a +1 racial bonus to Wisdom. Additionally, select either Arcana, Nature, Occultism or Religion, you gain advantage to all Recall Knowledge checks made with the selected skill regarding ancient lore.

KORNARGON

The origin of this ancient race is truly lost in the shadows. It is believed that once they were human but now they are something very different. Kornargon display the Shadow Plane's ancient influence through monochrome complexions, glowing eyes, and the casting of supernatural shadows.

The Kornargon were once humans who were banished to the plane of shadow as punishment for a crime committed by their ancestors. Over time, they adapted to their new environment, becoming skilled at navigating the shadows and developing unique abilities that set them apart from their human counterparts.

The Kornargon have a deep reverence for honour and hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct. They believe that their actions are a reflection of their character, and that upholding their code of honour is more important than personal gain or glory. They value loyalty, honesty, and courage above all else and consider it a great dishonour to go back on one's word or to betray the trust of others.

The Kornargon are known for their martial prowess, with a unique fighting style that emphasizes grace, speed, and precision. They have a complex social hierarchy, with the most honourable and skilled warriors holding the highest positions of power.

To outsiders, the Kornargon may seem mysterious and enigmatic, but those who earn their trust and respect will find them to be steadfast allies. While they are often feared for their abilities and their strict code of honour, those who take the time to understand them will find that their loyalty and sense of duty are unmatched.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

The Kornargon are tall and lean, with slender limbs and fingers that are suited for grasping and climbing in the shadowy terrain of their plane. Their skin is pale, devoid of pigment, and is highly reflective, giving them an eerie, otherworldly appearance. They have piercing white eyes and their hair is typically thick and curly, and ranges from black to a deep, midnight blue.

A starting Kornargon character has an initial age of 18+1d6 years but their lifespan is unknown.

Kornargon still hang to the honour of their pasts and often have loyalties which reflect this.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Mods Dex +1, Con +1, Wis -1

Medium; Speed: 25 feet Power Points: 0

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Nyxian, Low Tongue

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Kornargon Lore and Shadow Lore as a specialist skills.

OTHER ABILITIES

Darkvision: You can see in darkness without the need of a light source, though your vision in darkness is in black and white.

Skilled in Shadow: You have a knack for all things planar and shadowy. You gain a +1 racial bonus to the Planes and Stealth skills.

Shadow Stance: You gain the shadow stance ability (see below).

SHADOW STANCE

OPEN STANCE

Action 1 AP

When you enter this stance, you gain the concealed condition until the beginning of your next turn. At the beginning of each turn, whilst in the stance if you make a successful Sneak (Stealth) check that moves you a minimum distance of 10 feet, your concealed condition reactivates until the beginning of your next turn.

KORNARGON HERITAGES

Once you have selected the Kornargon race for your character, you must select one of the below heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

ERUI-IAR

When others of your kind remained in the plane of shadow attempting to scrape out a living, your people fought their way back to the material plane. You were forced to live on the outskirts of other civilisations, but managed to survive, nonetheless.

You lose the Wis penalty that other members of your race gain and also gain advantage to all Recall Knowledge (Culture) checks.

GALAD-IAR

Your people severed ties with the plane of shadow and have made their homes in the brighter planes of existence. You are often called the Bright Ones as you have a light not possessed by other members of your race.

You emit dim light within 5 feet of you. You can activate or suppress this ability as an action, which has the concentrate trait. Additionally, you can force fragments of your shadow to glow and cast dancing lights and light as ethereal cantrips using your spellcraft bonus.

OSP-IAR

Your people fled the plane of shadow in an attempt to find safer homes. Whether this plan failed or succeeded is a question for the scholars, but they eventually settled in the ethereal plane.

You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to locate undetected creatures within 60 feet when using the Search action. Furthermore, you increase the targets flat check to avoid being hit when concealed or hidden by 2.

TOVON-IAR

Your people live in the deepest and most treacherous regions of the shadow plane. You cast a deeper shadow than others of your kind.

You gain cold & essence resistance when you select this heritage.

ORC

To laugh is to taunt, to cry is to perish, to fight is to kill. Orcs more than any other of the core races live for combat and battle. They are born with the desire to kill and reap havoc upon their enemies (and each other). Tests of strength and brutality often cut their lives short, but what glorious and bloody lives they lead.

Orcs will often have difficulty working with others and have a hard time finding acceptance within non-orcish communities, many of which will at some point suffered at the hands of an orcish raid. If an orc can overcome these obstacles, their natural fighting prowess and loyalty can prove to become a boon for any village or town.

PHYSICAL DESCRIPTION

Orcs are physically bigger and broader than humans often reaching heights of over 7 feet and weights of up to 300 lbs. Orcs have heavy brows and jaws, often stooping when they move and stand, bringing their eye level down to that of the average humanoid. They often bare protruding fangs and wear scars, tattoos and tribal piercings with pride.

Orcs have very rough skin, iron like muscular frames and a very thick bone structure, which makes them superbly suited to war and conflict. Orc skin colour is typically green although some orcs have grey or black skin.

A starting orc character has an initial age of 13+1d4 years.

Orc loyalties are usually bloodthirsty and violent in nature.

It is unknown how long an orcs lifespan really is due to their warlike lifestyle. It is possible that they may even be immortal, but no scholar has ever recorded an Orc living more than about 50 years.

RACIAL MECHANICS

Ability Mods Str +2, Dex +1, Con +2, Int -1, Wis -1, Cha -1

Size: Medium; Speed: 25 feet Power Points: -1

LANGUAGES

Core Languages: Sharuk

Additional Languages: Choose from any common language.

SPECIALIST SKILLS

You gain Orc Lore as a specialist skill.

OTHER ABILITIES

Darkvision: You can see in darkness without the need of a light source, though your vision in darkness is in black and white.

Ferocious: Your warlike demeanour grants you a +1 racial bonus to all Melee Attacks and a +1-dodge bonus to DB.

ORC HERITAGES

Once you have selected the orc race for your character, you must select one of the below heritages. This heritage grants you some additional abilities.

SHARUK-DUR

Your people are often referred to as blood-orcs and are the most common of orcs believing that all blood is sacred. You relish spilling the blood of your enemies and have no fear when losing your own, making you much more resistant to bleeding.

All bleeding damage is considered 1 less for you (you ignore bleed 1) and the flat check to remove bleeding is 2 less.

SHARUK-MAR

You are giants amongst your people standing just over 7 feet tall on average. You are a little dim-witted but quick anger and very aggressive. You are sometimes called black orcs due to the charcoal hue of your skin.

You gain an additional +1 racial bonus to Con.

SHARUK-RIN

Known as bone-orcs, you are the master of night combat and are almost exclusively nocturnal. Many legends of monsters coming in the night and stealing children are accredited to these orcs. You have almost red skin and are a little shorter than other orcs

You are more nimble than other orcs gaining an additional +1 racial Dex modifier but reducing your Str racial modifier by 1. You also gain advantage on all Sneak (Stealth) checks.

SHARUK-XAL

You are one of the rare orc shamans or wise men sometimes known as grey orcs. You were born under a strange moon or during some other portent and have shunned the physical and violent ways (well maybe not completely) of your orcish kin in favour of developing more mystical skills. This has bent your form, and you seem withered and weather-beaten compared to others of your kind.

Your Str and Con racial modifiers are reduced to +1 but you also lose your penalties to Wis and Cha. Furthermore, your racial Power Points are +1 instead of -1 and you gain a +1 racial bonus to Spellcraft checks.

BACKGROUNDS

Every character that you create will have a different upbringing and origin which is determined by their background selection. Many legendary heroes began life as a humble merchant or grew up as the son of a tavern owner, practicing that trade until their family were killed by a giant raid. Your background pick will help flesh out your characters early life, from birth to wherever they are now. It is possible that your character is still an active member of the selected background.

When you create your character at 1st level you select one background of your choice. Once your background selection is made, it cannot be amended at higher levels so choose wisely. Your selected background will grant you a bonus feat, a +1-class bonus to up to three skills and a specialist skill.

Some backgrounds may also offer additional abilities which will be detailed in their descriptions.

ACOLYTE

You grew up living in a monastery or other religious enclave. You have left that life behind you but may still have ties to members of the religion that you once lived amongst.

BONUS FEAT

Theologian

SKILL BONUSES

Culture, Religion, Meditation

SPECIALIST SKILL

Religious Doctrine

ACROBAT

You have grown up earning your pay by performing as an acrobat. Maybe the work dried up, or perhaps something else drove you away from your home town…

BONUS FEAT

Sure Feet

SKILL BONUSES

Acrobatics, Athletics, Perform

SPECIALIST SKILL

Circus Lore

ANIMAL FRIEND

You have always had a natural connection with animals and have spent many hours training them. As you travel you befriend many animals.

BONUS FEAT

Animal Affinity

SKILL BONUSES

Handle Animal, Nature, Survival

SPECIALIST SKILL

Animal Lore

APPRENTICE

You were an apprentice to a craftsman. You may have been an apprentice to a blacksmith, tailor or some other specialist profession. For whatever reason, you were unable to continue your apprenticeship and have taken up the life of an adventurer.

BONUS FEAT

Specialist Crafter

SKILL BONUSES

Artistry, Crafting, Culture

SPECIALIST SKILL

Specialist skill related to your specialty

ARCANE APPRENTICE

You were taught lessons of magic by either a mercantile group of arcane casters or by an established member of a magical school.

BONUS FEAT

Magical Crafting

SKILL BONUSES

Arcana, Mental Focus, Power Manipulation

SPECIALIST SKILL

Spell Lore

ARCHAEOLOGIST

You have vast experience of archaeological digs and excavations. Something happened at the last dig that you were on that you will never forget…

SKILL BONUSES

Culture, Linguistics, Survival

SPECIALIST SKILL

Archaeology, One Ancient Civilisation Lore

BARBARIAN

You grew up in a harsh wilderness environment as part of a tribal society. You had no choice but to learn to survive from a young age and were taught to hunt, fight and live off the land. You are suspicious of outsiders and most things supernatural.

BONUS FEAT

Toughness

SKILL BONUSES

Athletics, Nature, Survival

SPECIALIST SKILL

Hunting

BARKEEP

You worked in a tavern or maybe even ran one. You learnt how to socialise and read people whilst pulling an excellent pint.

BONUS FEAT

Keen Insight

SKILL BONUSES

Diplomacy, Culture, Sense Motive

SPECIALTY SKILL

Barkeeping

BOUNTY HUNTER

Collecting the bounty on wrongdoers and absconders from the court has trained you in the skills of hunting people. These skills have transferred seamlessly to the life of an adventurer.

BONUS FEAT

Experienced Tracker

SKILL BONUSES

Culture, Sense Motive, Survival

SPECIALIST SKILL

Legal Lore

CHARLATAN

You have made your living through lies and deceit. Playing the part of a robbed noble in one town, the veteran war hero in the next or maybe a travelling salesmen selling placebo’s. Your tricks began to dry up and so you now are trying your hand at the career of adventurer…. Or maybe this is just your latest scam!

BONUS FEAT

Silver Tongue

SKILL BONUSES

Culture, Deception, Diplomacy

SPECIALIST SKILL

Underworld

COOK

The kitchen was your home throughout your childhood and into early adulthood. Cooking is your first love but for whatever reason, you are unable to work in the kitchens anymore.

BONUS FEAT

Seasoned

SKILL BONUSES

Crafting (Cooking), Culture, Survival

SPECIALIST SKILL

Culinary Lore

CRIMINAL

You grew up with undesirables and criminals. You may have been a member of an organised crime guild or perhaps you were a loner operating on the fringes of society. Regardless, you have left that world behind you in search of adventure.

SKILL BONUSES

Deception, Stealth, Thievery

SPECIALIST SKILL

Underworld

CULTIST

The people that you grew up with were strange by the standards of others but you were always fully immersed in their beliefs. You may have belonged to a group who worshipped dark powers or perhaps one that operated away from the prying eyes of authorities.

BONUS FEAT

Schooled in Secrets

SKILL BONUSES

Deception, Religion, Sense Motive

SPECIALIST SKILL

Lore related to your deity or cult

DETECTIVE

You were affiliated with law enforcement or perhaps solved crimes as an independent investigator. You have left that line of work after something went wrong with your last case.

BONUS FEAT

Streetwise

SKILL BONUSES

Culture, Perception, Sense Motive

SPECIALIST SKILL

Law Enforcement

DIPLOMAT

Engaging with foreign dignitaries or acting as an emissary to an enemy power have been your meat and drink through your life. Now things have changed.

SPECIAL

You begin play with two additional languages

Entertainment is all you have known from a young age. You grew up with a troupe of travelling musicians or actors and you have learnt to entertain crowds.

FARMHAND

You worked the land with plough and scythe, tending crops and livestock. Maybe your farm was destroyed by raiders, or perhaps you simply longed for something more.

Athletics, Culture, Survival

FIELD MEDIC

Where the army went, you followed, administering treatments to the wounded as you travelled. Sometimes your skills were called upon in the midst of battle. Regardless, you have learnt both to heal under pressure and something of the logistics of war.

LANGUAGES

In a realm where races, civilizations, and creatures of various origins converge, language is more than a mere tool for expression, it is a key to understanding, connection, and the weaving of narratives.

Within these section, you will discover the languages that shape the vibrant landscapes of your game.

At 1st level your race determines your beginning languages and determines any additional languages that you may select from having a high Intelligence ability score.

BONUS LANGUAGES

With a positive Intelligence score, you gain an extra number of languages equal to its value. You can select these languages from your character's racial list or from those offered by your region. Furthermore, for every 5 skill ranks you have in the Linguistics skill, you may learn an additional language.

Your GM may allow you to select different languages based upon the campaign.

LANGUAGE TYPES

Languages in this setting are categorized into the following distinct groups:

COMMON

This group encompasses widely spoken languages that bridge the gaps between different societies and races. Common languages serve as a universal means of communication, allowing individuals from diverse backgrounds to interact and understand each other. These languages are essential for trade, diplomacy, and cooperation on a broader scale.

LANGUAGE

UNCOMMON

These languages are less widespread and are often spoken by specific groups or communities. They might be used for specialized knowledge or secretive conversations.

LANGUAGE

CHAPTER 3 - CLASSES

Salinor, the elven mage of Mysthaven, stood as a beacon of ancient wisdom and a guardian of the natural world. His silver hair flowed like moonlight itself, a symbol of his deep connection to the arcane energies that thrummed beneath the earth. The ley lines that coursed through the grove were like the heartbeat of the land, and Salinor had learned to listen to them, to draw upon their power with reverence and care.

On this moonlit night, the tranquil grove became a stage for an unexpected encounter. Khajean, a necromancer steeped in forbidden knowledge, had followed him, lured by the promise of ancient magic and the hope of unlocking its secrets. Their meeting was one of stark contrast: Salinor, a master of life and balance, and Khajean, a seeker of dark truths, each representing a different path in the vast realm of magic.

In the brief, tense exchange that followed, Salinor's voice was firm yet tempered with a quiet compassion. He understood the allure of forbidden power but also knew the ruin it could bring. He offered Khajean a chance to step back from the precipice of darkness, to turn away from the path that led to corruption and decay.

The necromancer, though defiant, was not without a flicker of respect. He retreated, leaving behind a promise that their journeys would cross again. As the shadows swallowed Khajean, Salinor turned back to the ley line's whisper, his heart heavy with the weight of choices yet to be made. The grove fell silent once more, save for the soft hum of ancient magic, a reminder of the fragile balance Salinor had sworn to protect.

CLASSES

Your character class represents your skillset and core abilities. Your class describes how your apprenticeship and natural inclination influence your starting abilities and also how easy (or difficult) it is for you to develop Skills in various fields of expertise. It is usually a requirement that players design characters whose skills and abilities complement each other mechanically—for example, ensuring your party includes a healer, a combat oriented character, a stealthy character, and someone with command over magic—so you may wish to discuss options with your group before deciding.

Each character class provides you with numerous options, which really allow you to bring your character to life. Maybe you want to play a pious devotee of a deity, determined to end the plague of undead that has enveloped the land. Perhaps a stubborn hammer wielding warrior who loves nothing more than the sound of his weapon crunching his enemies bones. Or maybe a calm and considered master of the magical arts, whose only goal in life is her never ending lust for knowledge. These choices and more will help bring your character to life.

The first part of this chapter provides details of the character classes that you may select. The second part of the chapter concentrates on class feats, including archetype feats.

A character's class represents their skillset and core abilities. Your class will determine what skill groups you specialise in, what class feats you have access to and any other abilities. As you gain experience points (XP) for defeating monsters, roleplaying and overcoming various obstacles you will progress in level, gaining new powers and abilities.

LEVEL

Your level measures your overall power on a scale of 1 to 20 (and possibly beyond) and helps the GM determine appropriate challenges for you and your party. Most campaigns begin at level 1 with each Player Character possessing 10,000 Experience Points (XP).

It is assumed that starting characters would have already gained a certain level of expertise just by achieving level 1 in their class.

Some games may start at a higher level, in which case each character should start with the same amount of XP (determined by the GM).

As you complete adventures your total XP rises. Each time your total XP reaches the amount needed for the next level it goes up by 1 and you gain all of the benefits shown on the Level Table (see below). At this time you also gain any new benefits associated with your character class for progressing a level.

Levelling requires a brief period to reflect and train. You may generally only do so between adventures and during Downtime.

The Level Table below details a number of key abilities for your character.

Total XP: The amount of experience points required to achieve the indicated level.

Class Bonus: This bonus is added to any class skills that you have.

Ability Increase: At 3rd level and then every three levels thereafter, you may increase any one of your ability scores by +1.

Be aware that you may not increase the base value of an ability score above 6 with ability score increases.

Feats: This is the amount of feats you may choose from either general or specialist feats for your class.

CLASS ENTRIES

Players are usually given free rein to decide which class to pick. This may vary dependent upon the type of game that your GM is running. The race that you have picked will also have some bearing upon the class that you pick.

CLASS TYPE

Each character class belongs to one of three categories. These categories are Adept, Expert and Martial.

CLASS TYPE TABLE

Class

Type

Bard

Adept/Expert

Cleric

Adept

Crusader

Martial

Druid

Adept

Fighter

Martial

Ranger

Martial

Rogue

Expert

Wizard

Adept

DESCRIPTION

A brief description explaining what your class’s main purpose is and what its strengths are. Also included is an indication as to what role the class can play in a party of adventurers.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

These are the most commonly helpful ability scores for this class and also one ability score has a minimum requirement.

HIT POINTS

This entry tells you how many Hit Points per level you gain as a member of this class.

PROFICIENCIES

Gives the armour and weapons that the class is trained to use. You may expand upon these by selecting feats and may gain additional proficiencies from race and other options.

CLASS SKILLS

Your class will have a number of skills which gain a special bonus type called a class bonus. Your class bonus is determined by your class level.

SKILL POINTS

This is how many skill points you have to spend on skills each level. You may develop a maximum of 1 rank per level in any skill.

HIT POINTS

This entry will tell you how many hit points your character gains each time you take a level in the class. You also gain an additional amount of hit points each level equal to your Con HP mod and any racial modifiers.

CLASS ABILITIES

Your class will have access to a number of unique special abilities which will be explained here.

MAGICAL TRADITION

If you are a spell caster, a tradition of magic either arcane, divinity, ethereal or verdant will be listed here. If you are not a spell caster, you will still be required to select a magical tradition at 1st level. Once selected, this tradition cannot be changed so be sure to select wisely.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

If your class has spellcasting abilities, an ability score will be listed here which is added as a modifier to your spellcraft bonus. If your class does not have spellcasting abilities, this section will be left blank and you will gain a modifier to spellcraft based upon the tradition that you pick at 1st level as follows:

Arcane Int, Divinity Wis, Ethereal Cha, Verdant Con

CLASS SUMMARY TABLE

Each class also has a class table which shows the following information for each class:

BASE ATTACK BONUS

This is your character combat bonus. This value often abbreviated to BAB is used throughout the game to determine a number of other values and is also the bonus you use to make attack checks before modification. This value will be modified by ability scores and various other bonuses when making attacks.

BASE DEFENCE BONUS

This is your character defence bonus. This value often abbreviated to BDB is used throughout the game to determine a number of other values and is added directly to your DB.

FORT

This is your characters base Fortitude saving throw bonus which is added to your Constitution modifier to determine your total Fortitude saving throw. Fortitude saving throws are generally used to resist physical attacks such as death spells, disease and poison.

REF

This is your characters base Reflex saving throw bonus which is added to your Dexterity modifier to determine your total Reflex saving throw. Reflex saving throws are generally used to avoid area spells, breath weapons and traps.

WILL

This is your characters base Will saving throw bonus which is added to your Wisdom modifier to determine your total Will saving throw. Will saving throws are generally used to resist charm spells, fear affects and mental attacks.

BONUS FEATS

Your class will gain additional bonus feats, these feats can be used to select class feats for which you meet the prerequisites.

CASTER LEVEL

This is your class caster level for invoking spells.

POWER POINTS

This is the amount of power points your class receives every level.

BASE SPELLCRAFT BONUS

This is your base spellcraft bonus. Your casting ability score is added to this for spell casting checks. This value is abbreviated to BSB.

BARD

CLASS TYPE

Adept/Expert

DESCRIPTION

You are a master of artistry, a scholar of hidden secrets, and a captivating persuader. Using powerful performances, you influence minds and elevate souls to new levels of heroics. You might use your powers to become a charismatic leader, or perhaps a counsellor, manipulator, scholar, scoundrel, or virtuoso. While your versatility allows some to consider you a jack-of-all-trades, it’s dangerous to dismiss you as a master of none.

You can jumble and confound your adversaries in equivalent measure. Gifted with both weapons and enchantment, your actual abilities lie in inspiration.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Charisma (min +2), Dexterity, Intelligence

PROFICIENCIES

You are proficient in the use of light armour and shields. You are proficient in the use of all simple weapons, small blades, finesse weapons and the Shortbow.

CLASS SKILLS

Acrobatics, Arcana, Artistry, Culture, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Linguistics, Nature, Occultism, Perception, Perform, Planes, Power Manipulation, Religion, Sense Motive

SKILL POINTS

8 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

8 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Bard as you advance in levels.

BARDIC PERFORMANCE 

Action Free

To you the performance is everything and your magic is often inspired and rewarding. You may use your bardic performance in one of the following ways:

• Each time you cast a spell that has the composition trait, you may assign a temporary conviction point to any one of the spells targets (excluding yourself). This conviction point remains for the duration of the spell or until it is expended, whichever comes first.

• You may make a Perform skill check in place of a Spellcraft check when casting a spell which has the composition trait.

• You may make a Perform skill check in place of a number of social actions including, Aggravate, Create a Diversion, Feint, Encourage, Make an Impression, or Demoralise.

You may use bardic performance an amount of times equal to your Cha +1 each day.

BONUS FEATS

At 5th level you gain one bonus class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class traits (Adept, Bard or Expert) for these feats. You then gain an additional class feat at 10th level and then every 5 levels thereafter.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

At 1st level you may select any two PP 1 Bard Specialist Spells. You may learn additional Bard Specialist Spells by purchasing the Specialist Spell Feat.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are an ethereal instinctive spell caster. Your key stat for spell casting is Charisma, and you select your Spell Lists from the Ethereal Tradition.

At 1st level you may select any two PP 2 ethereal spells and add them to your spell repertoire. At 3rd level and then every two levels thereafter (5th, 7th etc) you may select a new ethereal spell and add it your repertoire.

You may cast these spells as long as you meet the casting requirements and do not need to memorise your spells.

At 5th level and then every two levels thereafter, you may swap any one spell from your repertoire for a new spell.

SONG & DANCE

A bard does not cast spells in the same way as other casters and each spell that you cast is part of a performance. When casting spells you always use one of your perform specialties and this allows you to add your class bonus to all Spellcraft checks and DC’s.

Furthermore, any casting components for spells which you cast are changed to those appropriate for your perform specialty type.

Be aware that this only applies when casting spells using Spellcraft. If you are using Bardic Performance the Class bonus does not apply.

BOOK OF NOTATIONS

As a bard you are constantly scribbling your songs, music and stories down to as you never know when you might need them. You keep a record of all such things and also gather together pieces of magical lore which you can intwine into your performances.

Each day during your daily preparation, you may select any one spell from your repertoire, or any one ethereal spell that you have a scroll for and cast it as a Specialist Spell until the following day.

At 5th level and then every 5 levels thereafter, you may select an additional spell to cast in this way each day.

CANTRIPS

You learn any two cantrips at 1st level. These cantrips may be selected from the ethereal magical tradition. These cantrips may be cast at any time and do not need to be memorised.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your charisma is your magical ability score. You add your Cha to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.
