CLERIC

CLASS TYPE

Adept

DESCRIPTION

You are blessed with the greatest of gifts, the ability to channel the power of the gods and mould it into powerful prayer and magic. Deities work their will upon the world in infinite ways, and you either serve them, or bend their will to serve you. Your spells might protect and heal your allies, or they might punish your foes and enemies, be at the will of the gods or not.

Play a Cleric if you wish to be the party healer and provide a little divine inspiration as well.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Wisdom (min +2), Charisma, Constitution

PROFICIENCIES

You are proficient in the use of light and medium armour and shields. You may use any simple weapon and any additional weapon as dictated by your deity.

CLASS SKILLS

Culture, Linguistics, Medicine, Meditation, Mental Focus, Planes, Power Manipulation, Religion, Sense Motive

SKILL POINTS

4 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

6 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Cleric as you advance in levels.

CHANNELS

As a cleric, you gain the ability to directly channel energy from the gods, or a specific deity you serve, to mend, protect, or restore life. You may use the Channels ability a number of times each day equal to your Charisma modifier +1.

Each time you use this ability; you may cast one of the following spells as an innate spell:

Cure, Inflict, Lifekeeping or Restoration

Channels is classed as an innate spell and thus requires no casting checks to use (see Chapter 9: Magic, for more details on innate spells).

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain the Heighten Spell feat.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

You gain any one PP 1 Specialist Spell at 1st level. This spell is based upon your deific aspect (see below).

PRIESTLY PATH

As a Cleric you have chosen a specific method by which you deliver your pious training. At 1st level you may select any one of the following Archetype feats as a bonus feat which becomes your Priestly Path:

Adventurer, Blessed by the Gods, Cloistered Priest, Enigma, Loremaster, Medic or War Priest

You must complete the progression requirements of this archetype feat before selecting another.

DEIFIC ASPECT

As a cleric you must select a deity or a divine aspect as your specialist field of study.

Your deific aspect grants you the following:

Edicts: A selection of edicts which must be followed.

Anathema: A selection of actions or behaviours that are strictly forbidden or deeply offensive to your deific aspect.

Suggested Ethics: A selection of ethics one of which you must select for your character.

Deific Skill: You gain a bonus class skill based upon your deific aspect.

Specialist Spells: As mentioned above, you select one of your deific aspects’ specialist spells at 1st level. You may learn additional Cleric Specialist Spells by purchasing the Specialist Spell Feat.

Bonus Spells: You gain a number of additional spells which you do not need to memorise as they are always available for you to cast.

Favoured Weapon: You add this weapon to your list of those with you are proficient with. Furthermore, you gain a +1-class bonus to all attacks made with this weapon.

Deific aspects and deities are explored in more detail in the Appendix.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are a divinity learned spell caster, and you select your Spell Lists from the Divinity Tradition.

To cast your spells, you must spend time in meditation during your daily preparation reciting from your prayer book. This process usually takes about half an hour. At the end of this time, you may select an amount of spells for which you meet the casting requirements, from the Divinity Spell List to commit to memory for the day equal to 2 + (level x 2). Spells committed to memory may be cast using your Power Points (Chapter 9: Magic).

CANTRIPS

Each day when you prepare your spells you may also learn any four divinity cantrips. You may select your cantrips from the Divinity spell list and may change them each day during daily preparation.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your wisdom is your magical ability score. You add your Wis to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

CRUSADER

CLASS TYPE

Martial

DESCRIPTION

You follow a code or purpose which is associated with your loyalties. From a young age you have always dedicated yourself to this purpose and will allow nothing to stand in its way. You may be a knight who has sworn to uphold the laws of the land, a freedom fighter who has vowed to overthrow a tyrannical regime or perhaps the servant of a demon who walks this earth to reap fear and terror upon the weak. Regardless of your cause, you are a mighty warrior who can draw upon the power of the gods to strengthen your blade.

To your allies, you are a shining light in combat and a force to be reckoned with by your enemies.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Charisma (min +2), Constitution, Strength

PROFICIENCIES

You have proficiency in all armour and shields. You may use all simple and martial weapons.

CLASS SKILLS

Artistry, Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Diplomacy, Handle Animal, Intimidate, Linguistics, Medicine, Religion, Sense Motive

SKILL POINTS

4 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

10 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Crusader as you advance in levels.

DEVOTION

Action Reaction: Trigger You fumble a check with either a class skill or favoured weapon attack.

Using your reserve and devotion to your cause you may expend 2 PP treat the check as a failure.

DIVINE RESOLVE

You are blessed by the power of your deity and may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1.

CRUSADERS MERCY

ESSENCE HEALING SOUL

Action 1 AP

As a Crusader you gain the ability to heal yourself of damage taken in combat as an innate ability. You may target yourself with a word of divine power which heals you of 1d8+4 hit points of damage. At 3rd level and then every 2 levels thereafter the amount healed increases by 1d8+4. You may use this ability an amount of times per day equal to your Charisma.

BONUS FEATS

At 4th level you gain one bonus class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class traits (Crusader or Warrior) for these feats. You then gain an additional class feat at 8th level and then every 4 levels thereafter.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

You gain any one PP 1 Specialist Spell at 1st level. This spell is based upon your deific aspect (see below).

DEIFIC ASPECT

As a crusader you must select a deity or a divine aspect as your specialist field of study.

Your deific aspect grants you the following:

Edicts: A selection of edicts which must be followed.

Anathema: A selection of actions or behaviours that are strictly forbidden or deeply offensive to your deific aspect.

Suggested Ethics: A selection of ethics one of which you must select for your character.

Deific Skill: You gain a bonus class skill based upon your deific aspect.

Specialist Spells: As mentioned above, you select one of your deific aspects’ specialist spells at 1st level. You may learn additional Cleric Specialist Spells by purchasing the Specialist Spell Feat.

Bonus Spells: You gain a number of additional spells which you do not need to memorise as they are always available for you to cast.

Favoured Weapon: You add this weapon to your list of those with you are proficient with. Furthermore, you gain a +1-class bonus to all attacks made with this weapon.

Your deific aspect also grants you either the Strike of Retribution (good) or Self Preservation (evil) reaction feat. If your deific aspect has neither the good nor evil trait then you may select one of the feats, but once selected, it cannot be changed.

Deific aspects and deities are explored in more detail in the Appendix.

DIVINE GRACE

At 2nd level you may add half your Charisma bonus to all of your saving throws.

DIVINE ALLY

At 4th level, your devotion attracts a spirit of your deity's alignment. Once you choose an ally, your choice can't be changed. The following are divine allies:

Blade Ally: A spirit of battle dwells within your armaments. Select one weapon when you make your daily preparations. In your hands, the item gains the effect of a property rune. You may choose called, courageous, disrupting, ghost touch, returning, or shifting.

Shield Ally: A spirit of protection dwells within your shield. In your hands, the shield's bonus increases by +1.

Steed Ally: You gain a young animal companion as a mount. Ordinarily, your animal companion is one that has the mount special ability, such as a horse.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are a divinity, instinctive spell caster and draw your spells from the divinity tradition.

At 1st level you may select any two PP 2 divinity spells and add them to your spell repertoire. At 3rd level and then every two levels thereafter (5th, 7th etc) you may select a new divinity spell and add it your repertoire.

You may cast these spells as long as you meet the casting requirements and do not need to memorise your spells.

At 5th level and then every two levels thereafter, you may swap any one spell from your repertoire for a new spell.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your charisma is your magical ability score. You add your Cha to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

DRUID

CLASS TYPE

Adept

DESCRIPTION

You are more than just a priest of nature. You belong to an ancient order of verdant magic. Druids are often found amongst tribal societies acting as priests, healers, lore master’s and law givers. As a Druid, you seek to preserve the natural balance of things.

Play a Druid if you want to be one with Nature and help your companions with your wise counsel and healing skills.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Constitution, (min +2), Dexterity, Wisdom

PROFICIENCIES

You are proficient with any non-metal armour or shield. You may use any non-metal weapon.

CLASS SKILLS

Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Handle Animal, Linguistics, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Power Manipulation, Survival

SKILL POINTS

6 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

6 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Druid as you advance in levels.

WILD EMPATHY

You have a connection to the creatures of the natural world that allows you to communicate with them on a rudimentary level. You gain a +2-class bonus to all checks involving communication with animals.

WILD SHAPE

You are one with the wild, always changing and adapting to meet any challenge. At 3rd level you may once per day, take the form of an animal as if using the Shape of the Animal spell (automatically warped to your maximum casting PP). You do not need to make a Spellcraft check for this change, the effect lasts for 10 minutes (1 hour if you use the 10-minute warping option) and you may reduce your size by one step (which increases accordingly with the default warping options).

At 5th level and then every two levels thereafter you may use wild shape an additional time each day.

Finally, you gain a +1-class bonus to all attacks made using natural weapons when using this ability or any form spell.

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain the Heighten Spell feat and the Wild Stride Feat.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

You gain any one PP 1 Druid Specialist Spell at 1st level. You may learn additional Druid Specialist Spells by purchasing the Specialist Skill Feat.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are a verdant, learned spell caster and may select your Spell Lists from the Verdant Tradition.

To cast your spells, you must spend time in communion with nature during your daily preparation. This process usually takes about half an hour and must be carried out in an outdoor rural or wilderness environment (GM discretion). At the end of this time, you may select an amount of spells for which you meet the casting requirements, from the Verdant Spell List to commit to memory for the day equal to 2 + (level x 2). Spells committed to memory may be cast using your Power Points (Chapter 9: Magic).

CANTRIPS

Each day when you prepare your spells you may also learn any four verdant cantrips. You may select your cantrips from the Verdant spell list and may change them each day during daily preparation.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your constitution is your magical ability score. You add your Con to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

DRUIDIC CODE

As a druid, you cannot tolerate affronts to nature and. You cannot use metal armour or shields and may not despoil natural places. If the code is broken, you may lose your druidic abilities (GM Discretion).

FIGHTER

CLASS TYPE

Martial

DESCRIPTION

You are the master of arms and combat. You possess unparalleled skills in fighting with all kinds of weapons, both melee and ranged, as well as in unarmed combat. You can also wear heavy, cumbersome armour and be more efficient and functional than any other character while doing that. You can take a formidable amount of punishment before giving up the fight.

Fighter is definitely the type of character you want to play if you prefer a direct, straightforward approach and if you want to be involved in epic battles and be remembered by your deeds of valour and your legendary fighting skills.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Strength or Dexterity (min +2), Constitution

PROFICIENCIES

You are proficient in the use of all armour and shields (including tower shields). You may use all simple and martial weapons.

CLASS SKILLS

Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Diplomacy, Handle Animal, Intimidate, Survival

SKILL POINTS

4 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

12 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Fighter as you advance in levels.

WARRIOR’S RESOLVE

You are a gritty front-line warrior and may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1.

MARTIAL TRAINING

Your martial training has exposed you to specialised schools of combat beyond the normal limits of your class. You may select one of the following Archetype feats:

Aegis, Archer, Armour Master, Cavalier, Champion, Vanguard or Warden

You do not need to meet the feat’s normal prerequisites or progression requirements when selecting this feat through Martial Archetype Training. This archetype feat does not prevent you from selecting another archetype feat later. It also does not require you to complete its progression requirements before selecting another archetype.

BATTLE READINESS

At 2nd level you learn to react to violence faster than other warriors, turning openings into immediate action. At the start of each round, you gain one additional reaction. This reaction can only be used to perform an action with the Reaction action type that also has either the Attack trait or the Martial trait. If an ability would allow you to make multiple reactions from a single trigger, you may still only use one reaction for that trigger unless the ability specifically states otherwise.

ARMOUR EXEMPLAR

At 3rd level, you learn to be more manoeuvrable whilst wearing armour. Whenever you are wearing armour, you reduce the armour check penalty by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by your armour by 1. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and 15th), these bonuses increase by 1 each time, to a maximum –4 reduction of the armour check penalty and a +4 increase of the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed.

WEAPON EXEMPLAR

At 4th level, you can select one group of weapons, as noted below. Whenever you attack with a weapon from this group, you gain a +1-class bonus on attack rolls and damage rolls. At 8th level and every four levels thereafter, you become further trained in another group of weapons. You gain a +1-class bonus on attack rolls and damage rolls when using a weapon from this group. In addition, the bonuses granted by previous weapon groups increase by +1 each. Bonuses granted from overlapping groups do not stack. Take the highest bonus granted for a weapon if it resides in two or more groups.

PRESS THE ADVANATGE

At 4th level, you know how to exploit a shift in battle before your enemy can recover. Once per round, when you achieve one of the following, you may immediately Step 5 feet or Interact as a free action:

• You inflict a critical hit.

• You disable an enemy (either reducing to 0 HP, killing them or rendering them unconscious).

• You successfully Shove, Trip, Disarm, Grapple, or otherwise succeed at a martial combat manoeuvre.

• An enemy within your reach fumbles an attack against you.

The Interact action must relate directly to the current combat, such as drawing a weapon, changing grip, drawing ammunition, opening or closing a door, grabbing an item, switching weapons, or manipulating battlefield gear.

At 13th level, when Press the Advantage allows you to Step, you may instead Stride up to half your Speed. This movement must either move you adjacent to an enemy, into cover, into a flanking position, or into a position that protects an ally.

UNBREAKABLE RESOLVE

At 9th level, your discipline allows you to endure effects that would break lesser warriors. Once per day, when you fail a Fortitude, Reflex, or Will saving throw, you may reroll the saving throw. You must use the second result.

At 15th level, you may use Unbreakable Resolve twice per day.

At 19th level, if the second result is a Partial, you may treat it as a Success.

WEAPON SUPREMACY

At 13th level, Your mastery of chosen weapons is so complete that near-misses become telling blows. When making a Strike with a weapon from one of your weapon groups selected with weapon exemplar, you treat a miss by 1 as a hit.

This does not apply if the attack was made with disadvantage.

At 19th level, you treat a miss by 2 or less as a hit.

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain one bonus class feat. You must meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class traits (Fighter or Warrior) for these feats. You then gain an additional class feat at 3rd level and then every 2 levels thereafter.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You have no spell casting abilities but must select a magical tradition at 1st level.

RANGER

CLASS TYPE

Martial

DESCRIPTION

You know how to live off the land and are skilled at spotting and taking down both opportune prey and hated enemies.

Some rangers believe civilization wears down the soul but still needs to be protected from wild creatures. Others say nature needs to be protected from the greedy, who wish to tame its beauty and plunder its treasures. You could champion either goal, or both. You might be a scout, tracker, or hunter of fugitives or beasts, haunting the edge of civilization or exploring the wilds.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Constitution (min +2), Dexterity, Wisdom

PROFICIENCIES

You have proficiency in non-metal light armour, medium armour and shields. You may use all simple and martial weapons.

CLASS SKILLS

Acrobatics, Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Handle Animal, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival

SKILL POINTS

6 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

10 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Ranger as you advance in levels.

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain the Favoured Terrain feat. At 4th level and then every 4 levels thereafter you may select an additional class feat. This class feat must be one for which you meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class trait (Ranger or Martial).

HUNT PREY

CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

You designate a single creature as your prey and focus your attacks against that creature. You must be able to see or hear the prey, or you must be tracking the prey. You may add your class bonus to all checks made against your prey

You can have only one creature designated as your prey at a time. If you use Hunt Prey against a creature when you already have a creature designated, the prior creature loses the designation, and the new prey gains the designation.

TRAP FINDER

You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps, to DB against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps. Even if you aren’t Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

If you have 10 or more ranks in the perception skill, your bonus increases to +4.

HUNTER’S METHOD

When you use Hunt Prey, you also apply one Hunter’s Method. You select your Hunter’s Method during daily preparation.

Hunter’s Method

Benefit

Precision Hunter

Once per round, the first time you damage your hunted prey with a Strike, you deal +1d6 precision damage. This becomes +2d6 at 9th level and +3d6 at 17th level.

Relentless Hunter

Your multiple attack penalty against your hunted prey is reduced by 1. At 11th level, it is reduced by 2.

Warden Hunter

You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to DB and saving throws against your hunted prey’s attacks and abilities.

Stalker Hunter

You gain a +1-circumstance bonus to Stealth, Perception, and Survival checks against your hunted prey. This increases to +2 at 10th level.

The Ranger may only have one Hunter’s Method active at a time.

SWIFT PURSUIT

At 6th level when your hunted prey moves away from you, you may Step 5 feet as a reaction.

At 13th level, you may instead Stride up to half your Speed as a reaction, but this movement must move you closer to your hunted prey.

TERRAIN MASTERY

At 9th level, when in one of your favoured terrains, you ignore natural difficult terrain and treat natural formidable terrain as difficult terrain. In addition, allies within 30 feet who can see or hear you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to Survival, Stealth, and Perception checks made in that terrain. At 15th level, this bonus increases to +2.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are a verdant instinctive spell caster and draw your spells from the verdant tradition.

At 1st level you may select any two PP 2 utility verdant spells and add them to your spell repertoire. At 3rd level and then every two levels thereafter (5th, 7th etc) you may select a new verdant utility spell and add it your repertoire.

You may cast these spells as long as you meet the casting requirements and do not need to memorise your spells.

At 5th level and then every two levels thereafter, you may swap any one spell from your repertoire for a new spell.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your constitution is your magical ability score. You add your Con to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

ROGUE

CLASS TYPE

Expert

DESCRIPTION

You are adept at disguise, stealth, and subterfuge. You can go unnoticed in a crowd or be silent and unseen like deadly shadows in a dark cave, as well as in the back alleys of a city. Your combat skills aren’t as good as the Fighter’s, but you’re still capable of defending yourself in a fight, even if you’re way more deadly when approaching the enemy by ambush.

Play a Rogue if you want to be sneaky, subtle, swift, and always a step ahead (or behind!) of any other character.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Dexterity (min +2), Wisdom, Charisma

PROFICIENCIES

You are proficient in the use of light armour and bucklers. You may use all simple weapons, all small weapons and shortbows.

CLASS SKILLS

Acrobatics, Artistry, Athletics, Climbing, Culture, Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidate, Linguistics, Perception, Sense Motive, Stealth, Thievery

SKILL POINTS

10 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

8 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Rogue as you advance in levels.

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain the any one bonus class feat. At 2nd level you gain the Evasion class feat.

At 3rd level and then every 2 levels thereafter you may select an additional class feat. These class feats must be ones for which you meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class trait (Rogue or Expert).

ARCHETYPAL PATH

Each rogue has their own way of doing things and you are no different. At 1st level you may select any one of the following Archetype feats which becomes your Archetypal Path:

Arcanist, Assassin, Gleeman, Gymnast, Mastermind or Warden

Unlike other archetype feats, you do not need to meet the progression requirements to select another archetype and thus may have two such feats running at the same time.

ROGUISH SKILL

Beginning at first level you may select one of the following skills which gains a +1-class bonus:

Acrobatics, Athletics, Climbing, Deception, Intimidate, Stealth, Thievery

At 5th level and then every 5 levels thereafter, you may select an additional skill to gain this bonus. You may not select the same skill more than once.

KILLER’S EDGE

You know how to turn precision, speed, and timing into lethal advantage. When you inflict a critical hit with an attack that has either the agile or finesse traits, you may increase or decrease the critical result by an amount equal to your class bonus.

This modifier stacks with any adjustment gained from Ambush, Sniping, or similar abilities.

SCOUNDRELS LUCK

You often push your luck to the extreme and may increase your conviction pool and conviction points by 1. Furthermore, you do not expend the conviction used when gaining advantage on a skill modified by Roguish Skill if the result of the check is a failure.

SNEAK ATTACK

Your ability to catch your targets unaware is unsurpassed. If you Strike a creature that is flanked or that has the flat-footed condition with an agile or finesse melee attack, or a ranged weapon attack, you deal an extra 1d6 precision damage. For a ranged attack with a thrown melee weapon, that weapon must also be agile or finesse. As your stealth skill increases, so does the amount of additional damage you inflict. When your stealth skill reaches rank 3 and then for every 3 additional ranks thereafter the amount of damage that you inflict increases by 1d6.

TRAP FINDER

You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Perception checks to find traps, to DB against attacks made by traps, and to saves against traps. Even if you aren’t Searching, you get a check to find traps that normally require you to be Searching. You still need to meet any other requirements to find the trap.

If you have 10 or more ranks in the perception skill, your bonus increases to +4.

PATTERN DISRUPTION

At 2nd level you can trace the subtle patterns of a magical device. When disarming magical traps, devices and locks, you treat the difficulty as Medium (+0 DC) instead of Very Hard.

OPPORTUNISTS STRIKE

At 3RD level You are at your most dangerous when an enemy is distracted, exposed, or unable to defend properly. Once per round, when you make a Strike with an agile or finesseable weapon against a target that qualifies for your Sneak Attack, you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

At 11th level, this bonus increases to +2.

Be aware that this bonus does not apply if the attack is made with disadvantage.

MAGICAL TRADITION

You have no spell casting abilities but must select a magical tradition at 1st level.

WIZARD

CLASS TYPE

Adept

DESCRIPTION

You are adept at the arcane skills, always immersed in your studies of dusty tomes and mouldy scrolls, seeking enlightenment and trying to uncover the deepest secrets and mysteries of magic.

You can cast subtle enchantments, wondrous magics capable of altering the very fabric of reality, and conjure the immense power of the Elements to deliver devastating attacks against their enemies. You are often very jealous of your secret arts.

You may want to play a Wizard if you want to awe your enemies and allies alike with the sheer power or subtle charm of your magic.

KEY ABILITY SCORES

Intelligence (min +2), Wisdom, Dexterity

PROFICIENCIES

You are not proficient in any armour. You are proficient with the dagger and quarterstaff.

CLASS SKILLS

Arcana, Artistry, Culture, Linguistics, Meditation, Mental Focus, Nature, Occultism, Planes, Power Manipulation, Religion

SKILL POINTS

4 + Int per level

HIT POINTS

4 + Con per level

CLASS ABILITIES

You gain the following abilities as a Wizard as you advance in levels.

ARCANE BOND

You place some of your magical power in a bonded item. During your daily preparation each day, you can designate a single item you own as your bonded item. This is typically an item associated with spellcasting, such as a wand, ring, or staff, but you are free to designate a weapon or other item. The item becomes a +1-spell adder which functions only for you. At 6th level and then every 6 levels thereafter, the bonus of the spell adder increases by +1.

WIZARD SCHOOL

At 1st level you must select a school of magic (see below). Your chosen school of magic grants you several benefits.

• All spells of your chosen school are more difficult to resist and increase their Save DC by 2.

• All spells of your chosen school are easier to cast and reduce their Casting DC by 2.

• Your school grants you a bonus Wizard specialist spell.

• Your school grants you an additional class skill.

• Your school grants you a unique ability.

BONUS FEATS

At 1st level you gain the Scribe Scroll and Heighten Spell feats as bonus feats. At 5th level and then every 5 levels thereafter, you may select an additional class feat. This class feat must be one for which you meet the prerequisites or match the appropriate class trait (Wizard or Adept).

MAGICAL TRADITION

You are an arcane learned spell caster and draw your spells from the arcane tradition.

At 1st level you may select any six PP 2 arcane spells and add them to your spell book.

To cast your spells, you must spend time studying your spell book. This process usually takes about half an hour. At the end of this time, you may select an amount of spells from your spell book to commit to memory for the day equal to 2 + (level x 2). Spells committed to memory may be cast using your Power Points (Chapter 9: Magic).

Each time you gain a level you automatically add two new arcane spells to your spell book. Arcane spells gained in this way cannot have a PP cost which is higher than the maximum that you can cast. You may add additional spells to your spell book by following the rules for learning spells which are detailed in Chapters 4 and 8.

CANTRIPS

Each day when you prepare your spells you may also memorise any four arcane cantrips. Cantrips do not need to be written into a spell book, and you have access to all arcane cantrips.

MAGICAL ABILITY SCORE

Your intelligence is your magical ability score. You add your Int to your Spellcraft bonus and as a static bonus to your PP.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

Your Wizard school grants you a unique Specialist Spell at 1st level and another at 7th level.

In addition to these spells, you may also select the following Specialist Spells by taking the Specialist Spell Class feat:

Alluring Caress (1), Detect Signature (1), Element Ward (7), Sacrificing Shield (1), Sickly Ray (1), Spell Storing (1), Umbral Veil (1), Veiled Secret (7), Wizard Strike (1)

THE WIZARD SCHOOLS

You gain the following abilities as a Wizard as you advance in levels.

ALTERATION

Sometimes called a Transmuter, you have the ability to transform and alter the physical world. You excel at changing the properties of objects, transmuting materials, and enhancing the abilities of yourself or others. Your spells can turn enemies into harmless creatures, transform objects into different forms, or grant temporary enhancements to your allies.

Skill Crafting

Specialist Spell Physical Boost (1), Shifting Form (7)

Enhancement: You gain a +1-status bonus to either your Strength, Constitution or Dexterity. You may change which ability score this effects during your daily preparation.

ENCHANTMENT

As an enchanter, you possess the power to influence the minds of others, compelling or charming them to your will. You excel at manipulating emotions, implanting suggestions, and controlling the actions of others. Your spells can charm, beguile, and manipulate both friend and foe.

Skill Diplomacy

Specialist Spell Enchanting Utterance (1), Haunting Miasma (7)

Enchanting Smile: You gain a +1-class bonus on Deception, Diplomacy and Intimidate skill checks. This bonus increases to +2 at 10th level and +3 at 20th level.

INSIGHT

Often called a diviner, you have the ability to peer into the future, perceive hidden truths, and unravel mysteries. You excel at gathering information, detecting secrets, and predicting outcomes. Your spells allow you to scry, see through illusions, and gain insights that can greatly benefit your party.

Skill Perception

Specialist Spell Seer’s Vision (1), Vigilant Eye (7)

Forewarned: You receive a bonus on initiative checks equal to your wizard level +10

INVOCATION

Sometimes called an evoker, you are a master of raw magical energy, capable of unleashing devastating spells that deal immense damage. You excel at offensive magic, creating explosions, summoning elemental forces, and wielding destructive spells. Your power lies in your ability to harness and shape the very essence of magic.

Skill Intimidate

Specialist Spell Force Bolt (1), Elemental Fury (7)

Intense Spells: Any invocation spell that you cast which inflicts damage increases its total damage by half its PP cost.

SHADOW

Sometimes called an illusionist, you are skilled in creating illusions that deceive the senses and confuse enemies. You excel at creating illusions that mimic reality, hide objects or people, or create distractions. Your spells can create phantasmal creatures, alter perceptions, and manipulate the minds of others.

Skill Deception

Specialist Spell Warped Terrain (1), Cloak of Invisibility (7)

Powerful Illusion: Any Shadow spell that you cast may have a 1 PP warping option applied to it for free.

SOUL

Known as a necromancer, you have a mastery of life and death magic and can manipulate the forces of the undead. You can raise and control undead minions, drain life force from your enemies, and even harness the power of death to heal or sustain yourself. Your spells often deal with life force manipulation and the boundary between life and death.

Skill Medicine

Specialist Spell Charm Undead (1), Life Siphon (7)

Necroscope: You may converse with the spirits of those who have died in the local area. You must make a Meditation skill check as if you were gathering information (as the Diplomacy skill).

TRANSLOCATION

Sometimes called a summoner or conjurer, you are the master of summoning and creating objects or creatures from other planes of existence. You can summon allies to aid in battle, create magical barriers, or conjure useful items. You have a knack for manipulating the fabric of reality and bending it to your will.

Skill Survival

Specialist Spell Augment Conjuration (1), Dimension Shift (7)

Summoner's Charm: Whenever you cast a translocation spell to summon a creature which has the conjured trait, the spells duration is doubled.

Be aware that you cannot double the duration again using the Extend Spell feat.

WARDING

Often called an abjurer, you focus on defensive magic and the protection of yourself and your allies. You excel at creating barriers, dispelling harmful effects, and warding against magical threats. You are skilled at countering and nullifying enemy spells and are often the first line of defence for their party.

Skill Sense Motive

Specialist Spell Protective Ward (1), Protector’s Sphere (7)

Resistance: You gain resistance to an energy type of your choice, chosen when you prepare spells. This resistance can be changed each day. At 20th level, this resistance changes to immunity to the chosen energy type.

CHAPTER 4 - SKILLS & ACTIONS

As Fumblebar the gnomish wizard hurtles through the air, his panicked attempt to grab hold of the rock face prove futile. His fingers scrape against the rough surface, but his limited training in climbing leave him woefully unprepared. Desperation grips his heart as the ground rushes up to meet him. He attempts to cast his Feather Fall spell, only to realise that he had forgotten to memorise it that morning. With a horrified expression frozen on his face, Fumblebar plummets down, unable to halt his downward trajectory. The realization of his impending doom hits him like a thunderbolt, and a wave of regret wash over him. He wishes that he had prepared the proper spells or considered the consequences before leaping off the cliff.

The wind howls past his ears, drowning out any other sound. The orcish war cries fade away into a distant echo, leaving only the sound of Fumblebar's racing heartbeat. Time seems to slow as he hurtles toward the ground, the world around him reduced to a blur of colours and shapes. In an instant, the impact arrives—an abrupt, bone-jarring collision. Fumblebar's body crumples upon contact with the unforgiving ground, bones shattering under the force. Agonizing pain shoots through his body, but it is short-lived as the darkness of oblivion envelops him.

Fumblebar's story ends tragically, a cautionary tale of the dangers that await the unprepared and reckless. His name is delivered in verse by many a bard, as tale of caution.

In the village of Tattermill Hollow, under twisted roots and emerald moss,

Lived Thimbletwig Tiddlegem, a gnome quite fond of gloss.

He read his scrolls, he brewed his teas, he wore a crooked hat,

And whispered runes to fireflies — imagine that!

Now Thimbletwig had once been young and brash and bold,

A friend of Fumblebar, whose tale is grimly told.

He'd heard the cliffside story, the fall that stole the light,

Of how poor Fumblebar forgot his wings mid-flight.

He'd wept a quiet tear the day the tale was sung,

And from that moment on, kept spells beneath his tongue.

He etched the words “PREPARE, THEN LEAP” on every wand and staff,

And even taught his squirrel to mock him with a laugh.

He trained with monks upon the peaks where clouds and silence dwell,

And practiced every feather spell until he knew it well.

When goblins raided Rindle Fen and shadows swept the land,

It was Thimbletwig who rose to lead, a scroll in each hand.

Upon a jagged bridge of bone, a chasm vast below,

He faced a cursed warlock and his breathless, wailing crows.

With shaking knees but sharpened wit, Thimbletwig stood his ground,

And when the bridge gave way — he simply floated down.

He drifted like a leaf on air, as runes flared from his pack,

And shouted to the skies above, “I won’t be caught off-track!”

The warlock, stunned, misjudged his step and vanished with a scream —

While Thimbletwig just landed safe and vanished in the steam.

He left behind a legend etched in stone and song,

Of how a gnome, through wisdom, proved that thinking isn’t wrong.

“Fumblebar leapt first,” he said, “and met a tragic end.

I leap prepared — that’s why I live, and still defend.”

SKILLS & ACTIONS

When playing a roleplaying game carrying out actions is a common occurrence. Your soldier has been running from the two alien entities for a considerable amount of time; how long can he keep this up? You approach a large gap in the floor of the corridor and need to leap across it; how far can you jump? Whether you are a grisly mercenary from the dark reaches of the north who has seen countless conflicts, a frivolous entertainer who can blend into any social situation, or a mad wizard seeking unlimited power, skills represent the backbone of what your character can do. In this chapter, you’ll learn about skills, their scope, and the actions they can be used for.

To determine what your character can and can’t do during play, skills are used to track every aspect of your characters capabilities.

Skills are learned abilities acquired through a combination of training (skill ranks, class bonus) and natural talent (ability score modifiers). These factors combine to form the parts of a skill check, which is a d20 roll, plus the skill’s bonus and any applicable modifiers.

SKILL BONUS

Your characters’ proficiency with a particular skill is measured by your skill bonus, which is added to any check made when you perform a task involving that skill.

If your character has a high skill bonus, they are more likely to succeed, even when attempting difficult tasks, while those with a low bonus will fail more frequently.

SKILL MODIFIER

Each skill will have a skill modifier which is worked out in the following manner:

Skill modifier = modifier of the skill’s key ability score + rank bonus + class bonus + other bonuses - penalties

When recording your skill modifier, you should only make a note of permanent modifiers which effect all aspects of the skill check. Certain bonuses are situational and only apply under certain circumstances. These should only be applied when the situation arises.

ABILITY SCORE

Each skill has an ability score, applied to the skill’s checks. Each skill’s ability score is noted in its description.

RANK BONUS

Ranks represent your training in a particular skill. As you gain experience during your adventures, you’ll develop new ranks in your skills, improving your chances of success.

Your maximum skill ranks in any one skill cannot be higher than your career level.

CIRCUMSTANCE BONUS

Circumstance bonuses typically involve the situation you find yourself in when attempting a check. You may only apply one circumstance bonus to any one check.

CLASS BONUS

You gain class bonuses from character class, feats and other sources. Class bonuses stack if gained from different sources.

ITEM BONUS

An item bonus represents a bonus which may be applied to armour, weapons or other items of equipment. Multiple item bonuses to the same value do not stack.

RACE BONUS

A racial bonus comes from the culture or race that the character hails from. Racial bonuses stack if gained from different sources.

STATUS BONUS

Status bonuses typically come from spells, other magical effects, or something applying a helpful, often temporary, condition to you. Once again you may only apply one status bonus to any one check.

OTHER BONUSES/PENALTIES

Any other bonuses or penalties that are applied to a skill are cumulative unless otherwise stated. The appendix at the end of this book has a full list of bonus types.

Any of the above bonuses may also be applied to your character as penalties in certain circumstances.

Be aware that if you gain multiple bonuses of the same type, only the highest bonus applies—you don’t add them together.

SKILL PROGRESSION

As your character advances in level, you gain additional ranks to assign to skills. You can assign these ranks to existing skills your character knows, improving them up to a maximum rank no higher than your career level, or you can assign earned skill ranks to entirely new skills, making your character trained with a rank in that skill.

SKILL RANK BONUS

Each skill rank that you have in a skill adds a +1 bonus to the skill’s total bonus

Be aware that you may never have more ranks in a skill than you have character levels.

USING SKILLS

You can perform various actions when using skills. The actions of some skills can be used untrained (0 ranks) where others need your character to be at least trained (1 rank or more) in the skill to use them. As your ranks in a skill increase it may enhance what you can do with it or open up new options.

Sometimes you will require a certain number of skill ranks in a skill to carry out certain actions.

SKILL CHECKS

When you need to determine if you can perform a specific action your GM will ask you for a skill check.

Find the skill that the GM has asked you to make and then roll a d20 adding your character’s relevant Skill Bonus, plus any possible modifier. The final result is then compared to the Difficulty Check (DC) of the action with the outcome as shown on the Action Resolution Table.

ACTIONS RESOLUTION TABLE

Check Result vs DC

Outcome

Exceeds by 20+

Heroic

Exceeds by 10+

Critical

Equals or Exceeds

Success

Fails by less than 5

Partial

Fails by 5+

Failure

Fails by 10+

Fumble

Fails by 20+

Blunder

Heroic: The check succeeds in the best way possible; this result is treated as a Critical with extra benefit.

Critical: The check works better than expected, you will usually receive some boon or bonus.

Success: The check works and you accomplish your task.

Partial: You complete about half of what you were attempting. In some circumstances this will allow you a follow up check, other checks will fail (such as jumping across a ravine!).

Failure: The check does not work, depending upon the situation you may be able to try again.

Fumble: Things go wrong in the worst possible way. You leave yourself in danger, break equipment or possibly grant an opponent a bonus against you.

Blunder: As fumble above, except that some nastiness will befall you.

Chaos: The check will normally be treated as a success, with some chaotic side effect occurring (often the result of a fumble if possible).

DIFFICULTY

Not all skill rolls are made under ideal conditions. Standing at the edge of a valley looking into the distance for an approaching army may be a straightforward manoeuvre on a sunny day. Add some fog and rain into the equation and the same manoeuvre becomes a little more difficult.

When a Skill Check is called for, the GM sets the DC. Most tasks and skills will have a DC assigned to them; others will be level based.

LEVEL MODIFIER

This modifier is applied to a check based upon the level of the task. This DC is used when the task that you are carrying out has a specific level. The DC is equal to the level of the task +14 unless noted otherwise.

DIFFICULTY MODIFIER

A difficulty modifier is determined by the GM and based upon how intricate the check is. Difficulty modifiers range from +10 to -10.

EXAMPLE DIFFICULTY

Difficulty

OPPOSED CHECKS

When someone or something tests your skill (or you test theirs), they attempt a check against your DC.

When an ability calls for you to use the DC for a specific skill, you can calculate it by adding 10 + your total modifier for that skill.

TAKING TIME

When there’s no hurry or stress upon you to accomplish a task, then you can declare that you are Taking Time to perform the action more carefully. Judging if a situation is suited for Taking Time must be decided by the GM.

Taking Time grants you a special +4 circumstance bonus to your Skill Check but employs at least twice the amount of time normally associated with the action.

AID

Sometimes you may need to assist other characters to accomplish a difficult task, or you may wish to accomplish a goal as a group. In such a situation, one character must be appointed as the lead character. All other characters make an Easy Skill check using the Bonus Check Table.

The resulting bonus is added as a circumstance bonus to the lead characters check.

Be aware, the GM has the final say if Aid can be used in each circumstance and how many characters may apply Aid.

Aid can also be used as a combat action using the Aid Defensive and Aid Offensive skill actions as detailed under Combat Actions.

TOOLS

Sometimes tools are needed to carry out a certain task as part of a skill check. If you do not have the required tools to carry out a task, the GM may apply penalties of up to -10 to the check or may not allow the check at all.

ARMOUR & SKILLS

Some armour imposes a penalty on specific skill checks. Dexterity based skills are often affected by such penalties. Additionally, armour can also interfere with the use of magic. These subjects will be discussed in later chapters.

BLIND CHECKS

It is sometimes appropriate that a skill check be made without the players knowledge. This is important when it is key for you to not know whether you have succeeded or failed. In such a scenario, the GM rolls the check for you and describes the outcome without revealing the result.

ADVANTAGE

Sometimes a feat, ability or situation will require a skill check to be rolled with either advantage or disadvantage. When a d20 check is rolled with advantage, you may roll the die twice and select the most desirable result. When a d20 check is made with disadvantage, then the roll is made twice selecting the least desirable result.

FLAT CHECKS

When there’s a chance something will happen or fail to happen based on pure chance, you attempt a flat check. A flat check never includes any modifiers, bonuses, or penalties, you just roll the d20 and compare the result on the die to the DC. Specific effects might adjust your DC for certain types of flat checks, but abilities that don’t specifically call out flat checks can’t change their DCs.

If more than one flat check would ever cause or prevent the same thing, just roll once using the highest DC.

AUTO CHECKS

Sometimes, requiring a skill check for every action used outside of an encounter can slow the game down and even cause unnecessary fumbling and chaos.

Choose a skill that you are trained in. You can forgo rolling a skill check for that skill to instead receive a result of 10 + your rank bonus (do not apply any other bonuses, penalties, or modifiers).

You may only auto-check when your character is deemed to not be in a stressful situation (such as an encounter).

SKILLS WHICH HEAL

You can use several skills to heal hit points and conditions. When using such a skill to heal a condition, you may only do so if the effect which caused the condition is no longer active.

Khang uses the Healing Trance action to heal some of his hit point damage and hopefully lower his Injured condition. He gets a critical on the check and triples his normal HP healing rate for the hour (normally 15 of his 150 hit points), so he heals 45 hit points. Unfortunately, his Injured condition has been caused by him losing 3 fingers on his left hand, so until the fingers have been sewn back on or replaced, he cannot heal the Injured condition.

BONUS CHECKS

Certain skills and checks will require that you make a bonus check. This check is made when you need to make a check to determine a modifier that can then be applied to another statistic or check (such as Aid).

To make a Bonus Check, work out all the modifiers of the check and its DC as normal and refer the result to the Bonus Check Table.

BONUS CHECK

Check Result

Circumstance Bonus

Blunder

-2

Fumble

-1

Failure

0

Partial

+1

Success

+2

Critical

+3

Heroic

+4

Nyphari assists Morden with his Gather Herbs (Survival) check by making an Aid check (see below). Nyphari has +8 in the Survival skill and the DC is 15. Nyphari rolls a 12 for a total result of 20 on her check. As this exceeds the DC by 5 (success), Nyphari grants Morden a +2-circumstance bonus to his check.

BASIC ACTIONS

Basic actions play a vital role in allowing every character, regardless of their specific skills or abilities, to perform common tasks and actions. These actions are universally available to all creatures, except in extraordinary situations where limitations may apply.

Basic actions encompass a wide range of activities that are not explicitly tied to specific skills or abilities. These actions are often simple and straightforward, representing tasks that characters can perform without requiring specialized training or unique capabilities.

AID DEFENSIVE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

You make a melee Strike against the target but are looking to assist your ally rather than inflict any damage. You weave and distract throwing the target off balance. Make an attack roll against the targets DB and compare the result to the Bonus Check table with the following results:

+ Result You grant the indicated bonus to your ally as a bonus to their Defence against the next attack from the target.

- Result Your attempt is ineffective, and you grant no bonus to your ally.

Fumble Roll on the appropriate attack fumble table.

Any bonuses granted expire at the beginning of your next turn if they are not used.

AID OFFENSIVE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

You make a melee Strike against the target but are looking to assist your ally rather than inflict any damage. You weave and distract throwing the target off balance. Make an attack roll against the targets DB and compare the result to the Bonus Check table with the following results:

+ Result You grant the indicated bonus to your allies next attack against the target.

- Result Your attempt is ineffective, and you grant no bonus to your ally.

Fumble Roll on the appropriate attack fumble table.

Any bonuses granted expire at the beginning of your next turn if they are not used.

AIM

CONCENTRATE

Action 3 AP

Requirements You are wielding a missile weapon and can see a target.

You remain very still and align your weapon with your target. You may spend up to 4 rounds aiming at your target and each round grants you a +1-circumstance bonus to your AB. Whilst aiming, you are flat-footed and if you take any other action besides this one, you lose all accrued aiming bonus.

ATTACK OF OPPORTUNITY

ATTACK

Trigger A target within reach uses an action with either the manipulate trait, movement trait or makes a ranged attack.

Action Reaction

You swiftly retaliate against the triggering creature with a melee strike. If your attack is a critical hit and the trigger was a manipulate action, you successfully disrupt their action, causing it to fail. This strike does not contribute to your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty does not affect this strike.

AVERT GAZE

Action 1 AP

You actively look away from a potential threat. You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to your saving throws against visual abilities that specifically necessitate looking at a creature or object. This bonus remains until the beginning of your next turn (unless of course you use another action to look again).

Be aware that the GM may apply a situational penalty to any actions made against a creature that you are actively looking away from.

CHARGE

ATTACK FLOURISH MOVEMENT OPEN

Action 3 AP

You take two Stride actions (minimum of 10 feet moved) and move directly towards your target. If your target is within reach at the end of your movement, you may make a melee Strike action against them with a +4-circumstance bonus to the attack roll.

You can use Charge while Burrowing, Climbing, Flying, or Swimming instead of Striding if you have the corresponding movement type.

You may use this action whilst mounted.

COUP DE GRACE

ATTACK SAVE

Action 3 AP

You can deliver a special attack called a coup de grace to an adjacent helpless opponent. You automatically hit scoring the maximum result for your attack (treat as 20 rolled). If the target survives the attack, they must make an Opposed Level based Fortitude Saving Throw or die.

However, if the target is immune to critical hits, the coup de grace does not deal critical damage or effects, nor does it force the target to succeed at a saving throw or die.

CRAWL

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are prone and your Speed is at least 10 feet.

You move 5’ whilst prone.

DELAY

Trigger Your turn begins, Action Free

By choosing to Delay, you temporarily remove yourself from the current initiative order, allowing you to wait for the opportune moment to act. Upon deciding to Delay, the rest of your turn is put on hold. You do not take any further actions until you decide to return to the initiative order, which you can do as a free action triggered by the end of any other creature's turn. When you return to the initiative order, your initiative permanently changes to the new position. While Delayed, you are unable to use reactions until you return to the initiative order, limiting your ability to react to immediate events.

It's important to carefully consider the timing of your return to ensure it aligns with your intended strategy.

It's worth noting that if you choose to Delay for an entire round without returning to the initiative order, the actions you had Delayed are lost. Additionally, your initiative remains unchanged, and your next turn occurs at your original position in the initiative order.

When you opt to Delay, any recurring damage or negative effects that typically occur at the start or end of your turn take immediate effect. This ensures that you don't avoid or delay the consequences of ongoing detrimental effects. Furthermore, any beneficial effects that would naturally end during your turn also expire when you Delay, as you are effectively skipping that turn.

DISARM

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have at least one hand free.

You try to remove a weapon or other object from the targets grasp. Attempt an Attack check against the target’s Attack DC. You take a -2-circumstance penalty to the check when attempting to disarm an opponent who is a size category larger than you. For each additional size category beyond that you take an additional cumulative -2 penalty.

Critical You disarm the target. The item this action was made against falls to the ground at the target’s feet (or another appropriate appendage).

Success The item nearly falls from the targets grasp, but not quite. Until the beginning of the creature's turn, the target takes a -2 circumstance when using the item. This penalty applies to their Attack DC for any subsequent disarm attempts.

Fumble You throw yourself off balance and become flat-footed until the beginning of your next turn.

DOUBLE SLICE

ATTACK FLOURISH

Action 3 AP

Requirements You are wielding a melee weapon in both hands.

You strike your target with both weapons in quick succession. Using your current multiple attack penalty, make two Strikes, one with each of your melee weapons. Both Strikes must be made against the same target. If the second Strike is made with a weapon that doesn’t have the agile trait, it takes a –2 circumstance penalty.

If both attacks hit, combine their damage, choosing the most beneficial against your current target. You can only inflict one critical and if either attack fumbles, then the other attack automatically misses.

This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

DROP PRONE

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are in contact with the ground.

You willingly drop to the ground gaining the prone condition.

ESCAPE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

To initiate your escape, you must select the specific source of the condition or impediment that you wish to break free from. It could be a creature's grasp, magical bindings, a physical obstacle, or any other relevant obstacle that is imposing the grabbed or immobilised conditions upon you.

Once you've chosen the target of your escape attempt, attempt an Acrobatics, Athletics or Unarmed Attack check against the effects DC with the following results:

Critical You break free removing the grabbed and immobilised conditions. You may immediately take any action with the move trait but may move no more than 5 feet.

Success You break free and remove the grabbed and immobilized conditions imposed by your chosen target.

Fumble You fail to escape your target and cannot attempt to Escape again until the beginning of your next turn.

FIGHT DEFENSIVELY

ATTACK DEFENCE OPEN

Action 2 AP

You take a single attack action whilst ducking, dodging or parrying incoming melee and missile attacks throughout the round. When you use this action, you gain a +2-dodge bonus to your DB and a -4-circumstance penalty to all attack actions (including this one) until the beginning of your next turn.

FLOWING MOVEMENT

Action Free

You attempt to change from one movement type to another without ending the initial action and expending an additional AP. Make a check appropriate to one of the movement types involved.

Success You move from one movement type to another without ending the action. All movement costs are combined to determine when the action ends.

Failure Your initial movement action ends as normal.

FULL DEFENCE

DEFENCE OPEN

Action 3 AP

Instead of attacking, you can duck and weave to avoid attacks until the beginning of your next turn. When you use this action, you gain a +4-dodge bonus to your DB until the beginning of your next turn. You may take a single Movement action as part of Full Defence. You can still use Free Actions whilst using Full Defence, but all other actions, including Reactions are prohibited.

GRAPPLE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have at least one free hand or have your target grappled or immobilised.

You attempt to grab a creature or object with your free hand. Make an unarmed check against the target's Fortitude DC.

You take a -4-circumstance penalty to the check when attempting to grapple an opponent who is 2 size categories larger than you. For each additional size category beyond that you take an additional cumulative -4 penalty. You can Grapple a target you already have grabbed or restrained without having a hand free.

If you have a target Grabbed, you may use an action at the beginning of your turn to maintain the Grab.

Critical Your target is Grabbed and takes a –4 circumstance penalty to checks made to Escape your Grapple until the end of your next turn.

Success Your target is Grabbed until the end of your next turn unless you move or your target Escapes.

Failure You fail to grab your target. If you already had the target grabbed or immobilised using a Grapple, those conditions on that creature or object end.

Fumble If you already had the target Grabbed or immobilised, it breaks free. Your target can either grab you, as if it succeeded at using the Grapple action against you or force you to fall and land prone.

INTERACT

MANIPULATE

Action 1 AP

You can grab an unattended or stored object, open a door or manipulate the terrain around you in a minor way.

Your GM may require you to make a successful skill check to determine if your attempt was successful.

PREPARE

CONCENTRATE FLOURISH

Action 1 AP

Requirements You can use reactions

You prepare to use a reaction that will occur outside your turn. Choose a single Reaction that you are able to use. You may use this reaction once as a free action until the beginning of your next turn.

READY

CONCENTRATE

Action 2 AP

You prepare an action of no more than 2 AP that will occur outside of your turn and a trigger which will prompt that action. Your turn then ends.

If the trigger does not occur before the beginning of your next turn, then the action is wasted. If, however, the trigger does occur before the start of your next turn, you may use the chosen action as a reaction.

Your action is subject to any applicable bonuses and penalties that are currently affecting you (such as multiple attack penalties).

You may use any additional AP for the turn before you ready an action on your normal initiative count, or after the action triggers.

RELEASE

MANIPULATE

Action Free

You drop an item that you are holding, release your hold on something or change grip from one-handed to handed or vice versa. Despite being a manipulate action, this action does not trigger reactions (such as Attack of Opportunity).

REPOSITION

MOVEMENT

Action 2 AP

Requirements Your speed is at least 10 feet, and you have at least one free hand.

You move up to half your speed (minimum of 5 feet) and at the end of your movement you may exchange positions with one adjacent, willing target. Any reactions provoked by this action effect you and not the willing target.

SHIELD BASH

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

You attack with a shield using is it as an impromptu weapon. This attack inflicts base damage based upon your shield type with the attacks fumble DC in parentheses.

Light 1d4 (6); Heavy 1d6 (8); Tower 1d8 (10)

If you use a shield bash action you lose any shield bonus gained to DB until the beginning of your next turn.

SHOVE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have at least one hand free or have a shield in your off hand.

You push a creature away from you. Attempt an unarmed attack check against your target's Fortitude DC. You take a -4-circumstance penalty to the check when attempting to shove an opponent who is 2 size categories larger than you. For each additional size category beyond that you take an additional cumulative -4 penalty.

Critical Your target is pushed up to 10 feet away from you. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction.

Success Your target is pushed back 5 feet. You can Stride after it, but you must move the same distance and in the same direction.

Fumble You lose your balance, fall, and land prone.

STAND

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

You stand up from prone.

STEP

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements Your speed is at least 10 feet.

You move 5 feet. This action doesn't trigger reactions (such as Attacks of Opportunity), that can be triggered by move actions.

You can't Step into difficult terrain, and you can't Step using a Speed other than your land Speed.

STRIDE

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

You move up to your Speed using any of movement types.

Stride is charged cumulatively, not per movement. Your Speed is the distance one Stride buys you, and you are only charged again when you exceed it — so at Speed 30, moving 10 feet, then another 10, then another 10 costs 1 AP in total, not 3. The thirty-first foot begins a second Stride and costs your second AP. Distance is counted after any terrain cost, so 10 feet through difficult terrain spends 20 feet of your first Stride. You cannot begin a movement you cannot pay for: if the distance would take you past a Stride boundary and you lack the AP for the next one, the movement is refused rather than allowed and charged later.

STRIKE

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

You attack with a weapon you're wielding or with an unarmed attack, targeting one creature within your reach (for a melee attack) or within range (for a ranged attack). See attacks above.

TAKE COVER

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are benefiting from cover, are adjacent to a feature that allows you to take cover or are prone.

You press up against a wall or duck behind an obstacle to take better advantage of cover. If you would have standard cover, you instead gain greater cover, which provides a +8-circumstance bonus to DB; and to Stealth checks to Hide, Sneak, or otherwise avoid detection. Otherwise, you gain the benefits of standard cover (a +4-circumstance bonus instead). This lasts until you move from your current space, use an attack action, become unconscious, or end this effect as a free action.

TRIP

ATTACK

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have at least one hand free.

You try to knock a creature to the ground. Attempt an unarmed attack against the target’s Acrobatics DC or Fortitude DC (whichever is higher). You take a -4-circumstance penalty to the check when attempting to trip an opponent who is 2 size categories larger than you. For each additional size category beyond that you take an additional cumulative -4 penalty.

Critical The target falls and lands prone taking the result of the attack as a Tiny Unarmed attack.

Success The target falls and lands prone.

Fumble You lose your balance and fall and land prone.

SPECIAL ACTIONS

These actions usually require you to have some kind of special ability or movement type.

BURROW

MOVEMENT

Requirements You have a burrow speed.

You dig your way through dirt, sand, or a similar loose material at a rate up to your burrow Speed. You can’t burrow through rock or other substances denser than dirt unless you have an ability that allows you to do so.

FLY

MOVEMENT

Requirements You have a fly speed.

You move through the air up to your fly Speed. Moving upward (straight up or diagonally) uses the rules for moving through difficult terrain. You can move straight down 10 feet for every 5 feet of movement you spend. If you Fly to the ground, you don’t take falling damage. You can use an action to Fly 0 feet to hover in place. If you’re airborne at the end of your turn and didn’t use a Fly action this round, you fall.

Some actions can be used with several different skills. When you make a general skill action check, your GM will advise you as to which skill to make the check on. This is very much situation dependent.

CREATE (TRAINED)

You can create objects using a crafting formula and a number of different skills. Some objects require a feat to create them.

CREATE MANIPULATE

You can make an item from raw materials. You need the Alchemical Crafting feat to create Elixirs, Herbs, Oils, Poisons and Vials, the Brew Potion feat to create potions, the Scribe Scroll feat to create magical scrolls and the Magical Crafting feat to create other magic items.

The GM determines the difficulty to Create the item based on its level, rarity, and other circumstances.

To Create an item, you must meet the following requirements:

• You must have a number of ranks in the skill that you are using to create, equal to or greater than the level of the item you are creating.

• You have the formula for the item

• You have an appropriate set of tools and, in many cases, a workshop.

• You have the specialty (mundane) or feat required to create the item.

You must supply raw materials worth at least half the item's Price. You always expend at least that number of raw materials when you Create successfully.

The amount of time it takes to create an item depends upon the result of your create check which must be made at the beginning of your project.

Success You do competent work. You complete an amount of work equal to your skill ranks x item level x success modifier (see below) in gold pieces per day. Once this amount exceeds the value of the item then you have completed it.

Partial You do average work. You complete an amount of work equal to your skill ranks x item level in gold pieces. If this amount is greater than the value of the item then you have completed it. You may make another create check the following day or continue daily with this amount of progress until the item is completed.

Failure For whatever reason, you are struggling to make any progress with the item and waste a day of work. You may make another check the following day.

Fumble Your work is truly shoddy. After 1d6 days of work you realise that the project has failed. You ruin the raw materials you supplied and must begin again.

A day of work is approximately 8 hours. If you spend more than 8 hours working on your item, the GM will require you to make an Exhaustion check (see Chapter 7).

Be aware that a level 0 item is classed as level 1 when determining how much work is completed.

CONSUMABLES

When crafting items with the consumable trait, you create them in batches, allowing you to make multiple items at once using the same amount of raw materials and cost. You must include all items in the batch, but you only need to make a single crafting check to create them.

The DC of the create check is modified based upon the amount of consumables that you wish to create.

AMMUNITION

Ammunition is also a consumable and is also created in batches. When making ammunition, you create the amount indicated in the equipment tables.

You may half this amount to decrease the DC by 2 or double it and increase the DC by 5.

You can invent new formula for items that you don’t know how to create. The process is the same as creating an item except that the DC is 5 higher and the cost of a formula is 10% that of the item you are creating.

EARN INCOME (TRAINED)

You can use a skill to earn money whilst not adventuring (GM discretion). You must be trained in the skill to do so. This takes time to set up, and your income depends on your proficiency rank and how lucrative a task you can find.

EARN INCOME

You use one of your skills to make money whilst not adventuring. The GM will assign a task level, representing the most rewarding job available, but you can also search for lower-level tasks at your discretion. Should you desire higher-paying work, you can invest time and employ your Diplomacy skill to Gather Information, conduct research, or engage in social interactions to uncover more lucrative opportunities.

When undertaking a job, the GM secretly establishes the DC for your skill check, ensuring an element of suspense and uncertainty as you strive to succeed in your assigned task. After your first day of work, you roll to determine your earnings. You gain an amount of income based on the task’s level, your level and this is further modified by your skill check result.

Income (gp) = task level x skill ranks

Critical You do outstanding work. Your skill ranks are considered to be 2 higher for working out your total earnings.

Success You do competent work. Gain earnings as detailed above.

Partial You do average work. Gain 50% earnings.

Failure You do shoddy work and get paid the bare minimum for your time. The amount of income you gain is divided by 10 (round down).

Fumble You earn nothing for your work and are fired immediately. You can’t continue at the task. Your reputation suffers, potentially making it difficult for you to find rewarding jobs in that community in the future.

Once you have begun a task, you can work on it on subsequent days without requiring additional skill checks. For each consecutive day you dedicate to the task, you earn the same amount as the initial day, until the task reaches its conclusion. The duration of the task is determined by the GM, with some tasks spanning a week or two, while others may extend over months or even years.

IDENTIFY POWER (TRAINED)

Using you’re a knowledge or lore skill, you can attempt to identify power in an item, location, or effect.

Tradition

Arcane

Arcana

Ethereal

IDENTIFY POWER CONCENTRATE SECRET

Once you discover that an item, location, or ongoing effect is magical, you can try to identify the particulars of its abilities. You choose the amount of time you wish to spend identifying the magic and apply the following modifiers: 10 minutes (+0), 1 minute (-2), 1 round (-5), 1 AP (-10). If your attempt is interrupted, you must start over. The GM sets the difficulty of your check. Cursed or esoteric subjects usually have higher difficulties or might even be impossible to identify using this activity alone.

Critical You learn all the attributes of the magic, including its name (for an effect), what it does, any means of activating it (for an item or location), and whether it is cursed.

Success For an item or location, you get a sense of what it does and learn any means of activating it. For an ongoing effect (such as a spell with a duration), you learn the effect’s name and what it does. You can’t try again in hopes of getting a critical success.

Failure You fail to identify the magic and can’t try again for 1 day.

Fumble You misidentify the magic as something else of the GM’s choice.

If the aura that you are attempting to identify is common (GM discretion) or something that you are already familiar with, the GM may deem that a check is unnecessary.

Furthermore, if the aura belongs to a visible spell effect or magical item, the GM may allow a 0 AP Recall Knowledge before an Identify check is required.

LEARN A SPELL (TRAINED)

If you’re a spellcaster, you can use the skill corresponding to your magical tradition (see above) to learn a new spell of that tradition. The price and difficulty to learn a spell of a specific level is detailed below.

LEARN A SPELL CONCENTRATE

You can gain access to a new spell of your tradition from someone who knows that spell or from magical writing like a spellbook or scroll.

To learn the spell, you must do the following:

• Spend 1 hour per PP of the spell, during which you must satisfy the learning requirements of your tradition (see Chapter 9).

• Have materials with the Price indicated in the table below (a scroll will cover this cost but not a spellbook).

• Attempt a skill check for the skill corresponding to your tradition. Uncommon or rare spells have higher difficulties.

• Have the minimum casting level required for the casting of the spell.

Once you learn the spell you may add it to your Spell Library and may cast it normally. You must still meet all of the requirements to cast the spell (see Chapter 9 – Magic).
