RECALL KNOWLEDGE (UNTRAINED)

To remember useful information on a topic, you can attempt to Recall Knowledge. You might know basic information about something without needing to attempt a check, but Recall Knowledge requires you to stop and think for a moment so you can recollect more specific facts and apply them. You might even need to spend time investigating first.

• Arcana: Recall Knowledge about ancient mysteries, arcane magic, arcane symbols, beasts, constructs and wyrms.

• Crafting: Recall Knowledge about any of your specialities, constructs, engineering materials and valuables.

• Culture: Recall Knowledge about heraldry, legends, local history, personalities, inhabitants, laws, customs, traditions and humanoids. The GM might allow Culture to apply to other creatures that are major elements of society in your region, such as the draconic nobility in a kingdom of humans ruled by dragons.

• Medicine: Recall Knowledge about diseases, injuries, poisons, and other ailments. You can use this to perform forensic examinations if you spend 10 minutes (or more, as determined by the GM) checking for evidence such as wound patterns. This is most useful when determining how a body was injured or killed.

• Nature: Recall Knowledge about fauna, flora, geography, verdant magic, weather, the environment, creatures of natural origin (like animals, beasts, fey, and plants), the First World, the Material Plane, and the Elemental Planes.

• Occultism: Recall Knowledge about aberrations, caverns, ethereal magic, oozes and spelunking.

• Planes: Recall Knowledge about the Inner Planes, the Outer Planes, the Astral Plane, the Ethereal Plane, eternals and planar magic.

• Religion: Recall Knowledge about divine agents, divine magic, gods and goddesses, mythic history, ecclesiastic tradition, holy symbols and undead.

RECALL KNOWLEDGE CONCENTRATE

Action Varies

You attempt a skill check to try to remember a bit of knowledge regarding a topic related to that skill. The GM determines the difficulty for such checks and which skills apply.

Critical You recall the knowledge accurately and gain additional information or context.

Success You recall the knowledge accurately or gain a useful clue about your current situation.

Fumble You recall incorrect information or gain an erroneous or misleading clue.

The DC will be modified based upon the amount time required/expended on the check (GM discretion).

RESEARCH (TRAINED)

You dedicate time and effort to investigate a subject or question by studying texts, consulting experts, or scouring information sources. Whether poring over ancient tomes by candlelight, cross-referencing dusty scrolls in a hidden archive, or interviewing sages and scholars over hours of intense discussion, Research is the pursuit of deep understanding. It’s more than a fleeting thought or a moment of insight—it’s deliberate, methodical, and often arduous work. Unlike a quick recollection, researching means asking questions no one nearby may know the answer to and refusing to rest until the truth is unearthed.

This action embodies the relentless intellectual curiosity of scholars, investigators, and Loremasters. It’s what separates the well-informed from the truly wise—and in the right hands, a day in the library can shape the outcome of a war or unveil secrets that change the world.

RESEARCH CONCENTRATE

Action Varies

You attempt a skill check using an appropriate Lore, Knowledge, or other applicable skill, determined by the GM based on your research method and topic. Research requires significantly more time than a Recall Knowledge check and can be part of a downtime activity.

Critical You uncover highly valuable or rare information, learn hidden truths, or discover information that significantly changes your understanding of the topic. You may gain an advantage or resource related to the research (GM discretion).

Success You gather solid, accurate information and form a clearer picture of the topic. Your research resolves your inquiry or helps you progress a related task.

Fumble You misinterpret the data, consult biased or incorrect sources, or draw flawed conclusions. Your research leads to a misleading or unproductive result.

The DC and the time required vary by topic complexity, available resources, and access to information. Assistance from libraries, experts, or specialized tools can improve your chances (GM discretion).

SPELL CONCENTRATION (TRAINED)

Sometimes you will be asked to make a check to either continue maintaining a spell or avoid losing magical energies when you take damage.

SPELL CONCENTRATION CONCENTRATE MENTAL

Action Free

Trigger You are interrupted (take damage) whilst casting or sustaining a spell.

You attempt to avoid losing the magical energies which you are currently harnessing. Make a check using the original DC for casting the spell with a Medium (DC +0) difficulty using the following results:

Critical You maintain the spell (if sustained) or cast it normally.

Success You maintain the spell (if sustained) or cast it normally but also gain 1 point of fatigue.

Partial As success, but you gain 2 points of fatigue.

Failure The spell fails, and you lose half the PP (if casting).

Fumble Your spell fails; you lose the PP (if casting) and must roll on the Spell Failure Table.

Blunder As fumble but you must also make a Magical Resonance roll.

The DC is increased as follows if the damage received was also a critical injury:
Minor (Hard +2)
Serious (Very Hard +5)

Deadly (Incredibly Hard +10)

STUDY TARGET (TRAINED)

Sometimes you will need to have detailed information about a target creature, location or object. This is usually linked with a spell or magical ability of some kind.

You may have an amount of ‘Studied Targets’ equal to your Int plus your level at any one time. You also gain a bonus to this amount based upon the combined number of ranks you have in “knowledge” skills which include Arcana, Culture, Nature, Occultism, Planes and Religion. You gain an additional ‘Studied Target’ for every 5 ranks you have in these skills combined.

Theolan is a 10th level Wizard with Int +5 and the following applicable skill ranks: Arcana 6, Culture 6, Planes 6

Theolan therefore has a total of 18 studied targets.

STUDY TARGET CONCENTRATE

Action 1 minute

You attempt a skill check to memorise a person, place, or thing in detail so that you may use those other spells to impersonate, travel to or summon a specific target later.

Success Your target is considered ‘Studied’.

Failure You have failed to study the target but may try again.

Fumble You believe that you have studied the target correctly, but something has gone wrong. When you cast a spell that links to this studied target later, things will not go according to plan (GM Discretion).

You may spend more or less time studying the target which offers the following modifiers.

1 round -2, 10 minutes +2, 1 hour +5

SUBSIST (UNTRAINED)

If you need to provide food and shelter, you can use the Subsist activity. This typically uses Culture if you’re in a settlement or Survival if you’re in the wild.

SUBSIST

You try to provide food and shelter for yourself, and possibly others as well, with a standard of living. The GM determines the difficulty based on the nature of the place where you're trying to Subsist. You might need a minimum amount of skill ranks to Subsist in particularly strange environments. It is assumed that you spend at least 8 hours carrying out this action whilst travelling, camping etc. You can Subsist for less than 8 hours, but if you do, you take a –5 circumstance penalty to the check.

Critical You either provide a subsistence living for yourself and one additional creature, or you improve your own food and shelter, granting yourself a comfortable living.

Success You find enough food and shelter with basic protection from the elements to provide you a subsistence living.

Failure You’re exposed to the elements and don’t get enough food, becoming fatigued until you attain sufficient food and shelter.

Fumble You attract trouble, eat something you shouldn’t, or otherwise worsen your situation. You take a –2 circumstance penalty to checks to Subsist for 1 week. You don’t find any food at all; if you don’t have any stored up, you’re in danger of starving or dying of thirst if you continue failing.

By taking a -2-circumstance penalty to the check, you may provide food and shelter for an additional target.

TRANSFER RUNES (TRAINED)

You can use one of the magical skills to transfer a magical rune from a runestone or other magical item.

TRANSFER RUNES MAGICAL MANIPULATE RUNE

Requirements You have a runestone with an inscribed rune, an item to transfer it to and have the Magical Crafting Feat.

You spend 10 minutes transferring a magical rune from a Runestone to another item.

Success You transfer the rune successfully.

Partial You transfer the rune successfully, but a small crack has appeared in the runestone which renders it useless for future rune storing.

Failure The runestone cracks and both the rune and runestone are lost.

Fumble As failure, but you have also destroyed the item you were attempting to transfer the rune too.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you can transfer the rune in 1 minute.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 5 you can transfer the rune in 1 round.

TRANSFERRING BETWEEN ITEMS

It is also possible to transfer a magical rune from one item to another. By increasing the difficulty of the check by 5 you can transfer the magical rune from one item to another.

Transferring runes from one item to another can be a costly business, however. A failure on the check destroys the item you are transferring from, and a fumble destroys both items!

ACROBATICS (Dex)

Acrobatics is a skill that measures your agility, balance, and coordination, allowing you to perform tasks that require finesse and precision.

Untrained Actions: Arrest a Fall, Balance, Escape, Hover, Squeeze, Tumble

Trained Actions: Aerial Manoeuvre, Catfall, Kip Up, Nimble Crawl

ARREST A FALL

Action Reaction

Trigger You fall

Requirements You have a fly speed.

You twist and turn to slow your fall. The DC for this check is 25, but this may be altered due to favourable or non-favourable conditions.

Success You fall without taking damage.

Failure You fall normally.

BALANCE MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

When faced with a narrow surface or uneven ground, you can use Acrobatics to navigate the terrain. You start this action while in an area that contains a narrow surface, uneven ground, or another similar feature. You are always flat-footed while on a narrow surface or uneven ground.

Critical You move up to your Speed.

Success You move up to your Speed, treating it as difficult terrain.

Failure You must remain stationary to keep your balance (wasting the action) or you fall. If you fall, your turn ends.

Fumble You fall and your turn ends.

HOVER

MOVEMENT

Action Free

Requirements You have a fly speed.

You can attempt to hover without expending an action. If you choose to not make a Fly check, you may expend 1 AP to hover in place.

Success You may hover in place as a Free Action.

Failure You must expend an action to hover as normal.

SQUEEZE

MOVEMENT

This action is reserved for exceptionally tight spaces where the passage is extremely narrow and restrictive. By twisting, bending, and compressing your body, you attempt to manoeuvre through a confined space. However, it's important to note that many tight spaces are considered difficult terrain, which means you can move through them more quickly and without the need for a specific check.

Critical You squeeze through the tight space at a speed of 10’ per round.

Success You squeeze through at a speed of 10’ per minute.

Partial You squeeze through at a speed of 5’ per minute.

Failure You fail to make any progress but may make another attempt in one minute.

Fumble You have wedged yourself into the tight space becoming stuck. While you’re stuck, you gain the immobilised condition to all actions except this one, which you may attempt again after 1 minute. You become unstuck if your subsequent check is a failure or greater but if you roll another fumble, you can no longer get free without assistance. A successful aid check (one that grants a bonus) from another creature allows you to make further checks to squeeze.

TUMBLE MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

You take a Stride action as part of this action. During this movement, you can try to either move through an enemy’s threatened area or move through the space of one enemy without provoking a reaction. Attempt an Acrobatics check against the enemy’s Fortitude DC or Acrobatics DC (whichever is higher) as soon as you try to enter its space.

Critical You move through the enemy’s space, treating the squares in its space as normal movement. If you don’t have enough Speed to move all the way through its space, your movement ends but you do not trigger reactions.

Success You move through the enemy’s space, treating the squares in its space as difficult terrain. If you don’t have enough Speed to move all the way through its space, you get the same effect as a failure.

Failure Your movement ends, and you trigger reactions as if you had moved out of the square you started in.

Fumble As failure except you also fall prone.

The DC is increased by 2 if you are trying to move through the enemy’s space.

AERIAL MANOEUVRE

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have fly speed.

As you soar through the air, you attempt a challenging manoeuvre. You must make an Acrobatics check. The GM has the final say in determining which manoeuvres are feasible based on the situation and surroundings.

Success Your manoeuvre is successful.

Failure Your manoeuvre fails, and the GM determines what this means to you.

Fumble As failure but the consequences of your failure have repercussions.

CATFALL MOVEMENT

Action Reaction

You attempt to reduce the severity of a fall by twisting your body and landing in a precise manner. Make a DC 30 Acrobatics check.

Critical You reduce the fall by an amount of feet equal to your Acrobatics skill bonus x5. If this reduces the distance fallen to less than 10 feet, you take no damage and land your feet.

Success You reduce the fall by an amount of feet equal to your Acrobatics skill bonus x2. If this reduces the distance fallen to less than 10 feet, you take no damage and land your feet.

Partial You reduce the fall by an amount equal to Acrobatics skill bonus.

Failure You fall normally.

Fumble You twist in a bizarre fashion and overcomplicate the fall. The fall distance is doubled for damage purposes.

KIP UP

MOVEMENT

Action Free

You can attempt to stand up from prone without using an action or triggering a reaction. Make a DC 20 Acrobatics check.

Success You spring to your feet in a flash without triggering a reaction.

Failure You stand normally.

Fumble You freeze failing to move and wasting 1 AP.

NIMBLE CRAWL

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are prone and your Speed is at least 10 feet.

You attempt to Crawl incredibly swiftly. The speed of your crawl is based upon a DC 20 Acrobatics check.

Critical You move up to your Speed.

Success You move up to your Speed, treating it as difficult terrain (every 5 feet costs 10 feet of movement).

Failure You crawl normally.

Fumble You freeze failing to move.

ARCANA (Int)

This skill represents your knowledge, understanding, and mastery of arcane and mystical arts. It encompasses your familiarity with spells, magical traditions, magical creatures, ancient artifacts, and the lore of the arcane world.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create, Identify Power, Learn a Spell, Research, Study Target, Transfer Runes

ARTISTRY (Int)

You are skilled in the creative arts, following your aesthetic sensibilities to bring to life the wonders of your imagination. Like Crafting, an Artistry skill is focused on creating something. However, what it creates is not necessarily a physical object; it could be a pattern or blueprint for an item, or a better method for creating a type of item. Thus, an Artistry (musical composition) check could be used to create a new song, but the important act of creation is the song itself, not the paper on which it is written or even the performance. An artist is not necessarily a skilled performer, though she might be.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Earn Income, Research

ARTISTRY SPECIALTIES

When you first develop this skill you must select one artistry specialty from the following list.

Specialty

Applicable Items

Choreography

Dance routines

Criticism

Evaluation & discussion of art

Literature

Writing literature & poetry

Musical Composition

Writing music and song

Philosophy

Theory and purpose

Playwriting

Writing plays and theatre

You may only make skill checks when using one of your specialties. You may learn additional specialties by selecting the Artistry Specialist Feat.

ATHLETICS (Str)

Athletics represents your ability to perform tasks that require raw power, endurance, and physical exertion.

Untrained Actions: Force Open, High Jump, Long Jump Trained Actions: Swim

FORCE OPEN ATTACK

Action 1 AP

You attempt to force open a door window, container or something else deemed appropriate by the GM.

If you do not have an appropriate tool (such as a crowbar) to assist with the task, the checks difficulty is increased by one step.

Critical You successfully open the target and cause no damage to it.

Success You force open the target and unless it is particularly sturdy or durable it gains the broken condition (GM discretion).

Fumble You jam the target shut, increasing the difficulty on future attempts to Force it Open by one step. If the target is a container which holds particularly fragile items, some of those items may well be destroyed by your efforts (GM discretion).

HIGH JUMP MOVEMENT

Action 2 AP

You make a Stride action (minimum of 10’ moved) and then make a vertical leap. The DC of the check is equal to 4 per foot jumped.

If you didn’t Stride at least 10 feet, the DC of the jump is doubled. The DC may also be increased or decreased due to the situation, as determined by the GM.

Success You make the jump.

Failure You leap half the required distance.

Fumble You don’t leap at all, and instead you trip and fall forward 5 feet landing prone.

By increasing the difficulty of the jump check by 2 you may High Jump for 1 AP.

LONG JUMP MOVEMENT

Action 2 AP

You make a Stride action (minimum of 10’ moved) and then make a horizontal leap. The DC of the check is equal to the amount of feet that you are attempting to jump.

If you didn’t Stride at least 10 feet, the DC of the jump is doubled. The DC may also be increased or decreased due to the situation, as determined by the GM.

Success You make the jump.

Failure You leap half the required distance.

Critical Failure You don’t leap at all, and instead you trip and fall forward 5 feet landing prone.

By increasing the difficulty of the jump check by 2 you may Long Jump for 1 AP.

Be Aware, when determining the difficulty of a jump that is both vertical and horizontal, you add the difficulty modifiers together.

SWIM MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

You attempt to move through a body of water or similar liquid. If the water is calm, you do not need to make a check (Routine) and may swim as if getting a success result. You may still may a check to attempt to swim faster.

If you end your turn in water and haven’t succeeded at a Swim action that turn, you sink 10 feet or get moved by the current, as determined by the GM. However, if your last action on your turn was to enter the water, you don’t sink or move with the current that turn.

Critical You move through the water 10 feet, plus 5 feet per 20 feet of your land Speed.

Success You move through the water 5 feet, plus 5 feet per 20 feet of your land Speed.

Fumble You make no progress, and if you’re holding your breath, you lose 1 round of air.

Be aware that the GM is unlikely to require a swim check for each action. The GM will use discretion as to how many checks are required when swimming.

CLIMBING (Dex)

The climbing skill is used for anything from climbing ladders to scaling the sheer face of a cliff. It can also be used to stop yourself from falling when close to a ledge.

Untrained Actions: Climb

Trained Actions: Grab an Edge

CLIMB MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You have both hands free

When you need to traverse an incline, whether it's moving upwards, downwards, or horizontally, you may need to attempt a Climb check. The difficulty of the check is determined by the GM, taking into account factors such as the steepness of the incline and the environmental conditions that may affect your climbing ability. You are considered flat-footed while climbing unless you have a Climb speed.

Critical You move 5 feet plus 5 feet per 20 feet of your land Speed (a total of 10 feet for most PCs).

Success You move 5 feet per 20 feet of your land Speed (a total of 5 feet for most PCs, minimum 5 feet if your Speed is below 20 feet).

Partial You move 5 feet.

Failure You hang but do not move anywhere.

Fumble You fall. If you began the climb on stable ground, you fall and land prone.

By increasing the difficulty of the climb check by 2 you may Climb with one hand occupied.

By increasing the difficulty of the climb check by 2 you ignore the flat-footed condition whilst climbing.

Be aware that the GM is unlikely to require a climb check for each action. The GM will use discretion as to how many checks are required when climbing.

GRAB AN EDGE

MANIPULATE

Trigger You fall and have an edge within your reach. Action Reaction

Requirements You have two free hands or are holding an item which would allow you to halt a fall (such as pick or grappling hook).

You can attempt to stop your fall by grabbing hold of a ledge or some other appropriate surface (GM discretion). The difficulty for the check is usually that of the Climb difficulty.

Critical You grab the edge or handhold. You still take damage from the distance fallen so far, but you treat the fall as though it were 30 feet shorter.

Success You grab the edge or handhold. You still take damage from the distance fallen so far, but you treat the fall as though it were 20 feet shorter.

Fumble You continue to fall, bang your head and are Stunned 3.

CRAFTING (Int)

You can use this skill to create, evaluate, understand, and repair mundane items and structures. Even if you’re untrained, you can Evaluate and Recall Knowledge.

Untrained Actions: Evaluate, Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create, Identify Alchemy, Repair, Research, Study Target

CRAFTING SPECIALTIES

When you first develop this skill, you must select one crafting specialty from the following list.

Crafting Skill

Applicable Items

Blacksmithing

Durable metal goods, including metal armour and weapons

Bookmaking

Books and paper

Cooking

Baking, brewing and meal prep,

Fletching

Bows, crossbows and their ammunition.

Glassmaking

Glass, including glassware and windows

Jeweller

Fine art, including jewellery

Leatherworking

Leather goods, including leather armour

Pottery

Ceramic goods

Shipbuilding

Ships and boats

Snares

Snares & Traps

Stonemasonry

Stone goods and structures

Tailoring

Clothing

Weaving

Textiles, baskets, and rugs

You may only make trained skill checks when using one of your specialties. You may learn additional specialties by selecting the Specialist Crafter feat.

EVALUATE

You spend some time determining the value of an item. You choose the amount of time you wish to spend evaluating the item and apply the following modifiers; 10 minutes (+0), 1 minute (-2), 1 round (-5), 1 AP (-10). If your attempt is interrupted, you must start over. The GM sets the difficulty of your check.

Critical You learn the exact value of the item and if it has magical properties (although not what those properties are).

Success You determine the exact value of the item and its resell value.

Failure You fail to determine the value of the item.

Fumble You evaluate the item incorrectly with the price being wildly inaccurate, subject to GM discretion.

You can also use this check to determine the most valuable item visible in a treasure hoard.

IDENTIFY ALCHEMY CONCENTRATE

Requirements Craft Alchemy feat, you have alchemist’s tools.

You can spend 10 minutes identifying the nature of an alchemical as long as you have alchemist tools. If your attempt is interrupted in any way, you must start over.

Success You identify the item and the means of activating it.

Failure You fail to identify the item but can try again.

Fumble You misidentify the item as another item of the GM’s choice.

REPAIR MANIPULATE

Requirements You have a repair kit.

You can attempt to fix a damaged item. This action requires you to spend 10 minutes dedicated to fixing the item, placing it on a stable surface, and using a repair kit with both hands.

The GM determines the difficulty of the repair, which is usually equal to the DC required to create the item.

Be aware that you cannot Repair a destroyed item.

Critical You restore 2 Hit Points per rank in the crafting skill.

Success You restore 1 Hit Point per rank in the crafting skill.

Fumble You deal 2d6 damage to the item. Ignore the item’s Hardness.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you can repair the item in 1 minute.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 5 you can repair the item in 1 round.

CULTURE (Int)

This skill represents your knowledge, understanding, and proficiency in the customs, traditions, and practices of various humanoid cultures. It encompasses your familiarity with different societies, their beliefs, values, and social structures.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge, Subsist Trained Actions: Research, Study Target

DECEPTION (Cha)

You can dupe those around you by lying, disguising yourself and other forms of subterfuge.

Untrained Actions: Aggravate, Bluff, Create a Diversion Trained Actions: Disguise, Feint

AGGRAVATE CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE

Action 2 AP

You can draw the attention of an enemy and force them to focus their attacks upon you. This action will have either the Auditory or Visual trait depending upon how you cause the aggravation. You make an opposed check against either your targets Sense Motive or Will DC (whichever is higher).

Critical The target is infuriated by your insults and will attack you and only you for the remainder of the encounter.

Success As critical above, but the target may make a Will Saving throw at the beginning of each turn to act normally.

Failure The target behaves normally.

Fumble As critical above, accept the target can choose to not attack if you they wish. If they choose to attack you, all attacks are made with a +4-circumstance bonus and the difficulty for you to resist their spells is increased by the same amount.

BLUFF AUDITORY CONCENTRATE LINGUISTIC MENTAL

You attempt to convince those around you that a falsehood is in fact true. You must spend a minimum of 1 round to do this but the amount of time is gauged by how long you spend upon the lie. You make a Deception check and compare it against the Sense Motive DC of every creature who can hear you. Based upon the nature of the lie, the GM might apply a circumstance penalty to the check. Furthermore, a target may make a Sense Motive check against your Deception DC at a later date if they are given reason to disbelieve your lie (GM discretion).

Critical The target believes your lie and suffers a -4-circumstance penalty to any future attempts to disbelieve it (within reason).

Success The target believes your lie.

Fumble The target doesn’t believe your lie and gains a +4-circumstance bonus against future attempts from you to Bluff them. This bonus is removed if your ever get a critical result against them with a future bluff.

CREATE A DIVERSION MENTAL

Action 1 AP

By employing a clever gesture, a well-executed trick, or employing distracting words, you create a diversion that effectively redirects the attention of creatures. With a single action, you can draw their gaze away from a particular point or individual, shifting their focus to something else entirely. If you use a gesture or trick, this action gains the manipulate trait. If you use distracting words, it gains the auditory and linguistic traits.

Attempt a Deception check and compare it to the Perception DC of the creatures whose attention you're trying to divert. Whether or not you succeed, you take a -4-circumstance penalty to attempt this against the target again for 1 minute.

Success You become hidden to each creature you succeed against. This lasts until the end of your turn or until you do anything except Step or use the Hide or the Sneak action of the Stealth skill. If you Strike a creature, the creature remains flat-footed against that attack, and you then become observed. If you do anything else, you become observed just before you act unless the GM determines otherwise.

Failure You fail to divert the creature.

DISGUISE

CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE

You change your appearance to that of someone else. Building a disguise takes 10 minutes and requires a disguise kit, but a simpler, quicker disguise might do the job if you’re not trying to imitate a specific individual (GM discretion).

If you directly interact with someone who has any reason to doubt your disguise (GM discretion), they may make a Pierce Disguise (Sense Motive) check against your Deception DC with the following results:

Critical Despite your best efforts, the target can see through your ruse and can discern your true identity if it has prior knowledge of you without the disguise.

Success The creature can tell that you are not who you claim you are.

Failure The target believes your disguise and has no reason to doubt your identity. You might have to make a new check if your circumstances or behaviour change.

FEINT MENTAL

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are within melee range of the target.

You twist and turn in such a way to as to conceal the true nature of your attacks. You attempt a Hard (DC +2) Deception check against your targets level DC. Your opponent may choose to use their Sense Motive DC, if higher.

Critical The target is left reeling by your unorthodox manoeuvres and becomes flat-footed against your melee attacks until the end of your next turn.

Success Your target is thrown for a moment but quickly recovers leaving them flat-footed against the next melee attack that you make against them before the end of your current turn.

Fumble What a calamity, if you are going to try this kind of stuff, take some lessons. You are flat-footed against the target’s melee attacks until the end of your next turn.

DIPLOMACY (Cha)

Through your adept negotiation skills and the art of flattery, you possess the ability to sway the attitudes of others.

Untrained Actions: Encourage, Gather Information, Make an Impression, Request Trained Actions: Barter, Command, Rally

ENCOURAGE AUDITORY CONCENTRATE EMOTION LINGUISTIC

Action 1 AP

You shout encouraging words to an ally within 30 feet, helping them recover from a mental effect. Attempt an Easy (+2) Diplomacy check. The ally is temporarily immune to your attempts to encourage for the next hour.

Critical The target may as a free action, immediately make a new saving throw to shrug off a mental effect with a +2-circumstance bonus.

Success The target may as a free action, immediately make a new saving throw to shrug off a mental effect.

GATHER INFORMATION SECRET

You canvass the local populace in an attempt to learn about a specific individual or topic chosen before you make your check. The amount of time this check takes is usually at least 1 hour but may take longer depending on the size of the canvassed area and other factors. The GM determines the difficulty of the check, along with any modifiers that may be applied (population, size of the settlement, bribes etc).

Critical You learn pretty much every applicable piece of information you can, based upon what is known by the local populace.

Success You gather several key pieces of information about the individual or topic.

Fumble You gather false information about the subject matter.

MAKE AN IMPRESSION AUDITORY LINGUISTIC MENTAL

With a reasonable amount of conversation, you engage the target in conversation in an attempt to impress upon them your best intentions.

As the conversation comes to an end, make a Diplomacy check against the Will DC of one target (the GM may modify this check based upon current circumstances).

Critical The target’s attitude toward you improves by two steps.

Success The target’s attitude toward you improves by one step.

Partial You may immediately roll again treating another partial as a failure.

Failure The target’s attitude toward you decreases by one step.

Fumble The target’s attitude toward you decreases by two steps.

REQUEST AUDITORY CONCENTRATE LINGUISTIC MENTAL

Action 1 AP

You may ask for the assistance of one NPC whose attitude is either friendly or helpful. The GM will determine the DC based upon what is asked of the NPC.

Critical The NPC agrees to your request wholeheartedly.

Success The NPC agrees to your request, but they might expect/request some kind of reward or amendments to the request.

Partial The NPC agrees to your request but has a proposal of their own which you must accept to make this a success.

Failure The NPC refuses the request, though they might offer an alternative which is more beneficial to them.

Fumble The NPC’s attitude toward you decreases by one step as they refuse your request.

BARTER AUDITORY LINGUISTIC MENTAL

You may use this action when dealing with any NPC to negotiate a better trade deal, whether buying or selling. This includes attempting to sell an item for more than the standard 20% resale value or purchasing an item for less than its listed price.

The time required varies by situation, but this action generally takes a minimum of one minute. The check uses a level-based DC (equal to the trader’s level) or the trader’s Diplomacy DC, whichever is higher.

The GM may apply modifiers based on the context, such as the trader's interest, local supply and demand, recent events, or your reputation.

If Selling an Item

Critical The trader is in real need of the item that you are selling and will purchase it from you for a price equal to 40% plus your diplomacy skill ranks of its original price.

Success The trader is happy to give you a good price for the item and will purchase the item for 20% plus your diplomacy skill ranks of its original price.

Partial The trader is only willing to buy the item at the normal 20%.

Failure The trader has an abundance of the item and will only offer you 10% of the original price.

Fumble Offended by your negotiation, the trader refuses to deal with you and may bar you from the shop.

If Purchasing an Item

Critical The trader sees you as a valuable customer or is eager to offload stock, you pay your diplomacy skill ranks +10% less than the listed price.

Success Your charm or reasoning pays off, you pay 10% less than the listed price.

Partial The trader appreciates the conversation but stands firm—you pay the listed price.

Failure The trader sees you as difficult or needy—you pay 10% more than the listed price.

Fumble The trader is insulted by your haggling and either refuses the sale or demands 20% more.

COMMAND AUDITORY CONCENTRATE EMOTION LINGUISTIC

Action 1 AP

You shout a command at an allied NPC. Attempt a Diplomacy check, comparing it to the Will DC of the target.

Critical The target carries out your command to the best of their ability until your request is completed or 1-minute passes, whichever comes first.

Success The target carries out your command to the best of their ability until the end of their next turn.

Failure The target ignores you and is immune to your commands for 10 minutes.

Fumble The target is enraged by your command and will attempt to do the opposite (GM discretion).

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you can double the amount of targets. Each time you increase the difficulty in this way, the amount of targets is doubled again.

RALLY AUDITORY CONCENTRATE EMOTION LINGUISTIC

Action 2 AP

You attempt to reduce panic. Attempt a Diplomacy check, comparing it to the Will DC of creatures in a 10-foot emanation around you who are frightened. Each of them is temporarily immune for 1 hour.

Critical Reduce the creature's frightened value by 2.

Success Reduce the creature's frightened value by 1.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you can double the size of the emanation. Each time you increase the difficulty in this way, the size of the emanation is doubled again.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 4 you reduce the AP cost by 1.

CHANGING ATTTUDES

In the TRG system, the interactions you have with non-player characters (NPCs) are governed by a system of attitudes. These attitudes serve as a concise summary of how NPCs perceive and respond to your character. They provide a starting point for understanding the initial disposition of the NPCs you encounter.

The attitudes are a useful tool for both players and GMs to gauge the general sentiment of NPCs towards your character. They range from hostile to helpful, with several degrees in between. It is important to note however, that these attitudes are not exhaustive and don't capture the full complexity of an NPC's personality or motivations.

The GM, as the arbiter of the game world, will provide additional depth and nuance to the attitudes based on the specific history, beliefs, and context of the NPCs. This ensures that the interactions feel organic and realistic, taking into account the intricacies of the story and the unique traits of the characters involved.

Furthermore, attitudes are not static and can change over time as the narrative unfolds. Your actions, choices, and words can influence an NPC's attitude, either positively or negatively, as they respond to your behaviour and the events that transpire.

• Hostile: The NPC will actively take risks to harm you.

• Unfriendly: The NPC Dislikes you, will not help you and wishes you ill.

• Indifferent: The NPC doesn't care about you either way. (The default starting attitude for most NPC’s.)

• Friendly: The NPC has a good attitude toward you and wishes you well, they won't necessarily stick their neck out to help you.

• Helpful: The NPC will take risks to help you.

HANDLE ANIMAL (Wis)

You are trained at working with animals, and can teach them tricks, get them to follow your simple commands, or even domesticate them. This skill also encompasses your ability to ride animals and other creatures.

Untrained Actions: Mount

Trained Actions: Command Animal, Express Rider, Guide with Knees, Stay in Saddle, Train Animal

MOUNT/DISMOUNT

MOVEMENT

Action 1 AP

Requirements You are adjacent to a willing mount.

You mount the creature and may ride it. You can also use this action to dismount if you are already mounted. This places you adjacent to the mount.

COMMAND AN ANIMAL AUDITORY CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

You command an animal to follow a course of action. Attempt a Handle Animal check against the animal’s Will DC. Based upon the nature of the command and the animals’ disposition towards you, the GM may apply a modifier.

This check automatically fails if the animal is hostile or unfriendly towards you. If the animal is helpful towards you, increase your degree of success by one step.

Critical The animal does as you command for the next minute.

Success The animal does as you command on its next turn.

Partial You may immediately expend another AP to treat this check as a success, otherwise treat as a failure.

Failure The animal is hesitant or resistant, and it does nothing.

Fumble The animal ignores you and takes a completely different action (GM discretion).

Commanded Animals

When issuing commands to an animal, it's important to recognize that they are independent creatures with limited intelligence. Unlike beings with higher cognitive abilities, animals have a more basic understanding of language and can comprehend only the simplest instructions.

While you can communicate with your animal companion or a trained creature, the level of complexity in their actions is restricted. For example, you can instruct your animal to move to a specific area, but you cannot provide a detailed path for it to follow. Similarly, you can command it to attack a certain creature, but you cannot specify the manner of its attack or ask it to make nonlethal strikes.

The specifics of how the animal carries out your command are determined by the GM.

The animal carries out your command as soon as it can, usually as its first action on its next turn. If you successfully commanded it multiple times, it does what you said in order. It forgets all commands beyond what it can accomplish on its turn. If multiple people command the same animal, the GM determines how the animal reacts. The GM might also increase the difficulty of the check if someone has already tried to Command the Animal that round.

You may increase the DC by 5 before rolling in an attempt carry out this action for 0 AP.

EXPRESS RIDER

MOVEMENT

You can get greater speed out of your mount, increasing its daily travel speed. Make a handle Animal check with the difficulty determined by the GM with the following results:

Critical Increase your mounts travel speed by 50%.

Success Increase your mounts travel speed by 20%.

GUIDE WITH KNEES CONCENTRATE MOVEMENT OPEN

Action Free (0 AP)

You can guide your mount with your knees so you can use both hands in combat.

Make your Ride check at the start of your turn.

Success You can us both hands this turn.

Partial You can us both hands this turn but any 2 handed actions suffer a -2-circumstance penalty.

Failure You can only use one hand this turn.

Fumble You fall out of the saddle and fall prone.

STAY IN SADDLE MOVEMENT

Action Reaction

You can react instantly to try to avoid falling when your mount rears or bolts unexpectedly or when you take damage.

Success You stay in the saddle.

Failure You fall out of the saddle.

Fumble You fall out of the saddle take a Light Bludgeoning critical.

TRAIN ANIMAL MANIPULATE

You can teach an animal to perform a specific action. This action can either be one of the basic actions that most animals will already know (see below), or a new basic action.

The difficulty of the check and the amount of time required (usually about 1 week) are determined by the GM.

Critical The animal takes to the action quickly, learning on 2-3 days (GM discretion). If the animal already knew the action, you can Command the Animal to take that action without attempting a handle Animal check. If it was a new basic action, add that action to the actions the animal can take when Commanded, but you must still make a check.

Success As critical but it takes the animal 1 week to learn the action.

Failure The animal doesn’t learn the trick.

BASIC ANIMAL ACTIONS

Animals have limited intelligence and therefore will only know a limited amount of actions. These actions are as follows:

Awareness (Perception), Drop Prone, Jump (Athletics), Stand, Stride and Strike.

It is possible for an animal to use other action based upon circumstances, but these cannot be commanded unless trained.

INTIMIDATE (Cha)

This Skill represents the ability to browbeat, coerce, and terrorize other people, through subtle threats or vulgar displays of power. In combat, characters can use this Skill to attempt to shift their opponent’s current disposition.

Untrained Actions: Aggravate, Coerce, Demoralise

AGGRAVATE CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE

Action 2 AP

You can draw the attention of an enemy and force them to focus their attacks upon you. This action will have either the Auditory or Visual trait depending upon how you cause the aggravation. You make an opposed check against either your targets Sense Motive or Will DC (whichever is higher).

Critical The target is infuriated by your insults and will attack you and only you for the remainder of the encounter.

Success As critical above, but the target may make a Will Saving throw at the beginning of each turn to act normally.

Partial The target will use their next action to attack you if you are within range of their attacks.

Failure The target behaves normally.

Fumble As critical above, accept the target can choose to not attack if you they wish. If they choose to attack you, all attacks are made with a +4-circumstance bonus and the difficulty for you to resist their spells is increased by the same amount.

DEMORALISE AUDITORY CONCENTRATE EMOTION FEAR MENTAL

Action 1 AP

You shout and taunt to provoke a reaction that disrupts your targets focus and potentially hampers their effectiveness in combat. Choose one target within 30 feet who you are aware of. You make an Intimidate check against that target's Will DC.

The difficulty of this check is increased by one step if you speak in a language that the target doesn’t understand. Regardless of your result, the target is temporarily immune to your attempts to Demoralize it for 10 minutes.

Critical The target becomes frightened 2.

Success The target becomes frightened 1.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you may demoralise an additional target. Each time you increase the difficulty in this way, another target is affected.

COERCE AUDITORY CONCENTRATE LINGUISTIC MENTAL

Subtlety is beyond you but threatening a target to get them to do what you want is more suited to your style.

After spending a reasonable amount of time in conversation with a target (at least 1 minute) you can see and that can either see or sense you, make an opposed Intimidate check against the target's Will DC, modified by any circumstances the GM determines.

Critical You get the information that you need from the target and they agree to follow your suggestions as long as they are not placed in direct harm. The target will comply with your request as long as you are still in close proximity but will become unfriendly (if they weren't already unfriendly or hostile) after about a day. It is unlikely however that they will attack you or cause you harm due to the fear that you have instilled into them (well for now at least).

Success As critical success, but once the target becomes unfriendly, they may decide to retaliate indirectly (report you to the authorities or help your enemies in some way).

Partial The target doesn’t do what you say.

Failure The target doesn’t do what you say, and their attitude towards you drops by one step.

Fumble The target doesn’t do what you say, and their attitude towards you drops by two steps. Furthermore, they are immune to further attempts by you to Intimidate them for at least 1 week.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 2 you may demoralise an additional target. Each time you increase the difficulty in this way, another target is affected.

LINGUISTICS (Int)

As a master of language, you possess a remarkable skill set that encompasses both spoken and written communication. Your linguistic abilities extend far beyond the confines of your native tongue, granting you the power to understand and communicate in multiple languages. Whether it be the elegant elven language, the guttural speech of orcs, or the ancient script of forgotten civilizations, you possess a deep understanding of various tongues.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create Forgery, Decipher Writing, Discern Secret Message, Research

CREATE FORGERY SECRET

You skilfully create deceptive documents, meticulously recreating their authenticity over a span of days or weeks. To produce a convincing forgery, you must possess the appropriate materials for writing. When engaging in the act of forgery, the GM makes a Secret Linguistics check to determine the outcome. If your attempt proves successful, the forged document is of such high quality that casual observers remain oblivious to its deceit. Only those who thoroughly scrutinize the document and make a deliberate effort to discern its veracity by performing a Sense Motive or Linguistics check against your Linguistics DC possess a chance of uncovering the ruse.

Success The observer does not detect the forgery.

Failure The observer knows your document is a forgery.

Be aware that observer who was fooled with a casual glance can still potentially examine the forgery at a later date if their suspicions become aroused.

DECIPHER WRITING CONCENTRATE SECRET

You attempt to interpret obscure or ancient text, crack a cipher or decode a hidden message. This takes 1 minute per page of text but may take longer based upon the nature of the text that you are deciphering (GM discretion).

The difficulty of the check is determined by the GM based on content and complexity of the text. If the text is in an unfamiliar language (one that you do not know), the GM will apply modifiers to the DC.

Critical You decipher and understand the full content of the text.

Success You understand the meaning of the text but will not be able to translate it word for word.

Partial You nearly have it, you may make the check again at +2 (after expending the same amount of time again).

Failure You can’t understand the text and take a –2 circumstance penalty to further checks to decipher it.

Fumble You mis-interpret the text.

DISCERN SECRET MESSAGE CONCENTRATE SECRET

Action 1 AP

If you overhear or otherwise intercept a secret message, you can attempt to learn its true meaning. Your check is compared to the Deception DC of the creature passing the secret message.

Success You learn the information contained in the secret message.

Failure You don’t detect any hidden meaning in the message

Fumble You detect false information from the message.

MEDICINE (Wis)

You have knowledge of the biology of many species and can treat several different types of wounds and ailments.

Untrained Actions: First Aid, Recall Knowledge, Resuscitation

Trained Actions: Research, Treat Disease, Treat Injury, Treat Toxin, Treat Wounds

FIRST AID FLOURISH MANIPULATE

Action 3 AP

Requirements You have a hand free.

You perform first aid on an adjacent creature that is bleeding. The difficulty of the check is determined by the amount that the target is bleeding.

Bleeding Severity

DC

Light (1-4 Hits)

20

Moderate (5-8 Hits)

25

Severe (9-12 Hits)

30

Dire (13+ Hits)

40

Critical You reduce the bleeding by 3.

Success You reduce the bleeding by 2.

Partial You reduce the bleeding by 1.

Fumble You increase the amount of bleed damage by 1.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by 4 you may reduce the AP cost of this action by 1 (min 1 AP).

RESUSCITATION FLOURISH MANIPULATE

Action 3 AP

Requirements You have a hand free.

You give medical assistance to an adjacent creature who has the Dying condition. This a Hard (+2) Level (targets) based DC.

Heroic You reduce the targets Dying condition by 3.

Critical You reduce the targets Dying condition by 2.

Success You reduce the targets Dying condition by 1.

Fumble You increase the targets Dying condition by 1.

Blunder Oops, perhaps they were already dead. You increase the targets Dying condition by 2.

By increasing the difficulty of the check by one step you may reduce the AP cost of this action by 1 (min 1 AP).

TREAT DISEASE MANIPULATE

Requirements You are using healer’s tools or have other appropriate medical equipment.

After spending 8 hours caring for a diseased creature, make an opposed Medicine check against the disease’s save DC. After you attempt to Treat a Disease for a creature, you can’t try again until after that creature’s next save against the disease.

Critical You grant the creature a +4 circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against the disease.

Success You grant the creature a +2 circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against the disease.

Partial You grant the creature a +1 circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against the disease.

Fumble Your efforts cause the creature to take a –2 circumstance penalty to its next save against the disease.

TREAT INJURY HEALING MANIPULATE

Requirements You are using healer’s tools or have other appropriate medical equipment.

You spend at least 8 hours caring for a living creature with an Injury of at least Light Severity.

Critical You quarter the healing times required for the injury.

Success You halve the healing times required for the injury.

Partial The injury is classed as being treated and will reduce in severity in its natural timeframe.

Fumble The Injury increases in severity by one step. If the Injury was already Crippling then the target must make a Fortitude Saving Throw against their own attack level or die.

TREAT TOXIN MANIPULATE

Requirements You are using healer’s tools or have other appropriate medical equipment.

You spend at least 1 minute treating a patient to prevent the spread of poison. Make an opposed Medicine check against the poison’s save DC. After you attempt to Treat a Poison for a creature, you can’t try again until after the next time that creature attempts a save against the poison.

Critical You grant the creature a +4 circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against the poison.

Success You grant the creature a +2 circumstance bonus to its next saving throw against the poison.

Fumble Your efforts cause the creature to take a –2 circumstance penalty to its next save against the poison.

TREAT WOUNDS HEALING MANIPULATE

Requirements You are using healer’s tools or have other appropriate medical equipment.

You spend 10 uninterrupted minutes mending minor bruising and scratches on one target. This target is then temporarily immune to Treat Wounds actions for 1 hour.

This check has a DC of 20 but may be modified based upon circumstances (GM discretion).

The result of your Medicine check determines how many Hit Points the target regains.

Critical The target regains 20 Hit Points.

Success The target regains 10 Hit Points.

Partial The target regains 5 Hit Points.

Fumble The target takes 10 damage and is now immune to your attempts to treat wounds until your next daily preparation.

You may increase the DC before rolling in an attempt to heal more hit point damage. For every 1 that you increase the DC, you may heal an additional 1 hit points (max of +20, doubled on a critical).

You may also increase the DC before rolling in an attempt to heal additional targets. For every 5 that you increase the DC you may heal an additional target.

MEDITATION (Wis)

You can meditate to focus your mind and body to gain awareness of a specific subject or heal yourself.

Trained Actions: Cleansing Trance, Clear Mind, Healing Trance, Power Recovery

CLEANSING TRANCE BONUS CONCENTRATE HEALING MENTAL

After meditating for 1 hour, you attempt to cure one poison or disease afflicting you. You may make a new saving throw against the effect, applying the bonus result from the Bonus Check Table.

CLEAR MIND BONUS CONCENTRATE MENTAL

After meditating for an appropriate time (usually at least one hour) on a task, you can make a skill check and apply the bonus result from the Bonus Check Table.

HEALING TRANCE CONCENTRATE HEALING MENTAL

After meditating for one hour, you heal yourself of physical damage. You cannot then use Healing Trance for 1 hour. You make an Easy (+2) level-based skill check. The result of your Meditation check determines the outcome.

Critical You triple the amount of hit points regained naturally.

Success You double the amount of hit points regained naturally.

POWER RECOVERY CONCENTRATE MENTAL

You may attempt to increase the amount of power points you regain whilst resting. After each hour of rest, you may make a Medium (DC +0) level-based check with the following results:

Heroic You regain an additional 2 PP per caster level.

Critical You regain an additional PP per caster level.

Success You regain an additional PP per two caster levels (round up).

Partial You regain an additional 1 PP.

MENTAL FOCUS (Wis)

You have trained your mind to overcome minor injuries, mental interruption and to quickly adapt to your surroundings.

With some additional training, you can also learn to focus your rage into a destructive frenzy, turning you into an unpredictable killing machine.

Untrained Actions: Spatial Awareness Trained Actions: Invoke Rage, Pain Tolerance, Revoke Rage, Spell Concentration, Stunned Manoeuvre

SPATIAL AWARENESS CONCENTRATE MENTAL

Action Free

There are a number of circumstances where you need to regain your bearings (such as being teleported). When such a situation arises, the GM will ask for this check (DC is level based).

Success You may act normally.

Failure You immediately lose 1 AP. If you have no AP remaining then you gain Stunned 1.

Fumble You immediately lose 2 AP. If you have no AP remaining then you gain Stunned 2.

INVOKE RAGE

CONCENTRATE EMOTION MENTAL RAGE

Action varies

Requirements You have the Frenzy feat; you aren’t fatigued or raging.

You laugh uncontrollably, bite your shield, or gnash your teeth as your eyes roll uncontrollably with a look of madness. Make a level-based check:

Heroic It takes you 1 action to rage.

Critical It takes you 2 actions to rage.

Success It takes you 3 actions to rage.

Failure You fail to rage after using 3 actions but may roll again next round.

Fumble You froth and growl for 3 actions, your blood vessels bulging in the side of your head and then you see red. You rage but cannot discern friend from foe for the duration. You gain the confused condition, and your rage does not end until the condition does.

Whilst raging you apply the following:

• You cannot use any action which has the Defence trait.

• You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to all Strength and Constitution based checks.

• You gain temporary HP equal to your class bonus x 20.

• You take a -2-circumstance penalty to DB.

• You cannot use actions with the concentrate trait unless they also have the rage trait.

• You cannot cast spells.

• You are immune to stun.

• You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to all Will saving throws.

Your rage last until you end it using a Revoke Rage action (see below) or after 1 minute.

You may choose to extend your rage for a further minute by making an additional Mental Focus check. The difficulty of this check increases by one step each time.

PAIN TOLERANCE CONCENTRATE FLOURISH MENTAL

Action Free

You grit your teeth and push the pain that you are experiencing to the back of your mind for a period of time base upon a DC 20 skill check.

Critical You ignore up to 1 point of the dazed, injured or weakened condition until the end of your next turn.

Success You ignore up to 1 point of the dazed, injured or weakened condition until the end of your current turn.

Fumble You simply cannot push through the pain and are immune to this check for 1 hour.

You may increase the DC before rolling in an attempt to ignore more pain. For every 4 that you increase the DC, you may ignore an additional point of the selected condition.

REFOCUS

CONCENTRATE MENTAL

Action 1 AP

You steel your mind and centre your will, attempting to restore an ability with the Focus trait. You make a level-based check with the following results

Critical You instantly regain the use of the ability and may use it again immediately (AP dependant).

Success You regain the use of the ability and may use it again at the beginning of your next turn.

Partial You fail to regain the ability and must wait 1 minute before using it can be used again.

Failure You fail to regain the ability and cannot attempt to Refocus that ability again for 10 minutes.

Fumble You fail to regain the ability and cannot use it again until your next daily preparation.

Blunder As fumble, but your mind also backlashes; you take 1d4 mental damage per level (basic Will).

REVOKE RAGE

CONCENTRATE EMOTION MENTAL RAGE

Action varies

Requirements You have the Frenzy feat, you are raging.

You focus your inner anger and release your primal energy ending your rage state. Make a level based Mental Focus check to end your rage.

Use the following results:

Critical It takes you 1 actions to end your rage.

Success It takes you 2 actions to end your rage.

Partial It takes you 3 actions to end your rage.

Failure You fail to end your rage after using 3 actions but may roll again next round.

Fumble You fail to end your rage after using 3 actions and must continue to rage for the full minute. When your rage ends, you are fatigued 2.

When you eventually come out of Rage, you are fatigued 1 for 1 hour.

STUNNED MANOEUVRE CONCENTRATE MENTAL

Action Reaction manoeuvre

You can ignore effects that stun you by sheer power of will. When you are subjected to an effect that gives you the Stunned condition you may attempt to lower the amount of stun that you take. The DC of the check is based upon the level of the creature or effect that delivered the stun with a Very Hard (+5 DC) difficulty.

Critical You ignore the stun completely.

Success You reduce the stun taken by half (round up).

Fumble You increase the stun taken by 1

NATURE (Wis)

You know a great deal about the natural world, including animals, fey and various beasts. You also have an understanding of herbs and other natural concoctions, as well as knowledge of all things related to Verdant magic. Even if you’re untrained in Nature, you can use it to Recall Knowledge.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create, Identify Power, Learn a Spell, Research, Study Target, Transfer Runes

OCCULTISM (Int)

This skill represents your knowledge, understanding, and mastery of ancient philosophy and obscure creatures such as aberrations. It encompasses your familiarity with ethereal magic and all things spiritual.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create, Identify Power, Learn a Spell, Research, Study Target, Transfer Runes

PERCEPTION (Wis)

You can use all of your senses (hearing, taste, touch, sight, and smell) to notice danger, pick out fine details, and search for hidden objects or creatures.

Untrained Actions: Awareness, Search, Time Sense

AWARENESS CONCENTRATE

Action Free

Awareness allows you to remain keenly aware of your surroundings, enabling you to notice significant occurrences. It is the fundamental purpose of the Perception skill, serving a multitude of purposes as determined by the GM. Whether you strive to act swiftly in a surprise round, catch a glimpse of something vital from your peripheral vision, or uncover the presence of concealed beings nearby, an Awareness check proves invaluable. Notably, Awareness does not require taking a specific action, though you must maintain consciousness and possess functional senses to do so.

The difficulties for an Awareness check to notice things are determined by the GM based on the circumstances.

SEARCH CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

Using the Search action allows you to focus your attention on locating specific objects or beings, such as revealing an invisible creature that has made its presence known or uncovering a hidden creature within the vicinity. Additionally, you can dedicate time to meticulously examine an area for concealed traps, perils, or any intriguing items that might be cleverly concealed or elude immediate notice. This comprehensive search usually takes around 1 minute to investigate an area no larger than 20 feet by 20 feet (or smaller if the GM deems it cluttered or intricate).

TIME SENSE CONCENTRATE

Action Varies

You attune your senses to the subtle passage of time, gauging how much has passed or detecting irregularities in its flow. This can involve noticing changes in ambient light, bodily rhythms, or environmental cues. In some cases, you might detect temporal anomalies caused by magic, unnatural forces, or planar shifts. The GM sets the DC based on the complexity of the situation or anomaly.

Critical You pinpoint the exact amount of time that has passed and detect even the subtlest irregularities, including hidden magical time effects or shifts in chronology.

Success You accurately estimate the passage of time or confirm that time is behaving normally.

Fumble Your internal sense of time is completely off, possibly causing you to misjudge an event’s timing or miss signs of a temporal disturbance.

This action may be taken passively or actively, depending on the situation.

Spending more time observing your surroundings can improve your accuracy (GM discretion).

You might be asked to roll Time Sense when emerging from unconsciousness, navigating a timeless space, or evaluating whether a teleportation effect displaced you in time.

PERFORM (Cha)

The specialties in this skill allow you to perform to an audience with dance, song and tale. You are skilled at one form of entertainment, from singing to acting to playing an instrument.

PERFORM SPECIALTIES

When you first develop this skill, you must select one perform specialty from the following list.

Skill

Example

Acting

Comedy, drama, pantomime

Comedy

Buffoonery, limericks, joke-telling

Dancing

Ballet, waltz, jig

Keyboard

Harpsichord, piano, organ

Percussion

Bells, chimes, drums

Stringed Instruments

Fiddle, harp, lute, mandolin

Wind Instruments

Flute, pan pipes, trumpet

Singing

Ballad, chant, melody

Tales

Epic, storytelling

You are skilled in the art of performance, utilizing your talents to captivate and entertain audiences, whether it be to awe a crowd or earn a livelihood. You may learn additional specialties by selecting the Perform Specialist Feat.

Untrained Actions: Entertain Trained Actions: Earn Income

ENTERTAIN

Action 1 AP or more

When delivering a short performance such as a song, dance, or a series of jokes, you can use the Entertain action. This action is ideal for swiftly demonstrating your talent or leaving a strong impression. While a brief performance may not have an immediate effect, it could influence the difficulty of future Diplomacy checks or potentially alter the attitudes of those who witnessed it (GM discretion).

Critical Your performance leaves a lasting impression on the observers, ensuring that they will share stories and tales of your exceptional ability with others.

Success You demonstrate your skill and talent, earning the genuine appreciation of the observers who recognize and admire the high quality of your performance.

Failure Your performance is a bit naff and instantly forgettable.

Critical Failure What was that, if your audience has things to throw at you I suspect that they will.

PLANES (Int)

This skill represents your knowledge and understanding of anything related to another plane of existence. This includes knowledge of the planes as well as creatures which originate from planes other the prime plane.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge, Subsist Trained Actions: Research, Study Target

POWER MANIPULATION (Int)

Requirements Adept

You are able to attune your senses to the finer points of magic around you, noticing subtle differences in its weave and even manipulating it. Power manipulation skills are unique in that they require the use of Power Points to work.

Trained Actions: Dispel, Recharge Item, Sense Power, Sigil, Spell Concentration

DISPEL CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE WARDING

Action 2 AP; Range 120 feet.

Target one spell or effect which you are aware of

You unravel the magic behind a spell or effect. You expend an amount of PP up to the maximum that you can use to cast a spell and then make the check (which classes as a counteract check) against the target magical item or effect with the following results.

Critical You dispel the effect and only expend half the PP.

Success You dispel the effect and expend the PP.

Partial You fail to dispel the effect but only expend half the PP.

Failure You fail to dispel the effect and expend the PP.

Fumble You fail to dispel the effect, expend the PP and trigger a resonance event (see chapter 9).

If you successfully counteract a magic item, the item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. This doesn't change the item's non-magical properties. If the target is an artifact or similar item, you automatically fail.

RECHARGE ITEM ALTERATION CONCENTRATE

Requirements You have the spells that are contained within the item on your spell list.

Action 10 minutes; PP Cost 2

You concentrate on a charged magical item that you have invested and attempt to increase its natural recharging capability.

You spend 10 minutes holding the item and chanting and then make a skill check with the DC based upon the level and rarity of the item. Once you have used this skill successfully, the charged item becomes temporarily immune until your next daily preparation.

Heroic: You accelerate the natural charging process of the item, and it regains an additional 1 PP per caster level.

Critical You accelerate the natural charging process of the item, and it regains an additional 1 PP per 2 caster levels (round up).

Success You accelerate the natural charging process of the item, and it regains an additional 1 PP per 4 caster levels (round up).

Partial The item is resistant to your efforts; you may continue for another ten minutes and attempt the check again or treat as failure below.

Failure The item is resistant to your efforts, and you fail to increase its recharge rate.

Fumble Your efforts not only fail but block the items natural recharging process. The item regains no PP during this 24-hour period and becomes temporarily immune to this skill until your next daily preparation. Furthermore, you may trigger a Magical Resonance Event.

Be aware that you may only make one successful recharge check per item per day.

SENSE MAGIC - BROAD CONCENTRATE INSIGHT

Area 20-foot emanation

Action 2 AP

You send out a pulse that registers the presence of magic. You receive no information beyond the presence or absence of magic. You can choose to ignore magic you're fully aware of, such as the magic items and ongoing spells of you and your allies.

Some magical auras such as those from a different tradition, illusions, magical traps and divinations are more difficult to locate. If such an aura is within the radius of your spell, your power manipulation check is used as an opposed check against the spells DC (or level DC if spell DC unknown) with the following modifiers and result:

Type of Aura

Mod

Magic is of a different tradition

-5

Active Shadow Magic

-10

Active magical trap

-10

Active Insight Magic

-5

Critical You sense the aura normally and automatically identify it.

Success You sense the aura normally.

Failure The magical aura is hidden to you.

Once magic is detected, you may use other skills and abilities to ascertain exactly what that magic is.

SENSE MAGIC - FOCUSED CONCENTRATE INSIGHT

Range 10 feet; Area 5-foot square

Action 3 AP

As per Broad but you detect the presence of absence of magic in a 5-foot square. You may move your focus each round.

Be aware that sense magic can penetrate barriers, but 3 feet of wood or dirt, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or a thin sheet of lead blocks it.

SIGIL CONCENTRATE MANIPULATE WARDING

Ranks 2

Action 1 minute; PP Cost 1

You harmlessly place your unique magical sigil, which is about 1 square inch in size, on the targeted creature or object. The mark can be scrubbed or scraped off with 5 minutes of work. If it's on a creature, it fades naturally over the course of a week. This is a DC 20 check with the following results.

Critical Your sigil is scribed and may be visible or invisible.

Success Your sigil is scribed and visible to all.

Failure You have failed but may try again.

Fumble Your sigil is incorrect and may resemble someone else’s. (GM Discretion).

NEGATIVE PPIt is impossible to have a negative PP value under normal circumstances. If for some reason (such as a dispel action) your PP value would drop below 0 you instead take 5 Soul Drain for every PP that you would fall below 0.NEGATIVE PPIt is impossible to have a negative PP value under normal circumstances. If for some reason (such as a dispel action) your PP value would drop below 0 you instead take 5 Soul Drain for every PP that you would fall below 0.

RELIGION (Wis)

The secrets of deities, dogma, faith, and the realms of divine creatures both sublime and sinister are open to you. You also understand how magic works, though your training imparts a religious slant to that knowledge. Even if you’re untrained in Religion, you can use it to Recall Knowledge.

Untrained Actions: Recall Knowledge Trained Actions: Create, Identify Power, Learn a Spell, Research, Study Target, Transfer Runes

SENSE MOTIVE (Wis)

You possess the ability to discern falsehoods and gain insights into the true intentions of creatures you engage with.

Untrained Actions: Detect Deception, Pierce Disguise Trained Actions: Read Emotion, Sense Mental Effect

DETECT DECEPTION CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

You have a knack for spotting lies and half-truths. When you suspect a creature is being deceptive, you may make a Sense Motive check against their Deception DC.

Critical You recognize the target is lying and discern what they are attempting to conceal.

Success You realize the target is lying, but not what they're hiding.

Failure You believe that the target is telling the truth.

Fumble As failure but you take a -4-circumstance penalty on all future Detect Deceptions check against the target until you achieve a Critical Success against them using this skill.

PIERCE DISGUISE CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

You can recognize that a creature has changed its appearance. Sometimes, if you are being particularly alert for those in the area who might be in disguise, the GM might allow you to do this without taking an action. This check is opposed by the Deception Check of the disguised creature. If you succeed, you realize the creature is disguised and not who it seems, but not necessarily who or what the disguised creature is beneath that disguise. If the disguised creature is impersonating a particular individual that you know, the GM might grant you a bonus to your Perception check.

READ EMOTION CONCENTRATE

Action 1 AP

You study a creature's micro expressions, posture, and vocal tone to infer their current emotional state. Make a Sense Motive check against the target's Will DC.

Critical You accurately identify the creature's emotional state and whether it is being influenced by emotion-based effects (fear, charm, etc.).

Success You correctly identify the creature's current emotion (e.g., anger, fear, guilt).

Failure You cannot discern their emotional state.

Fumble You misread the creature’s emotions entirely, potentially drawing incorrect conclusions.

SENSE MENTAL EFFECT CONCENTRATE

By examining any one creature within 30 feet, you can ascertain whether they are currently affected by a mental effect, even if the creature is unaware of the effect.

You choose the amount of time you wish to spend interacting with the creature and apply the following modifiers: 10 minutes (+2), 1 minute (0), 1 round (-2), 1 AP (-5), Free (-10).

The difficultly of this check is typically the save difficulty of the effect, but it can be higher or lower based on how overt the manifestation of the mental effect is, as determined by the GM.

Critical You determine that the creature is currently affected by a mental effect and may make an appropriate skill check to determine what the effect is as a free action.

Success You determine that the creature is currently affected by a mental effect but cannot tell exactly what that effect is.

Failure You fail to sense a mental effect.

Fumble If the target is affected by a mental effect, you believe it to be something beneficial. Otherwise, you believe that they are affected by a false effect.

STEALTH (Dex)

You are skilled at avoiding detection, allowing you to slip past foes, hide, conceal an item or strike from an unseen position.

Untrained Actions: Conceal an Object, Hide, Sneak Trained Actions: Ambush, Sniping

CONCEAL AN OBJECT MANIPULATE SECRET

Action 1 AP

You hide a small object upon your person to prevent other creatures from noticing it. The item can have a size of no larger than small.

To actively hide an item from someone you must make a check against their Perception DC to avoid the item being discovered. Alternatively, if a creature is actively searching for your hidden item they must make a Perception check against your Stealth DC to notice the item.

Success The searcher finds the object.

Failure The object remains undetected.

HIDE SECRET

Action 1 AP

You take advantage of cover or concealment to obscure yourself from view. The GM secretly rolls your Stealth check and compares it to the Perception DC of each creature observing you, considering any cover or greater cover you have. The bonus from cover or greater cover enhances your Stealth check in this situation.

Success If the creature had visual contact with you, you now transition from being observed to being hidden. If you were already hidden or undetected by the creature, you maintain your previous state.

If you manage to successfully hide from a creature but subsequently lose cover or greater cover against it or are no longer concealed from it, you return to being observed. Your hidden status is also lost if you perform any action other than Hide, Sneak, or Step. When you attempt to Strike a creature, it remains flat-footed against your attack, and you become observed again. If you perform any other action, you become observed just before taking that action, unless the GM decides otherwise. In some cases, the GM might allow you to perform a particularly inconspicuous action without being noticed, potentially requiring another Stealth check.

If a creature uses a Search action to detect your presence and observes you, you must successfully Hide to become hidden from that creature again.

SNEAK

MOVEMENT SECRET

Action 1 AP

You can move silently and unnoticed from one location to another. While making a Sneak check, you can move up to half your speed using any available movement type.

If you're already undetected by a creature and there are no possible means for it to observe you (such as being invisible, the observer being blinded, or being in darkness when the creature can't see in darkness), a critical failure on your Sneak check results in a regular failure instead. You will remain undetected even if you lose cover or concealment against that creature.

At the end of your movement, the GM secretly rolls your Stealth check and compares it to the Perception DC of each creature you were hidden from or undetected by at the start of your movement. If you maintain cover or greater cover against a creature throughout your movement, you gain a +2-circumstance bonus (or +4 for greater cover) to your Stealth check. However, the bonus increase from Taking Cover does not apply because you are actively moving. If, at the end of your movement, you are neither concealed from a creature nor have cover or greater cover against it, you automatically become observed by that creature.

Success During your movement, you remain completely undetected by the creature. This undetected condition continues until the end of your movement.

However, as soon as you perform any action other than Hide, Sneak, or Step, you become observed by the creature. If you attempt to Strike the creature, it remains flat-footed against your attack, but you become observed. If you engage in any other action, you become observed just before you act, unless the GM decides otherwise.
