RESELLLING EQUIPMENT

Your character will collect a large amount of gear and items over the course of an adventure or campaign and at some point will need to sell some of it. As a general rule, any item can be sold automatically for 20% of its original price as long as the settlement that you are in has a level greater than the items.

If you need a higher price for a piece of gear you may use the diplomacy skill to take the barter action (see chapter 4).

ITEM LEVEL

Every item the game will have a level which affects how you interact with it in a number of ways. As a general rule, the lower the level of an item, the lower its complexity for construction, identification, repair and valuation. You cannot craft an item that has a level higher than your own. If an item has no level listed in its description then it will have a default of ‘0’. Your GM should always be aware of what items are available in the game and although characters can use items which are of a higher level, introducing such items into the game should be done wisely.

STARTING GEAR

Your character begins play with 50 x wealth mod (see below) in gold pieces (gp) to spend on gear. Items with an uncommon rarity can be purchased only if you have special access from abilities you selected during character creation or your GM gives you permission to purchase them.

Once you’ve purchased your starting items, there are three main ways to gain new items and equipment: you can find them during an adventure, make them using the Crafting skill, or purchase them from a merchant.

STARTING WEALTH

Each character has a wealth score. This score determines your starting coin and is determined by a number of elements including charisma, background and class.

CHARISMA

You add your Charisma as a bonus to your starting wealth. Ignore any negative modifiers to Charisma.

Be aware that a characters wealth score may start below 0 and this will indicate a character who begins in debt or is indebted to an employer, lord, master etc. If your character begins with a wealth score of 0 or less you will have to determine the exact details with your GM.

CARRYING & USING ITEMS

You carefully allocate your belongings into three categories: held, worn, and stowed.

Held items are those grasped within your hands, taking advantage of your agility and immediate accessibility. Whether wielding two weapons or a powerful two-handed tool, your hands are your instruments of action and defence.

Worn items, on the other hand, find their place in pockets, belt pouches, and sheaths. These conveniently located items can be swiftly retrieved or returned with a 1 AP (Interact) action, allowing for quick access during combat or other urgent situations. From potions to throwing knives, worn items serve as a readily available arsenal, enabling you to adapt to changing circumstances.

Finally, stowed items reside within backpacks or similar containers. Though securely held, retrieving these items requires more time and effort. Changing the way, they are carried or drawing them usually demands the expenditure of a 1 AP (Interact) action, emphasizing the need for strategic planning. When time is of the essence, the more accessible held and worn items prove to be your best allies.

It is worth noting that utilizing items effectively often demands the expenditure of multiple actions. Whether it's consuming a potion, donning a piece of armour, or rummaging through a backpack, you must balance your actions wisely to optimize your chances of success. In the heat of battle, every decision can mean the difference between victory and defeat.

ENCUMBRANCE

Carrying especially heavy or unwieldy items can make it more difficult for you to move, as can overloading yourself with too much gear. To determine how much your character can carry before accruing penalties you must work out your weight allowance.

WEIGHT ALLOWANCE

The amount that you can carry without adverse effect is a base of 50 lbs. This is modified by your strength ability score x10 in lbs.

Weight Allowance = 50 + (strength x 10)

If you exceed your weight allowance you gain the encumbered condition.

WEIGHT OF COINS

For coins to register as weight for encumbrance purposes you must carry 50. Each 50 coins will register as 1 pound of weight.

BROKEN CONDITIONBroken is a condition that affects objects. An object is broken when damage has reduced its Hit Points to 0 or less. With the exception of armour (see below), a broken object can't be used for its normal function, nor does it grant bonuses. If an item is reduced to a negative amount of Hit Points equal to 50% of its total, then it is destroyed. A broken item still imposes penalties and limitations normally incurred by carrying, holding, or wearing it. Broken armour has it DR reduced by 50% until it loses the condition.If an effect makes an item broken automatically it is reduced to 0 HP. BROKEN CONDITIONBroken is a condition that affects objects. An object is broken when damage has reduced its Hit Points to 0 or less. With the exception of armour (see below), a broken object can't be used for its normal function, nor does it grant bonuses. If an item is reduced to a negative amount of Hit Points equal to 50% of its total, then it is destroyed. A broken item still imposes penalties and limitations normally incurred by carrying, holding, or wearing it. Broken armour has it DR reduced by 50% until it loses the condition.If an effect makes an item broken automatically it is reduced to 0 HP.

ITEM DAMAGE

Unfortunately, items are not indestructible. Just like a character an item can take damage and when it sustains enough damage become broken or destroyed. An item has a HP value and DR which is determined by its material. Each time an item takes HP damage, reduce it by an amount equal to the items DR.

An item only usually takes damage when it is targeted directly by an attack, although the GM may determine that some area effects also damage items.

If an item takes damage it may become broken or ultimately destroyed entirely. It becomes broken when its Hit Points are reduced to 0. If its HP are reduced to a negative value equal to half its HP (round up) it is destroyed. A broken item has the broken condition until Repaired above 0 HP. Anything that automatically makes an item broken immediately reduces its Hit Points to 0. if the item had more Hit Points than that when the effect occurred. A destroyed item can’t be Repaired.

An item’s DR and Hit Points usually depend on the material the item is made of. Some examples of item DR and Hit Points are given below.

You may sometimes need to resize an existing item. Your GM will determine the exact parameters of what can and cannot be resized. Resizing would use the crafting skill to determine results.

ITEM QUALITY

The majority of purchased equipment is of a relatively standard level of quality. A sword purchased from a smith in town, although made slightly differently to the smith for the city across the river will effectively provide the same bonuses and penalties.

Sometimes, items are made to a greater or lesser standard. These items are collectively known as superior items.

SUPERIOR ITEMS

Items that are made to a greater standard are referred to as superior items. Superior items provide a bonus to any checks that the item can be used for (medicine for healer’s tools, disable device for thieves’ tools etc).

Armour, shields and weapons have their own rules for superior items, and this is explained in their respective sections later in the chapter.

Superior Items are split into three different categories; Expert, Master and Legendary.

EXPERT QUALITY

An expert quality item adds a +1-item bonus to any relevant checks. An expert quality item has its level increased by +2.

MASTER QUALITY

A master quality item adds a +2-item bonus to any relevant checks. A master quality item has its level increased by +8.

LEGENDARY QUALITY

A legendary quality item adds a +3-item bonus to any relevant checks. A legendary quality item has its level increased by +14.

To determine the new cost of a quality item, add the base value of the item to the minimum cost of an item of the new level.

INFERIOR ITEMS

Items can also be inferior, and an inferior item applies a quality item penalty to any checks that the item can be used for.

An inferior quality item applies a -1-item penalty to any relevant checks. The price of an inferior quality item is halved and the DC to craft is Easy (+2).

SPECIAL MATERIALS

An item will often be constructed of a special material. Many of these materials require items to be superior when crafted.

Weapons constructed of a special material automatically overcome that type of resistance.

ADAMANTINE

RARE

Highly coveted and challenging to extract, adamantine possesses a dark, iron-like appearance with exceptional hardness and durability. It is renowned for its ability to withstand powerful blows and maintain a sharp edge, making it an ideal material for crafting armour and weapons. Its scarcity and remarkable properties make it a prized resource among adventurers and blacksmiths alike, sought after for its ability to provide superior protection and formidable weaponry on the battlefield.

An adamantine item has its level increased by +5.

All items constructed from adamantine have double the amount of HP and increase base DR by 1.

Adamantine weapons inflict an additional die of base damage.

COLD IRON

UNCOMMON

Cold iron, mined from the depths of the earth and forged at lower temperatures, retains its unique properties that are effective against certain creatures such as fey. By bypassing their innate physical resistance, cold iron weapons and items are specifically crafted to counter the defences of such creatures, making them a valuable asset in encounters where these supernatural beings are encountered. The meticulous process of mining and forging cold iron ensures its potency in combating magical and otherworldly adversaries.

A cold iron item has its level increased by +2.

Cold iron items are slightly more durable and have 10% more HP than a normal metal item (usually made of Steel).

DENSEWOOD

UNCOMMON

Densewood, a peculiar and remarkably resilient material, is typically harvested from the ancient trees found on the outskirts of magical forests. Possessing innate magical properties, this extraordinary wood is highly sought after by artisans and craftsmen for its ability to enhance the enchantment and durability of magical items. Its unique origin and mystical nature make it a prized resource in the crafting of enchanted weapons, wands, and other enchanted artifacts.

A Densewood item has its level increased by +2.

Densewood items are more durable than normal wooden items and possess double the amount of HP. Additionally, Densewood shields have 1 greater DR and Densewood weapons gain the Keen Trait.

DRAGONHIDE

RARE

Dragonhide, a prized material coveted by armour smiths, offers exceptional quality and resilience in the creation of armour and shields. Derived from the hides of dragons, this unique material can only be utilized in the crafting of medium or heavy armour as well as metal shields. With its innate durability and the mystical essence infused within, dragonhide armaments provide formidable protection to those who bear them, reflecting the strength and mystique of the mighty dragons themselves.

A dragonhide item has its level increased by +3.

Dragonhide armour and shields have 50% more HP than a normal item. A dragonhide shield provides an additional +2 DB when used against the energy type of the dragon the scales were harvested from.

Dragonhide armour grants the wearer resistance against the same energy type.

Armour and shields made of dragonhide are generally lighter and weigh approximately 20% less. All armour penalties are also reduced by 1.

EAOG

RARE

Eaog, an intriguing material resembling pale green crystal, possesses unique properties that set it apart. Despite its crystalline appearance, Eaog can be shaped and forged like iron. Surprisingly, Eaog weighs only half as much as iron but possesses equal strength. Its true value lies in its inherent resistance to magic. This exceptional resistance makes Eaog highly sought after by those who seek protection from the mystical forces that permeate the world.

An Eaog item has its level increased by +6.

All items constructed from Eaog have double the amount of HP and increase base DR by 2.

Eaog armour weighs half as much as other armour, and all penalties are reduced by 2 (min 0). All Spell Casting DCs are increased by 2 and the wearer also gains a +2-item bonus to all saving throws against magic.

Eaog weapons inflict an additional die of base damage and gain the Keen trait.

MITHRIL

RARE

Mithril, a remarkably rare and precious metal, possesses a silvery lustre that glimmers with an enchanting radiance. Despite its lightweight nature, mithril retains the same exceptional hardness as steel. Its unique combination of lightness and strength makes it highly coveted by artisans and adventurers alike. Mithril armour and weapons offer superior mobility and agility without compromising on durability, allowing the wearer to move swiftly and gracefully while enjoying the protection of this extraordinary metal.

A mithril item has its level increased by +4.

Mithril items weigh half as much as a normal item and have 50% additional HP. Mithril armour reduces all penalties by 2 and increases max Dexterity by the same.

Mithril weapons are classed as silver for overcoming resistance and gain the Keen trait.

SILVER

UNCOMMON

Silver weapons are imbued with a supernatural potency that makes them particularly effective against certain creatures, such as infernus and werewolves. The silver's purity and mystical properties make it a potent weapon against supernatural foes, bypassing their resistances or defences. However, it is worth noting that silver, being a softer metal than steel, may be less durable and require more frequent maintenance and care to ensure its effectiveness in battle.

A silver item has its level increased by +1.

Silver items weigh half as much as a normal item but are less durable and have half the HP. Armour made from silver is purely ceremonial and reduces its DR by 2 (minimum of 0).

Silver weapons overcome the appropriate resistance but reduce their damage die size by 1 step.

Theurgists possess the knowledge and skill to create a unique form of silver known as alchemical silver. This specialized silver is crafted with meticulous care and precision, resulting in a material that retains all the advantageous properties of regular silver, such as its effectiveness against supernatural creatures, without the inherent drawbacks or limitations. While the production of alchemical silver requires greater investment and expertise, its enhanced quality ensures that it serves as an exceptional weapon against those vulnerable to silver.

This item has its level increased by +2 and has all the benefits of silver with none of its penalties.

The level of an item constructed with a special material is modified based upon its final price (round down).

MAGICAL BONUSES

It is also possible to enhance an item using magic. To do this an item can be magically infused to increase its bonus. Enhancing mundane items with magic is explored in chapter 11.

ITEM FORMULAS

A formula is a set of instructions on how to make a specific item with the Craft action. You must be able to read the language that the formula is written in, and some crafting guilds will write their formulas in obscure languages and codes to prevent rivals from copying them.

PURCHASING FORMULAS

You can purchase a formula for an item if it is available to buy for cost of approximately 10% of the items purchase price. It usually takes an hour to copy a formula into your book after purchase.

REVERSE ENGINEERING

If you have an item, you can try to reverse-engineer its formula. This uses the Craft activity and takes the same amount of time as creating the item from a formula would. You must first disassemble the item. After the base downtime, you attempt a Crafting check against the same DC it would take to Craft the item with the same results for cost and time.

It is also possible to create formula from scratch using the Research action. To do this you must have the Inventive Crafter general feat.

ARMOUR & SHIELDS

Armour makes you more difficult to hurt and, in some cases, harder to hit. It may also slow you down. Armour also has a negative modifier on spellcasting which prevents many casters from wearing it.

DEFENCE

You can shield yourself from harm by wearing armour and other protections, but your ability to absorb damage and avoid blows is represented by your Defence Bonus (or DB for short) and Damage Reduction (DR for short).

DEFENSIVE BONUS

Defensive Bonus (or DB, for short) is a special difficulty which determines how hard it is for your character to be struck with an attack during combat. As with other DC’s, the attacker must equal or exceed your DB to score a successful hit on you.

Defensive Bonus is calculated using the following formula:

Defensive Bonus = 10 + BDB + Dex + other bonuses + penalties.

You can temporarily improve your DB with several defensive actions; while spells, conditions, and other effects can modify it in other ways, so your DB will probably change quite often during the game.

DONNING & REMOVING ARMOUR

Getting in and out of armour is time consuming—so make sure you’re wearing it when you need it! Donning light armour takes 5 rounds, medium armour takes 4 minutes, and heavy armour takes 10 minutes; these times are doubled when donning a full suit of armour.

ARMOUR STATISTICS

The armour table provides the statistics for suits of armour that can be purchased and worn, organized by category. The columns in the table provide the following statistics.

LEVEL/PRICE

The armour level determines how difficult the armour is to craft and repair. The price speaks for itself.

ACP

Any armour heavier than leather, as well as any shield, hurts a character’s ability to use Dexterity- and Strength-based skills. An armour check penalty applies to all Dexterity- and Strength-based skill checks.

Be aware that if you wear armour that you not proficient in, all penalties are doubled.

MAX DEX

This number is the maximum Dexterity bonus to DB that this type of armour allows. Dexterity bonuses in excess of this number are reduced to this number for the purposes of determining the wearer’s DB. Heavier armours limit mobility, reducing the wearer’s ability to dodge blows. This restriction doesn’t affect any other Dexterity-related abilities.

SUITS OF ARMOURTo save some time at the bottom of the armour table is a section called suits of armour. Each of these suits includes greaves and bracers of an appropriate material and may also include a helmet (if stated). Use of full suits can speed up play and make the creation of armour easier for PC and GM alike. SUITS OF ARMOURTo save some time at the bottom of the armour table is a section called suits of armour. Each of these suits includes greaves and bracers of an appropriate material and may also include a helmet (if stated). Use of full suits can speed up play and make the creation of armour easier for PC and GM alike.

DR

This is the armours base value for resisting damage (Damage Reduction). This value is halved (round down) when resisting certain energy attacks (or bypassed entirely for some). As you become more experienced the DR provided by your armour also increases, this is represented by you gaining a DR multiplier as your BDB increases.

HP

This column lists the armour’s Hit Points (HP). This measures how much damage the armour can take before it’s destroyed or gains the broken condition.

SPEED

This value reduces your speed whilst the armour is worn.

WEIGHT

How much the armour weighs in lbs.

TRAITS

Some critical hits will vary depending upon the material of the armour that you are wearing.

ARMOUR FITTINGS

All armour detailed below is considered to be a shirt or breastplate with its base statistics, sometimes referred to as partial armour. To increase your armours coverage and overall bonus (and often penalties) you must add bracers, greaves and helmets. When you add armour fittings, all bonuses and penalties are applied directly to the base armour.

BRACERS

Bracers may be added to armour to offer protection to the arms and hands.

GREAVES

Greaves may be added to armour to offer protection to the legs and feet.

HELMET

A helmet must be added to armour separately and can be worn alone. Helmets are considered to provide protection for the head, face and neck.

CRITICAL AMENDMENT

Whenever a critical injury result is modified in your favour due to you wearing armour, your armour takes an amount of damage equal to the base damage of the attack.

NATURAL DR VS CRITICALS

Natural armour does not have a separate amount of HP like manufactured armour and therefore cannot take damage in the same way. If you reduce the effects of a critical due to having natural armour, you instead take half the additional HP damage (which of course bypasses DR)

SUPERIOR ARMOUR

Instead of adding bonuses, superior armour reduces the ACP of the armour and adds bonuses to Max Dex and HP. The initial level of the armour is also modified using the rules for superior items as found earlier in the chapter.

When crafting superior armour, it is possible to add one or more traits, which affects its level and cost. Expert armour may have one additional trait when crafted, master two and legendary three.

SUPERIOR ARMOUR TRAITS

Each superior armour trait is described below with its game mechanics. Each armour trait increases the total level of the armour (before any magical modifiers) by 1.

Cushioned: This trait adds extra padding to the armour increasing protection against bludgeoning attacks. The armour grants + 1 DR against bludgeoning damage.

Flame Resistant: The armour has been treated with flame resistant materials. The armour grants +1 DR against fire attacks.

Heavy: The item has been made using strengthening techniques which make it heavier and more durable. ACP penalties are increased by 1 and the Max Dex is reduced by 1. The DR of the armour is increased by 1 and its weight of the armour is also increased by 25%.

Insulated: The armour has been crafted with a layer of non-conductive fabric. The armour grants +1 DR against electricity attacks.

Lightweight: The item has been created to make it slightly lighter and easier to manoeuvre in. ACP is reduced by 1, Max Dex increased by 1 and Speed penalties reduced by 5. Furthermore, the weight of the armour is reduced by 25%.

Reinforced: This trait adds ribs or metal studs to the armour increasing its resistance against edged weapons. The armour grants +1 DR against slashing damage. The weight of the armour is also increased by 25%.

Warm: The armour is lined with furs and wools. The armour grants +1 DR against cold attacks.

SLEEPING IN ARMOUR

If you choose to sleep in your armour, you run the risk of gaining the fatigued condition. After a nights rest you must make a DC 20 Fortitude Saving throw.

Success You have no fatigue

Failure You gain fatigue 1

Fumble You gain fatigue 2

This check has the following modifiers:

Light Armour +5, Heavy Armour -5, Rigid -1, Metal -2

ARMOUR DESCRIPTIONS

Each type of armour is described in more detail below.

FURS/PELTS

Heavy winter clothing is a practical ensemble comprised of thick layers of furs, animal pelts, and wool, designed to shield individuals from the harsh cold of winter. While it may lack the sophistication of more specialized armours, it serves as an affordable option favoured by peasants, mountain dwellers, and tribal warriors. The multiple layers provide decent insulation against the cold, granting a substantial +2 item bonus to resist the chilling effects of wintry environments. However, its bulkiness and lack of water resistance make it a hindrance when soaked, resulting in a significant -8 check penalty.

PADDED

Padded armour, consisting of layers of padding or quilted fabric, provides a modicum of protection and insulation in colder climates. While it offers some resistance against the elements, it lacks the durability and sturdiness necessary to effectively shield against direct attacks. Its main purpose lies in providing comfort and a degree of warmth, rather than serving as a formidable defence against foes.

LEATHER

Leather armour, crafted from animal hides and tanned leather, strikes a balance between lightness and flexibility, offering moderate protection against minor attacks. Its pliable nature allows for ease of movement, making it a preferred choice for those seeking mobility and agility in combat. While it may not withstand heavy blows or powerful strikes, it provides a certain level of defence against lighter assaults.

REINFORCED LEATHER

Reinforced leather armour, also known as ringmail or studded leather, is an enhanced version of traditional leather armour that incorporates metal studs, rings, and other protective elements. The addition of these metal pieces provides increased defence against slashing and piercing attacks, reinforcing the leather's natural resilience. The studs and rings are strategically placed to offer improved coverage without sacrificing mobility, making studded leather armour a popular choice for those seeking a balance between protection and agility.

HIDE

Hide armour is crafted from the durable and thick hides of resilient creatures. It is constructed by stitching together multiple layers of coarse leather or attaching exterior pieces of leather filled with padding or fur. The resulting armour provides decent protection against attacks, with its layered construction and reinforced padding offering moderate defence. As the armour sustains damage, it can be repaired by restitching gashes or adding fresh pieces of hide, resulting in a distinctive patchwork appearance for well-worn suits. Hide armour is a practical and rugged choice for those seeking reliable protection in harsh environments.

HARDENED LEATHER

Hardened leather armour is crafted from thick and durable leather that has been treated through a process of boiling and shaping. The leather is hardened and moulded into rigid plates, which are then carefully assembled to create the armour. This type of armour provides excellent protection against various forms of attacks, including slashing and piercing strikes. However, the rigid nature of the armour limits mobility and flexibility, making it somewhat restrictive in movement. Despite its limitations in agility, hardened leather armour remains a popular choice for those seeking reliable and robust protection in combat.

CHAINMAIL

Chainmail is a type of armour made from interlocking metal rings, forming a flexible mesh-like structure. The rings are carefully linked together to create a fabric-like material that can be draped over the body. Chainmail is known for its ability to absorb impacts and protect against cutting and slashing attacks. The flexibility of the linked rings allows for relatively unrestricted movement compared to heavier armour types. However, chainmail can still be quite heavy and may restrict agility to some extent. It is a popular choice among warriors and knights seeking a balance between protection and manoeuvrability on the battlefield.

SCALEMAIL

Scale mail is a type of armour composed of numerous small metal scales that overlap and are attached to a backing material. The scales are typically made of metal, such as steel or bronze, and are arranged in rows to provide coverage across the body. The scales are connected by rings or other fasteners, allowing for some flexibility and movement. Scale mail offers a balance between protection and mobility, as the individual scales can deflect and absorb blows while still allowing the wearer to manoeuvre relatively freely. However, scale mail does not provide the same level of coverage as heavier armours like splint mail or plate armour.

LAMELLAR

Lamellar armour is a form of protective gear that consists of small plates, typically made of materials such as iron, steel, lacquered leather, horn, or even stone. These plates are arranged in parallel rows and connected together using cords or laces. The plates overlap and interlock, forming a flexible and durable surface that provides effective protection against slashing and piercing attacks. Lamellar armour offers good mobility and flexibility to the wearer while still offering decent defensive capabilities.

BANDED MAIL

Banded mail is a type of armour composed of overlapping strips or bands of metal that are fastened onto a sturdy backing of leather or chainmail. The metal plates are larger than those found in scale mail or splint mail, providing more extensive coverage and enhanced protection. The interconnected metal bands and multiple layers of underlying armour make banded mail a formidable defence against slashing and piercing attacks. While it offers greater protection, it may be slightly heavier and restricts movement more compared to other armours.

SPLINT MAIL

Splint mail is a type of armour constructed from overlapping layers of metal strips that are affixed to a backing of leather or sturdy fabric. The splints used in this armour are larger and more durable compared to those found in scale mail, providing increased protection against attacks. However, the trade-off is reduced flexibility and manoeuvrability due to the rigid nature of the splints.

PLATEMAIL

Plate mail is a form of armour that combines large metal plates with a layer of leather or chainmail underneath. The metal plates are strategically positioned to provide extensive coverage and exceptional protection against attacks. While plate mail offers superior defence, its weight and bulkiness significantly restrict mobility, making it more suitable for heavily armoured warriors who prioritize maximum protection over agility. The durability and resilience of plate mail make it a favoured choice for knights, paladins, and other heavily armoured combatants on the battlefield.

LEATHER HELMET

A leather helmet is a headgear made from layered leather or heavy furs. It provides basic protection for the head but offers limited defensive capabilities compared to more advanced helmets. While wearing a leather helmet, the wearer may experience a slight hindrance to their perception, resulting in a -1 item penalty to perception checks.

METAL HELMET

A metal helmet, such as a bascinet or pot helm, provides comprehensive protection for the head, covering the skull, ears, and nose. It is designed to withstand direct blows and offers solid defence in combat. However, wearing a metal helmet can slightly impede the wearer's perception, resulting in a -1 item penalty to perception checks.

FULL HELMET

A full helmet, equipped with a visor for maximum protection, provides unparalleled defence against even heavier direct blows. The complete helm encompasses the entire head, leaving little exposed and ensuring superior safety in combat. However, wearing a full helmet significantly restricts the wearer's awareness and perception, resulting in a substantial -2 item penalty to perception checks.

LEATHER GREAVES

Padded leather protection for the lower legs (knee, shin, and foot).

CHAIN GREAVES

Chain greaves take the form of a long skirt made of chainmail that is further protected by steel greaves, or individual leggings of tighter-fitting chain reinforced by padding, steel knee plates, and leather straps.

METAL GREAVES

Metal protection for the knee, shin, and foot.

LEATHER BRACERS

Leather wraps for the forearms.

CHAIN BRACERS

Loose fitting chain sleeves fitted to the shoulder and ending in a pair of gauntlets..

METAL BRACERS

Metal covering for the forearm and hand. Metal bracers are treated as gauntlets for attacking purposes.

SHIELDS

A shield is a protective item typically wielded in one hand and is designed to block or deflect incoming attacks and provide additional defence. Shields can vary in size, shape, and material, ranging from small bucklers to large tower shields. They are often made of metal, wood, or a combination of both.

Except for the buckler, all shields require one hand to hold, thus preventing the hand from holding or utilizing any other items while the shield is equipped. Shields share similar statistics as armour but come with a few additional details specific to their functionality and use in combat.

SHIELD STATISTICS

The shield table provides all of the vital statistics required when using a shield. The columns in the table provide the following statistics.

LEVEL/PRICE

The shield level determines how difficult it is to craft and repair. The price speaks for itself.

DB

This is the bonus provided by the shield which is added to your DB as a Shield bonus. To gain this bonus the shield must be equipped and held in one hand. A shield bonus cannot be applied against an attack if you are unaware of it or you are flat-footed. Furthermore, if you are unable to act at the beginning of your turn, you cannot apply your Shield bonus to DB.

Be aware that multiple Shield bonuses do not stack.

ACP

Like armour, a shield may apply an armour check penalty. This penalty applies to all Dexterity- and Strength-based skill checks and affects your character as long as the shield is equipped.

Be aware that if you equip a shield that you not proficient with, all penalties are doubled.

WEIGHT

How much the shield weighs in lbs.

DR

Your shields DR value is used in conjunction with the Shield Block feat. This value is increased in line with BDB in the same way as armour (see armour above).

HP

This column lists the shield’s Hit Points (HP). This measures how much damage the shield can take before it’s destroyed or gains the broken condition.

SHIELD BASH DAMAGE

When a shield is used to attack (using the Shield Bash action see Chapter 4), its damage type is always bludgeoning unless a specific rule in the shield’s description overrules this.

SHIELD DESCRIPTIONS

Each type of shield is described in more detail below.

BRAZADOKUR

This dwarven shield is a heavy shield characterized by its jagged and razor-sharp sides. It is commonly wielded by dwarven skirmishers, who utilize them in pairs to deliver devastating attacks. Some dwarven scoundrels also appreciate the impressive look and ease of use of these shields.

When wielding two dwarven war shields in melee combat using the Double Slice action, the first shield inflicts an additional +2 damage. Both shields gain the versatile slashing trait, allowing for more flexibility in combat, and the second shield is classified as agile, which means it incurs lower multiple attack penalties. However, it's important to note that a hand holding a dwarven war shield cannot be used for any other purposes while in use.

BUCKLER

A buckler is a small metal shield that is strapped to your forearm. It offers certain advantages and limitations compared to larger shields. While carrying a buckler, you can use a bow or crossbow without any penalties. Additionally, you have the option to wield a weapon with your shield arm, whether it's an off-hand weapon or assisting in wielding a two-handed weapon. However, doing so incurs a -1 penalty on attack rolls, which combines with any other penalties for fighting with your off hand or using two weapons.

If you choose to use a weapon in your off hand while wielding a buckler, you temporarily lose the buckler's Defensive Bonus (DB) bonus until your next turn, and you cannot use an action to raise your shield. Similarly, if you cast a spell with somatic components using your shield arm, you also lose the DB bonus until your next turn. It's important to note that you cannot perform a shield bash action with a buckler.

KLAR

A klar is a tribal weapon that traditionally consists of a short blade attached to the skull of a large horned lizard. However, skilled smiths have the ability to craft k-lars entirely out of metal. The traditional klar is considered a light wooden shield with armour spikes, while the metal klar is classified as a light steel shield with armour spikes.

In terms of functionality, the klar serves as both a shield and a weapon. It provides defensive capabilities like a shield, allowing the wielder to block and deflect incoming attacks. The spikes on the klar also add offensive potential, enabling the wielder to make piercing attacks against opponents.

The klar holds cultural significance as a tribal weapon, often associated with specific traditions and rituals. Its unique construction and combination of defensive and offensive attributes make it a distinctive and versatile choice for those skilled in its use.

LIGHT STEEL/WOODEN SHIELD

When you equip a light steel shield, you secure it to your forearm and hold it with your hand. The light steel shield is designed to be relatively lightweight, allowing you to carry other items in the hand that holds the shield. However, you cannot effectively wield weapons while holding the shield.

Both light wooden shields and light steel shields offer similar benefits in terms of basic protection and attack bonuses. They provide a defensive barrier that can block and deflect incoming attacks, increasing your chances of avoiding damage. The specific shape and materials of the shield may vary, but their fundamental purpose remains the same.

It's worth noting that there are differences in how light wooden shields and light steel shields interact with certain spells and effects. While a druid can make use of a light wooden shield, they are unable to utilize a light steel shield. This distinction reflects the druid's connection to nature and their preference for more organic materials.

MADU

The madu is a unique shield characterized by its round shape and the presence of two animal horns extending from opposite edges of the shield. This design not only provides protection but also serves as a distinctive offensive feature. The shield is crafted to fit over your arm like a glove, making it extremely difficult for opponents to disarm you.

When you raise the madu as part of a fight defensively action, the penalty to your attack rolls is significantly reduced to -15. This allows you to maintain a strong defensive posture while still retaining some offensive capability. Additionally, if you choose to attack with the shield using the shield bash action, the madu inflicts 1d4 piercing damage, making it a versatile weapon in close combat.

It's important to note that while wielding a madu, you cannot hold anything else in the hand that bears the shield. This ensures that you have a secure grip on the shield and are ready to defend and counterattack effectively. While traditional madus are typically crafted from leather and animal horn, it is also possible to create them entirely from metal, providing additional durability and strength.

HEAVY STEEL/WOODEN SHIELD

The weight of a heavy steel shield is significant, making it impossible to use your shield hand for any other purpose. This emphasizes the shield's role as a dedicated tool for protection.

Both heavy wooden shields and heavy steel shields offer the same fundamental benefits in terms of defence and attack. They provide solid protection against incoming attacks and can be used to enhance your combat capabilities. However, there are differences in how they interact with certain spells and effects. Specifically, a heavy wooden shield can be utilized by druids, while a heavy steel shield is not compatible with their abilities.

Regardless of the material used, a heavy shield is a reliable option for those seeking robust defence on the battlefield. Its weight and sturdiness make it suitable for warriors who prioritize durability and security in combat situations.

PARRYING SCABBARD

A parrying scabbard is a specialized sheath designed for defensive purposes. When using a parrying scabbard, you can draw it and the weapon it holds with a 1 AP (Interact) action, allowing you to wield the weapon in one hand and hold the scabbard in the other.

Similar to a weapon with the parry trait, a parrying scabbard can be utilized for defence. The parrying scabbard provides a +1-shield bonus to your DB whilst wielded. It's worth noting that parrying scabbards are specifically designed to work with swords that can be wielded in one hand.

TOWER SHIELD

A tower shield is a massive shield designed to provide extensive coverage, offering protection to a large portion of the wielder's body. These shields are typically constructed using a combination of wood and metal reinforcement to ensure durability and strength. One notable feature of the tower shield is its ability to grant the wielder an enhanced defensive bonus when taking cover. By utilizing the shield to "Take Cover," you can position yourself in a way that maximizes the shield's protective capabilities. This action grants you a Standard Cover bonus, in addition to the normal bonus provided by simply raising the shield.

When crafting a superior shield, it is possible to add one or more traits, which affects its level and cost. An expert shield may have one additional trait when crafted, a master shield two and a legendary shield three.

SUPERIOR SHIELD TRAITS

Each superior shield trait is described below with its game mechanics. Each shield trait increases the total level of the shield (before any magical modifiers) by 1.

Balanced: The shield is crafted with a fine balance which reduces its check penalty by 1 (minimum of 0). This trait may be applied multiple times.

Boss: A circular piece of metal is attached to the centre of the shield allowing it to become more powerful when using the shield bash action. The attack dice is increased by one step.

Lightweight: The weight of the item is reduced by 1 lb for a buckler or light shield, 2 lbs for a heavy shield or 5 lbs for a tower shield. This trait may be applied multiple times.

Spikes: The shield is constructed with metal spikes protruding from it. The shield gains the versatile (piercing) weapon trait when used to make the shield bash action.

WEAPONS

The average fantasy campaign setting would be a pretty difficult place without a weapon or two. Most characters and creatures have access to weapons of varying sizes and shapes. Some use swords, others bows and others powerful axes which may be used to cleave your foes in twain.

There are a number of rules mechanics that are required when using weapons in the game. The weapons table gives information on all of the common weapons available.

This is not an exhaustive list, and there are many more weapons available.

Beyond the name of the weapon, the table also has the following information:

PRICE

This is the common price of the weapon if purchased from an established weapon smith. This price may fluctuate depending upon availability.

LEVEL

This is the items level for craft, identification and repairing purposes.

DAMAGE

This is the dice the base damage which is inflicted by the weapon. Damage is explored in more detail in Chapter 8. The letter after the damage die is the damage type, Bludgeoning (B), Piercing (P), Subdual (N) or Slashing (S).

SIZE

This is the size of the weapon, which determines how many hands a creature must use when fighting with the weapon.

A creature can use any weapon one handed that is their size or smaller. Weapons that are one size category larger can be used one handed with a -6 penalty, or two-handed (if such a weapon is used two-handed, your melee damage bonus is multiplied by 1.5). Weapons that are two sizes or more larger cannot be wielded by your character.

Weapons can be resized for smaller and larger characters. Resizing a weapon will also affect its cost and weight as discussed earlier in the chapter.

FUMBLE DC (FDC)

When you roll a natural 1 on an attack check with a weapon, you have a chance of suffering an attack fumble. This value is used when determining if you fumble or not. Attack fumbles are explained in detail in Chapter 7. If you are not proficient with a weapon, you must check for a fumble on an UM 2 and not a 1.

WEIGHT

This entry gives the weapon’s weight. A weapon’s weight is increased or decreased if it’s sized for creatures that aren’t Medium size (GM discretion).

GROUP

A weapon or unarmed attack’s group classifies it with similar weapons which is often used with feats and abilities.

WEAPON GROUPS

The available weapon groups are:

Axe: Battle Axe, Greataxe, Handaxe, Zokarrin

Brawling: All Unarmed Attacks, Brass Knuckles, Gauntlet, Spiked Gauntlet, Cestus

Club: Club, Light Mace, Heavy Mace, Staff, Footman’s Mace, Greatclub, Morning Star, Sap

Knife: Dagger, Sickle, Elendaris

Spear: Long Spear, Spear, Lance, Trident

Polearm: Bardiche, Glaive, Halberd, Ranseur, Scythe

Sword: Bastard Sword, Broadsword, Falchion, Greatsword, Khopesh, Rapier, Scimitar, Short Sword, Sword Cane, Double-Blade, Katana, Sil’maril, Tel’dorin

Flail: Flail, Footman’s Flail, Spiked Chain, Whip

Hammer: Light Hammer, Mattock, Warhammer, Anar Dhagor

Pick: Greatpick, Light Pick, Pick

Dart: Blowgun, Dart, Javelin, Shuriken

Bow: Hand Crossbow, Heavy Crossbow, Light Crossbow, Composite Longbow, Composite Shortbow, Longbow, Shortbow, Repeater

Sling: Sling, Bola, Riath-Elenya

TRAITS

Any other information pertaining to the weapon is found in this entry.

2-Handed: The weapon requires two hands when making attacks regardless of its size.

Agile: The multiple attack penalty you take with this weapon on the second attack on your turn is –4 instead of –5, and –8 instead of –10 on the third and subsequent attacks in the turn.

Armour Rending (AR): The weapon’s attacks ignore the listed Armour DR. When a weapon and its ammunition both have this quality, their AR values are combined.

The AR of a quality weapon increases for each quality step (expert, master, legendary) it has. Expert is x2, Master is x3 and Legendary x4.

It is important to note that this trait also effects natural armour DR and not just manufactured.

Clumsy: This weapon is unwieldy and prone to mishap. The weapon follows the normal rules for weapon fumbles if an UM 1 is rolled on an attack check. If an UM 2 is rolled, this may also be a fumble check with the DC being half of the listed value.

Be aware that if you attack with a clumsy weapon that you are not trained to use, you fumble on an UM 1 or 2. If an UM 3 is rolled, this may also be a fumble check with the DC being half of the listed value.

Concealable: This weapon is designed to be inconspicuous or easily concealed. You gain a +2-circumstance bonus to Conceal an Object (Stealth) checks if a weapon has this trait.

Deadly: The increment between the severity of a critical is reduced by 1 when attacking with this weapon.

AV with Deadly

Critical Severity

5-13

Minor

14-22

Serious

23+

Deadly

Disarm: You can use this weapon to Disarm even if you don’t have a free hand. This uses the weapon’s reach (if different from your own). If you fumble a check to Disarm using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a fumble. Even on a critical, taking the item necessitates a free hand.

Double: A double weapon may be used to double slice and always treats the second attack as agile.

Exotic: An exotic weapon has a trait (often racial) which makes it unique in some way. Exotic weapons require special training through a feat. If you use an exotic weapon without the correct training your AB suffers a -4 penalty and it gains the Clumsy trait.

If your race matches that of the weapon’s racial trait, it is considered a martial weapon.

Finesse: You can use your Dexterity instead of Strength when making attack rolls using this melee weapon. You still use your Strength modifier when calculating damage.

Free Hand: This weapon is usually integrated into your armour, thus freeing up your hand for other tasks. Its unique design prevents disarming attempts, allowing you to wield additional items and perform various actions. However, if the hand is occupied or in use, attacking with the free-hand weapon is not possible. Yet, when the hand is unoccupied and idle, you can utilize abilities that require a free hand or even those that demand wielding a weapon in that hand.

Hand & a Half: The weapon may also be use two-handed. This increases weapons damage as if it were a size larger (see above).

Keen: When determining the result of a Critical Injury from this weapon, increase the weapon’s AV by 1 (after all other modifiers). This can both enable a critical and increase its severity.

Load: This entry indicates how many AP (Interact) it takes to reload the weapon. This may be carried over rounds if necessary.

Mighty: The mighty trait includes a value. On a critical hit, the weapon’s base damage increases by this amount.

Parry: This weapon may be employed for blocking incoming attacks, providing a measure of protection against adversaries. While wielding this weapon, you can use it in your off-hand, gaining a +1-shield bonus to DB.

Penetrating: This weapon treats all armour as none when used to make attacks within its first range increment.

It is important to note that this trait also effects natural armour DR and not just manufactured.

Powerful: The weapon gains a bonus to AB when fired at a target within 20 feet.

Propulsive: You add half your Strength damage modifier (if positive) to damage rolls with a propulsive ranged weapon. If you have a negative Strength damage modifier, you add your full-Strength modifier instead.

Quick Load: You can reload this weapon as a free action once per round. After your first load, it costs one action to reload the weapon.

Range: Indicates the first range increment for a ranged weapon.

Reach: Weapons with this trait increase the reach at which you can make melee attacks (usually 5 to 10 feet). Such attacks are subject to a -2 penalty to AB.

Serrated: This weapon has nasty jagged edges and causes bleed damage to be more severe. Any bleed results from criticals (or other sources when using the weapon) are increased by 1.

Shove: You can use this weapon to Shove even if you don’t have a free hand. This uses the weapon’s reach (if different from your own) and uses your attack bonus with the weapon instead of your unarmed attack bonus. If you fumble a check to Shove using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a fumble.

Silent: The weapon makes no noise when attacking increasing the DC of Sniping (Stealth) checks by 2.

Spin: If you fire this weapon as your next action after loading it, you inflict the weapons base damage. You can use a special spin action to increase base damage. If you Spin for 1 AP increase the base damage by 1, 2 AP increases the base damage by 2.

Spread: If loaded with pellets instead of a single bullet, this weapon attacks all targets in a cone equal to half its normal range.

Sweep: This weapon makes wide sweeping or spinning attacks, making it easier to attack multiple enemies. When you attack with this weapon, you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to your attack roll if you already attempted to attack a different target this turn using this weapon.

Thrown: You can throw this weapon as a ranged attack. A range is also displayed which indicates the weapons first range increment.

Trip: You can use this weapon to Trip even if you don’t have a free hand. This uses the weapon’s reach (if different from your own) and uses attack bonus with the weapon instead of your unarmed attack bonus. If you fumble a check to Trip using the weapon, you can drop the weapon to take the effects of a failure instead of a fumble.

Unsteady: This weapon is difficult to aim without taking measures to stabilize it. Firing this weapon has a –2 circumstance penalty unless the weapon is rested upon a solid surface before firing.

Versatile: This weapon can be used to deal a different type of damage to the target when attacking. You must choose the damage type before you make the attack.

Volley: This ranged weapon is less effective at close distances. Your attacks against targets that are within 20 feet take a –2 circumstance penalty.

WEAPON DESCRIPTIONS

Below you will find a brief description of each weapon.

ANAR DHAGOR

This gnomish hooked hammer is a remarkable double weapon, showcasing the ingenuity of its design. Its haft is equipped with a hammer head on one end and a long, curved pick on the other, making it a versatile tool for various tasks. Whether delivering powerful blunt strikes or precise piercing attacks, this weapon offers the wielder a range of options in combat.

BARDICHE

Sometimes known as a poleaxe, this weapon features a lengthy shaft ranging from 5 to 7 feet in length. Its distinguishing characteristic is a long-bladed axe-head positioned at the top. With its sharp edge, the bardiche delivers devastating chopping strikes, while its pointed head allows for effective thrusting attacks, making it a versatile weapon on the battlefield.

BASTARD SWORD

A bastard sword is a versatile weapon that combines the characteristics of a broadsword and a greatsword. It typically possesses a straight, double-edged blade, measuring around 36 to 48 inches in length. The hilt is designed to accommodate either one or two hands, providing the wielder with flexibility in combat. The bastard sword strikes a balance between speed and power, allowing for precise cuts, thrusts, and parries in the hands of a skilled warrior.

BATTLE AXE

A battleaxe is a fearsome weapon characterized by a sturdy haft and a large, heavy blade. It is designed for close-quarters combat, featuring a single-edged, sharpened blade with a pronounced curve. The haft provides leverage for powerful swings and strikes, while the weight of the axe head delivers devastating impact. The weapon can be used one or two-handed.

BLOWGUN

A blowgun is a compact and lightweight weapon that utilizes a hollow tube for propelling projectiles with breath force. Typically made of bamboo or metal, it is designed for stealthy and precise attacks. The blowgun fires small, lightweight darts or pellets with remarkable accuracy over short to moderate distances. It is a silent weapon, allowing for covert strikes and ambush tactics.

BOLA

This throwing weapon consisting of weights connected by cords or ropes. When hurled through the air, the cords entangle the target, immobilizing or tripping them. Bolas are commonly used for capturing or restraining prey or adversaries from a distance, relying on the entangling effect of the interconnected weights to impede their movement. The simplicity and effectiveness of the bola make it a valuable tool for hunters and individuals seeking to incapacitate their targets without causing significant harm.

BRASS KNUCKLES

These weapons fit snugly around the knuckles and allow you to deal lethal damage with an unarmed strike.

BROADSWORD

This classic weapon is renowned for its wide, straight blade and versatility in combat. It features a double-edged blade with a sharp point, typically measuring around 30 to 40 inches in length. The broadsword excels in close-quarters combat, capable of delivering devastating cuts and thrusts. Its sturdy construction and balanced design make it a popular choice among knights and warriors, providing both offensive and defensive capabilities on the battlefield.

CESTUS

A cestus is a type of hand-to-hand combat weapon consisting of a padded glove or strap equipped with metal spikes or studs. It is designed to enhance the striking power of punches and close-quarters attacks. It is a formidable weapon for hand-to-hand combat, allowing fighters to inflict more damage and potentially incapacitate opponents swiftly. The cestus is favoured by those who seek to combine the agility and skill of unarmed combat with the advantages of enhanced offensive capabilities.

CLUB

A club is a simple melee weapon characterized by its straightforward design and effectiveness. Typically made of a sturdy, dense material such as wood or metal, a club consists of a solid, cylindrical shaft with a blunt striking surface.

COMPOSITE LONGBOW

This bow is a powerful and efficient ranged weapon designed for accuracy and long-range combat. It is constructed from multiple materials, typically layers of different types of wood or other flexible materials, bonded together. The composite construction allows the longbow to store and release more energy when drawn, resulting in increased projectile velocity and greater impact force. The longbow is typically taller than the archer, measuring around 5 to 6 feet in length, with a slightly curved shape. It requires considerable strength to draw and wield effectively. This weapon is known for its superior range and penetrating power, making it a favoured weapon among skilled archers and hunters.

Be aware that this weapon cannot be used whilst mounted.

COMPOSITE SHORTBOW

This bow is a compact and versatile ranged weapon that offers a balance between power and mobility. It is crafted using a combination of materials, such as layers of different types of wood or reinforced with bone or horn, to enhance its performance. The composite construction allows the shortbow to deliver greater force and accuracy compared to a traditional shortbow. It is shorter in length, making it easier to manoeuvre in close-quarters or tight spaces. The composite shortbow is known for its speed and agility, making it a preferred choice for archers who require quick and precise shots.

DAGGER

This versatile weapon can be held in one hand and is primarily used for close combat. Its small size allows for quick and precise stabbing motions against opponents. Additionally, a dagger can also be thrown at a target as a ranged weapon.

DART

This thrown weapon is larger than an arrow but shorter than a javelin. It typically has a short shaft of wood ending in a metal tip and is sometimes stabilized by feathers or fur.

DOUBLE-BLADE

A double blade features twin blades extending from opposite sides of a central, short haft. By wielding the double blade, the user can seamlessly transition between offensive manoeuvres, utilizing both blades in a synchronized and deadly manner. The weapon's balanced construction and versatile grip provide the wielder with enhanced control and the ability to strike from different angles.

ELENDARIS

This unique weapon resembles a large, single-edged throwing knife. It features a distinct crescent-shaped blade with a sharp point and often has a handle or hilt designed for a secure grip. It can be thrown with precision to strike distant foes, used for melee attacks at close range, or even employed in skilled combat techniques that utilize its unique shape.

FALCHION

A falchion is a single-edged, slightly curved sword with a heavy and wide blade, designed for powerful slashing attacks. The weight and design of the blade allow for powerful and forceful swings, making it highly effective for delivering devastating chops and cleaving through targets.

FLAIL

A flail is a medieval weapon composed of a spiked metal ball connected to a handle by a chain or flexible link, allowing for swinging and striking with powerful, unpredictable movements.

FOOTMAN’S FLAIL

A footman’s flail is an imposing medieval weapon consisting of a spiked metal ball attached to a handle by a sturdy chain or thick, rigid links, enabling the wielder to deliver devastating and crushing blows with its formidable weight and reach.

FOOTMAN’S MACE

This mace is a formidable weapon that features a long handle and a large, heavy metal head designed to deliver devastating impact through powerful swings, making it capable of crushing armour and bones with tremendous force.

GAUNTLET

This metal glove lets you deal lethal damage rather than nonlethal damage with unarmed strikes. A strike with a gauntlet is otherwise considered an unarmed attack.

GLAIVE

A glaive is a polearm weapon with a long, single-edged blade attached to a long shaft, typically featuring a curved or pointed tip, allowing for sweeping strikes and thrusting attacks from a distance, making it ideal for both slashing and piercing manoeuvres in combat.

GREATAXE

A single-edged or double-edged axe with a heavy, wide blade, known for its heavy and wide design that enables it to deliver devastating chops and cleaving strikes in combat.

GREATCLUB

A greatclub is a massive, blunt weapon resembling an oversized wooden club, typically made from a solid piece of sturdy wood, used for delivering powerful and bone-crushing strikes in close combat. Its sheer size and weight make it a formidable choice for warriors seeking raw impact in battle.

GREATPICK

This weapon features a long handle and a large, pointed metal head with a sturdy pick-like tip, designed to puncture armour and deliver devastating thrusting attacks.

GREATSWORD

A towering two-handed sword, nearly matching the height of its wielder, possesses a lower blade that is intentionally blunted to provide a secure grip and enhanced leverage during intense close-quarter combat encounters. This immense weapon showcases its intimidating size and grants its user the advantage of additional force and control in the midst of battle.

HALBERD

A polearm featuring a 5-foot shaft crowned by a head that incorporates an axe blade for slashing strikes, a rear beak for hooking manoeuvres, and a top spike for thrusting attacks, offering versatility and formidable reach in melee engagements.

HANDAXE

Originally crafted as a tool, this weapon has evolved into a short and lightweight combat implement, featuring a pointed head. It excels at slicing through unarmoured adversaries and can also be thrown as a ranged weapon.

HAND CROSSBOW

Known among criminals and rogues as an assassin’s bow; this compact crossbow is favoured for its discreet nature. It propels small bolts, often employed for delivering poisonous payloads. While it can be fired with one hand, it necessitates the use of both hands for reloading, ensuring precision and potency in each shot.

HEAVY CROSSBOW

This crossbow boasts unparalleled shooting power, though it comes with drawbacks. While incredibly potent, it is burdensome to carry and challenging to aim and reload. It grants a significant +4 circumstance bonus when targeting foes within 20 feet, delivering devastating strikes.

HEAVY MACE

A weighty mace, typically featuring a geometrically shaped head, serves as a formidable weapon renowned for its efficacy against armoured adversaries. Its substantial mass and piercing elements make it a lethal choice, capable of delivering devastating blows and effectively bypassing defences, posing a significant threat to even the most heavily armoured foes.

JAVELIN

The thin spear is meticulously balanced for throwing with precision, making it an ideal weapon for ranged combat. However, due to its slim design, it is not intended for effective use in close-quarters melee engagements, lacking the necessary weight and structure for such encounters.

KATANA

The katana is a distinctive sword with a graceful curve and a single cutting edge, renowned for its exceptionally sharp and lethal blade. Its design emphasizes both elegance and deadliness, making it a favoured weapon among skilled swordsmen and a symbol of traditional eastern craftsmanship.

KHOPESH

This impressive heavy blade is characterized by a distinctive convex curve towards the end, reminiscent of a scimitar. With a typical length ranging from 30 to 36 inches, it excels at both slashing and hooking manoeuvres, enabling the wielder to bypass defences and trip adversaries. The elegant and lethal nature of the khopesh often inspires artisans to adorn it with intricate and ornate embellishments, adding to its overall allure.

LANCE

The lance is a specialized weapon primarily designed for jousting, a sport of mounted combat. It is not typically employed in regular melee or battlefield encounters. When used from horseback and during a charge, the lance demonstrates its full potential, utilizing specific statistics and benefits. However, it is important to note that the lance can only be effectively wielded while the user is mounted on a horse, limiting its usability in other contexts.

LIGHT CROSSBOW

Mechanical bow throwing weighted bolts. Devastating at shorter ranges and capable of penetrating even through plate. +2 AB when attacking targets within 20 feet.

LIGHT HAMMER

The throwing hammer is a compact variant of the warhammer, featuring a wooden or metal shaft culminating in a metal head. It is designed to be lighter and more agile than its larger counterpart, allowing for effective throwing. Its reduced weight enables swift and accurate projectile attacks, providing versatility in combat scenarios where ranged engagement is advantageous.

LIGHT MACE

The mace is a compact and lightweight weapon characterized by a wooden shaft and a solid metal head. Primarily used as a sidearm, it offers a versatile option for close-quarters combat. The mace's design allows for quick and efficient strikes, leveraging the concentrated weight of the metal head to deliver powerful blows against armoured opponents or unarmoured foes alike. Its compact size makes it convenient to carry, providing a reliable and effective weapon for various situations on the battlefield.

LIGHT PICK

This weapon, adapted from the pickaxe tool, has a head with a slightly curved, armour piercing spike and a hammerlike counterweight.

LONG SPEAR

This elongated spear, measuring between 6 to 9 feet in length, is designed specifically for tight formation combat. Its extended reach allows infantry units to create a defensive wall of sharp points, keeping enemies at a safe distance and preventing cavalry charges from breaking through their ranks. The weapon’s primary purpose is to impale and neutralize mounted opponents, using its length and piercing tip to effectively counter the speed and mobility of cavalry units.

LONGBOW

This bow is a traditional and iconic ranged weapon known for its simplicity and effectiveness. It is a tall and straight bow, typically made from a single piece of wood, such as yew. The longbow's design allows for a longer draw length, generating significant force when the bowstring is released. This results in impressive projectile speed and considerable range. The longbow requires considerable strength to wield effectively, as it relies on the archer's ability to draw the string fully. It is valued for its accuracy and piercing power, making it a favoured weapon of skilled archers and hunting.

MAIN-GAUCHE

The main-gauche is a slender-bladed weapon, typically accompanied by a basket hilt, known for its versatility and defensive capabilities. It is commonly wielded in the offhand as a complementary tool to a primary weapon or as a lighter alternative to a shield.

MATTOCK

Often called Bec de corbin or lucerne hammer, it is essentially a war hammer head mounted on a shaft. Heavy but powerful and versatile.

MORNING STAR

This weapon consists of a wooden or metal handle with a spiked metal head. It is characterized by a round, ball-like structure studded with sharp spikes. The spikes are designed to deliver crushing blows and puncture armour, making the morningstar particularly effective against heavily armoured opponents.

QUARTERSTAFF

A hardened wooden staff with or without metal tips, swung with one or both hands. Its main advantage is its cheapness and the ability to be disguised as a walking cane or tool - but is in fact a dangerous weapon in skilled hands.

RANSEUR

The ranseur is a polearm with a distinctive design reminiscent of a trident. It features a long shaft with a single spearhead at the tip, accompanied by two shorter, curving blades on either side. The primary spearhead allows for thrusting attacks, while the flanking blades add versatility by providing options for slashing and hooking manoeuvres.

RAPIER

The rapier is a slender and elegant sword with a narrow, sharply pointed blade. It is known for its agility and finesse, making it ideal for thrusting attacks and precise manoeuvres. The hilt of a rapier is typically designed with a protective cup-shaped guard to provide hand protection during duels and combat. Its lightweight construction and balanced design allow for swift and precise movements, making it a popular choice among duellists and skilled swordsmen.

REPEATER

This clever crossbow features an ingeniously designed catch mechanism at the top of the flight grove, just in front of the latch, which automatically loads a bolt from a magazine and resets the string each time the weapon is fired. A typical repeater magazine holds five bolts. Reloading the magazine takes a full round.

RIATH-ELENYA

This sling-staff is a unique weapon crafted specifically for the smaller stature of halflings. It consists of a long wooden staff with a sling attached at one end. The staff is designed to provide stability and leverage when using the sling, allowing halflings to wield it effectively. The sling-staff combines the versatility of a sling with the added reach and control provided by the staff. It enables halflings to deliver accurate and powerful ranged attacks, making it a favoured weapon among their adventurous kind.

SCIMITAR

The scimitar is a curved, single-edged sword with a slightly convex blade. It is characterized by its distinctive sweeping curve, which gives it a sleek and elegant appearance. The blade of a scimitar is typically sharp on the curved edge, allowing for powerful slashing attacks. The hilt of a scimitar is often adorned with intricate designs and may feature a guard to protect the hand during combat. The scimitar is known for its versatility, being effective both on horseback and in close-quarters combat.

SCYTHE

The scythe is an agricultural tool with a long, curved blade attached to a wooden handle. It is commonly associated with farming and harvesting crops, but it can also be adapted into a deadly weapon. The blade of a scythe is typically sharp and curved, resembling a large sickle. It is designed for sweeping slashing motions, making it effective for cutting through vegetation or delivering powerful strikes in combat. The long handle allows for extended reach and provides leverage when swinging the blade. The scythe's menacing appearance and association with the harvest have also made it a symbol often associated with death.

SHORT SWORD

A shortsword is a versatile one-handed weapon with a straight double-edged blade, typically measuring around 20 to 30 inches in length. It is designed for close-quarters combat and offers a balance between speed and cutting power. The blade is narrower than that of a broadsword, allowing for quick and precise strikes. The weapon is light, easy to use and carry and often used as a sidearm or secondary weapon.

SHORT BOW

A shortbow is a compact and manoeuvrable ranged weapon commonly used for hunting or warfare. It is commonly used by archers who value speed and agility in combat. Despite its smaller size, a shortbow can still deliver considerable force and accuracy over moderate distances. It is a versatile weapon that can be used for both hunting small game and engaging enemies in battle.

SHURIKEN

A shuriken is a small piece of metal with sharpened edges, designed for throwing. A shuriken can’t be used as a melee weapon.

Although they are thrown weapons, shuriken are treated as ammunition for the purposes of drawing them and crafting quality or otherwise special versions of them, and of what happens to them after they are thrown.

SIL’MARIL

This slender and agile weapon embodies the grace and speed of elven combat techniques. It features a narrow and lightweight blade, typically single-edged, designed for swift and precise strikes. The blade is shorter in length compared to traditional swords, allowing for enhanced manoeuvrability and close-quarters combat. These swords are crafted with exquisite precision, often adorned with intricate engravings or delicate filigree, reflecting the elven appreciation for artistry and beauty.

SLING

A sling is a simple projectile weapon consisting of a long strap or cord with a pouch at one end. It is used to launch projectiles, typically small stones or lead bullets, at high speeds. To use a sling, the user holds one end of the strap, places the projectile in the pouch, and swings the other end in a circular motion. With a sudden release of the strap, the projectile is flung forward with significant force and accuracy. A sling can be used to throw found rocks at a -2-attack bonus. A sling is treated as a thrown weapon for determining damage modifiers.

SPEAR

A spear is a long, polearm weapon consisting of a pointed metal blade attached to a wooden shaft. It is a versatile weapon with a range advantage, allowing for thrusting attacks at a distance.

SPIKED CHAIN

A spiked chain is a flexible weapon consisting of a long chain with metal spikes attached at regular intervals. It is typically wielded with two hands, allowing for a wide range of striking techniques. The spiked chain can be swung, wrapped around opponents, or used to disarm and trip adversaries.

SWORD CANE

A sword-cane is a discreet weapon concealed within the guise of a walking cane. The cane's handle contains a hidden blade, usually a slender and sharp rapier-like sword, that can be unsheathed for self-defence or combat. It serves both as a functional walking aid and a weapon of surprise, providing its wielder with the element of surprise and the ability to defend themselves when needed.

TEL’DORIN

Sometimes called a curve blade, this elegant and graceful weapon is favoured by elven warriors. It features a slender, curved blade that resembles the shape of a crescent moon. The blade is typically single-edged, with the convex side honed to a sharp edge. The elongated handle allows for versatile grips and swift manoeuvres. The elven curve blade combines the finesse of a sword with the slashing power of a larger weapon, making it effective in both close-quarters combat and swift, sweeping attacks. It is often crafted with intricate engravings or embellishments, reflecting the artistry and craftsmanship of the elven culture.

TRIDENT

A trident is a three-pronged spear-like weapon characterized by its long shaft and distinct triple-pointed head. Each of the prongs is typically sharp and designed for impaling or hooking targets. Like a spear, it can be wielded with one hand or thrown.

WARHAMMER

A warhammer is a formidable weapon characterized by its sturdy wooden shaft and a large, heavy metal head. The head of the hammer can be either single-sided or double-sided, designed specifically for delivering powerful bludgeoning strikes. With its weight and solid construction, the warhammer is well-suited for crushing armour, smashing through defences, and dealing devastating blows to adversaries.

WHIP

A very difficult weapon to master, developed from a tool. It can be used to either slash with its spiked tail or grapple an opponent. Becomes quite ineffective and then useless at shorter ranges. Can’t be used against adjacent creatures but has a 15-foot reach.

ZOKARRIN

This weapon is forged with exceptional craftsmanship by skilled dwarven artisans. It features a sturdy haft made of high-quality wood or metal, complemented by a sharp, bearded axe head. The axe head is typically double-bladed, with a crescent-shaped design that combines chopping power with piercing capabilities. Renowned for its durability and keen edge, the dwarven waraxe excels at cleaving through armour and delivering devastating strikes in the hands of a skilled wielder. It is a symbol of dwarven martial prowess and craftsmanship, favoured by warriors who seek a versatile and deadly weapon on the battlefield.

NATURAL ATTACKS

Any character or creature can use an unarmed attack. In the above weapon tables a number of natural attacks are provided. Most humanoids will only have access to the Unarmed Strike attack. This attack can be made with any body part (in theory) using and has the Agile and Finesse traits, inflicting subdual damage.

It is important to note that natural attacks are not weapons and abilities and effects that work with weapons do not work with natural attacks.

IMPROVISED ATTACKS

It is possible to attack with just about anything. Chair legs, iron bars, rocks or any other item that comes to hand. When attacking with an item that’s primary purpose is not a weapon, then you suffer a -4-circumstance penalty to the attack. Most improvised weapons will inflict 1d4 damage, but the GM will have the final say on this, as well as the type of damage inflicted.

AMMUNITION

Many of the above ranged weapons require ammunition to be launched from them when making an attack. Ammunition is priced below in standard quantities which are in brackets next to its title.

Any load action times are dependent upon the ammunition being stored in a convenient container (bolt case, quiver, etc).

At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield.

ARROWS

These projectiles are the ammunition for bows. The shaft of an arrow is made of wood. It is stabilized in flight by fletching at one end and bears a metal head on the other.

ARROWS, BLUNT

These arrows are used to subdue targets rather than kill them. They have rounded wooden tips that deal bludgeoning damage instead of piercing. Furthermore, an archer can choose to inflict subdual damage with the arrows by taking a -4-circumstance penalty to their attack.

ARROWS, DISTANCE

These arrows are used for long range attacks in battles. They are fitted with heavy iron heads which allow them to travel greater distance, whilst inflicting less damage. These arrows increase the range increment of the bow by ten feet but reduce damage (-1 item) and remove the deadly trait.

ARROWS, PENETRATING

These arrows are crafted with high density tips which have superior armour piercing qualities. An attack from one of these arrows gains AR 1.

BLOWGUN NEEDLES

These thin, light needles are typically made of hardwood and stabilized with fletching of down or fur. They are often hollow so they can be used to deliver poison.

BOLTS

Shorter than traditional arrows but similar in construction, bolts are the ammunition used by crossbows.

BOLT, FIRE

This intricate wooden crossbow bolt contains a hollow chamber which is filled with fire oil. On a successful strike, the bolt explodes and inflicts an additional 3 fire damage and 1 splash damage.

BOLTS, PENETRATING

These bolts are crafted with high density tips which have superior armour piercing qualities. An attack from one of these bolts gains AR 2.

SLING BULLETS

These are small metal balls, typically either iron or lead, designed to be used as ammunition in slings.
