EQUIPMENT

All characters need basic equipment to survive when accomplishing great things. Sometimes the right piece of equipment such as rope or a lantern can save the day.

Armour and weapons are a vital part of an adventurer’s kit, but they are everything that is needed. A successful adventurer has a whole host of equipment to call upon.

GOODS

This category provides a number of items which are important to an adventurer’s life. Each item is listed below with a description and the table at the beginning of the section gives you the name of the item, its price in gold pieces and its weight in pounds.

This list is far from exhaustive but should give you a good start with any equipment that you need.

ASTROLABE

An astrolabe is a complex astronomical instrument used for measuring the positions of celestial bodies and determining time, consisting of a rotating disk with marked scales and adjustable components.

AXE, WOODSMAN

A woodsman's axe is a rugged and versatile tool, featuring a sharp blade on one side for cutting through timber and a sturdy, weighted head on the other for splitting logs. It may also be used as an improvised hand axe.

BACKPACK

This leather knapsack is a portable and versatile bag worn on the back, typically with shoulder straps, designed to carry belongings and provide convenient storage during travel or daily activities. Whilst wearing the backpack, your Strength score is considered 1 higher for the purposes of carrying capacity.

BEDROLL

A typical bedroll is a compact and portable sleeping pad or mattress, often bundled with blankets or sleeping bags, used for comfort and insulation while camping or sleeping in the outdoors. It can be rolled and tied into a tight coil for storage or transport. This item grants you a +4-item bonus to resist environmental cold.

BLOCK & TACKLE

A block and tackle is a mechanical system consisting of pulleys and ropes, designed to increase the force applied to lift or move heavy objects by distributing the load across multiple lines. Block and tackle take 5 minutes to set up. Your Strength score is considered 2 higher for lifting.

BRAND

Commonly used to mark cattle and slaves. With a Coup de Grace action, this item permanently scars flesh with a specific mark.

BRASS EAR

A brass ear is a conical-shaped, horn-like device made of brass or some other metal, used as a hearing aid to amplify sounds. By holding this ear trumpet to your ear and placing the other end against a door or wall, you reduce the DC penalty for listening through a door or wall by 5.

BUOYANCY VEST

A buoyancy vest is a type of personal flotation device designed to provide buoyancy and assist in keeping a person afloat in water, commonly used for water activities and safety purposes. Wearing a buoyancy vest allows you to float in water with a lowered risk of sinking. If you end your turn in water while wearing a buoyancy vest and haven't succeeded at a Swim (Athletics) action that turn, attempt a DC 5 flat check. On a success, you do not sink, though you can still get moved by the current, as determined by the GM.

CALTROPS

Caltrops are small, multi-pointed metal devices strategically placed on the ground to impede or injure opponents by causing punctures and damage to tires or footwear. You can scatter caltrops in an empty square adjacent to you with a 1 AP (Interact) action. The first creature that moves into that square must succeed at a DC 20 basic Reflex save or take 1d6 piercing damage. Once a creature takes damage from caltrops, enough caltrops are ruined that other creatures moving into the square are safe.

Deployed caltrops can be salvaged and reused if no creatures took damage from them. Otherwise, enough caltrops are ruined that they can't be salvaged.

CANDLE

For 1 hour, a candle sheds enough light to increase the illumination level by one step to a maximum of Step 5 (Dim Light).

CHAIN

This 10-ft. heavy working chain can bear 2,000 lbs. A character bound with chain may escape with a successful 1- minute Escape check (DC 25).

CHEST, LARGE

This sturdy wood and leather chest may be shod with metal and feature a lockable latch. It can hold up to 300 lbs of items.

CHEST, SMALL

As a large chest, except that it can hold up to 100 lbs of items.

COMPASS

This magnetic, solar, or lunar compass helps a traveller stay on course, telling direction and granting a +5-item bonus to Sense Direction (Survival) checks.

CONCEALED SHEATH

This leather sheath provides ample storage for items weighing up to 1 lb, commonly utilized for daggers, wands, thieves' tools, and similar objects. By discreetly attaching it to inconspicuous locations such as inside a boot, under a bracer, or within a sleeve, you gain a +2-item bonus to Conceal an Object (Stealth) checks and DCs to hide or conceal the item within.

CRAFTING BOOK

This invaluable book serves as a repository for recording formulas related to non-magical items, enabling you to document and preserve up to 20 different formulas upon purchase, providing a comprehensive reference for crafting various practical creations.

CROSSBOW BOLT CASE

Crafted from sturdy wood, this case serves as a reliable storage solution, capable of securely housing up to twenty crossbow bolts, ensuring easy access and protection for ammunition during your adventurous endeavours.

EARPLUGS

Fashioned from waxed cotton or cork, these earplugs provide a +5-item bonus to your saving throws against effects with the auditory trait, effectively safeguarding your hearing. However, due to their nature, they impede the ability to hear, imposing a -2-item penalty on Perception checks related to sounds. Inserting or removing the earplugs can be done with a 1 AP (Interact) action.

FLAG/STANDARD

This item possesses the ability to evoke both fear and awe in those who observe it, providing a +1-item bonus when using Diplomacy checks to sway allies or Intimidate checks to instil fear in adversaries, enhancing the wielder's persuasive and intimidating presence.

FLINT & STEEL/TINDERBOX

You may use this item to start a fire. It is often a time-consuming process and even in perfect conditions, at least a 3 AP action using the Subsist action.

FORMULA BOOK

A formula book is a repository containing the essential formulas required for crafting alchemical and magical items. Capable of storing up to 20 different formulas, this book preserves the intricate knowledge and instructions necessary for item creation.

Formulas may also be recorded on parchment sheets, tablets, and almost any other medium available (GM Discretion).

GAME

Dice, playing cards, chess, and other amusements can help you relax.

GLASSES/GOGGLES

This eyewear has tinted lenses or narrow eye slits, granting you a +2-item bonus to saving throws against attacks that cause blindness with bright light.

GRAPPLING HOOK

With a rope securely fastened, the act of throwing a grappling hook presents an opportunity to facilitate climbing. To anchor the grappling hook, an attack roll with the secret trait is required, targeting a specific DC determined by the chosen point of attachment, typically DC 20 or higher. Success grants the reassurance of a secure hold, providing stability during ascent. However, a fumbled attempt deceives with a false sense of security, leading to an unfortunate discovery when the hook unexpectedly dislodges, potentially causing an unanticipated and perilous fall while still partway up.

GROOMING CASE

This item improves your Appearance giving a +1-item bonus to social skill checks (GM discretion).

HAMMMER, TOOL

This crafting tool is useful for delivering impactful strikes, serving not only as a reliable instrument for pounding and shaping materials but also doubling as an improvised light hammer in combat.

HOLY BOOK

Contained within the pages of this sacred manuscript are the divine scriptures bestowed by the gods themselves. Reserved for the pious and devout, certain divine spellcasters, like clerics, can harness the power held within this holy book as a divine focus, enabling them to channel specific abilities and cast selected rituals and spells. To access its divine essence, the religious text must be reverently held in one hand, symbolizing the profound connection between the caster and their faith.

HOLY SYMBOL - SILVER

This piece of silver bears the striking depiction of a deity, serving as a revered religious symbol. Bestowed with sacred significance, divine spellcasters, particularly clerics, possess the ability to wield this religious symbol as a divine focus, channelling its divine power to access specific abilities and cast chosen spells. To harness its divine energy, the religious symbol must be respectfully held in one hand, creating a tangible connection between the caster and the divine forces they serve.

HOLY SYMBOL - WOOD

Carved into this sacred piece of wood is a profound image symbolizing a deity of divine significance. Revered by divine spellcasters, especially clerics, this religious symbol holds the power to serve as a divine focus, granting access to specific abilities and the casting of chosen spells. To unlock its divine potential, the religious symbol must be held respectfully in one hand, establishing a tangible connection between the caster and the divine energies they draw upon.

HOLLY & MISTLETOE

Plants of extraordinary significance, possessing otherworldly properties, serve as verdant foci for esteemed spellcasters attuned to the primal forces of nature, like druids. These botanical treasures, such as a bundle of holly and mistletoe, hold the key to channelling specific abilities and casting selected spells. To harness their verdant energy, a druid must reverently hold the bundle of holly and mistletoe in one hand, embracing the inherent connection between themselves and the natural world. Additionally, alternative primal foci exist, tailored to druids with different affinities and focuses within the vast realms of nature.

HOURGLASS

This ingenious timing device comprises two interconnected glass bulbs, each filled with sand. As time elapses, the sand gracefully sifts from the upper bulb to the lower, a journey that precisely spans the duration of one hour. This hourglass, with its measured flow, serves as a reliable and visually captivating tool for tracking the passage of time with remarkable accuracy.

JAR/JUG

This container can hold coin of up to 5 lbs, alternately, it can hold 2 quarts of liquid.

LADDER

This simple 10-foot ladder consists of two long boards with wooden steps nailed into them at 1-foot increments.

LANTERN, BULLSEYE

Resembling a modern marvel, this remarkable item functions like a flashlight, utilizing a focused beam of light emitted through a small front opening. It increase the illumination level by two steps to a maximum of Step 6 (Twilight) in a 75-ft. cone and consumes 1 pint of oil per 4 hours of use.

LANTERN, CANDLE

Exquisite in its simplicity, this delicate paper lantern eschews the use of oil and instead employs the warm glow of candles. Emitting a gentle and subtle light, it casts a faint radiance, increasing the illumination level by two steps to a maximum of Step 5 (Dim Light). To sustain its gentle luminosity, the lantern consumes one candle per hour of continuous use, allowing for a portable source of light.

LANTERN, HOODED

With a cleverly designed hood that can be lowered to conceal its light without extinguishing it, this versatile lantern offers flexibility in controlling its illumination. This lantern increases the illumination level by two steps to a maximum of Step 7 (Flickering Light). The lantern consumes approximately 1 pint of oil for every 4 hours of continuous use, ensuring a steady source of light during extended periods of exploration or activity.

LANYARD

This cord attaches another item to the user’s wrist or belt, preventing it from leaving his square even when it’s dropped or disarmed.

MAGNET

This item can attract and hold 2 lbs. of metal.

MAGNIFYING GLASS

This quality handheld lens gives you a +2-item bonus to Perception checks to notice minute details of documents, fabric, and the like.

MANACLES

These metal restraints can bind a Small or Medium creature. Escaping the manacles requires a successful DC 20 Escape check. Breaking them requires a successful DC 20 Strength check. Each set of manacles comes with one key. Without the key a creature can pick the manacles’ lock with a successful DC 15 Thievery check.

MAP, AVERAGE

When trekking through the depicted area, the user’s Travel Speed increases by 1 MPH and they gain a +2-item bonus with Survival checks to avoid getting lost.

MAP, DETAILED

As an average map plus information about monsters, treasure, and other local features, granting a +2-item bonus to Recall Knowledge checks about the area.

MIRROR

This hand-held mirror is about a foot across. Unlike many higher-quality glass mirrors, this one is made out of polished steel and sturdy enough that you can drop it without risk of breakage.

MUG

Whether it is a simple pottery cup or an elaborate drinking stein with a handle and decorative lid that flips up, this cup may be used to hold any sort of beverage. Tankards are commonly made out of clay or tin.

MUSIC BOX

This delicate clockwork device may be wound up to play a single tune.

MUSICAL INSTRUMENT

Lutes, lyres, fiddles, pipes, and other instruments can raise spirits — and very occasionally, tame savage beasts. The GM might rule that an especially large handheld instrument (like a tuba) has greater weight.

OIL

Oil is most commonly used as lantern fuel, but you can also set a pint of oil aflame and throw it. You must first spend an Interact action preparing the oil, then throw it with another action as a ranged attack. If you hit, it splatters on the creature or in a single 5-foot square you target. You must succeed at a DC 10 flat check for the oil to ignite successfully when it hits. If the oil ignites, the target takes 5 fire damage.

PIPE

Puffing on a packed pipe for 1-minute grants a +1-circumstance bonus with Meditation checks for the next hour.

POLE (10 FT.)

This ubiquitous adventuring item grants a +2-item bonus with Jump checks and can be used to trigger traps. It can also be used as an improvised quarterstaff (-10 to attack).

POUCH, COIN

This container can hold up to 50 coins and weighs 1 lb. per 25 coins held.

POUCH, AMMO

A cloth or leather pouch can hold up to 20 sling bullets or 50 blowgun needles, among other things.

QUIVER

A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.

RAM, PORTABLE

A portable ram is a specialized tool designed for the purpose of breaking down doors or other barriers. It consists of a long handle with a sturdy metal head at one end. The head is typically shaped like a ram's head, hence the name.

When using a portable ram to break down a door, you gain a +4-item bonus on the check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you fortune on this check.

RING, POISON

The wearer may expose a target with a successful Unarmed Attack that inflicts damage. This item may hold 1 dose of poison.

ROPE, HEMP

This 50-ft. rope can bear 1,000 lbs. Hemp rope, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 30 Athletics check.

ROPE, SILK

This light and compact 50-ft. rope can bear 750 lbs. Silk rope, has 4 hit points and can be burst with a DC 40 Athletics check.

SACK

This heavy canvas sack, useful for carrying adventuring gear and other supplies, holds about 25 lbs. A leather thong threaded through loops at the bag’s end allows it to be tied shut easily.

SADDLEBAGS

When wearing saddlebags, an animal’s Strength score is considered 1 higher for carrying capacity.

SAW

When a character uses a saw, his Strength score is considered 1 higher for clearing brush. This item may also be used to cut wood.

SEAL/SIGNET RING

This item bears an image that may be pressed into hot wax to seal a document. This image is often a coat of arms, monogram, or other personal symbol.

SCALE/HAND

The simple device accurately measures weight.

SHOVEL

When a character uses a shovel, his Strength score is considered 2 higher for clearing rubble. This item may also be used as an improvised light pick.

SNOWSHOES

When a character wearing snowshoes is moving on snow and ice, they ignore the penalty for difficult terrain and reduce greater difficult terrain to difficult terrain. Land speed when walking on any other surface is reduced by 10.

SPYGLASS

A typical spyglass lets you see eight times farther than normal. A fine spyglass adds a +2-item bonus to Perception checks to notice details at a distance.

TENT

Tents come in a variety of sizes and accommodate between one and 10 people. A small tent holds one Medium creature and takes 20 minutes to assemble, a medium tent holds two creatures and takes 30 minutes, a large tent holds four creatures and takes 45 minutes, and a huge tent holds 10 creatures and takes 90 minutes (two Small creatures count as a Medium creature, and one Large creature counts as two Medium creatures). Huge tents are large enough to accommodate a small fire in the centre. Packing up a tent takes half as long as assembling it.

TORCH

A torch burns for 1-hour, shedding light and increasing the illumination level by two steps to a maximum of Step 7 (Flickering Light) for 1 hour. If a torch is used in combat, treat it as an improvised club that also inflicts 1 fire damage.

WATERSKIN

When it’s full, a waterskin contains roughly 1 days’ worth of water for a Small or Medium creature.

WHISTLE

This item’s squeal can be heard a mile away outdoors and 500 ft. away indoors.

WRIST SHEATH

This is a sheath designed to be strapped to your forearm and hidden under a long sleeve. The sheath can hold one forearm length item, such as a dagger, dart, or wand, or up to five arrows or crossbow bolts. As a 1 AP move action, you can bend your wrist to cause some or all of these items to drop into your hand (provoking attacks of opportunity as normal). You have a +2-item bonus on Conceal an Object (Stealth) checks made to oppose the Perception check of someone observing or frisking you to determine items in the sheath. You can only wear one wrist sheath per arm.

WRIST SHEATH (Spring Loaded)

This item works like a standard wrist sheath, but releasing an item from it is a 0 AP action that does not provoke. Preparing the sheath for this use requires cranking the sheath’s tiny gears and springs into place (a 3 AP manipulate action that provokes an attack of opportunity).

KITS & TOOLS

Kits and tools are collections of items that are assembled for a specific purpose or skill. They are often designed to assist characters in performing tasks more effectively or efficiently. For example, Thieves Tools include tools such as lock picks, tension wrenches, and small mirrors to aid in picking locks. A Medical Kit may contain bandages, antiseptics, and medical instruments for treating wounds and injuries.

Some of these items may be required to perform certain actions or provide a bonus to an action.

The exact contents of each kit are left up to the Game Master, though some basics are provided as an overview.

ALCHEMY LAB

This lab is used for making alchemical items and provides a +4-circumstance bonus on Crafting (alchemy) checks.

ALCHEMY TOOLS

These tools are required when using the Crafting Skill to make alchemical items. It is not possible to make alchemical items without these tools.

ARTISAN TOOLS

You need these tools to create items from raw materials with the Crafting skill. Different sets are needed for different work, as determined by the GM.

COMPONENT POUCH

A component pouch serves as a container specifically designed to hold the various material components and special items necessary for casting spells. Typically made of durable and waterproof leather, a component pouch is often worn on a belt for easy access during spellcasting.

The purpose of a component pouch is to provide a convenient and organized storage solution for the numerous material components required by spells. It contains separate compartments and divisions to keep the components sorted and readily available for use. This allows spellcasters to quickly retrieve the necessary components during the casting of their spells without the need for searching through a jumble of items.

Be aware that a component pouch is not designed to hold components with specific costs, such as rare gemstones or expensive spell reagents.

A component pouch may be used 100 times before it needs to be refilled.

COOKWARE

This includes pots, pans and eating utensils.

CROWBAR

When Forcing Open an object that doesn't have an easy grip, a crowbar makes it easier to gain the necessary leverage. Without a crowbar, prying something open takes a –2 item penalty to the check to Force Open (similar to using a shoddy item).

DISGUISE KIT

This small wooden box contains cosmetics, false facial hair, spirit gum, and a few simple wigs. You usually need a disguise kit to set up a disguise in order to Impersonate someone using the Deception skill. You can create 10 disguises with this kit before it is exhausted.

HEALERS TOOLS

This collection of bandages and herbs is required to make most Medicine checks. A healer’s kit is exhausted after 10 uses.

HERBALISM KIT

This kit contains a variety of instruments such as clippers, mortar and pestle, and pouches and vials used by herbalists to create remedies and potions. This kit is required to make herbal remedies and poisons.

REPAIR KIT

A repair kit allows you to perform simple repairs while traveling. It contains a portable anvil, tongs, woodworking tools, a whetstone, and oils for conditioning leather and wood. You can use a repair kit to Repair items using the Crafting skill.

REPLACEMENTS

You purchase this item to replenish the consumable elements of other kits.

SCRIBES KIT

Canvases, scrolls, pens, ink, and other writing implements.

SNARE KIT

This kit contains all of the required tools to make a snare or trap.

THIEVES TOOLS

You need thieves' tools to Pick Locks or Disable Devices (of some types) using the Thievery skill.

SERVICES

It is not always possible for you to carry out every task on your own. Towns and settlements play a vital role in providing essential services and support to adventurers. These services can range from healing and spellcasting to equipment repair, information gathering, and more.

REPAIRS

While you or your party may possess crafting skills, you might not always have the necessary time or resources to perform repairs yourself. In such cases, seeking the assistance of a skilled crafter or blacksmith in a town or settlement becomes crucial.

To repair an item, typically the following conditions must be met:

• Crafting Requirements: The crafter must have the necessary crafting ranks and specialty to repair the type of item.

• Cost: The cost of repairing an item is typically 10% of the item's worth. This may vary depending upon local conditions and material requirements (GM discretion).

The item is repaired to its full HP value.

RETAINER

It is sometimes necessary to acquire the services of a retainer for a specific task. Such tasks include pretty much any action form the skills chapter. You might need a retainer to scout an old mine for you in advance, providing you with a map, or a teamster to drive your horses and tend to them whilst you are exploring the ancient crypt.

The GM will have records of which retainers are available at any given time. As a general rule, an individual settlement will not have retainers with more ranks in a specific skill than its level.

Your GM may assign modifiers to the cost of a retainer as follows:

SPELLCASTING

Gaining the services of a spellcaster to cast a specific spell can be an expensive affair, but cheaper than purchasing a scroll, potion or wand. To find the spell in the first place you must make a Gather Information check with a level DC equal to the minimum caster level required top cast the spell.

For every two difference between the minimum caster level required and the level of the settlement, the DC is modified by one difficulty category.

MOUNTS & VEHICLES

This section includes mounts and vehicles. Mounts and vehicles play an important role in many adventures, providing transportation and assistance to adventurers. Whether it's riding a horse into battle or using a cart to transport goods, having the right mount or vehicle can greatly aid your journey.

All of the prices are for purchasing the animal or vehicle, it is possible to rent animals or vehicles, and this will usually be at 5% of the purchase price per day. A cautious vendor may however require some kind of deposit or bond up front if they feel that your venture may involve a level of danger.

MOUNTS & ANIMALS

Steeds of the animal type, particularly those with animal intelligence, can be skittish and prone to fear during combat situations. This can pose challenges for adventurers who rely on such steeds for transportation or combat support. Any animal intelligence steed immediately gains the fleeing and frightened 4 conditions when a combat begins. You may use Command an Animal and Ride actions (Handle Animal) to calm the creature. Non-animal mounts and military mounts do not suffer from this issue.

MOUNT STATISTICSStatistics for mounts can be found in TRG Fiend & Fables.MOUNT STATISTICSStatistics for mounts can be found in TRG Fiend & Fables.

VEHICLES

There will be times when your party will need a vehicle to transport them and/or their goods from one location to another. This may be to travel a great distance across a windswept desert, or perhaps an ocean voyage from one continent to another.

A selection of vehicles available can be found here, but the options are limited only by the campaign, your imagination and GM approval. Vehicle statistics are displayed in the following format:

VEHICLE NAME

A brief description of the vehicle.

Level The vehicles level will be displayed here which determines its DC for piloting and construction. If the vehicle has any modifiers to either craft or pilot, they will be displayed here.

Check The skill required to pilot the vehicle is listed here.

Size The vehicles dimensions which will be displayed as length, width and height.
Defensive Qualities Listed here will be the vehicles DB, Fort Save, Hardness, HP and any immunities.

Speed The speed of the vehicle (when correctly manned) will be listed here.

Qualities How many crew required to pilot the vessel, how many passengers it can carry, and any other important information is detailed here.

CANOE

A canoe is a lightweight and slender boat typically made of wood. It has a sleek design with a pointed bow and stern, allowing it to glide smoothly through the water. Canoes are propelled by a paddle, which is used to push and pull the water for forward motion and steering.

Level 1 (Easy DC -2); Check Athletics

Length 10 feet; Width 3 feet; Height 2 feet

DB 10; Fort +6; Hardness 4, HP 10; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed swim 30 feet (rowed)

Crew 1; Passengers 1; Load 800 lbs

CART

A simple draft wagon is a vehicle designed for hauling cargo overland. It features a sturdy construction with a single axle and a flat bed, providing ample space for carrying goods, supplies, or other items. The wagon is typically pulled by draft animals such as horses or oxen, utilizing their strength to transport heavy loads. The flatbed allows for easy loading and unloading of cargo, and it may be equipped with removable side panels or stakes to secure the goods during transportation.

Level 1; Check Ride

Length 10 feet; Width 5 feet; Height 4 feet

DB 10; Fort +6; Hardness 4, HP 10; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 1 Large creature)

Crew 1; Passengers 1; Load 1,000 lbs

CARRIAGE

A carriage is a robust vehicle designed to provide shelter and protection for both cargo and the driver. It features a sturdy frame, solid walls, and a roof that completely encloses the interior space. The vehicle is typically used for transporting passengers or valuable cargo that requires protection from the elements.

Level 4 (Easy DC -2); Check Ride (Handle Animal)

Length 10 feet; Width 10 feet; Height 7 feet

DB 14; Fort +8; Hardness 5, HP 30; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 2 Large creatures)

Crew 1; Passengers 2; Load 800 lbs

CHARIOT

A chariot consists of a lightweight, two-wheeled cart pulled by horses and driven by a skilled charioteer. The charioteer stands in the chariot, often holding the reins with one hand while wielding weapons such as spears, javelins, or bows with the other. The wheels of the chariot are typically spoked, allowing for smoother movement and manoeuvrability.

Level 2 (Hard DC +2); Check Ride (Handle Animal)

Length 5 feet; Width 5 feet; Height 4 feet

DB 10; Fort +6; Hardness 5, HP 20; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 1 Large creature)

Crew 1; Load 400 lbs

GALLEY

A galley is a long, slender vessel powered primarily by oars. It has a low, streamlined profile and is typically propelled by rowers seated in banks or tiers along the length of the ship.

Level 13; Check varies

Length 120 feet; Width 20 feet; Height 25 feet

DB 24; Fort +20; Hardness 15, HP 120; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Weakness Fire Manoeuvrable With a full complement of skilled rowers, a rowed galley can turn swiftly, turn in place, and even row backwards. Each 90-degree turn made in less than a vehicle length costs 5 extra feet of movement. It can row backwards no faster than half its speed, and it can’t turn while rowing backwards.

Speed swim 30 feet (rowed, wind)

Crew 22 (20 rowers); Passengers 6; Load 15 tons

ROWBOAT

This small watercraft is guided by row or sometimes a small sail.

Level 1; Check Athletics

Length 10 feet; Width 5 feet; Height 3 feet

DB 10; Fort +6; Hardness 5, HP 12; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed swim 20 feet (rowed)

Crew 1; Passengers 2; Load 1,000 lbs

SAILING SHIP

A multi masted ship with three or more head sails.

Level 12; Check varies

Length 80 feet; Width 20 feet; Height 25 feet

DB 22; Fort +18; Hardness 15, HP 100; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Weakness Fire Sluggish This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.

Speed swim 40 feet (wind)

Crew 9; Passengers 10; Load 10 tons

SCHOONER

A schooner is a sailing vessel characterized by a single mast and two or more head sails (fore-and-aft sails) that are set on separate masts or booms. It is known for its versatility and speed, making it a popular choice for both commercial and recreational purposes.

Level 9; Check varies

Length 30 feet; Width 15 feet; Height 20 feet

DB 20; Fort +14; Hardness 10, HP 80; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Weakness Fire Sluggish This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes.

Speed swim 30 feet (wind)

Crew 4; Passengers 6; Load 10 tons

SLEIGH

A light vehicle for traversing arctic terrain.

Level 2; Check Ride

Length 10 feet; Width 5 feet; Height 4 feet

DB 12; Fort +8; Hardness 5, HP 12; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; Sluggish This vehicle must move twice its length for each 90-degree turn it makes Ice Traverser Ice and snow are not difficult terrain to a sleigh, but all other terrains are difficult terrain for it.

Speed the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 2 Large creatures or 6 Medium creatures)

Crew 1; Passengers 1; Load 500 lbs

WAGON

This two-axle cargo hauler is pulled by a single steed or horse team and provides decent cover during poor weather.

Level 2; Check Ride

Length 10 feet; Width 10 feet; Height 7 feet

DB 10; Fort +8; Hardness 5, HP 12; Immunities critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

Speed the Speed of the slowest pulling creature (pulled by 2 Large creatures)

Crew 1; Passengers 2; Load 1,500 lbs

ALCHEMICAL ITEMS

Alchemical items differ from magical items as they are created using natural or scientific means. There are many items which are placed into this category and although not all of them are considered alchemical, it is a catch all category for these substances and items.

There are numerous alchemical items ranging from potent herbs to volatile explosives. The uneducated may mistake some of the effects of alchemical items for magic, but this is not the case.

To craft alchemical items you must have the Alchemical Crafting feat.

The items in this section are broken down into a number of sub-categories; Elixirs, Herbs, Oils, Poisons and Vials.

REAGENTSSome of the items in this section have a Reagent entry at the end of their description. This entry describes how the item can be used in conjunction with magical spells.REAGENTSSome of the items in this section have a Reagent entry at the end of their description. This entry describes how the item can be used in conjunction with magical spells.

LEVEL & COST

Each item is described and given a stat block at its base level, which is effectively the item in its simplest form. Most of the items here can be crafted to a higher level and details of how an alchemical items abilities are affected by a level increase are explained in its description.

ELIXIRS

An elixir is an alchemical item which must be consumed to gain its benefits.

ACTIVATING ELIXIRS

You usually Interact to activate an elixir as you drink it or feed it to another creature. You can feed an elixir only to a creature within reach that is either willing or unable to prevent you from doing so. You usually need only one hand to consume an elixir or feed it to another creature.

ANTI-PLAGUE

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR HEALING

Base Level 1

Base Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

An anti-plague protects you against disease. Upon drinking this elixir, you gain a +2-item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against disease for 24 hours. If you are currently inflicted with a disease, you may immediately make a new saving throw to resist it.

Higher Level For every additional 4 levels of the elixir, the bonus increases by +1.

Reagent If used in conjunction with any spell used to suppress or cure a disease, apply the elixirs bonus to any subsequent counteract check.

ANTITOXIN

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR HEALING

Base Level 1

Base Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

An antidote protects you against toxins. Upon drinking this antidote, you gain a +2-item bonus to Fortitude saving throws against poisons for 24 hours. If you are currently affected by a poison, you may immediately make a new saving throw to resist it.

Higher Level For every additional 4 levels of the elixir, the bonus increases by +1.

Reagent If used in conjunction with any spell used to suppress or remove a poison, apply the elixirs bonus to any subsequent counteract check.

BLOOD-BLOCK

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR HEALING

Base Level 2

Base Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

Applying this salve to a bleeding wound reduces the bleed by 1 point and reduces any further bleed damage by 1 for the next hour per application. After an hour, if the bleed effect hasn’t been properly treated, the injury resumes bleeding and more salve must be applied. Though blood-block can be applied successively to the same injury, applying multiple doses doesn’t cure additional damage.

Higher Level For every additional 3 levels of the elixir, the reduction to bleed is increased by 1.

Reagent If used in conjunction with any spell used to suppress or stop bleeding, increase the amount of bleeding stopped by the amount the elixir stops.

FIST OF ROCK

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR MORPH

Level 4

Price 130 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

Your fists become hard as stone. For 1 hour, your fists deal 1d6 base bludgeoning damage and lose the nonlethal trait.

HEALTH

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR HEALING

Base Level 1

Base Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

This alchemical draught boosts the natural healing process by providing rapid relief. When you drink this elixir, you regain 1d6+2 hit points.

Higher Level For every additional 2 levels of the elixir, the amount healed increases by 1d6+2.

LEAPING JUICE

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR

Base Level 1

Base Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

This rather sour solution adds a spring to your step. You gain a +2-status bonus to Jumping checks for 1 minute.

Higher Level For every additional level of the elixir, the bonus increases by +1.

SMELLING SALTS

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR

Level 2

Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

These sharply scented gray crystals cause people inhaling them to regain consciousness. Smelling salts grant you a new saving throw to resist any spell or effect that has already rendered you unconscious or stunned. If exposed to smelling salts while dying, you immediately become conscious, but must still make dying checks each round. A container of smelling salts has dozens of uses if stoppered after each use, but depletes in a matter of hours if left open.

SOOTHE SYRUP

ALCHEMICAL CHANCE CONSUMABLE ELIXIR

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

This sweet and wholesome-tasting blue liquid creates a sense of warmth and comfort. Soothe syrup coats your stomach and makes it much more difficult for you to succumb to queasiness. For 1 hour after drinking soothe syrup, you gain advantage on saving throws made to resist effects that would make you sickened.

Higher Level For every additional 2 levels of the elixir, the effect last for an additional hour (max 5).

SPEED

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE ELIXIR

Base Level 2

Base Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

Enzymatic compounds in this elixir strengthen and excite the muscles in your legs. You gain a +5-foot status bonus to your Speed for 1 minute.

Higher Level The level of the elixir may be increased by 4 levels which increases the bonus by +5 (max +20).

It may also be increased by 1 level to increase the duration to 10 minutes or by 4 levels to increase the duration to 1 hour.

Reagent Acts as an extend Metamagic if used in conjunction with a spell that increase your movement.

HERBS

Herbs and useful plants and fungi abound in most wilderness regions, and while these valuable plants can be obtained in special markets or shops, the skilled herbalist knows where to go to gather these resources by hand in the wild.

To locate herbs in the wilderness, a gather herbs skill check must be made (see Chapter 4 Skills).

PREPARING HERBS

Most herbs must be prepared to prevent them from spoiling. Preparing a herb follows the usual rules for crafting, except a Nature check can be made instead of a Crafting (alchemy). The DC of the check to prepare the herb increases by 5 in this case. If you fail this check by 10 or more, the dose of the herb is ruined; if you fail by less, you can try again with the same herbs.

HERB LIFESPAN

A raw, unprepared herb spoils 24 hours after it is harvested. A prepared herb spoils after 1 month unless otherwise noted in its entry.

ANGELSTEP

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 2

Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (1 AP)

This iridescent white shelf fungus is said to have first grown from the footsteps of an angel, though some claim it instead comes from the footsteps of a djinni.

As part of an attempt to stabilize a dying creature, a dose of raw angelstep can be rubbed on the creature to grant a +4-item bonus to the Resuscitation (Medicine) check made to stabilize the creature. A dose of angelstep pigment applied to the skin of a medium or smaller creature helps to protect that creature against death for 2d4 hours. The next time the wearer of angelstep pigment gains the dying condition, it gains a +4-item bonus on its next check to recover. The pigment loses its effect once all these checks are attempted or once the victim is stabilized.

Terrain: temperate or warm deserts.

BLACK AMARANTH

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 3

Price 85 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact, Manipulate (3 AP)

Black amaranth grows in small clusters from the remains of the dead.

A dose of black amaranth paste can be applied to a dead body to slow decay. One dose used on a Tiny or smaller creature delays the onset of decay for 3 days. Two doses are needed for Small creatures, 3 for Medium creatures, 6 for Large creatures, 12 for Huge creatures, 24 for Gargantuan creatures, and 48 for Colossal creatures.

Terrain: temperate or warm forests or plains.

BLOODY MANDRAKE

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 3

Price 85 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact, Manipulate (3 AP)

Bloody mandrakes grow from the corpses of intelligent creatures who had supernatural powers in life. This plant’s unsettlingly humanoid-shaped tuber-like roots increase fertility and vitality.

One dose of bloody mandrake paste smeared on the lips (this is a free action) during spellcasting can be used as an additional material component when casting spells that remove afflictions and conditions or that provide a morale bonus. Doing so grants a +1-item bonus to the spellcraft check to cast the spell.

Terrain: any plains or swamps.

BONE REED

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 2

Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (1 minute)

This aquatic grass resembles translucent white horsetail.

A creature that sleeps for at least 8 hours in 1 day with a bone reed bound to one of its arms or legs heals double the normal ability damage and gains a +2-item bonus to recovery checks. A bone reed loses its effectiveness after use. Binding a bone reed to a limb requires 1 minute of work.

Terrain: any swamps.

DREAM LICHEN

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 12

Price 3,060 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (1 minute)

This multi-coloured, shimmering lichen grows in places where powerful magical creatures have slept and dreamt.

A creature that sleeps for at least 8 hours with a dose of dream lichen in contact with its body has vivid dreams in which it endures and recovers from a supernatural affliction. Upon waking, the creature can attempt a new saving throw against a single curse or mind-affecting effect from which it is currently suffering. Additionally, the user automatically doubles the amount of the Drained condition they remove after a night’s rest.

Terrain: anywhere the boundaries between the Material Plane and the Dimension of Dreams grow thin.

FIRQUELINE

CONSUMABLE HERB UNCOMMON

Level 7

Price 550 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (2 AP)

Firqueline is a vibrant blue moss that grows on the side of large trees.

When this herb is consumed it clots the blood and removes bruising and minor pain. You regain 3d6+6 hit points, stop 5 points of bleeding and lessens one injury by 1.

Terrain: any forests or jungles.

KRITILLISH

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage apply to an inanimate object

Activate Interact (2 AP)

Kritillish is a mildly poisonous blue fungus which if consumed can cause madness. If applied to an inanimate object, it will emanate light as a torch for 24 hours, after which it crumbles and falls away. This light can only be diminished by magical means.

Terrain: underground caves.

LIMORSOR

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (2 AP)

Limorsor plants are green and leafy with small yellow flowers.

When this herb is consumed it accelerates the natural healing process and immune system. You regain 1d6 hit points, stop 1 point of bleeding and gain a +1-item bonus to saving throws against disease and poison for 10 minutes.

Terrain: any forests, plains or edge of freshwater water sources.

MOLY

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 11

Price 2,185 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (3 AP)

Moly is a plant with flowers white as pure milk and roots black as night.

Anyone wearing or carrying fresh moly gains a +2-item bonus on saving throws against spells and spell-like abilities. Moly remains fresh in this way for only 12 hours, regardless of magical attempts to preserve it. When processed into a powder it may be used to counteract a magical effect.

Terrain: any forests or plains.

NIGHTSAGE

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 4

Price 130 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (2 AP)

The fragrant purple blossoms of this night-blooming wildflower are so deep in hue that they appear almost black.

When dried nightsage is lit on fire, it produces a thin but pleasant-smelling smoke almost like that produced by a stick of incense. A dose of nightsage burns for 10 minutes and can be extinguished and reignited for multiple uses (but it is always used in 1-minute increments, regardless of the actual time spent burning).

While nightsage burns, each corporeal undead creature within a 5-foot radius gains a +2-status bonus on saving throws against essence energy effects. Necromancers are fond of supplying their undead minions with small thimbles containing a burning stick of nightsage that can be worn while carrying out their commands. A moderate or stronger wind extinguishes a burning stick of nightsage.

Terrain: any jungles.

REGLEN

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 12

Price 3,060 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (2 AP)

Reglen is a strange purple moss that can be found growing under the shadows of great trees.

This herb must be prepared before use. If it is taken without preparation, you must make a Fortitude saving throw or gain the sickened 2 condition.

Once prepared, Reglen is a powerful healing agent which heals you of 7d6+18 hit points, stops all bleeding and reduces an injury by 4.

Terrain: any forests or jungles.

WINTERBITE

CONSUMABLE HERB

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (2 AP)

The white-veined leaves of this minty sprig carry a pleasant and soothing scent.

When held under the nose and, a dose of prepared winterbite releases a pungent, sweet odour that clears the sinuses and sharpens the senses. For the next hour, the user of a dose of prepared winterbite gains a +2-item bonus on scent-based skill checks.

Terrain: any cold.

OILS

Oils can be very useful in an adventuring environment and can provide a quick solution to many problems. All of these tools can be made by a character with the Craft (alchemy) skill; the DC to craft the item is based upon its level.

ACTIVATING OILS

An oil must be applied to an object or creature unless an individual description states otherwise. The actions required to apply an oil are detailed in its description. The oil must also be in your hand ready to apply, so it may require an additional action (or more perhaps) to retrieve the oil.

ADAMANTINE BLANCH

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE

Level 7

Price 525 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (2 AP)

You can pour a vial of this dark liquid onto one melee weapon, one thrown weapon, or 10 pieces of ammunition. When used on a melee or thrown weapon, rather than ammunition, the blanch lasts for 1 minute. When you use it on ammunition, the blanch is expended on a given piece of ammunition after firing it, whether it hits or not. An adamantine blanch contains small amounts of fire oil, so it must be used all at once; an opened vial ignites to melt the adamantine onto the weapon and is quickly consumed. The weapon or ammunition counts as adamantine instead of its normal material for any physical damage it deals, if applicable.

ARMOURGUARD

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE

Base Level 4

Base Price 130 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (2 AP)

This clear resin protects metal armour, shields or any other metal item. When applied to a metal item it adds a +2-item bonus to the items HP for the next 24 hours. Furthermore, a shield gains a +1-item bonus to DB and armour gains a +1-item bonus to DR.

Higher Level For every additional 4 levels of the elixir, the HP bonus increases by +5, CR by +1 and DB by +1.

COLD IRON BLANCH

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE

Level 3

Price 85 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (2 AP)

You can pour a vial of this dark liquid onto one melee weapon, one thrown weapon, or 10 pieces of ammunition. When used on a melee or thrown weapon, rather than ammunition, the blanch lasts for 1 minute. When you use it on ammunition, the blanch is expended on a given piece of ammunition after firing it, whether it hits or not. A cold iron blanch contains small amounts of fire oil, so it must be used all at once; an opened vial ignites to melt the cold iron onto the weapon and is quickly consumed. The weapon or ammunition counts as cold iron instead of its normal material for any physical damage it deals, if applicable.

NULLADIR

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (1 AP)

This oil is often stored in the form of small, salty pellets in a dry container, though it can also be mixed with a flask of water and carried that way. Nullladir neutralizes acid; a vial of pellets or a flask of nulladir-water is enough to render a cubic foot of acid safe to touch in 1 minute, though this is usually too slow to prevent damage from a thrown vial of acid or the contents of a large monster’s gullet. Nulladir vapours are slightly irritating to the eyes, nose, and mouth, causing sickened 1 for 3 rounds after close exposure (Fortitude DC 16 negates).

SILVERSHEEN

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE

Level 2

Price 50 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

Activate Interact (2 AP)

You can slather this silvery paste onto one melee weapon, one thrown weapon, or 10 pieces of ammunition. Silversheen spoils quickly, so once you open a vial, you must use it all at once, rather than saving it. For the next hour, the weapon or ammunition counts as silver instead of its normal material for any physical damage it deals.

POISONS

Poisons are the tools of assassins and provide a subtle way to harm an opponent further in combat, or slowly away from a conflict.

Poisons are usually created from natural resources enhanced to make them more potent.

Each poison's stat block includes the Price and features for a single dose. Poison doses are typically kept in a vial or some other type of safe and secure container.

APPLYING A POISON

Applying a poison is an Interact action unless specified differently in the poison’s description. A poison requires at least one free hand to apply to release into the air or apply to food or drink. If you are applying a poison to a weapon or item, this requires two hands.

Each poison description contains a usage entry which indicates the number of hands required.

Saving throws to resist a poison are level-based fortitude saves unless stated otherwise.

ARSENIC

ALCHEMICAL CONSUMABLE INGESTED POISON

Level 1

Price 25 gp

Usage held in 1 hand

Activate Interact (1 AP)

VIALS

Vials are alchemical weapons which can be thrown at targets to inflict harm. Each of these substances can be made with Alchemy (Crafting or Nature) checks. These weapons explode when they hit a creature or surface.

Alchemical weapons have a range increment of 20 feet and attack as martial thrown weapons (with their own attack group).
