CHAPTER 9 – MAGIC

Magic is the miraculous, a departure from the ordinary, the ability to bring about a new thing, a new phenomenon, and an effect that lies outside what is ordinarily possible. Through force of will, spellcasters change the essential nature of the world, altering the fabric of reality to suit their needs. Whether calling forth a demon from the Abyss or evoking a lightning from her fingertips, the spellcaster restructures the laws of reality to achieve a desired end. Sure, a cleric invokes the blessing of his god, while a wizard recalls complex magical formula, but the process and energy harnessed is the same regardless of the user.

In TRG magic is a wide and varied art of power and subtlety. Some practitioners of magic spend years locked away with dusty spell tomes, learning the intricate details of the occult. Others are simply born with their power and have no true understanding of where or why they possess such power.

MAGICAL TRADITIONS

There are four magical traditions from which the power of a spell can be drawn from.

ARCANE

Arcane magic is a complex and intricate form of magic that is wielded by highly skilled and knowledgeable individuals. Arcane casters draw their magical power from their deep understanding of the underlying principles and forces that govern magic. Through years of study and practice, they learn to harness and manipulate arcane energies to shape reality itself. Their magic is characterized by precise rituals, intricate spellcasting gestures, and the incantation of ancient words of power.

Associated Skill: Arcana; Ability Score: Intelligence

Aura Colour: Red

DIVINITY

Divinity Magic is a mystical and potent form of magical power granted by deities or celestial beings. Those who wield this magic, often referred to as Divinity Casters or Godbinders, are chosen or blessed by the gods to serve as conduits for their immense power.

Associated Skill: Religion; Ability Score: Wisdom

Aura Colour: Blue

ETHEREAL

Ethereal Magic is a mystical and profound form of magic that draws upon the spiritual and mental energies of individuals. Practitioners of Ethereal Magic, often called Spirit weavers or Mind walkers, delve into the depths of consciousness, harnessing the essence of the spirit and the power of the mind to shape and manipulate reality.

Associated Skill: Occultism; Ability Score: Charisma

Aura Colour: Purple

VERDANT

Verdant Magic draws its power from the natural world, tapping into the energy and essence of the elements, plants, and creatures that inhabit it. Practitioners of Verdant Magic, often referred to as Green weavers or Nature Mages, have a deep connection with the environment and the life force that flows through it.

Associated Skill: Nature; Ability Score: Constitution

Aura Colour: Green

MAGICAL SCHOOLS

All spells, all magic items, and most other magical effects fall into one of the eight schools of magic. These schools broadly define what the magic is capable of. Every spell has the trait corresponding to its school. Some spellcasters, like specialist wizards, have particular acumen with a certain school of magic.

ALTERATION

This school focuses on the alteration and transformation of matter and creatures. It allows casters to change the properties of objects, shape-shift, or transmute one substance into another.

ENCHANTMENT

This school revolves around the manipulation and influence of the minds and emotions of others. Enchanters are skilled in casting spells that charm, beguile, and persuade, allowing them to control and shape the perceptions and actions of individuals.

INSIGHT

This school delves into the realms of foresight, intuition, and gaining insights into the past, present, and future. Practitioners can gain knowledge and unravel mysteries through their heightened perception.

INVOCATION

This school focuses on the direct manipulation and harnessing of elemental energies. It is the art of conjuring raw power and unleashing it upon the world in the form of devastating spells and destructive forces.

SHADOW

This school revolves around the creation of illusions, deceiving the senses and manipulating perceptions. It allows the caster to create realistic illusions that can fool even the keenest of observers.

SOUL

This school delves into the manipulation of life force and the energies of the soul. It involves communing with spirits, manipulating life and death energies, and sometimes healing or reanimating the deceased.

TRANSLOCATION

This school deals with the manipulation of space, enabling casters to summon creatures, objects, or energies from other planes of existence while also having the ability to instantaneously transport themselves and others across vast distances.

WARDING

This school specializes in protective spells and the defence against harmful forces. It is concerned with creating barriers, warding against magical and physical threats, and dispelling or countering hostile magic.

SPELLCRAFT

The ability to cast spells is represented by a special attribute called Spellcraft. To determine your Spellcraft attribute, add your BSB to your tradition ability score. This may be modified further by feats and abilities.

CASTER STYLE

Some spell casters spend hours poring over dusty tomes and old scrolls, searching for the knowledge of spells and ancient magical techniques. Other casters are born with their power and discover their magical skills naturally.

These two types of caster type are Learned and Instinctive and both develop their magical skills in different ways as detailed below. When you first select your character class, your caster type options will be provided there.

LEARNED

Learned casters store their magical knowledge in tomes, prayer books and sometimes other living creatures (such as familiars). The area in which a learned spell caster stores their spells is referred to as a Spell Library.

At 1st level, you will be granted spells which are added to your spell library automatically. Each time you gain a level, you will be granted additional spells to add to your spell library.

A learned caster must spend at least thirty minutes during their daily preparation, studying their Spell Library to be able to cast spells.

Once you have completed your daily study, you can memorise spells as determined by your class and other modifiers (such as feats).

If a learned caster is unable to study their Spell Library, they can only cast cantrips that day.

SPELL LIBRARIES

As a rule, Arcane casters use Spell Books for their Spell Libraries. Divinity casters draw their spells directly from a deific entity. Ethereal casters tattoo their Spell Library onto their bodies. Verdant Casters inscribe runes into a Natural Reservoir (a staff, robe or another item made from natural materials).

ARCANE LEARNING REQUIREMENTS

Arcane casters learn their spells from sources of knowledge such as scrolls, tomes and other casters and must have a suitable source of knowledge available to them during the learning process.

DIVINITY LEARNING REQUIREMENTS

Divinity casters have access to all divinity spells and may select any available to them each day by spending an hour in prayer during daily preparation.

ETHEREAL LEARNING REQUIREMENTS

Ethereal casters do not rely on the written word as much as other casters and therefore do not need external sources to learn new spells. Ethereal casters may use scrolls in the normal way but can also learn new spells with simple contemplation (Very Hard +5 DC). An Ethereal caster may also use the Meditation (1 hour) skill as an Aid action to enhance their chances of success.

VERDANT LEARNING REQUIREMENTS

Verdant casters draw their power from the natural world and like divinity casters may draw their spells from any available to them. During daily preparation they must spend an hour in quiet communion with nature as appropriate to their beliefs.

INSTINCTIVE

As an Instinctive Caster, you have access to a much smaller collection of spells but have no need to study or maintain a Spell Library.

Your character begins play with spells as determined by your class and gains spells automatically when gaining a new level. Additional spells can be obtained by purchasing the Magical Discovery feat (see chapter 5).

You can cast any spell that you know assuming you meet any prerequisites.

SPELL AVAILABILITY

Not all magic is equally known. In many worlds, spells beyond the traditional core traditions are uncommon, forgotten, or jealously guarded. This rule introduces rarity tiers to spells, influencing how casters access them.

SPELL AVAILABILITY TIERS

Spells are divided into the following categories, which determine how a caster may learn or select them:

COMMON SPELLS

These are widely known, well-documented spells that are part of formal magical instruction or are otherwise easily accessible in the world. All spells listed in the Core Rulebook are considered Common. Casters may freely add these spells to the repertoire through level up picks.

UNCOMMON OR RARE SPELLS

Spells introduced in supplemental materials—such as Inner Mastery, Fury & Finesse, Fiends & Fables, and other sourcebooks—are not assumed to be known by default. These spells are considered Uncommon or Rare, depending on the setting and campaign context. Casters cannot select these spells using automatic spell picks upon levelling unless the GM rules otherwise.

Instead, these spells must be learned through in-world effort, such as:

• Researching the spell in a library or arcane archive.

• Discovering a lost scroll, spellbook, or rune-inscribed relic.

• Being taught the spell by a mentor, master, or other creature with knowledge of it.

• Experimenting and unlocking the spell through downtime actions and skill checks.

A GM may adjust availability as appropriate for their world—some regions or cultures may treat even Core spells as restricted or lost, while others may widely teach powerful spells from supplemental sources.

SPELL LEVEL

In TRG Prime, spells do not technically have a level but instead have a PP cost. The PP cost of spell can range from 0 (for a cantrip) to as high as 20 and beyond.

SPELL PP COST

The base PP cost of a spell is indicated in its description. Warping options increase the PP cost of the spell and determine its final casting DC (see below).

Each caster can utilise a maximum amount of PP per Cast a Spell action equal to their caster level +1,

Signus is an 8th level Druid with a caster level of 8. The maximum amount of PP that he can utilise during any one spell casting action is 9.

CANTRIPS

A cantrip is a special type of spell which is easier to cast and learn than other types of spell. Casting a cantrip has a much lower DC than other spells (and often doesn’t require a check at all). It cannot be warped using Metamagic or warping options but may have a standardised set of Caster Level Modifications which are applied automatically as you increase in levels. Cantrips have a cost of 0 PP and are always treated as the PP that you are able to cast for counteract purposes.

The amount of cantrips that you have access to will be determined by your class or other character features.

POWER POINTS

Mere knowledge of magic and spell formulas isn’t enough to turn a simple scholar into a full-fledged wizard. One must possess the will and the force to empower the words they chant, bending reality to their whims.

The amount of magical energy that you can harness and use over a given period is represented by a value called Power Points (PP’s).

The total number of Power Points available to you calculated as follows:

Power Points (PP) = Class PP + Magical Ability Score + racial mod + other mods

RECOVERING POWER POINTS

Once your PPs are depleted, they may be regained (up to the maximum) in the following 3 ways:

• If you are active, the amount of power points that you regain is one every three hours.

• If you are resting, you regain 1 PP per two caster levels (round up) for every hour of rest.

• If you are sleeping (or whatever it is Elves do), you recover 50% of power points for each half of a full night’s rest.

Be aware, you may only benefit from a maximum of 1 sleep cycle in any given 24-hour period. Any time sleeping beyond that is classed as Resting.

You may also make a Power Recovery (Meditation) check to increase the amount of power points that you regain whilst resting.

SPELL TRAITS

There are three main spell traits which determine how a spell is cast and how it interacts the environment. These traits are Utility spells, Save spells, and Attack spells. Each type of spell uses its own resolution method, which is described below. All spells require a Cast a Spell action to cast.

UTILITY SPELLS

These spells have the Utility Trait and encompass the great majority of spells, including everything that is neither an Attack Spell, nor a Save spell. Utility spells will not work on non-willing targets, so there is no Saving Throw required for this type of spell. Since many Utility spells are beneficial, (i.e. Healing spells), a character’s aura does not usually resist beneficial magic. Therefore, Utility spells may be cast on unconscious characters to give them aid. From time to time, however, a character will not wish to be healed or even returned from the dead. Even though the character is unconscious, this is a choice that is always left up to the player running the character. If a player does not wish for his or her character to be healed or raised from the dead, the spells will automatically fail. This means that the player controlling the character will be the one to decide if a character is willing to be the target of the spell, regardless of the character being conscious or not. For non-player characters, monsters, etc., the GM is the arbiter of whether they choose to resist a Utility spell, in which case it fails.

SAVE SPELLS

These spells have the Save Trait and assault the mind or body of the target. To resolve a successfully cast Save spell, the defending character must roll equal to or higher than the Save DC, adding their bonus in the appropriate saving throw. Save spells will usually have an entry of Will, Fortitude, or Reflex in the Save section of the spell description, although some Save Spells may require a skill check to resist.

ATTACK SPELLS

Attack spells have the Attack Trait and are physical manifestations of an element or other force that is then used to attack a target. Your Cast a Spell check to successfully cast the spell and your attack roll are one and the same. If the spell is cast successfully, the result of the check is also your attack roll, and you determine an Attack Value in the same way as other attacks. Unless otherwise stated in the spell’s description, an Attack Spell will fumble if an unmodified 1 is rolled on the spell check.

CASTING SPELLS

There are a few rules around casting a spell. Casting a spell is handled in some ways like using a skill but has several specific requirements.

CASTING REQUIREMENTS

You may attempt to cast any spell that you know, if you meet the caster level requirement, you have enough PPs, you meet the daily requirements (Learned) and the PP cost requirements (see class and above).

It is possible to cast spells that are beyond your normal PP limit, which is called overcasting. Overcasting is discussed in more detail later in this chapter.

You must also be able to satisfy any components that the spell needs.

CASTING CHECK

To cast a spell, you must make a Cast a Spell (Spellcraft) action. There are several modifiers which apply to this check which are explore in more detail below.

CAST A SPELL

You select a spell from your repertoire and set in motion the required actions to cast it. The number of AP (or time) required is dependent upon the individual spell being cast.

Each spell will have traits associated with it and will behave according to its individual description.

Once all modifiers have been determined, a Spellcraft check is made to complete this action.

Heroic You cast the spell and halve (round up) the Total PP (after warping options added) cost of the spell.

Critical You cast the spell and halve (round up) the Base PP (before warping options added) cost of the spell.

Success You cast the spell normally in accordance with its usual parameters.

Chaos: You trigger a resonance event (see later in the chapter).

Partial The spell fails but you lose no PP.

Failure The spell fails; you lose half the PP (round down).

Fumble Your spell fails; you lose the PP and must roll on the Spell Failure Table.

Blunder Your spell fails and you must roll on the Spell Failure Table at +20.

There are a few modifiers and requirements that affect this check as explored below.

Some GMs may wish to make the Save DC of a spell more difficult if its result is Critical or Heroic. If this is the case, a Critical result makes the Save DC Hard (+2), and Heroic Very Hard (+5). If you apply this result, you do not save any PP when casting the spell.Some GMs may wish to make the Save DC of a spell more difficult if its result is Critical or Heroic. If this is the case, a Critical result makes the Save DC Hard (+2), and Heroic Very Hard (+5). If you apply this result, you do not save any PP when casting the spell.

BASE SPELL DC

Like any other check, the Cast a Spell action has a DC which must be achieved to successfully cast your spell. Before making the Cast a Spell check you must determine this DC which is a level-based DC using the PP cost of the spell as the level.

Cast a Spell DC = 10 + (Spell PP cost) x1.5

CASTING TIME

The number of AP (or time) required to cast, differs from spell to spell, but if a spell requires 1 or more AP to cast, you may use extra casting time to enhance your chances of success.

EXTRA CASTING TIME

When making a spell casting check you may take extra time while casting a spell to gain a bonus to casting it. The amount of extra casting time you take is based upon the casting time of the spell that you are attempting to cast.

Spell Casting Time

Extra Casting Time Increments

Free or Reaction

n/a

1–3 AP

3 AP

1 minute

1 minute

More than 1 minute

n/a

For each additional casting increment taken, beyond the initial casting time, you gain a +1-circumstance bonus to the casting check. You cannot gain more than a +5 to the casting check by taking extra time.

If you willingly stop without casting, all accrued bonuses are lost and the process must be started anew, but no PPs are spent until the Spell is cast.

If you are interrupted (take damage etc) whilst preparing a spell in this way, it is treated as Taking Damage whilst casting (see below).

Be aware, you cannot apply extra casting time to spells that have a casting time of more than 1 minute or less than 1 AP.

CASTING CANTRIPS

Under normal circumstances a Spellcraft check is not required to cast a cantrip (PP 0 spell). If penalties are applied to the check for taking damage or other modifiers, then a check must be made against a Casting DC of 10. Of course, if an attack cantrip is cast, then a spellcraft check must still be made to resolve the attack check.

CASTING FOCUS

Sometimes you will learn how to cast spells using a focus item such as a wand, holy symbol, or staff. Using such a focus item can greatly increase the flavour of the game. When creating a spell using character, you have the option of casting spells with a focus item. This item could be a wand, a staff, or even a weapon.

There are both benefits and drawbacks to using a focus, and once you decide to learn how to cast spells with a focus, it cannot be changed later.

When using a focus item, you must hold it in your hand while performing the gestures associated with casting a spell.

You gain a +1-item modifier to all casting attempts while using your focus. On the downside, if you should ever lose your focus, or be unable to use it for any reason, then you receive a -2-circumstance modifier to all spell casting attempts. Casting a spell without a focus also increases the danger of any fumbles. Should a spell be fumbled when cast without the focus, you take a +10 to the Fumble Roll.

Your focus gains the invested trait and can also be used in place of a somatic component.

During your daily preparation it is possible to change your focus to another item, which requires the usual investment process.

SPELL COMPONENTS

A spell description lists the components required to cast each spell. Each component adds certain traits to the Cast a Spell action, and some components have special requirements. There are three commonly used components.

MATERIAL

A material component refers to one or more tangible substances or objects that are consumed by the spell's energies during the casting process. Any spell that requires this component gains the manipulate trait, forcing you to have a vacant hand to retrieve and use the material component. The component is expended in the casting (even if the spell is disrupted).

Except in extreme circumstances, you can assume all common components are included in a material component pouch.

SOMATIC

A somatic component involves a deliberate and exact movement of the hand. You need to ensure that you have at least one unoccupied hand available to perform a somatic component. Any spell that requires this component gains the manipulate trait. You can use this component while holding something in your hand, but not if you are restrained or otherwise unable to gesture freely.

Spells that require you to touch the target require a somatic component. You can do so while holding something as long as part of your hand is able to touch the target (even if it’s through a glove or gauntlet).

VERBAL

A verbal component entails a spoken incantation. To fulfil a verbal component requirement, you must be capable of speaking with a resolute voice. The spell gains the concentrate trait.

Your GM may allow characters to substitute some components for others which are more flavoursome for your character. A bard using a musical instrument or a cleric using a holy symbol are two examples.

IGNORING COMPONENTS

You may attempt to avoid using a specific component when casting a spell if you have the specific Metamagic feat which allows you to do so.

CASTING PENALTIES

There are several factors which can make casting a spell more difficult. Warping the spell does this, but is not a penalty, as this simply increases the PP cost and thus the DC of the Casting Check.

Casting penalties are adverse situations which make the casting of a spell more difficult, thus applying a penalty.

TAKING DAMAGE

You may take damage or even a critical injury whilst casting a spell. If you are struck for hit point damage whilst casting a spell, your spell casting check is automatically a failure. If you are struck for a critical whilst casting a spell your spell casting check is automatically a fumble.

Be aware that you may attempt a Spell Concentration check (see chapter 4) to avoid the spell failing.

If you are taking recurring damage or bleed, the amount of damage you are taking is applied as penalty to your casting check.

MAGICAL INTERFERENCE

Magic is a fickle and often volatile creature. If you are targeted by another spell whilst casting a spell of your own, you take a -2-circumstance penalty to your casting check.

VIGOROUS MOTION

If you are riding on a moving mount, taking a bouncy ride in a wagon, on a small boat in rough water, belowdecks in a storm-tossed ship, or simply being jostled in a similar fashion, you take a -2-circumstance penalty to your casting check.

VIOLENT MOTION

If you are on a galloping horse, taking a very rough ride in a wagon, on a small boat in rapids or in a storm, on deck in a storm-tossed ship, or being pitched roughly about in a similar fashion, you take a -5-circumstance penalty to your casting check.

VIOLENT WEATHER

If you try to cast a spell in violent weather you will also suffer a penalty to your casting check. The GM will assign a circumstance penalty of between -2 & -10 based upon the specific weather conditions.

COVER MODIFIERS

Targets of a spell may gain cover from its effects. Furthermore, targeting an ally with a Utility spell may also be subjected to penalties from cover. To determine if the target of your spell gains a cover bonus, use the rules from Chapter 6. If the spell is a non-penetrating area effect, determine cover from the areas centre.

As a rule, Attack spells take any penalties to the attack roll, Save spells apply the penalty to the Save DC and Utility spells apply the penalty to the casting check.

SPELL TARGET IN MELEE

If you target a creature with an Attack spell whilst they are in melee, your spell is subject to a -4-circumstance penalty.

OTHER MODIFIERS

The GM is free to add modifiers for just about anything that they deem appropriate (these modifiers may even sometimes be positive!).

DEFENSIVE CASTING MENTAL

Action Free

Trigger You are casting a spell and choose to try to avoid an attack of opportunity or other reaction.

You may Defensive cast to avoid an attack of opportunity or other reaction provoked by casting a spell. When you defensive cast, your Spell Casting DC becomes Very Hard (DC +5).

If the result of your Spell Check is a fumble or blunder whilst defensive casting, you still provoke.

CASTING IN ARMOUR

Spellcasters usually shun armour, as its weight often proves a distraction to those not accustomed to it. Each different power source has its own unique relationship with armour. If a spell caster uses a spell whilst wearing prohibited armour, the DC of any spellcraft checks increases by the armours DR bonus x2.

ARCANE

Arcane spellcasters are prohibited from wearing any armour whilst casting.

DIVINITY

Divinity spellcasters may wear any armour whilst casting spells.

ETHEREAL

Ethereal spellcasters are prohibited from wearing heavy armour or wearing helmets whilst casting.

VERDANT

Verdant spellcasters are prohibited from wearing metal armour whilst casting.

The Transcend Armour feat can remove armour casting penalties.

SPELL ATTACK CHECKS

When casting an attack spell, a singular "Cast a Spell" check is made, and its outcome serves as the determining factor for both the act of spellcasting and the accuracy of the attack itself. Upon confirming the successful casting of the spell, the result of the "Cast a Spell" check seamlessly transitions into your attack roll, becoming the foundation for calculating your Attack Value (AV).

Assuming your attack spell's Cast a Spell check is successful, the established mechanics for hitting a target and critical hits (including their associated damage) mirror those of conventional attacks.

This means that attack spells are as equally adept at triggering critical hits, as their non-spell counterparts.

SAVING THROWS

Some spells require the target(s) to make a saving throw to resist or avoid their effects. Such spells us the following rules.

SPELL SAVE DC

The more complex the spell, the more difficult it is to resist its effects. To determine the Save DC of a spell use the following formula:

Save DC = 10 + PP Cost + Casting Ability Score + Other Modifiers

Be aware that warping a spells effect with additional PP increases the DC to resist its effects.

SAVE SPELL

When casting a Save spell, the target must make a Saving Throw to resist the effects of the spell. If the spell is cast successfully (see above), the target(s) must make a Saving Throw against the Spell DC (see above).

Basic Saving Throw

A save spell that inflicts damage may require a Basic Saving Throw and if this is the case, will follow the below format based upon the result of the targets saving throw:

Critical The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Partial The target takes full damage.

Failure As partial but the target also takes additional base damage and a critical based upon how much they fail by.

Save Failed By

Critical Severity

Bonus Damage

5-14

Minor

+1 base

15-24

Serious

+2 base

25+

Deadly

+3 base

RANGE, AREAS & TARGETS

There are three key elements to determine what a spell or ability (such as a breath weapon) can affect. Such things have varying ranges, can target, create areas, or manifest objects within those specific distances, ranging from a few feet to incredible distances spanning miles, continents, or beyond, allowing for a wide array of possibilities.

TOUCH RANGE

When casting a spell with a range of touch, you need to physically make contact with the target, using your unarmed reach to determine if you can reach them. If the target is unwilling, you must make an attack roll, using your Spellcraft Bonus. If the attack successfully lands, it doesn't cause any damage, but it triggers the spell's effects as intended.

TARGETS

Some spells require you to select a target. To successfully target a subject, it must be within the spell's designated range, and you should have the ability to perceive it either through sight or another primary sense. However, with the GM's approval, you may attempt to target a creature you cannot see by relying on your Perception skill. It's important to note that failing to target a particular creature does not affect how the spell impacts any other targets it might have.

Spells that have the potential to affect multiple creatures within an area possess both an Area entry, which describes the spell's range of influence, and a Targets entry, indicating the number or type of creatures it can directly affect. In cases where a spell has an area, but no specific targets listed, it typically affects all creatures within the designated area without discrimination.

Certain spells impose limitations that restrict you to willing targets, meaning the target must give consent for the spell's effects to take hold. A player can declare if their character is willing or unwilling at the time the spell is cast. This allows for flexibility in decision-making, enabling players to react and interact with spells even in challenging circumstances, such as when their character is paralyzed, unconscious, or even dead (GM discretion).

AREAS

Certain spells have the ability to impact an area, and while some spells may specify a particular defined area, most areas fall into the categories outlined below.

When casting a spell that affects an area, you have control over selecting the point from which the spell originates. However, beyond choosing the origin point, you have no direct control over which creatures or objects within the area will be affected by the spell. The spell's effects encompass all eligible targets within the designated area, leaving the outcome to the whims of fate.

A spell with an area can be a cone, line or radius. A diagram of areas is shown below. If the spell originates from your position, the spell has only an area; if you can cause the spell’s area to appear farther away from you, the spell has both a range and an area.

CONE

A cone-shaped spell can either be released from an intersection or side of your space. Examples of different cones are shown in the diagrams below.

LINE

A line-shaped spell can again be released from an intersection or side of your space. It starts from your space and extends to the limit of its range or until it strikes a barrier that blocks line of effect. A line-shaped spell affects all creatures in hexes that the line passes through.

RADIUS

A radius issues forth from each side of your space, extending out to a specified number of feet in all directions.

Be aware that because the sides of a target’s space are used as the starting point for the radius, a radius from a Huge or larger creature affects a greater overall area than that of a Large or smaller creature.

Emanation

A special type of radius which emanates from you (the caster) and moves with you.

LINE OF EFFECT

A line of effect is a straight, unblocked path that indicates what a spell can affect. A line of effect is cancelled by a solid barrier. It’s like line of sight for ranged weapons, except that it’s not blocked by fog, darkness, and other factors that limit normal sight.

You must have a clear line of effect to any target that you cast a spell on or to any space in which you wish to create an effect. You must have a clear line of effect to the point of origin of any spell you cast.

BREACH

An area effect spell will generally be blocked by solid objects and non-magical barriers. If a spell has the breach trait, it bypasses non-magical barriers and can counteract magical ones in an attempt to pass through them.

DISBELIEVING ILLUSIONS

The school of shadow creates a number of spells which are classed as illusions. If a spell specifically states that you may attempt to disbelieve it, then you can make a Will save or Sense Motive check against the DC of the spell with the following results:

Critical You can see through the effect completely and it is no longer visible to you.

Success You realise that the effect is not real, but can still perceive any applicable effects

Partial Something is off but you can’t quite place it, you can attempt to disbelieve again in one minute or some further information about the effect is discovered.

Failure What illusion, looks pretty real to you and you cannot attempt to disbelieve again unless you are provided with irrefutable evidence to prove it is false (such as an ally walking through an illusory wall).

Fumble As failure but you cannot attempt to disbelieve this illusion again.

DURATIONS

The duration of a spell refers to how long its effects persist, and spells with durations longer than an instant have a specified Duration entry. The duration can be measured in different units of time, such as turns, rounds, minutes, or more extended periods. For spells with a duration in rounds, the remaining rounds decrease by 1 at the start of each turn of the spellcaster until reaching 0 and ending the spell.

Certain spells can have ongoing effects that persist even after the spell's duration ends, and these effects are not considered magical themselves.

If a spellcaster dies or becomes incapacitated while a spell is still active, the spell continues until its duration expires.

SUSTAINED DURATION

A spell with a duration of “sustained”, is spell that requires an element of concentration from you each round. Sustained spells last until the end of your next turn. If however, you use the sustain action (see below), during your turn, you may extend the duration of the spell.

SUSTAIN A SPELL CONCENTRATE

Requirements You have at least one spell active with a sustained duration, and you are not fatigued.

Action Cost 1 AP

Choose one spell with a sustained duration you have in effect. The duration of that spell continues until the end of your next turn. Some spells might have slightly different or expanded effects if you sustain them. If you need to sustain a spell for 1 minute or longer you will need to make an exhaustion check as described in chapter 7, longer than 10 minutes (100 rounds) and you must expend the Power Points for the spell again (no check required) for every additional 10 minutes (or part thereof).

If your Sustain a Spell action is interrupted (by damage or some other variable), the spell immediately ends unless you make a Spell Concentration check.

Be aware that you cannot recover Power Points whilst you are sustaining a spell.

EXTENDED DURATIONS

If a spell’s duration says it lasts until your next daily preparations, you cannot regain the PP from casting the spell until it expires. If a spell has a duration of unlimited, you cannot regain the PP until the spell is dismissed.

DISMISSING

Certain spells possess the option of being dismissed before their full duration ends, allowing you to prematurely terminate their effects by using the Dismiss action.

DISMISS

CONCENTRATE

Action Cost 1 AP

You have the ability to bring an end to a specific spell effect or magic item effect. However, it is crucial to ensure that the effect in question is one that can be dismissed according to the rules and limitations outlined by the spell or item. Dismissal may result in either the complete termination of the effect or its cessation for specific targets, depending on the nature and specifications of the spell or item.

IDENTIFYING SPELLS

In certain situations, it becomes necessary to identify a spell, particularly when its effects are not immediately apparent. If you happen to observe the casting of a spell and have that specific spell in your repertoire, you can automatically identify it.

If you wish to identify a spell that is not in your repertoire, you must dedicate an action during your turn to attempt to identify it through Recall Knowledge. Visual manifestations or verbal casting components of a spell are usually what allow you to notice it being cast. However, if you aim to identify long-lasting spells already in effect, you need to use Identify Magic instead of Recall Knowledge since you do not have the advantage of witnessing the spell being cast.

Be aware that to actively identify a spell as it is being cast (rather than after it is cast) requires the Spell Recognition feat (see chapter 5).

SPELL WARPING

Some Spells may be Warped, which means that you can choose to cast them for a higher PP cost, obtaining a more powerful effect. There are two types of Warping option available to you which are Unique Warping Options and Metamagic Feats, both of these options are explained below.

UNIQUE WARPING OPTIONS

Many spells have Unique Warping Options in their description. Each unique Warping Option may be selected multiple times, unless the Spell description specifically prohibits doing so.

METAMAGIC FEATS

Metamagic Feats are a special kind of spellcasting feat which allow you to apply a generic warping option to any of your spells. Not all spells can be Warped with Metamagic Feats and this is usually due to the spell not having the required parameter to warp.

APPLYING WARPING OPTIONS

The final PP cost of a Warped Spell is equal to its Base PP cost, plus the PP cost of the Warping Options chosen.

You can only Warp a Spell to a PP cost that you could normally cast. In other words, you cannot use a Spell’s Warping Options to break any casting requirements. You can apply multiple warping options and the same option more than once if applicable.

Be aware that specific warping options which are detailed in a spells description always override the generic warping options provided by Metamagic feats, even if the generic option is better.

INNATE SPELLS

Certain spells are natural to your character, typically coming from your race or a magic item rather than your class. You can cast your innate spells even if you aren't a member of a spellcasting class. The ability that gives you an innate spell tells you how often you can cast it—usually once per day—and its magical tradition.

Innate spells are refreshed during your daily preparations.

Innate spells require no PP to cast, always require the base actions to cast and are always warped to the maximum treating your character level as their caster level, unless stated otherwise in their description.

INNATE ATTACK SPELLS

Some innate spells may require an attack roll. To determine your attack bonus with an innate spell, use the following formula:

Innate Attack Bonus = magical ability score + level.

Saros can cast Eldritch Touch as an arcane innate spell. Saros is level 6 and has an Intelligence of 3. His attack bonus with the spell is therefore +9.

INNATE SAVE SPELLS

Some innate spells may have a save DC. To determine your innate spell, save DC use the following formula:

Innate Save = 10 + magical ability score + level.

Saros also can cast Fear as an arcane innate spell. Saros is level 6 and has an Intelligence of 3. His save DC with the spell is therefore +19.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

Specialist spells are a focused branch of magic which uses slightly different game mechanics to that of normal spells.

The specialist spells which are available to you is determined by various character picks, primarily your class and secondly your archetype feats. You can learn specialist spells only through special class features or feats, rather than choosing them from a spell list.

Specialist spells are cast in the same way as normal spells with the following exceptions:

• Specialist spells are far easier to cast than other spells and are treated as having a casting difficulty of Very Easy (DC -5).

• The maximum amount of PP that can be utilised when casting a specialist spell is equal to your character level and not your caster level.

• Specialist spells with the attack trait have an attack bonus equal to your magical ability score + level or your spellcraft bonus, whichever is higher.

• Specialist spells with the save trait have a save DC. equal to your magical ability score + level +10 or your spellcraft bonus +10, whichever is higher.

Nyphari is a 6th level bard who casts the Inspire Courage specialist spell. As a 6th level bard, Nyphari has a caster level of 3 and a maximum PP per casting of 4. Because Inspire Courage is a specialist spell, the maximum amount of PP that Nyphari may expend upon the spell is 6 (her character level) and not 4.

HIGH MAGIC

High magic is an ancient form of magic which is available to very few casters. High magic is only available through the purchase of feats, by certain monsters and Classes such as the Magi, Warlock and Witch.

High Magic will be explored in more detail in future TRG supplements.

CONTROL LEVELS

Your character may have the ability to control or master other creatures. This can range from summoned creatures to created undead or dominated humanoids.

There is a limit to how many creatures may be controlled at any one time. This limit is called your control levels which determines how many levels of creatures you may control at any one time.

Your control levels are equal to the sum of your tradition attribute modifier, your character level and a bonus based upon your character class.

To determine how many control levels your character has refer to the following table

CONTROL LEVELS

Character Level

Magical ability score

Class

Modifier

Cleric, Druid, Wizard

+1 per level

Wizard (Conjurer, Enchanter)

+2 per level

Jamie McGregor is a 14th level crusader with a magical ability score of 5. She gains 14 control levels from her level, and another 5 from her ability score for a total of 19 control levels.

Avrok is a 7th Cleric with a tradition ability modifier of 4. He gains 14 (7+7) control levels from his character level and 4 from his ability score. This gives Avrok a total of 18 control levels.

You may have an amount of creature levels controlled at any one time equal to your control levels. If you exceed this amount then the highest-level creature that you currently have under your control can make a DC 20 Will saving throw every round to release itself. This process will continue until you have less than equal to your control levels under your control.

OVERCASTING

Normally, you're limited to casting spells with a Power Point (PP) cost equal to or lower than your caster level +1. However, there are situations where you can surpass this restriction through a process called overcasting. To initiate an overcasting attempt, you need sufficient PP to cast the spell. You must then opt for one of the following overcasting methods: Sacrifice or Magic Ritual.

SACRIFICE

It is possible to overcast a spell by sacrificing your own life force. To do this you make a Spellcraft check increasing the DC by 2 for each PP the spell exceeds your PP limit by. The spell is then resolved as normal.

When overcasting in this way you must make a Fortitude Saving throw using the PP cost of the spell as the attack level with any penalties to the Spellcraft check applied normally.

Heroic You gain Soul Drain 2d6.

Critical You gain Soul Drain 1d10+1 per PP above your normal maximum level.

Success You gain Soul Drain 2d10+2 per PP above your normal maximum level.

Failure You gain Soul Drain 4d10+4 per PP above your normal maximum level and also take a Serious Essence Critical.

Fumble You gain Soul Drain 5d10+5 per PP above your normal maximum level and also take a Deadly Essence Critical.

If your Hit Points are reduced to 0 or less by this damage you are completely consumed by the spell that you’re casting.

MAGIC RITUAL

You can choose to cooperate with one or more spell casters in a magic ritual in an attempt to Overcast a spell.

To begin a magic ritual, all characters that are involved must be willing and close enough to be able participate (this is usually within the range of the spell being attempted). One character must become the rituals primary caster. Any other characters involved in the ritual are classed as secondary casters. The primary caster of the ritual must know the spell that is being attempted or have some kind of written formula for it such as scroll or spellbook. The secondary casters must have the ability to cast spells (having a minimum caster level of 1).

A magic ritual permits the Primary caster to cast a spell of a number of PP higher than their normal maximum by 2 x the amount of secondary casters.

Quinn decides to utilise a ritual to overcast a spell with a PP cost 4 higher than his maximum. He will need to find at least two secondary casters to help him with this.

This magic ritual check is modified by the checks made by each of the Secondary casters.

Critical The Primary caster gains a +4-circumstance bonus to the Spellcraft check.

Success The Primary caster gains a +2-circumstance bonus to the Spellcraft check.

Failure The Primary caster takes a –4 circumstance penalty to the Spellcraft check.

Fumble The Primary caster takes a –10 circumstance penalty to the Spellcraft check.

The ritual is also subjected to a number of other modifiers.

RITUAL MODS

The final result is determined as a normal Spell Casting Check (see page 240), except that the maximum result is a success.

Should the Primary Caster obtain a failure, fumble or blunder on the Spell Casting Check, the ritual fails and all participants will be subject to the consequences.

SPELL DANGERS

Magic is not necessarily an exact science and will always come with certain risks. There are two potential areas of risk when manipulating magic, spell fumbles and resonance events.

SPELL FUMBLES

When dealing with the powers of the weave fumbling a spell can be extremely dangerous.

Whenever you roll a Fumble or Blunder result on a Spellcraft check to cast a spell, the spell automatically fails (missing its target if it was an attack) and you must roll a Top Open Ended percentile dice, adding any modifiers from the Spell Fumble Modifiers table.

This check is called a Spell Fumble check and uses the table below. The result of this Roll is then confronted with the Spell Failures Table, and its effects are immediately applied, substituting those of the Spell cast.

251-300

You summon a creature with an EL of your level +2. This creature has a diametrically opposed ethos to yours and remains for 1 rnd per PP of the spell. The creature attacks you and will do everything in its power to kill you.

301-350

You take a Deadly Critical, gain Fatigued 5 and the spell effects a random target within range at +50.

351+

You open a permanent gate to the Abyss and are promptly sucked through. You are then take a Deadly Critical and 8d12 damage...ouch.

RESONANCE EVENTS

When manipulating magic of any tradition, safety is a fleeting illusion. Even the most basic cantrips unleash a Resonance, a reverberation that disrupts the delicate tapestry of reality, beckoning the attention of foul and dark forces. Beware, for whenever you roll a 66 on a Spell Fumble or a Spell Critical Injury Result, you invoke a Resonance Event.

To determine the outcome of a Resonance Event, make a Top Open Ended percentile check, adding any modifiers from the Resonance Modifiers table.

CHAPTER 10 - GRIMOIRE

Magic shall be the undoing of our empire if we come to rely upon its wielders too much and yet without where are we, for surely, we cannot trust those accursed scientists.

SPELL DESCRIPTION

Spells are presented here in alphabetical order. Each spell has a few parameters which are explained below.

SPELL PARAMETERS

Each spell uses the following format. Entries appear only when applicable, so not all spells will have every entry described here.

SPELL NAME PP COST

TRAITS

Tradition This entry lists the applicable tradition for the spell.

Cast The amount of time it takes to cast the spell is listed here. If a spell costs an amount of AP to cast it will be represented by a number and then AP (2 AP).

Spells that can be cast as a Reaction are notated with an ‘R’ and Free actions with an ‘F’. Spells that take longer to cast list the time required, such as “1 minute.” After this, the spell's components are listed. If Casting the Spell has a cost, requirements, or a trigger, that information is also listed in this section. A cost includes any money, valuable materials, or other resources that must be expended to cast the spell.

Range, Area, and Targets This entry lists the range of the spell, the area it affects, and the targets it can affect, if any. If none of these entries are present, the spell affects only the caster.

If the area or range has a (B) next to it, the spell is considered to breach and bypasses barriers.

Saving Throw Some spells will allow the target to make a saving throw and if this is the case then this information will be presented here. Any details on the particular results and timing of the save appear in the text unless the entry specifies a basic saving throw.

Base Damage If a spell inflicts damage, the amount will be given in its description. Each damage inflicting spell will have a Base Damage Value which is used to determine additional damage when warping the spell and inflicting criticals.

Be aware that if a spell does not have a base damage entry, it’s damage is not increased by factors which increase base damage.

Duration Most spells have a fixed duration which is measured in rounds, minutes, hours or some other increment of time.

If a spell has no duration entry, then its effects happen and wink out in a fraction of an instant.

If the spell has a duration of ‘Sustained’ it may be maintained with an action each round (see chapter 7).

If a spell has an (S) after its duration the spell does not end if it is not sustained but has no effect for the current round.

If a spell has a (D) after its duration the spell may be dismissed (see chapter 7).

Warping Available Warping Options (along with the number of additional PP required) are listed right after the Spell’s description. Unless specified otherwise, each Warping Option can be selected multiple times.

Any warping option with this font colour replaces the core function of the spell with a new effect. When this warping option is applied, the base version of the spell is replaced and no longer takes effect.

If a spell has an applicable variable, you may apply any of the Metamagic feat options found in Chapter 7.

Be aware that specific warping options which are detailed in a spells description always override the Metamagic warping options in Chapter 9, even if the Metamagic option is better.

In some cases, a spell will gain an automatic enhancement if you warp it to a certain level of power. This is notated as follows:

PP #

Caster Level Modifications If this option is present in a spell description it details any automatic enhancements a spell gains as your caster level increases. Such modifications are determined as follows:

Caster Level # The spell gains a new option at the stated Caster Level.

So, Caster Level 4+ would indicate that the modifier is applied at caster level 4 and every 4 caster levels thereafter.

ABJURERS STRIKE PP 18

UTILITY WARDING

Tradition arcane, divinity, ethereal

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets 1 weapon

Duration 1 minute

You touch a weapon granting it wondrous power for a short period of time. For the duration of the spell the weapon treats all targets as unarmoured and ignores all magical bonuses to DB.

If this spell is cast upon a missile weapon, then it affects the ammunition that is fired from it.

ACID ARROW PP 8

ACID ATTACK INVOCATION

Tradition arcane, verdant

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 60 feet; Targets 1 creature

Base Damage 1d8; Duration Sustained (1 minute)

You imbue one of your hands with acidic energy. As part of casting the spell you launch an arrow of acid at one target within range which inflicts 3d8 acid damage and 1d4 recurring damage. At the beginning of each turn, you may Sustain the Spell to make an Attack action using your Spellcraft skill to launch an additional arrow of acid at one target within range.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: The damage increases by 1d8 and the recurring damage by 1.

ACID BOLT PP 4

ACID ATTACK INVOCATION

Tradition arcane, verdant

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 creature

Base Damage 1d6

You unleash a crackling bolt of corrosive acid that streaks toward your target with destructive force. If you hit, you deal 4d6 acid damage plus 2 splash acid damage and on a critical hit, the target also takes 1 recurring acid damage.

ACID CLOUD PP 12

ACID PENETRATING SAVE TRANSLOCATION

Tradition arcane, verdant

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 120 feet

Area fog spreads in 20-ft. radius, 20 ft. high

If the stored spell originally targeted one or more creatures, it will now specifically target the creature that triggered the glyph. Similarly, if the stored spell had an area of effect, that area will centre itself on the creature that activated the glyph. The spell ends immediately upon its activation.

The glyph functions as a magical trap, employing your spell DC for both the Perception check required to notice it and the Thievery check needed to disable it.

It attacks as a broadsword inflicting force damage using your Spellcraft bonus for attack purposes.

MAGIC JAR PP 12

ESSENCE EVIL SAVE SOUL

Tradition arcane

Cast 1 minute (focus, somatic, verbal)

Range 120 feet; Targets 1 living creature

Duration 8 hours; Saving Throw Will Negates

By casting magic jar, you place your soul in a gem or large crystal (known as the magic jar), leaving your body lifeless. Then you can attempt to take control of a nearby body, forcing its soul into the magic jar. You may move back to the jar (thereby returning the trapped soul to its body) and attempt to possess another body. The spell ends when you send your soul back to your own body, leaving the receptacle empty. To cast the spell, the magic jar must be within spell range, and you must know where it is, though you do not need line of sight or line of effect to it. When you transfer your soul upon casting, your body is, as near as anyone can tell, dead.

While in the magic jar, you can sense and attack any life force within 100 feet. You do need line of effect from the jar to the creatures. You cannot determine the exact creature types or positions of these creatures.

Attempting to possess a body is a 3 AP concentrate action. It is blocked by circle of protection or a similar ward. You possess the body and force the creature’s soul into the magic jar unless the subject succeeds on a Will save. Failure to take over the host leaves your life force in the magic jar, and the target automatically succeeds on further saving throws if you attempt to possess its body again.

If you are successful, your life force occupies the host body, and the host’s life force is imprisoned in the magic jar. You keep your mental ability scores, level, class, skills, loyalties, and mental abilities. The body retains its physical ability scores, HP, natural abilities, and automatic abilities.

As a 1 AP action, you can shift freely from a host to the magic jar if within range, sending the trapped soul back to its body. The spell ends when you shift from the jar to your own body.

If the host body is slain, you return to the magic jar, if within range, and the life force of the host departs (it is dead). If the host body is slain beyond the range of the spell, both you and the host die. Any life force with nowhere to go is treated as slain.

If the spell ends while you are in the magic jar, you return to your body (or die if your body is out of range or destroyed). If the spell ends while you are in a host, you return to your body (or die, if it is out of range of your current position), and the soul in the magic jar returns to its body (or dies if it is out of range). Destroying the receptacle ends the spell, and the spell can be dispelled at either the magic jar or the host’s location.

TRANSLOCATION UTILITY

Tradition arcane, ethereal

Cast 1 minute (material, somatic, verbal)

Range touch

Targets you and up to 5 willing creatures touched

Duration 8 hours (D)

You and the creatures you touch are transported along a coiling path of shadow, reaching the edge where the Material Plane meets the Plane of Shadow. Although the effect is mostly illusory, the path itself has a quasi-real nature.

Due to the blurred reality between the two planes, you cannot discern specific details of the terrain or areas you pass over during the journey. It is also impossible to accurately predict where your travel will conclude. This makes the spell unsuitable for scouting or spying purposes. Additionally, when the spell effect ends, the targets appear roughly 1 mile from their intended location on the Material Plane.

SPECIALIST SPELLS

Specialist spells are granted by your race, character class and archetype feats. Their descriptions follow the same format as normal spells as discussed at the beginning of this chapter with the exception that a magical tradition is not provided as this will always be based upon your primary tradition.

Each of the spells will have at least one trait relating to a race, class or archetype.

If you initiate hostile actions against the target, the spell immediately ends. After the spell ends, the target may not realize that they were charmed unless your subsequent interactions or actions contradict their expectations, allowing you to maintain a friendship through normal means.

DETECT SIGNATURE PP 1

INSIGHT UTILITY WIZARD

Cast 3 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 50 feet; Targets 1 active spell

Duration 1 minute

You detect the signature of any active spell. This only tells you the class of who cast the spell, not who they are, or any other information. Each caster has a unique signature, so you will always be able to differentiate between the signature of one spell caster and another without needing to make any checks. This spell has several unique warping options.

Trace Signature – This allows you to track the caster of a specific signature detected by this spell. For you, it is as if you are following a trail of phosphorescent light between the detected spell and its caster. The actual tracking of this trail is accomplished by making a Very Easy (-5 DC) Tracking skill check with a difficulty equal to the level of the caster. For every two hours since the casting of the spell being traced, the DC is increased one step, to a maximum of Incredibly Hard (+10).

Detect Expired Spell – This allows you to detect a spell whose duration has already expired. You will detect any expired spells within a 10' radius, and you may search a different 10' radius within range each round.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: per additional piece of information about the spell.
