You emit a radiant aura of protective magic that envelops you and your allies. Within the area, you all benefit from a +1-status bonus to your DB. You can Sustain the Spell each round to extend the radius of the aura by 5 feet, up to a maximum of 30 feet.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: status bonus increases by 1 (max +5).

PROTECTOR’S SPHERE PP 7

UTILITY WARDING WIZARD

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Area 15-foot radius

Duration sustained up to 1 minute

A shielding aura radiates from you, providing protection to both you and your allies. You gain Physical Resistance (adamantine). Furthermore, any ally within the area of effect also gains this resistance.

WARPING OPTIONS

+6 PP: The resistance also applies against adamantine.

+10 PP: The resistance applies against all damage.

PURGE THE UNLIFE PP 7

CLERIC ESSENCE SAVE SOUL

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Area 30-foot cone

Saving Throw Basic Fortitude

Base Damage 1d12

You unleash a torrent of divine energy that severs the unholy ties of undeath. Each undead creature within the area takes 4d12 essence damage.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase damage by 1d12.

QUICK TIME PP 1

BARD COMPOSITION EMOTION ENCHANTMENT UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Area 60-foot radius

Duration sustained (1 minute)

You move with a spirited rhythm, quickening the pace of your allies' movement. Both you and all allies in the area gain a +10-foot status bonus to all Speeds for 1 round.

RADIANT AEGIS PP 1

ALIGNED AURA CRUSADER LIGHT UTILITY WARDING

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Area 10-foot emanation

Duration Sustained (1 minute)

A halo of energy appears around which grants your allies a +1-status bonus to DB against attacks made by creatures with an opposing aura type to your own.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase the radius by 10-foot (max 50 feet).

+3 PP: increase the bonus by +1 (max +5).

REAPER’S RESONANCE PP 1

CLERIC EVIL SOUL UTILITY

Cast R (verbal)

Trigger A creature within 20 feet of you dies or is destroyed (in the case of an undead).

Duration 1 minute

The essence of the departed creature heals your wounds. You gain a surge of vitality, healing HP equal to the level of the triggering creature plus 5. If the triggering creature was undead, the amount healed is doubled.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: for every 5 HP healed (round down), you may also reduce any bleeding damage by 1.

REINCARNATED EMBRACE PP 7

CLERIC HEALING ESSENCE SOUL UTILITY

Cast 10 minutes (material, somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets 1 dead animal, beast, humanoid, plant or wyrm creature.

You retrieve the soul of a recently dead creature and restore it to life in a different form. As the spell is completed, the dead body of the creature (which must be present and intact), is returned to life but its physical form changes to that of a different creature of the same type. The creature’s race changes completely for the purpose of game mechanics, but all existing feats (racial or otherwise) remain the same.

This spell can only revive a creature that has been dead for less than an hour. Once reincarnated, the creature initially has no memory of anything that has occurred within the last 24 hours and has no PP or spells memorised. Memories, PP and spells return upon the next daily preparation.

Be aware that if a character chooses to not be returned to life, the spell has no effect.

RENEWAL’S TOUCH PP 7

CLERIC ESSENCE SOUL UTILITY

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets 1 living creature

Duration 1 minute

You imbue the target with restorative healing energy, allowing them to use that energy to heal their wounds. Upon casting the spell, the target is immediately healed of 2d8+16 HP. Additionally, at the beginning of each of the targets turns, it may choose to use one of the following effects for 2 AP (concentrate):

• Heal 1d8+8 HP

• Stop 1 point of bleeding

• Reduce the fatigued condition by 1

• As part of a recovery check (Free Action) ignore fumble and blunder results

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase the healing by 1d8+8.

+2 PP: target may reduce bleeding by an additional 1.

+2 PP: the target may also reduce the injured condition by 1 or the dazed and weakened conditions by 2.

+2 PP: reduce the fatigued condition (or another condition if you have used that option) by an additional 1.

+4 PP: the target may also reduce the soul drain condition by 5.

RESILIENT FORTITUDE PP 7

CLERIC UTILITY WARDING

Cast R (somatic); Trigger An attack or effect would deal damage to you.

Your indomitable might blends with divine energy to shield you. You gain resistance against the triggering attack or effect.

WARPING OPTIONS

+10 PP: you instead gain immunity.

REVEALING GLANCE PP 7

CLERIC INSIGHT REVELATION UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Area 30-foot radius

Duration 1 round

Your divine insight pierces through illusions, revealing the truth beneath. The GM makes a secret counteract check against each illusion partially within the area. Instead of counteracting the illusion, you gain the ability to see through it, perceiving the true nature of what lies hidden (e.g., seeing through an illusory disguise spell to reveal the creature's true form without ending the illusion).

The area of revelation moves with you throughout the duration of the spell, and the GM makes a secret counteract check whenever a new illusion enters the area.

WARPING OPTIONS

+5 PP: You can allow everyone to see through illusions you succeed against, not just yourself.

REVELATION DIVINE PP 1

ADVANTAGE CLERIC INSIGHT UTILITY

Cast R (verbal)

Trigger You attempt a Search (Perception) check, or you attempt a skill check to Recall Knowledge with a skill you're trained in.

With a brief prayer and the guidance of your deity, you tap into the vast well of divine knowledge that surrounds you. When you trigger this spell, your connection to your deity grants you divine revelation, enhancing your ability to uncover information. You gain advantage on the triggering check.

SACRIFICING SHIELD PP 1

UTILITY WARDING WIZARD

Cast R (somatic)

Range 30 feet

You shield your ally by absorbing their wounds. The HP damage that would have been inflicted upon them is reduced by 5. However, you absorb this damage instead, and any immunities, weaknesses, or resistances you possess do not come into effect.

Be aware that you only absorb HP damage with this spell and suffer no effects from any other part of the attack.

WARPING OPTIONS

+1 PP: damage you redirect increases by 1.

+2 PP: you may also absorb any condition that the target suffers.

SEARING BURST PP 7

DRUID ELEMENTAL INVOCATION SAVE

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 120 feet; Area 20-foot radius

Saving Throw Basic Reflex

Base Damage 1d8

You cause the area of effect to become charged with elemental energy. When you cast this spell, select an element type from the following: acid, cold, electricity or fire. There must be an appropriate element for you to draw upon as follows:

Acid – Solid or packed earth that you are in contact with.

Cold – Packed snow or ice. If the air temperature is less than -5C you can draw the energy from the air.

Electricity – You must outdoors and the weather must be overcast.

Fire – You must be able to draw upon an open flame.

All creatures within the area of effect take 5d8 damage of the appropriate element type.

SEER’S VISION PP 1

CHANCE CONCENTRATE INSIGHT UTILITY WIZARD

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 willing living creature

Duration until the end of your next turn

You glimpse the targets near future, foreseeing a pivotal moment. Roll a d20 and record the result. When the target attempts a non-secret saving throw or skill check, they may use the recorded number instead of rolling, ending the spell. Casting this spell again immediately cancels any active instance of Seer’s Vision.

SHIFTING FORM PP 7

ALTERATION MORPH UTILITY WIZARD

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Duration 1 minute (D)

You change your form in a minor way, gaining one of the following abilities:

• A +20-foot status bonus to your Speed.

• A climb or swim Speed equal to half your Speed.

• Darkvision.

• Gain a pair of claws. These are medium, agile finesse unarmed attacks that inflict slashing damage.

• Scent.

SHIFTING STEP PP 1

CLERIC SHADOW UTILITY

Cast R (somatic)

Trigger An enemy misses you with a melee attack.

Duration until the end of your next turn

You move and enshroud yourself in shadow. You Step and become concealed.

SICKLY RAY PP 1

ATTACK SOUL WIZARD

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 living creature

A sickly green ray of energy is released from your outstretched palm. The result of your attack determines the outcome of the spell.

Critical Inflicted The target becomes sickened 2 and slowed 1 as long as it's sickened.

Hit for Damage The target becomes sickened 1.

Miss The target is unaffected.

This spell inflicts no actual HP damage.

SILENT BINDING PP 1

CLERIC SAVE WARDING

Cast 2 AP (material, somatic)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 creature

Saving Throw Fortitude; Duration varies

You impose a binding silence upon the target, preventing it from divulging important information. While under this spell's effect, the target can still speak and perform verbal spell components, but its whispers are muffled, making them inaudible to creatures more than 10 feet away without a successful Perception check against your spell DC. This also interferes with auditory and linguistic effects, as well as communication. The duration of the spell depends on the target's Fortitude save.

Critical The target is unaffected.

Success The duration is 1 round.

Failure The duration is 1 minute.

Fumble The duration is 10 minutes.

SONG OF DESPAIR PP 1

BARD COMPOSITION ENCHANTMENT FEAR UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Area 30-foot emanation

Duration sustained (1 minute)

Foes within the area are filled with a deep sense of despair, causing them to be afflicted with fear. They become frightened 1 and cannot reduce their frightened condition below 1 as long as they remain within the area.

SOOTHING BALLAD PP 13

BARD COMPOSITION EMOTION ENCHANTMENT HEALING UTILITY

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets you and up to 9 allies

You use the power of performance to soothe the ailments of your allies:

• The spell attempts to counteract fear effects on the targets.

• The spell attempts to counteract effects imposing paralysis on the targets.

• The spell restores 8d8 HP to the targets.

• The spell lowers the severity of one Injury (only once per injury) by 1.

WARPING OPTIONS

+1 PP: : when used to heal, soothing ballad restores 1d8 more HP.

SOOTHING WORDS PP 1

CLERIC DRUID EMOTION ENCHANTMENT

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 ally

Duration 1 round

You calm the target with your simple prayers or words. The target gains a +1-status bonus to Will saving throws. This bonus increases to +2 against emotion effects.

In addition, when you Cast this Spell, you can attempt to counteract one emotion effect on the target.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: bonus to saves increases by +1 (max +4).

SPELL STORING PP 1

UTILITY WARDING WIZARD

Cast 1 minute (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets your arcane bond

Duration until next daily preparation

The next spell that you cast within one round is stored in your Mage Staff. The stored Spell has no immediate effect (other than of being stored), but you can then release the spell at any time for 1 AP.

You may only have one spell stored in your staff at any one time and if you cast the spell again the last spell you stored is dismissed.

WARPING OPTIONS

+4 PP: the stored spell is released as a reaction, the specifics of which you must determine when casting.

+8 PP: the stored spell is released as a free action.

SPIRIT OF THE HUNT PP 1

RANGER SOUL UTILITY

Cast 1 minute (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets 1 living target

Duration 10 minutes

A spirit animal blesses the targets senses granting advantage on Search (Perception) checks for the duration.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: also gain advantage on Track (Survival) checks.

+2 PP: target an additional creature.

SPOIL THE PROFANE PP 1

ALIGNED CRUSADER SOUL UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Range touch; Targets a weapon you are currently wielding

Immediately after casting the spell, make a melee or ranged weapon Strike against a creature within range. On a hit, in addition to normal damage the target becomes weakened 1 until the beginning of your next turn. If the target has an opposing aura, it also takes 1d6 secondary aligned damage.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase secondary damage by 1d6 (max 5d6).

+3 PP: increase the weakened by 1 (max +5).

STASIS PP 7

ALTERATION CLERIC SAVE

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 creature or up to 10 lbs of objects

Saving Throw Will; Duration varies

Time freezes in its tracks around a chosen object or creature, rendering it immobile. The target must make a Will save to resist this effect. An inanimate object that is unattended automatically fumbles its save.

Critical The target is unaffected.

Success The target is stunned 1 as time thickens around it.

Failure Time comes to a complete halt for the target for 1 round. During this period, the target becomes impervious to all forms of damage and cannot be targeted by anything. No rounds pass for any timed effects, conditions, afflictions, or other ongoing effects that may affect the target. While in this state of stasis, the target becomes immovable, defying even the forces of gravity.

Fumble As failure, but the target is held in stasis for 3 rounds. At the end of each of its turns, it can attempt a new save to reduce the remaining duration by 1 round or end it entirely on a critical.

SURGE OF THE TEMPEST PP 1

AIR DRUID ELECTRICITY INVOCATION SAVE

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 creature

Saving Throw Reflex

Base Damage 1d12

You envelop your target in a tempest of raging winds, turbulent clouds, and electrifying lightning. The storm unleashes a surge of electrical energy, dealing 1d12 damage. The target must make a basic Reflex save to partially avoid the effects. In the event of a fumble, the target is not only struck with the damaging electricity but also becomes temporarily dazzled for 1 round and suffers from 1 recurring electricity damage.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: The initial damage increases by 1d12, and the recurring electricity damage on a fumble increases by 1.

SWIFT SONATA PP 1

BARD COMPOSITION EMOTION ENCHANTMENT UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Range 30 feet; Targets 1 ally

Duration sustained (1 minute)

Your performance infuses the target with a surge of rhythmic energy, enhancing their speed. The target becomes quickened and can use the additional action to Strike, Stride, or Step.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: affect an additional ally.

TALON STRIKE PP 1

RANGER INVOCATION UTILITY

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets a weapon you are currently wielding

Duration 1 minute

Your attacks with the target weapon tear at the target with the ferocity of a wild animal inflicting 1d6 secondary slashing damage.

WARPING OPTIONS

+4 PP: increase the secondary damage to 2d6.

TOUCH OF OBEDIENCE PP 1

CLERIC ENCHANTMENT MENTAL SAVE

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Range touch; Targets 1 living creature

Saving Throw Will; Duration varies

With your commanding touch, you corrode the essence of the target, weakening its resistance to manipulation. The target must make a Will saving throw to resist your influence.

Critical The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes a -1-status penalty to Will saves until the end of your current turn.

Failure The target takes a -1-status penalty to Will saves until the end of your next turn.

Fumble The target takes a -2-status penalty to Will saves for 1 minute.

TOUCH OF UNDEATH PP 1

CLERIC ESSENCE SAVE SOUL

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Range touch; Targets 1 living creature

Saving Throw Fortitude

Base Damage 1d6

You sap the targets lifeforce, dealing 1d6 essence damage. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage, and a minor critical.

Fumble The target takes double damage, and a light critical.

TRUTHFUL WORDS PP 1

CLERIC INSIGHT UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Duration sustained (1 minute)

You confidently speak a truthful statement, devoid of any intention to deceive or manipulate. The statement must be concise, consisting of no more than 25 words. As you speak, a radiant symbol of your deity appears above you, signifying your sincere belief in the statement's truth. Those who witness this display know that you believe your words to be true.

Each time you Sustain this Spell, you can repeat this effect.

UMBRAL VEIL PP 1

DARKNESS INVOCATION UTILITY WIZARD

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Range touch; Targets 1 willing creature

Duration 1 minute

You enshroud the target in a swirling mantle of shadows, obscuring their presence and making it harder for others to see. Within a 20-foot emanation centred on the target, the illumination level is reduced by three steps (to a minimum of 2).

By using a 1 AP (Interact) action, the target can remove the cloak of shadows and leave it behind as a decoy, where it continues to diminish the light for the remaining duration of the spell. If someone retrieves the cloak after the original target discards it, the cloak dissipates, and the spell abruptly ends.

UNITY PP 7

CHANCE CLERIC UTILITY WARDING

Cast R (verbal)

Trigger You and 1 or more allies within range are targeted by a spell or ability that allows a saving throw.

Range 30 feet

Targets each ally targeted by the triggering spell

You release a wave of energy which engulfs your allies, granting them your innate resistance. Each ally can use your saving throw modifier instead of its own against the triggering spell. Each ally decides individually which modifier to use.

UNLIVING VITALITY PP 7

CLERIC ESSENCE EVIL SOUL UTILITY

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Range touch; Targets 1 willing undead creature

Duration 1 minute

You revitalize an undead creature, granting it natural healing. The target is granted fast healing 5, for the duration of the spell.

WARPING OPTIONS

+1 PP: The fast-healing increases by 1 (max 10).

VEILED PRESENCE PP 1

CLERIC SHADOW UTILITY VISUAL

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Duration 1 minute

As you merge into a crowd of similar beings, your features blend into a faceless visage. Your appearance becomes indistinct and unremarkable. You gain a +2-status bonus to Deception and Stealth checks, allowing you to seamlessly blend into the crowd and go unnoticed. Additionally, you effortlessly navigate through the crowd, ignoring any difficult terrain it may present.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase the bonus by 1 (max +5).

VEILED SECRET PP 7

MENTAL UTILITY WARDING WIZARD

Cast 1 minute (somatic, verbal)

Range 10 feet

Targets you and any number of willing allies

Duration 1 hour

You hide a secret, ensuring its protection from prying spies. Select a specific piece of information known by at least some of the targets. It is essential that the targeted creature remains within range for the full minute while you cast the spell. Those who possess the chosen knowledge gain a +4-status bonus to skill checks, to effectively conceal the secret. Additionally, they receive the same bonus to saving throws against spells that specifically aim to extract the knowledge and any effects that attempt to coerce its disclosure.

If you cast this spell again, any previous Veiled Secret spell you had cast will be nullified, and its effects will cease.

VERDANT SNARE PP 1

ALTERATION RANGER UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Range 30 feet; Area 10-ft radius

Roots and vines lash out, creating natural difficult terrain until the start of your next turn.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase the radius by 10-feet (max 50- feet).

+3 PP: duration becomes 1 minute.

VIBRANT THORNS PP 1

ALTERATION CLERIC DRUID MORPH PLANT UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Duration 1 minute

Your body grows thorny brambles, which exact a toll on those who dare to strike you, while also thriving on the essence of life magic. Whenever a creature adjacent to you or a creature that hits you with an unarmed attack lands a melee blow, they suffer 1 piercing damage. Furthermore, whenever you cast an essence spell, the potency of your thorns intensifies, inflicting 1d6 damage on those who come into contact with them until the beginning of your next turn.

WARPING OPTIONS

+4 PP: The damage increases by 1, or 1d6 after you cast a essence spell.

VIGILANT EYE PP 7

INSIGHT UTILITY WIZARD

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Range 500 feet

Duration 1 hour

You create an invisible floating eye at a location within range. When created, this eye must be in your line of sight. The eye can't move, but you can see in all directions from that point as if using your normal visual senses.

When the spell's duration ends, you can spend 2 PP as a free action to extend the duration for another hour, though as normal, it ends immediately during your next daily preparations.

WAR CRY PP 7

CLERIC INVOCATION SONIC UTILITY

Cast R (verbal)

Trigger An ally within range inflicts a critical strike with a melee weapon

Range 30 feet; Targets the triggering ally

Your deific cry imbues your ally’s weapon with power. The weapon used to make the Strike deals an additional 1d6 sonic damage and the ally can immediately attempt an additional attack against the same target as a free action using their current multiple attack penalty.

WARPED TERRAIN PP 1

SHADOW UTILITY VISUAL WIZARD

Cast 1 AP+ (somatic, verbal)

Range 60 feet; Area 5-foot radius or more

Duration 1 minute

You conjure illusory hazards that cover the ground. These illusions create false hazards, causing any creature that traverses them to perceive the area as difficult terrain. However, a creature can attempt to disbelieve the illusion by using a Search action or other means of interacting with it. If successful, the creature sees through the deception and can move through the area unaffected for the remaining duration of the spell.

By investing additional actions while casting the spell, you can expand the radius of the illusion. Each extra AP spent increases the radius by 5 feet, allowing you to extend the deceptive terrain up to a maximum of 10 extra feet when utilizing 3 AP.

WARPING OPTIONS

+6 PP: : you can make the illusion appear in the air rather than on a surface, causing it to function as difficult terrain for flying creatures.

WASH AWAY SIN PP 1

ALIGNED CRUSADER ESSENCE HEALING SAVE SOUL

Cast 2 AP (somatic, verbal)

Area 15-foot cone

Saving Throw Basic Will

Base Damage 1d6

Allies in the cone regain 1d8 HP and gain +1 status bonus to saves vs. fear and disease until the start of your next turn.

Creatures with an opposed aura take 1d6 essence damage.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase both the healing and damage by 1 die.

+4 PP: cone increases to 30-feet.

WEAPON SURGE PP 1

CLERIC INVOCATION UTILITY

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Range touch; Targets 1 weapon you're wielding

You imbue your weapon with divine energy. On your next Strike with that weapon before the start of your next turn, you gain a +1-status bonus to the attack roll, and the weapon deals an additional die of damage.

If the target weapon leaves your possession, weapon surge immediately ends.

WELLSPRING OF VALOUR PP 1

ALIGNED AURA CRUSADER HEALING UTILITY WARDING

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Area 20-foot emanation

Duration Sustained (1 minute)

You create an aura of vitality which grants allies a +1-status bonus to attack rolls vs any creatures of an opposed aura.

Whenever an ally in the aura first takes damage each round, they regain 1d6 HP from the wellspring’s restorative flow.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: increase the radius by 10-foot (max 50 feet).

+4 PP: increase the bonus by +1 and the healing by 1d6.

WILD MORPH PP 1

ALTERATION DRUID MORPH

Cast 1 AP (somatic)

Duration 1 minute

You draw upon your Wildshape power, altering a portion of your physical form. You gain a single natural attack form from one of your Studied Targets.

WARPING OPTIONS

+2 PP: You gain an additional natural attack form (max 3).

+2 PP: You instead gain a movement type from one of your Studied Targets.

+4 PP: instead gain special ability from one of your Studied Targets.

If this spell is used to gain an ability from a creature that you would not normally gain whilst you are wildshaped into its form, the duration of this spell changes to that of your Wildshape ability.

WIZARD STRIKE PP 1

ADVANTAGE INSIGHT WIZARD

Cast 1 AP (verbal)

Duration until the end of your turn

A fleeting glimpse into the future grants’ certainty to your next strike, ensuring its accuracy. The next time you make an attack check before the end of your turn, the attack gains advantage.

ZEALOUS BATTLECRY PP 7

CLERIC CHANCE EMOTION ENCHANTMENT UTILITY

Cast R (verbal)

Trigger You and at least 1 ally are about to roll initiative.

Range 10 feet; Targets you and the triggering ally

You ignite the flames of righteous anger within yourself and a chosen ally. Both you and the target ally roll a d100, and the higher result is used for determining initiative rolls.

CHAPTER 11 – MAGIC ITEMS

The cloaked sorcerer knelt among the shattered stones of the forgotten citadel; his fingers blackened with dust and time. Each fragment he turned over, each crumbling stair he descended, brought him closer to the prize whispered of in forbidden tomes. He could feel it—its pulse, like a heartbeat in the void—calling to him through centuries of silence.

Magic items are a crucial aspect of any fantasy roleplaying game, adding depth and excitement to the gameplay. They bring a touch of enchantment and can bestow fascinating and unique abilities, even upon characters who are not inherently magical.

In TRG, magical items serve as valuable rewards for the daring exploits and courageous acts of your character. Whether earned through bravery or acquired through foolhardiness (depending on one's perspective), these items are often discovered in treacherous dungeons or obtained from the lairs of defeated creatures. They grant you extraordinary capabilities that would be otherwise unattainable, or they enhance existing skills in extraordinary ways.

This chapter delves into the rules governing the utilization of magical items, shedding light on their mechanics and how they interact with other facets of the game. By delving into this knowledge, you can fully appreciate the wonders and intricacies of these mystical artifacts.

INVESTMENT

Some items hold incredible power, but their secrets cannot be unlocked without forming a unique connection. This bond, known as Investment, is essential for fully harnessing the potential of these magical artifacts. When an item possesses such a requirement, it is marked with the Invested trait, signifying the need for a personal connection between the bearer and the item itself.

Without becoming invested to an item, you can only use its most basic or non-magical functions. Items that provide a static bonus will still function without investment (unless stated otherwise in the individual items description).

Each character can benefit from three invested items at 1st level. You gain a bonus to the amount of items that you can invest equal to your spellcasting ability score. At 5th level and then every 5 levels thereafter, you may invest an additional item.

Mikhail is a 1st level cleric with a Wisdom Ability modifier of +2. This means that Mikhail can invest a maximum of 5 items per day.

Be aware that if an item has multiple invested traits, you only need to use one investment slot to use all of the item’s capabilities.

To invest an item, you must use the Invest Item action.

INVEST ITEM CONCENTRATE Requirements You have an item with the invested trait that has not been invested by another character in the last 24 hours.You spend 10 minutes investing your energy into a magical item. Once you’ve Invested the Item, you benefit from its constant magical abilities as long as you meet its other requirements. Your investment to the item ends if you no longer satisfy prerequisites, if the item is more than 100 feet away from you for at least 24 hours, if you die, or if another creature successfully invests the item (assuming you have not invested it). You can also voluntarily end investment by using this action. Be aware that you must have knowledge of the items functionality before you can invest it. This can be by identifying the item yourself, or another character who has identified the item explaining its abilities.INVEST ITEM CONCENTRATE Requirements You have an item with the invested trait that has not been invested by another character in the last 24 hours.You spend 10 minutes investing your energy into a magical item. Once you’ve Invested the Item, you benefit from its constant magical abilities as long as you meet its other requirements. Your investment to the item ends if you no longer satisfy prerequisites, if the item is more than 100 feet away from you for at least 24 hours, if you die, or if another creature successfully invests the item (assuming you have not invested it). You can also voluntarily end investment by using this action. Be aware that you must have knowledge of the items functionality before you can invest it. This can be by identifying the item yourself, or another character who has identified the item explaining its abilities.

USING MAGIC ITEMS

Using a magic item’s properties might mean wearing or wielding it. A magic item meant to be worn must be donned in the intended fashion: boots go on the feet, gloves on the hands, hats and helmets on the head and rings on the finger. Magic armour must be donned, a shield strapped to the arm, a cloak fastened about the shoulders. A weapon must be held.

The majority of magic items can be utilised by small, medium and large creatures with little issue. Magic rings and other items that are worn on the body will usually resize to the wielder (that’s a Kind of Magic). Not all items will follow this process, however. Armour, shields and weapons will only resize if a specific resizing rune has been applied to them first (see runes).

As with all things, your GM has the final say on what can and cannot be resized.

ITEMS & INNATE SPELLS

If a magic item allows you to use an innate spell, the level used to determine the DC and attack check of the item is determined by the items level and not yours.

DUPLICATE ITEMS

You will not normally be allowed to wear two items of the same type and gain their benefits. So you would not be able to gain the magical benefits of two different sets of magical boots or gloves.

Items such as rings can be worn on multiple fingers (and even toes if your GM allows it), but you must adhere to the rules for Bonus Types which can be found in the Appendixes.

Any item that comes as part of a pair (such as gloves) only impart their benefits if both items are worn.

Your GM may also deem that certain items malfunction if you choose to use one half of a paired magical item instead of failing outright.

ACTIVATING MAGIC ITEMS

Some magical items require you to carry out an action of some kind to activate them. Other items provide a constant modifier or perhaps an additional modifier when activated as well.

Using a magic item is similar to casting a spell in that it requires a specific action; this is the activate item action.

ACTIVATE ITEM

Requirements The item must be invested by you. If the item requires you to Interact with it, you must be wielding it (if it’s a held item) or touching it with a free hand (if it’s another type of item).

You call forth the effect of an item by properly activating it. This is a special activity that takes a variable number of actions, as listed in the item’s stat block.

ACTIVATE ACTIONS

Each magic item will have an activation entry if it requires such. There are a number of different activation components which add the indicated traits to the Activate Item action.

Some of these actions have already been covered in other areas of the book but are duplicated here for consistency.

COMMAND

AUDITORY CONCENTRATE

The item has a command word which must be spoken to activate it. The command word will be discovered when the item is identified except in rare circumstances.

CONTEMPLATIVE

CONCENTRATE

The item requires pure concentration to activate. This requires you to focus upon something very specific (often the outcome of using the item). Once again, this information will be gleaned when the item is identified.

ENGAGE

MANIPULATE

The item require you to move it, thrust it, wave it around or take some other type of kinetic action. This action is similar to the Interact basic action. As with any other interact action, you must use your hands (or other appropriate appendage).

CAST A SPELL

A magic item with this activation entry requires you to use the Cast a Spell activity to Activate Item. This happens when the item replicates a spell. Each type of item will explain how this action applies to it.

CONSUMABLE ITEMS

Some items are used up when they are activated. A potion or an elixir must be swallowed, or an oil applied to the body. The writing vanishes from a scroll when it is read. Once used, a consumable item loses its magic.

POWER POINTS

Some magic items have a certain amount of power points that must be expended to activate their properties. The number of power points that an item has remaining is revealed when the item is identified. Additionally, when an item regains power points, the creature Invested to it learns how many power points it regained.

MAGIC ITEM CATEGORIES

Magic items are divided into a number of categories. Some of these categories have specific rules attached to the use of the items contained with them and such rules are explained in their individual descriptions.

ARMOUR & SHIELDS

Magic armour (including shields) offers improved, magic protection to the wearer. Also included are a number of runes which may be applied armour and shields.

CHARGED ITEMS

These items contain spells or effects which have a limited amount of power points and may need to be recharged for continual use. Such items include, rods, staves and wands.

CONSUMABLES

These items are single use items which are expended after activation. Such items included here are ammunition, potions, scrolls and talismans.

WEAPONS

Magic weapons are created to overcome damage reduction and can have a variety of combat powers. Also included are a number of magical runes which can be applied to weapons.

WONDROUS

This is a catch all category for anything that doesn't fall into the other groups. Anyone can use a wondrous item (unless specified otherwise in the description).

MAGIC ITEM DESCRIPTIONS

Each magical item has a description and a list of properties. Below is an example item which gives the structure of a magical item entry. Some of these entries may vary based upon their individual abilities.

ITEM NAME

TRAIT 1 TRAIT 2

Level The level of the item.

Price The value of the item in gold pieces (gp).

Usage This entry determines how the item is used.

Activation The amount of AP required to activate the item appears here with the specific activation components.

Weight How much the item weighs in pounds.

A description of the item and its abilities.

Craft Requirements Just as with normal items, a formula is required to craft an item (see Chapters 4 & 6). Some items may have special crafting requirements and if so this will be explained here.

LEVEL

The level of an item is an indicator of its power level. The level of an item determines a number of things such as how hard it is to identify, craft and sometimes activate.

There is no limit to the level of an item that a character may use, if the item is available then it can be used regardless of level. Some items require skill checks as part of their activation and the DCs of such checks may be difficult if the level of the item is too high.

When crafting magical items, it is important to remember that you must add up the total cost of all modifiers before determining the total level.

Hadley the crafter is making his expert chainmail magical by adding some magical runes. He adds a Potency I rune followed by an Energy Resistance I rune. The total cost of these runes is 5,450 gp which is added to the 655-gp cost of his expert full chainmail for a total item cost of 6,105 gp. This makes the total level of the item level 9.

PRICE

This is the purchase cost of the item and is also used when crafting the item. If a character wants to sell an item, they can sell it for 20% of this price, assuming they are in a location with a suitable buyer.

USAGE

This item entry will explain how the item can be used. Some items must be held, other items must be worn, and some others must be affixed to weapons etc.

CRAFT REQUIREMENTS

Some items will have specific requirements which are needed when creating the item using the crafting skill. These may be racial requirements, a specific material which has to be used, a spell which must be cast or some other criteria.

RUNES

Runes are magical inscriptions of power which may be applied to various non-magical items. At their most basic, a potency rune which is the core rune used to apply magic to an item provides a magical bonus to actions performed with that item. Some magical items must first be imbued with a potency rune before other magic can be applied to them.

INSCRIBING RUNES

A rune can be inscribed directly onto an item or onto a runestone. If a rune is inscribed directly onto an item, it can be done as part of the original process or applied to an existing item. An item can never have two runes of the same type and can only have one Potency Rune. If you inscribe a Potency Rune onto an item that already has one, the previous rune is destroyed. The same applies if you scribe the same rune onto an item for a second time.

A rune may also be inscribed onto a special stone known as a Runestone. Creating a rune in this way follows the normal crafting rules but stores the rune for later use.

RUNESTONE

MAGICAL

Level 1

Price 80 gp

Usage held in 1 hand; Weight 1 lb

This smooth, granite like stone seems to reflect light and is etched with strange circular patterns. Its natural form makes it the perfect conduit for storing magic and be used to store magical runes.

You can inscribe only one rune upon the stone at any one time. Once the stone is etched, it gains the school and tradition traits of the rune etched upon it. When a rune is transferred from the runestone to another object, the runestone loses these traits.

TRANSFERRING RUNES

If a rune has been inscribed onto a Runestone it may be transferred to an item at a later date. This process incurs no cost but requires a successful Transfer Runes Crafting check (see Chapter 4).

POTENCY RUNES

It is possible to enhance an item using magic. To do this a magical potency rune can be inscribed into the item to enhance its item bonus. How potency runes specifically interact with each item is explored below.

ITEM COST & LEVELAs discussed in Chapter 6, quality and material adjustments to an item increase its level for cost purposes. To determine the cost and level of an enchanted item, you begin with the cost of the non-magical item that you are in enchanting. You add to this the cost of any magical adjustments and then determine the new level by consulting the appropriate item cost table provided in each section. ITEM COST & LEVELAs discussed in Chapter 6, quality and material adjustments to an item increase its level for cost purposes. To determine the cost and level of an enchanted item, you begin with the cost of the non-magical item that you are in enchanting. You add to this the cost of any magical adjustments and then determine the new level by consulting the appropriate item cost table provided in each section.

ARMOUR & SHIELDS

Magical armour and magical shields provide a much-needed defensive resource for frontline warriors and stealth based combatants alike. There is a vast array of magical abilities which can be placed into armour and shields ranging from additional DB to skill bonuses and spell-like effects.

All enchanted armour and shields must first be imbued with a potency rune. The potency rune imbues the item with magic, provides it with a bonus and allows other runes to be etched upon it.

There are also several specific suits of magical armour and shields. These are also described after the runes.

The quality of the armour or shield restricts both the maximum power level of the potency rune and the amount of additional runes that may be applied to it.

CHARGED ITEMS

Charged items contain power points which may be used to release spells or other effects. The most common Charged Items are Rods, Staves and Wands, although other types of charged items also exist. To use the spell contained in a charged item requires holding it (typically in one hand) and Activating by using the Cast a Spell action, which takes the spell’s normal number of AP.

When casting a spell from a charged item, you may do so in one of two ways.

USING SPELLCRAFT

To cast the spell contained in a charged item using Spellcraft, you must meet the following requirements:

• Your caster level must meet the PP requirements (see chapter 9)

• The spell must be from your tradition of magic (although you do not need to know it).

If you meet all the above requirements you may Cast a Spell from the item using Spellcraft as an Easy check (DC -2).

USING THE SCHOOL TRADITION SKILL

If you do not meet the above requirements, you may instead cast the spell contained within a charged item by using the spells tradition skill: Arcana, Occultism, Nature or Religion. To do this, you must meet the following requirements:

• Your rank in the required skill must be equal to or greater than the PP cost of the spell.

• You must have the Use Magic Device feat.

If you meet all the above requirements you may cast the spell from the item using your Tradition Skill as a Hard check (DC +2).

RECHARGING

A charged item if invested will slowly replenish its power points albeit at a much slower rate than a living creature. During daily preparation, an invested, charged item will regain 1 PP for every 10 PP (or part thereof) it has at maximum charge each day.

CHARGE DEPLETION

If a charged item is ever reduced to less than 0 PP you must make a d100 check on the Item Depletion table

ITEM DEPLETION

D%

Result

01-10

The item explodes affecting all creatures within a 10’ radius per item level. This inflicts 1d4 force damage per level of the item with a Basic Reflex Save (level based).

11-40

The item crumbles to dust, forever destroyed.

41-65

The item is depleted and gains the broken condition. It may be repaired and recharged normally.

66

The item randomly changes into another charged item. Roll on the Resonance Event table at +20.

67-90

The item is depleted and may be recharged normally

91-99

The item strangely recharges itself.

100

The item recharges itself and has its maximum charges increased by 1.

CHARGED ITEM LEVEL & COST

Each of the charged items have different methods of determining both their level and cost.

RODS

To determine the level of a rod, add up the total amount of PP required for its base spells or abilities. Or if the rod creates a Metamagic effect on an existing spell, the rods level must be at least the minimum level required to cast that spell.

STAVES

A staff is always at least 2 levels higher than the highest PP spell that it contains, so a staff with up to 8 PP spells would be at least a 10th-level item. Furthermore, if a staff contains spells from more than one school of magic its level is increased by 1.

Aelar has a staff which contains the following spells:
Burning Hands (PP 2), Magic Missile (PP 2), Fleeting Speed (PP 4) and Fireball (PP 6).

The highest PP of the contained spells is 6 which gives the staff a level of 8. Since the staff contains spells from two different schools of magic, its level is further increased by 1, meaning that this staff has a level of 9.

WANDS/OTHER

To determine the level of a wand or another charged item, use the PP cost of the contained spell +1.

RODS

A magical rod is usually a thin baton approximately three feet in length. Unlike other charged items, Rods rarely have spells contained within them but instead contain power points which may be used to supplement the spellcasting abilities of the wielder. A rod may be used as a somatic component for spell casting.

A rod will always contain 10 power points when first created.

STAVES

A magical staff is to a spellcaster what the sword is to a warrior and is a powerful and often ornate weapon or tool imbued with magical properties. It is typically a long staff made of wood, metal, or a combination of both, and serves as a conduit for spellcasting or other magical abilities.

A magical staff can also be used as a weapon and will often have a potency rune engraved onto it.

Staves have multiple spells contained within them which may be cast if the invested wielder meets the Charged Item casting restrictions (detailed at the beginning of this section).

Each spell that you can cast from a staff may be warped using its own pool of power to a maximum PP of no more than the items level.

A staff may be used as a somatic component for spell casting.

When first created, a staff will contain an amount of PP equal to its level x2. This value is also the maximum amount of power points which a staff may contain when fully charged.

Each staff description lists the spells that it can be used to cast and in parentheses gives spells PP cost (when cast at base cost).

WANDS

Short, slender items typically made of wood; a wand lets you cast a specific spell without expending your reserve of power points. A wand may be used as a somatic component for spell casting.

When first created the spell in a wand must be warped to the amount of PP that it will be cast with and this amount of PP can never change. The wand will contain enough power points to cast the spell contained within it three times. This value is also the maximum amount of power points that a wand may contain when fully charged.

A wand may be created to allow it to freely use its warping options within the confines of its PP limits. Doing this increases the level of the wand by 1.

CONSUMABLE ITEMS

We continue the magical item descriptions with consumable items. Any magical item that has the Consumable trait may only be used once.

CONSUMABLES & AMMUNITION

The rules outlined in chapter 4 regarding the crafting of items with the consumable trait also extend to magical consumables, emphasizing batch production; however, magical ammunition is an exception to this, being created in sets of 10, while retaining the flexibility to adjust DCs for crafting quantities, as detailed in chapter 4.

Consumables includes the following subcategories, with any special rules appearing at the start of the section.

Ammunition – Consumables launched from ranged weapons.

Unguents– Liquids that you apply to a target creature or object.

Potions– A magical liquid that activates upon consumption.

Scrolls – Magical parchment containing spells

Other Consumables – Any consumable that does not fall into one of the other categories.

CONSUMABLE LEVEL

A consumable has a level equal to the PP of the spell it creates. If the item has a bonus, this will be determined separately.

AMMUNITION

These magic items are designed to be used with various ranged weapons. Ammunition can be imbued with magical enhancements in the same way that weapons can.

Any item bonus granted from ammunition does not stack with the item bonus from the firing weapon.

ACTIVATE AMMUNITION

Ammunition is activated automatically when it is launched.

MAGICAL ENHANCEMENTS

Any magical enhancement that can be applied to a ranged weapon can be applied to ammunition unless the description states otherwise. Ammunition costs are worked out in the same way as weapons but per batch rather than an individual item.

UNGUENTS

Oils are liquids that are typically applied to an object and are used up in the process. Applying an oil usually takes two hands: one to hold the jar containing the oil, and another to extract the oil and apply it. You can only apply an oil to an item or creature within your reach. It is impossible to apply an oil to an unwilling target, unless they are in some way incapacitated.

POTIONS

A potion is a magical liquid activated when you drink it, which uses it up. You can activate a potion with an Interact action as you drink it or feed it to another creature. You can feed a potion only to a creature that is within reach and willing or otherwise so helpless that it can’t resist. You usually need only one hand to consume a potion or feed it to another creature.

SCROLLS

A scroll is a single spell inscribed onto a piece of parchment spell. Any spell can be scribed onto a scroll. The spell on the scroll can only be cast once and then the scroll is destroyed. You cannot warp a spell cast from a scroll and do not need to provide any material components as they will have been provided when the scroll was created.

USING SPELLCRAFT

To cast the spell contained in a scroll, you follow the same guidelines as using a charged item (see above).

WEAPONS

Magical weapons are extraordinary tools infused with arcane energies, granting them extraordinary properties and abilities beyond those of mundane weapons. These enchanted armaments become symbols of power and serve as invaluable assets to adventurers as they embark on epic quests, battling formidable foes and unravelling the mysteries of fantastical realms.

All enchanted weapons must first be imbued with a potency rune. The potency rune imbues the item with magic, provides it with a bonus and allows other runes to be etched upon it.

There are also a number of example weapons. These are described after the rune descriptions.

The quality of the weapon restricts both the maximum power level of the potency rune and the amount of additional runes that may be applied to it.

Any magical item that is not covered by one of the above categories falls into the wondrous category. The items in this category are not related in any way and may contain a wide variety of abilities. Determining the cost and level of a wondrous item is a little more complex than other items but then table below details some of the main bonuses and modifiers that you may need to consider when creating them.

To determine the final cost of a wondrous magic item, add up the cost of all its individual abilities. To determine the items level, always round down to the nearest price if its total does not match one of the below values.

Base DR This grants you DR. You may only benefit from the highest Base DR that you gain.

DB Bonus This is a status bonus to DB. If the bonus only applies to a specific aspect of DB, lower the level of the ability by one.

If the bonus to DB is a type other than status, then increase the level of this ability by one.

DR Bonus This is a status bonus to DR.

If the bonus to DR is a type other than status, then increase the level of this ability by two.

Resistance An item can grant either energy resistance or physical resistance. Resistances are explained in more detail in chapter 7.

Save Bonus This is a resistance bonus that the magical item applies to all three saving throws. If the bonus is only applied to one saving throw then reduce the level of the effect by two, or by one if it applies to two saving throws.

Furthermore, if a resistance bonus is only applied to a single specific part of a saving throw, then lower the level of this ability by two. If the bonus applies to more than one specific part of a saving throw, then lower level of the ability by one.

If the bonus to a saving throw is a type other than resistance, then increase the level of this ability by one.

SPELLS

It is the same process to apply a spell to a wondrous item as to armour and weapons.

Skill Bonus This is the total amount of skill bonuses that the item applies when used. If a skill bonus is only applied to a single specific action of a skill, then lower the level of this ability by two. If the bonus applies to more than one specific skill action but not the entire skill, then lower level of the ability by one.

This is a Status Bonus. If the item grants a different type of bonus to a skill, the level of the ability is increased by one.

Spell Adder This is the Spell Adder bonus that the item applies when invested. Spell Adders from multiple sources can be applied but remember that your item investment limit will restrict the amount that you can have.

A Spell Adder allows a spell caster to cast one or more spells each day with put expending PP. The spell lore check still has to be made but no PP are deducted from the casters PP total. The amount of spells that the adder can be used to cast each day is indicated by its value.

Stat This bonus is applied as a status bonus to your ability score(s). If the bonus is situational and does not apply to all aspects of the ability score, then lower the level of the ability by two. You may apply additional, equal value stat bonuses to the item by increasing its level by 2.

Other Bonuses Any other bonus that can be applied to a character which is not covered here will generally use the Skill Bonus values above.

CHAPTER 12 – GM STUFF

In the time before time, when even the stars were yet but a soft sigh upon the void, the Old Ones stirred. These ancient intelligences—vessel and architect of all that would be—gathered in silent congress and wove into being the world called Traris. With gentle hands they moulded rolling hills and carved deep valleys. From their breath sprang mighty rivers, gleaming like silver threads across the land, and oceans vast and unknowable. Their voices sang the mountains into being—sentinels of stone whose snow‑capped peaks caught the first light of dawn. Under their touch, fields of emerald grass and jewel‑bright blossoms spread like living tapestry, and forests thrummed with waking life.

For countless millennia, Traris was a realm of placid wonder, tended by the steady wisdom of the Old Ones. But as the endless ages passed, the younger among them grew restless. Beauty alone no longer satisfied their hunger for novelty and challenge. So they bent their formidable power to a new design: from loam and flame, from deep root to airy cloud, they fashioned the Dragons.

These first Dragons—sleek, elegant creatures—were born of every realm of Traris. In the highest crags they built eyries of ice and wind; in the sun‑drenched sands they carved lairs of glass and shimmer; beneath the ocean’s surface they wove palaces in coral and pearl; and in jungles of emerald gloom, they found kinship with vine and vine‑bound ruin. Each Dragon was given a magic of its own fire that roared like the heart of a volcano, waters that whispered haunting songs, storms that howled with unbridled fury, and verdant breath that coaxed living things to strange growth. The Old Ones beheld their handiwork and rejoiced in its perfection.

But the younger Old Ones, ever craving fresh excitements, turned their eyes upon these winged marvels. They delighted in the raw power and caprice of the Dragons, and in time their whims flowed into the creatures themselves—tiny, imperceptible shifts of nature that, given centuries, grew monstrous. The proud Fire Dragons became consumed with ambition, their flame a blazing embodiment of greed. The Forest Dragons, once serene guardians of green realms, grew secretive and jealous, weaving illusions of dread. Ice and storm, earth and water—all were warped by hidden desires. The land that had known harmony now trembled under the first rumblings of discord.

Thus were sown the seeds of the Dragon Wars. For nearly two thousand years, the sky and ground alike were torn asunder by their battles. Volcanic fire rained on peaceful plains; hurricanes swirled in frantic vengeance; forests were levelled by savage assaults. Castle and village fell before their wrath, and the rivers ran black with soot and blood. When the dust finally settled, the Dragon race lay broken, their numbers a mere fraction of their first soaring multitudes. Traris itself was scarred: mountains cleft, seas choked with ash, and forests lay in ruin.

In the war’s waning days, the surviving Dragons—hardened by grief and guilt—slipped away into hidden places. Fire‑drakes burrowed deep into earth’s burning heart; ice‑wyrms fled to polar wastes; storm‑serpents vanished into endless tempests; and forest‑wyrms melted into the green shadows they once ruled. Traris, wounded and weary, drew a tentative breath of peace.

Yet even in that fragile calm, the echoes of the Old Ones’ restlessness lingered. For Traris’s story was only half‑told. The world would yet face fresh trials—mortal heroes and forgotten gods, new magics and ancient prophecies—and its fate would again hang on the balance between chaos and creation. So the saga of Traris moved onward, its pages inscribed in starlight and flame, a testament to ends and beginnings—and to the relentless, wondrous forging of worlds.

Welcome to Chapter 12 of the TRG Prime core rulebook, aptly titled "GM Stuff." In this chapter, we delve into the essential tools, guidance, and resources that empower Game Masters (GMs) to craft immersive and captivating adventures within their boundless fantasy realms.

As a GM, you hold the keys to unlock the mysteries of the campaign and this chapter serves as your invaluable compendium, equipping you with the knowledge and tools necessary to create memorable experiences for your players.

Within the pages of this chapter, you will find a wealth of resources designed to enhance your storytelling abilities and provide guidance on running engaging game sessions. From Campaign Planning to Experience Point Awards, "GM Stuff" covers a wide array of topics to support you in your role as the storyteller and game facilitator.

THE GAMESMASTER (GM)

In TRG, the Game Master (GM) assumes a vital and multifaceted role that brings the game world to life and facilitates immersive storytelling. The GM serves as the visionary architect, the master storyteller, and the impartial referee, guiding the players through a tapestry of adventures and challenges within a vibrant and dynamic fantasy realm. Here, we explore the essential role of the GM in a fantasy RPG.

WORLD BUILDER

The GM is responsible for crafting the game world, breathing life into its landscapes, civilizations, and inhabitants. They envision rich and immersive settings, complete with cities, dungeons, wilderness, and all the details that make the world feel authentic and alive.

NARRATOR & STORYTELLER

As the central storyteller, the GM weaves epic tales that captivate the players' imaginations. They craft engaging narratives, present intriguing plotlines, and introduce compelling characters and events that drive the story forward. Through vivid descriptions, dialogue, and dramatic tension, the GM sets the stage for the players' heroic exploits.

NON-PLAYER CHARACTERS (NPCS)

The GM takes on the role of NPCs, portraying a diverse cast of characters that the players encounter. Whether they are allies, adversaries, or curious denizens of the game world, the GM breathes life into these NPCs, imbuing them with unique personalities, motivations, and quirks.

GAME SYSTEM ARBITER

The GM interprets and enforces the rules of the game system, ensuring fairness and consistency. They adjudicate conflicts, resolve challenges, and determine the outcomes of player actions, all while maintaining a balanced and enjoyable gameplay experience.

ENCOUNTER DESIGNER

The GM designs and orchestrates exciting encounters, be they battles against fearsome monsters, diplomatic negotiations with influential figures, or solving intricate puzzles. They balance the difficulty, consider the players' abilities, and create challenges that offer opportunities for heroism and strategic thinking.

IMPROVISER

A key skill of a GM is the ability to adapt and improvise on the fly. They respond to player choices, unexpected actions, and the unpredictability of the game. The GM embraces the dynamic nature of the RPG, creating engaging experiences even in the face of unforeseen circumstances.

FACILITATOR AND COLLABORATOR

The GM fosters a collaborative and cooperative atmosphere, ensuring that all players have opportunities to contribute to the story. They provide guidance, encourage roleplaying, and facilitate player agency, allowing each player to shape their character's destiny and impact the game world.

ATMOSPHERE CREATOR

Through their descriptions, sound effects, music, and ambiance, the GM creates a vibrant atmosphere that immerses the players in the game world. They set the tone, evoke emotions, and evoke a sense of wonder or dread, transporting the players to realms of fantasy.

RULE OF FUN

Above all, the GM prioritizes the enjoyment and engagement of the players. They strive to create memorable experiences, epic moments, and a sense of accomplishment. While upholding the rules, the GM embraces the rule of fun, tailoring the game to the players' preferences and fostering an environment where everyone can participate and have a great time.

In a fantasy RPG, the GM's role is to be a master of ceremonies, a guide through the realms of imagination, and the conduit that connects players to the wonders and perils of the game world. With creativity, storytelling prowess, and a passion for facilitating memorable experiences, the GM shapes the adventure and creates a shared narrative tapestry that the players will cherish for years to come.

CAMPAIGN PLANNING

Planning and implementing a campaign in TRG is an exhilarating and rewarding endeavour that allows GMs to create epic and immersive experiences for their players. Here, we present a step-by-step guide to help GMs effectively plan and implement a captivating campaign.

DEFINE THE VISION

Begin by defining the vision for your campaign. Determine the genre, themes, and tone you want to explore, as well as the overarching story or central conflict that will drive the narrative. Consider the setting, its history, and the main factions or organizations that will be prominent within the campaign world.

ESTABLISH GOALS & MILESTONES

Set specific goals and milestones for the campaign. Identify key events, major plot points, and pivotal moments that will shape the story. These milestones will act as guideposts and help structure the campaign's progression, allowing players to feel a sense of accomplishment as they advance through the story.

A COMPELLING CAST

Develop a diverse cast of non-player characters (NPCs) who will interact with the players. Craft memorable personalities, backgrounds, and motivations for these NPCs, making them feel like authentic inhabitants of the game world. Consider both allies and adversaries to provide a balanced and engaging experience.

DESIGN STORY ARCS

Break down the overarching story into smaller story arcs or chapters. Each arc should have its own narrative focus, challenges, and opportunities for character development. Determine the major events and potential outcomes of each arc, allowing flexibility for player choices and actions to influence the story's direction.

KEY LOCATIONS

Identify significant locations within the campaign world and flesh them out with details. Develop maps, descriptions, and notable features of these locations, making them immersive and memorable for the players to explore. Include dungeons, towns, landmarks, and other points of interest that are relevant to the campaign's narrative.

CREATE ENGAGING CHALLENGES

Craft a variety of quests and challenges for the players to undertake. These can include combat encounters, puzzles, investigations, social interactions, or exploration-based challenges. Ensure that the challenges align with the campaign's themes and progress the story in meaningful ways.

EMBRACE PLAYER AGENCY

Encourage player agency by providing opportunities for meaningful choices and consequences. Design encounters and events that allow players to shape the story through their decisions and actions. Remain flexible and be prepared to adapt the campaign based on player choices, allowing their agency to influence the narrative.

BALANCE PROGRESSION & EXPLORATION

Strike a balance between narrative progression and player exploration. Provide a mix of story-driven moments and opportunities for players to engage with the game world freely. Include side quests, optional encounters, and opportunities for character development outside of the main storyline.

PREPARE SESSION OUTLINES

Outline each session by breaking down the key events, encounters, and interactions that will occur. Create a rough structure to ensure a coherent flow and maintain pacing throughout the sessions. Be flexible and adapt the session outline based on player choices and developments during gameplay.

SESSION PREPARATION

Prior to each session, prepare the necessary materials, such as maps, handouts, and NPC stat blocks. Review the session outline, familiarize yourself with the key story elements, and anticipate potential player actions. This preparation will enable smoother gameplay and immersive storytelling.

PROVIDE PLAYER REWARDS

Consider providing rewards to players as they progress through the campaign. These rewards can include experience points, treasure, magical items, or other resources that enhance character progression. Ensure that rewards are balanced and meaningful, motivating players to engage further with the campaign.

Rewards are explored in greater detail later in this chapter.

EVOLVE & ADAPT

Remain open to adapting the campaign based on player feedback and evolving dynamics. Be attentive to the players' interests, playstyles, and preferences, and incorporate their feedback to enhance their enjoyment. Flexibility and adaptability are key to creating a satisfying and engaging campaign experience.

By following these steps, GMs can effectively plan and implement a campaign that captivates players, immerses them in a vibrant game world, and offers them unforgettable adventures. Remember to embrace creativity, nurture player engagement, and relish the collaborative storytelling experience that tabletop RPGs provide. May your campaign be filled with epic moments and cherished memories!

ENCOUNTER BUILDING

It is important in any RPG to ensure that the encounters that a PC party face are structured, balanced and engaging. To make certain that this is the case, appropriate adversaries must be selected and the challenge of each encounter weighed up very carefully.

THREAT LEVEL

When determining how much of a challenge an encounter is, a series of seven difficulties, called Threat Levels are used (just like check difficulties).

INCREDIBLY EASY

Incredibly easy encounters pose minimal threat to the player characters, often involving foes significantly weaker or outnumbered. These encounters are designed to provide a quick victory for the players, requiring little strategy or resource expenditure.

VERY EASY

Very easy encounters offer little challenge to the player characters, with adversaries that pose a minor threat or lack significant offensive capabilities. The focus is more on roleplaying, exploration, or non-combat challenges rather than combat itself.

EASY

This encounter offers a modest challenge to the player characters. The adversaries pose a credible threat, but the PCs have a reasonable chance of success. It requires some strategic thinking and resource management, but victory is expected for a well-prepared and competent group.

MEDIUM

This encounter presents a balanced challenge to the player characters. The adversaries are on relatively equal footing with the PCs in terms of strength and abilities. It demands careful tactics, resource management, and effective teamwork. The outcome of the encounter is uncertain and success requires effort.

HARD

This encounter poses a significant challenge to the player characters. The adversaries are stronger or more numerous than the PCs, requiring careful planning, optimal resource utilization, and tactical decision-making. Success is not guaranteed, and the PCs may face potential setbacks or losses.

VERY HARD

A very hard encounter presents a significant test of the player characters' capabilities. The adversaries are highly skilled, possess powerful abilities, or significantly outnumber the PCs. The encounter requires exceptional teamwork, strategic thinking, and resource management to overcome. It may involve a high level of risk, potential setbacks, or the need for clever tactics to achieve victory.

Encounters of this magnitude are usually used as final boss fights at the end of a campaign chapter or standalone adventure.

INCREDIBLY HARD

An incredibly hard encounter is an extreme test of the player characters' abilities. The adversaries are exceptionally powerful, possess unique abilities, or outnumber the PCs significantly. The encounter represents a significant threat, requiring exceptional skill, resource management, and creative thinking to survive. Success may come at a great cost, and victory is hard-won but highly rewarding.

Such encounters are normally used at the climax of a campaign.

ENCOUNTER XP BUDGET

After determining the desired threat level, it's time to construct the encounter using the provided XP budget, as each creature within the encounter consumes a portion of that budget.

BUDGET PER CHARACTER

The Threat Level grants an XP budget for each character involved in the encounter as shown below.

A party of four PC’s move into a forest glade and have to deal with the local fey threat. As this is a relatively minor encounter which is not really intended to test the party too much, the GM decides that it has a Threat Level of Very Easy. The GM therefore has an XP budget of 100 per PC for a total of 400 XP for the encounter.

EFFECTIVE LEVEL & AVERAGE PARTY LEVEL

Once you have selected the Threat Level and know your XP budget for the encounter, you can work out the required level and number of adversaries. To do this, you must first work out the average level of the PC party (APL). This is done by adding the total levels (EL) of the PC party together and dividing by the number of party members (include any permanent NPCs in this value).

Once you have the APL, determine the XP value for each creature by deducting Effective Level (EL) from the APL.
