APPENDIX 4 - DIVINE ASPECTS

In the vast and mystical landscapes of TRG, divine aspects hold a paramount place, bestowing profound power and purpose to those chosen ones, the clerics, crusaders and other characters that manipulate the powers of divinity. These divine aspects, reflections of the deity's own strengths, virtues, and domains, not only shape the cleric's or crusader's abilities but also profoundly influence their missions and values.

As conduits of divine energy, these individuals manifest their god's will on the mortal plane, their unique abilities a testament to their deity's influence. Whether they wield these divine aspects to heal, to harm, to protect, or to prophesise, they remain the tangible embodiments of divine intervention in a setting teeming with magic and mystery.

Each divine aspect is used to portray a deity or divine power in your campaign setting and is easily adapted. Any PC or NPC that utilises the Divinity Tradition to cast spells must select a Divine Aspect.

Each Divine Aspect uses the following format:

ASPECT NAME

TRAITS

A description of the divine aspect and how it is often depicted, including some example symbols.

Edicts: The edicts of a deific aspect serve as the guiding principles or commands that followers, like clerics or crusaders, must uphold. These edicts embody the core values, morals, and teachings of the associated deity and shape the behaviour and actions of their followers.

The faithful are expected to follow these edicts faithfully. Deviating from these can result in loss of favour or divine abilities, as it's considered a betrayal of their deity's principles. Conversely, strict adherence can lead to divine blessings, enhanced abilities, or increased favour with their deity.

Anathema: Anathema refers to actions or behaviours that are strictly forbidden or deeply offensive to a specific deific aspect. These prohibitions contrast directly with the edicts of a deific aspect and are considered severe violations of its principles and values. When clerics, crusaders, or other divine agents commit an act that is anathema to their deific aspect, they risk losing their divine favour and abilities.

Suggested Ethics: The ethics which are promoted by followers of this divine aspect. A cleric, crusader or other divinity caster must select one of these ethics.

Class Skill: This skill is granted as a class skill to clerics who select the deific aspect.

Specialist Spells: These spells may be learnt by clerics and crusaders who select this deific aspect by taking the specialist spell feat or through class picks (cleric).

Bonus Spells: Each bonus spell is automatically learnt by a cleric at the level indicated in parentheses. These spells are always available and do not have to be learnt using one of the clerics spell slots.

Favoured Weapon: A cleric or crusader who selects this deific aspect is automatically proficient with this group of weapons.

DAWN

GOOD

The aspect of dawn is a deity that embodies the power and radiance of the rising sun. It is often depicted as a figure with a serene and compassionate countenance, adorned with golden robes that emanate a warm and comforting light. The god's presence brings about a sense of renewal, healing, and vitality, symbolizing the dawning of a new day.

Edicts: The followers of the aspect of dawn are tasked with promoting healing, restoration, and enlightenment. They are expected to utilize their abilities to bring solace and rejuvenation to those in need. The followers are called to embody compassion, kindness, and empathy, offering their aid to the sick, injured, and downtrodden. They are also encouraged to seek the truth, shed light on darkness, and inspire hope in others.

Anathema: The followers of dawn, are forbidden from causing harm (unless protecting the weak), spreading suffering, or engaging in acts of cruelty. They must not misuse their healing abilities to manipulate or exploit others. The followers are prohibited from engaging in necromantic practices or dark magic that disrupts the natural balance of life. They must not deliberately obstruct or obscure the truth, and they should refrain from spreading despair or extinguishing hope in others.

Suggested Ethics: Altruism, Benevolence, Harmony

Class Skill: Diplomacy

Specialist Spells: Arc of Fire, Death’s Defiance, Deflect Flame, Healer’s Grace, Luminance, Luminous Flare, Revealing Glance, Truthful Words

Bonus Spells: Orb of Fire (1); Burning Hands (2); Fireball (6); Wall of Fire (8)

Favoured Weapon: Mace

DEATH

BALANCE

The deific aspect of death is a profound and enigmatic entity, cloaked in ambiguity and silent whispers. It is frequently portrayed as a figure enveloped in shadow, with penetrating eyes that hold the allure of veiled truths and inevitable endings. The presence of this aspect resonates with a sense of inevitability and tranquillity, resonating deeply with those who understand that death is not an end, but a part of the eternal cycle of life.

Edicts: Those aligned with the deific aspect of death are propelled by an inherent understanding of life's inevitable conclusion and the transition that follows. They are urged to embrace the cyclical nature of existence, to respect the end of life as much as its beginning, and to provide comfort and guidance to those nearing their journey's end. Followers are called upon to meditate on mortality, recognize the beauty in life's transience, and help others find peace in their passage, taking solace in the eternal cycle and the spiritual growth it affords.

Anathema: For those embodying the deific aspect of death, anathema lies in disrupting the natural cycle of life and death. They must not artificially prolong life beyond its destined span or hasten death before its time. The fear of death and attempts to avoid it are considered aberrations. Resisting the inevitable transition, whether through necromancy or other unnatural means, is deemed a violation of the highest order. Followers are expected to uphold the sanctity of the cycle, ensuring each life meets its end when it should, no sooner, no later.

Suggested Ethics: Altruism, Harmony, Prudence

Class Skill: Intimidate

Specialist Spells: Banish Fatigue, Death’s Defiance, Delayed Respite, Healer’s Grace, Purge the Unlife, Renewals Touch, Touch of Undeath, Unliving Vitality

Bonus Spells: Dead Tongue (1); Spectral Hand (3); Speak with Dead (6); Death Ward (10)

Favoured Weapon: Scythe

JUSTICE

GOOD ORDER

The aspect of justice is a deity that embodies the ideals of courage, justice, and righteousness. It is often depicted as a muscular, imposing figure with armour and weapons, radiating an aura of strength and confidence. The god's face is stern, with eyes that seem to pierce through falsehoods and deceit. The god is often accompanied by loyal knights, soldiers, and other champions of justice.

Edicts: The followers of justice are expected to uphold the principles of justice, fairness, and equality. They are encouraged to defend the innocent, protect the weak, and punish the wicked. The followers are expected to be honest, brave, and true, and to always act with honour and integrity. They are also expected to help those in need, to fight against oppression and tyranny, and to stand up against injustice and corruption.

Anathema: The followers of justice are forbidden from engaging in acts of cruelty, cowardice, or treachery. They are not allowed to harm innocent people or to use violence or force without just cause. The followers are also forbidden from engaging in acts of corruption or dishonesty, or from siding with oppressors or tyrants. Finally, the followers must not break their oaths or betray their trust, as this goes against the deity's teachings of honour and integrity.

Suggested Ethics: Benevolence, Harmony, Justice

Class Skill: Diplomacy

Specialist Spells: Confident Veil, False Arrogance, Physical Surge, Resilient Fortitude, Revealing Glance, Truthful Words, Weapon Surge, Zealous Battlecry

Bonus Spells: Guidance (1); True Strike (2); Haste (6); Elemental Shield (10)

Favoured Weapon: Broadsword

MAGIC

BALANCE

The aspect of magic is an elusive and profound deific aspect, enveloped in enigma and murmurs of arcane wisdom. Often depicted as a figure veiled in shimmering auras, its eyes hold the enchantment of mystic knowledge and latent potentials. The presence of this aspect induces a sense of wonder and mystery, resonating with those intrigued by the boundless possibilities of the arcane and captivated by their own pursuit of magical mastery.

Edicts: Adherents of the deific aspect of magic are driven by an unquenchable thirst for arcane knowledge, the mysteries of the cosmos, and the mastery of magical forces. They are urged to pursue their scholarly curiosities and magical ambitions, even in the face of daunting challenges or societal misunderstanding. The followers are called upon to decipher arcane secrets, unravel metaphysical mysteries, and harness the energies that shape reality, revelling in the discovery of unknown spells and the fulfilment of their intellectual passions.

Anathema: For the followers of magic, actions that suppress, degrade, or endanger the pursuit and practice of magic are anathema. They cannot condone the burning of ancient texts, the stifling of magical innovation, or the oppression of magical beings. Followers must shun those who use magic with reckless disregard for its potential consequences, exploit magic for wanton destruction, or manipulate it for deceitful ends. The callous disposal of magical artefacts, disregard for magical lore, or harm to magical creatures are seen as the deepest betrayals, warranting the severest of consequences.

Suggested Ethics: Ambition, Anarchy, Prudence

Class Skill: Arcana

Specialist Spells: Destructive Roar, Fateful Temptation, Guiding Stone, Revealing Glance, Revelation Divine, Silent Binding, Stasis, Unity

Bonus Spells: Magic Missile (1); Magic Mouth (4); Fly; (6); Wall of Force (12)

Favoured Weapon: Staff

MURDER

EVIL

The aspect of murder is a dark and enigmatic deity, shrouded in mystery and whispers. It is often depicted as a figure cloaked in shadow, with piercing eyes that hold the allure of hidden knowledge and forbidden desires. The god's presence evokes a sense of temptation and darkness, appealing to those consumed by their own ambitions and secrets.

Edicts: The followers of the aspect of murder are driven by their insatiable hunger for power, wealth, and control. They are encouraged to pursue their selfish desires and ambitions at any cost, without regard for the well-being or lives of others. The followers are called to manipulate, deceive, and exploit those around them, revelling in the acquisition of secrets and the satisfaction of their darkest urges.

Anathema: The followers of murder are forbidden from acts of selflessness, mercy, and honesty. They must not exhibit empathy or compassion towards others, treating them merely as means to an end. The followers are prohibited from acts of kindness or generosity, as well as from revealing their own secrets or betraying the trust of their fellow followers.

Be aware that such characters might not be suitable for all RPG campaigns, especially those focused on heroic and virtuous storytelling.

Suggested Ethics: Ambition, Deception, Prudence

Class Skill: Stealth

Specialist Spells: Fools Riches, Mind’s Double, Precious Metals, Purge the Unlife, Reaper’s Resonance, Shifting Step, Silent Binding, Veiled Secret

Bonus Spells: Ghost Sound (1); Self Mirage (2); Invisibility; (4); Phantasmal Killer (8)

Favoured Weapon: Dagger

NATURE

BALANCE

The aspect of nature is a powerful deity that embodies the beauty and wildness of the natural world. It is depicted as a humanoid figure with long, flowing hair made of leaves and vines, wearing robes of green and brown. The god's face is serene and peaceful, with eyes that seem to reflect the beauty of the surrounding natural world. The god is often accompanied by animals, birds, and other creatures that are sacred to the deity.

Edicts: The followers of nature are expected to protect and preserve the natural world. They are encouraged to live in harmony with nature and to use its resources responsibly. The followers are expected to plant and cultivate crops, protect forests and animals, and promote sustainable living. The followers are also expected to treat all living beings with respect and compassion.

Anathema: The followers of nature are forbidden from harming or destroying the natural world. They are not allowed to cut down trees, pollute rivers, or hunt animals for sport. The followers are also forbidden from using magic that harms nature or disrupts the natural balance of the world. They must not kill animals unless it is necessary for survival or for the protection of other beings. Finally, the followers must not engage in acts of wanton destruction or violence, as this goes against the deity's teachings of harmony and balance.

Suggested Ethics: Autonomy, Benevolence, Harmony

Class Skill: Nature

Specialist Spell: Fools Riches, Guiding Stone, Localised Quake, Nature’s Bounty, Precious Metals, Soothing Words, Unity, Vibrant Thorns

Bonus Spells: Natural Defence (1); True Strike (2); Wall of Thorns (6); Tree Walk (10)

Favoured Weapon: Longbow

PANDEMONIUM

CHAOS EVIL

The aspect of pandemonium is a captivating and volatile force, shrouded in disorder and malevolence. Often visualized as an entity entwined with the fierce, primal energy of a riotous whirlwind and the cruel, dark countenance of demons, its presence is both unsettling and fascinating. The aspect's aura incites a sense of wild liberation and brutal strength, beckoning those who relish in unbounded freedom and who are unafraid to dabble in the darkness that lies beyond the veil of order.

Edicts: The followers of pandemonium are driven by an unwavering desire for personal freedom, unrestrained expression, and indulgence in their darkest desires. They are encouraged to defy societal norms, break traditional boundaries, and pursue their untamed instincts, irrespective of the chaos and discord they might sow. The followers are implored to foster turbulence, revel in disorder, and embody the capriciousness that underpins existence, deriving joy from the unpredictable twists of fate and the fulfilment of their unchecked desires.

Anathema: The followers of pandemonium are vehemently opposed to the constructs of order, discipline, and predictability. Any acts promoting systemic harmony, adherence to traditional rules, or the suppression of personal freedoms are considered an affront to their chaotic beliefs. They must resist all attempts to bind their free spirit, eschew rigid structures, and condemn those who seek to bring uniformity and orderliness. Detesting predictability and stability, they find abhorrence in upholding laws or submitting to any form of control, viewing such actions as stifling their innate chaotic essence.

Be aware that such characters might not be suitable for all RPG campaigns, especially those focused on heroic and virtuous storytelling.

Suggested Ethics: Anarchy, Malevolence, Nihilism

Class Skill: Intimidate

Specialist Spells: Arc of Fire, Coercive Retribution, Deflect Flame, Destructive Roar, Devastating Might, Localised Quake, Physical Surge, Resilient Fortitude

Bonus Spells: Burning Hands (1); Scorching Ray (4); Flaming Weapon (6); Disintegrate (12)

Favoured Weapon: Khopesh

TIME

BALANCE ORDER

The aspect of time is a profound and enigmatic force, shrouded in the infinity of time and the depth of knowledge. Often symbolized by an ageless figure, whose eyes shine with the wisdom of eras past, present, and future, this deific aspect inspires a sense of awe and reverence. Its presence kindles a thirst for understanding and the pursuit of wisdom, appealing to those who seek to learn from the past, comprehend the present, and foresee the future. The burden of timeless knowledge and the cadence of eternal time resonate within its followers, steering their quest towards intellectual satisfaction and understanding of time's continuum.

Edicts: Adherents of the aspect of time are instilled with an enduring sense of curiosity and respect for the progression of time and the accumulation of wisdom. They are guided to continuously seek enlightenment, to understand the intricate tapestry of past, present, and future, and to apply the lessons of history for better judgement. The followers are encouraged to pursue knowledge, to exercise patience, and to appreciate the natural flow of time. They are tasked to be reflective, thoughtful, and considerate in their actions, honouring the wisdom that comes with time and using it to make informed decisions and predictions.

Anathema: The followers of time are forbidden from indulging in rash actions, making hasty decisions, or distorting the course of time for selfish gains. Disregarding the natural progression of time, ignoring the lessons of the past, or acting without careful thought and consideration are considered grievous sins. Similarly, wilfully spreading ignorance, suppressing knowledge, or encouraging recklessness stands in stark opposition to their beliefs.

Suggested Ethics: Ambition, Harmony, Prudence

Class Skill: Perception

Specialist Spells: Banish Fatigue, Confident Veil, Death’s Defiance, Delayed Respite, Fluidity, Lucky Break, Stasis, Unity

Bonus Spells: True Strike (1); Fleeting Speed (4); Haste (6); Time Hop (8)

Favoured Weapon: Spear

TYRANNY

EVIL ORDER

The aspect of tyranny is a dark and oppressive deity, embodying absolute control, domination, and the abuse of power. It is often depicted as a figure draped in regal garments, adorned with symbols of authority and surrounded by an aura of fear and submission. The god's presence instils a sense of dread and subservience, and its followers seek to impose their will upon others through force and oppression.

Edicts: The followers of tyranny are driven by their thirst for power and control over others. They are expected to subjugate and dominate those beneath them, establishing oppressive systems of governance and enforcing their rule through fear and intimidation. The followers are called to suppress dissent, crush resistance, and uphold the principles of authority, hierarchy, and ruthless governance.

Anathema: The followers of tyranny are forbidden from acts of compassion, mercy, or empathy. They must not show weakness or question the established order. The followers are prohibited from acts of kindness, fairness, or egalitarianism. They must not promote freedom, equality, or individual rights. It is important to note that such characters may be suitable for campaigns that explore the consequences and conflicts arising from oppressive regimes and the struggle for liberation.

Be aware that such characters might not be suitable for all RPG campaigns, especially those focused on heroic and virtuous storytelling.

Suggested Ethics: Ambition, Deception, Exploitation

Class Skill: Deception

Specialist Spells: Arc of Fire, Coercive Retribution, Deflect Flame, False Arrogance, Fateful Temptation, Shifting Step, Touch of Obedience, Veiled Presence

Bonus Spells: Orb of Fire (1); Charm Kind (2); Hold Kind (6); Crushing Despair (10)

Favoured Weapon: Flail

WAR

ORDER

The aspect of war is a powerful and formidable deity, embodying the spirit of conflict, strength, and strategic warfare. It is often depicted as a towering figure clad in armour, wielding mighty weapons and exuding an aura of power and martial prowess. The god's presence inspires both fear and awe, and its followers seek its favour to attain victory on the battlefield.

Edicts: The followers of war are called to embrace the art of combat and warfare. They are expected to be disciplined, courageous, and skilled warriors, honing their abilities through training and dedication. The followers are encouraged to defend their realms, protect their allies, and uphold honour and glory on the battlefield. They strive for victory, valour, and the pursuit of martial excellence.

Anathema: The followers of war are forbidden from acts of cowardice, treachery, or unnecessary violence. They must not kill prisoners or foes who have surrendered. The followers are prohibited from using warfare as a means to oppress or subjugate others unjustly. They must not forsake their comrades or abandon their responsibilities on the battlefield. It is important to note that such characters may be suitable for campaigns that explore the complexities and consequences of war.

Suggested Ethics: Autonomy, Justice, Prudence

Class Skill: Athletics

Specialist Spells: Banish Fatigue, Death’s Defiance, Destructive Roar, Devastating Might, Physical Surge, War Cry, Weapon Surge, Zealous Battlecry

Bonus Spells: Shield (1); True Strike (2); Haste (6) Stun Relief (10)

Favoured Weapon: Battleaxe

APPENDIX 5 - LUCK

LUCK

Being an adventurer can often be a very unforgiving task. It is amazing that characters progress through levels of experience at all with the many dangers that they face. The luck mechanic below can sometimes ease the life of the average treasure seeking character.

INITIAL LUCK

Each player (not character) begins at 1st level with a luck score of 15. This may be amended further by a number of character options.

If you bring in a new character at some later point during the campaign due to death, retirement etc, you transfer the current luck score from your previous character to the new.

LUCK CHECK

CHANCE FLOURISH

A luck check may be made to amend a number of elements in the game. Each time you make a luck check, your luck score may decrease (see below).

You may make a luck check up to once per round to attempt to do the following:

• Apply fortune to a skill check

• Apply fortune to an attack check

• Apply fortune to a saving throw

To make a luck check roll a d20 and apply your luck score against a static DC of 20 (some game mechanics and abilities may alter this DC) with the following results.

Critical Luck is truly on your side today. Your luck check succeeds and you do not reduce your luck score.

Success You are lucky this time and check succeeds. You reduce your luck score by 1 (min 2).

Failure Your luck has simply deserted you today. Your check fails and you reduce your luck score by 1 (min 2).

Fumble Luck is another creatures friend it would seem. If you were using luck to affect a skill, attack or saving throw the check gains disadvantage or a -5 penalty (whichever is worse). You also reduce your luck score by 1 (min 2).

Be Aware that you may only apply a fortune effect to a check once and therefore cannot use other abilities such as Halfling Luck to reroll a check after luck has been applied.

MONSTER/NPC LUCK

Some powerful or major NPC’s and monsters may be allowed to have a luck score. Such creatures may make a check (as detailed above) to negate your use of luck and for nothing else.

Such creatures will have a small pool of luck points which they can use to negate a luck check before it is made (thus you do not waste a check and lose luck). Rules for monsters and luck are covered in more detail in the Fiends & Fables sourcebook.

HALFLING LUCK

A character with the halfling luck feat reduces luck DC’s by 2 in addition to the feats normal benefits.

REGAINING LUCK

Once expended, there are the following ways to regain luck.

Rolling a Natural 20

If you roll an unmodified 20 on a check whilst in a situation that the GM deems strenuous (usually a check where a failure has detrimental effects), you regain 1 luck.

Dangerous Critical Damage

If you take a critical injury with a modified result of higher than 90 you regain a 1 luck.

Other Situations

The GM may deem that a particular action requires a luck reward, although such circumstances should be extremely rare.

Be aware that if you are using both the Luck and Conviction rules, you may only use one of these to affect the outcome of an individual check in any given round.

TRG – CHARACTER SHEET
